role: This corpus is the ground-floor engine of the wild (MacLane/Okutsu–Montes) side of the proof. It fixes an abstract "stage" — one level of the valuation tower at a prime, carrying a weight function, a residual (initial-form) map into Laurent polynomials over the current residue field, and realizer axioms — and develops the whole calculus of key-adic developments over it: existence and uniqueness of developments, the attained-minimum weight law, slot decomposition, digit multiplicativity, graded-piece structure, and the transition-step realizer supply. Its capstone converts membership in a higher-Newton-polygon stratum into an explicit "landing cylinder" — finitely many triangular digit equations on development coefficients — and — given coordinate presentations of the stratum that are hypothesized here rather than constructed — a stratum cut by k digit equations has exact, level-independent density 1/pᵏ: the mechanism that makes wildly ramified densities computable and prime-uniform. The definition layers (the stage, the stage-core invariant, the landing cylinder) are the interface the HC1 tower-induction and HC2 classifier-bridge corpora build on; three statements were machine-refuted during development and restated, with the refutation records kept on disk.
oneLiner: Residual and landing engine: stratum membership becomes exact digit counts

nodes.title: A stage of the valuation tower
nodes.math: One level of the valuation tower over $\mathbb{Z}_p[X]$, with its bookkeeping: coprime side data $(e,h)$ with Bézout $es+ht=1$ (and $t=0$ when $e=1$); a monic key polynomial $\Phi$; a stage valuation $w$ obeying the exact product law $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$ for nonzero $f,g$ (a genuine valuation — the graded-ring corpus's side valuations, by contrast, postulate only the inequality $w(f)+w(g)\le w(fg)$), the ultrametric law, value group $\mathbb{Z}$, and $w(\Phi)=h$ together with the parent stage's valuation $w_{\mathrm{prev}}$, related by the stretch $w(B)=e\,w_{\mathrm{prev}}(B)$ on the coefficient space $C_\Phi=\{B:\deg B<\deg\Phi\}$; residue fields $F_Q\le K$ (the fixed base residue field $F_Q$ inside the current residue field $K$) inside a fixed ambient finite field $F$; and a residual (weight-normalized initial form) map $R:\mathbb{Z}_p[X]\to K[z^{\pm1}]$ with $R(fg)=R(f)R(g)$, the ultrametric addition/dominance laws, $R(\Phi)=z^s$, monomial coefficient digits $R(B)=c\cdot z^{-t\,w_{\mathrm{prev}}(B)}$ ($c\in K^\times$), the attained-minimum law at the key, and realizers: each occurring coefficient weight is realized with digit scalars sweeping a coset $F_Q^\times\,b$ of the base-field orbit, and above the key threshold with arbitrary scalars in $K^\times$.
nodes.lean:
structure Stage (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] where
  e : ℕ
  h : ℕ
  s : ℤ
  t : ℤ
  he : 1 ≤ e
  hh : 1 ≤ h
  hcop : Nat.gcd e h = 1
  hbez : (e : ℤ) * s + (h : ℤ) * t = 1
  he1t : e = 1 → t = 0
  Φ : Polynomial ℤ_[p]
  hmonic : Φ.Monic
  hdeg : 1 ≤ Φ.natDegree
  w : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → ℤ
  wPrev : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → ℤ
  K : Subfield F
  FQ : Subfield F
  hFQ_le : FQ ≤ K
  R : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → LaurentPolynomial ↥K
  hwmul : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → w (f * g) = w f + w g
  hwult : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → f + g ≠ 0 → min (w f) (w g) ≤ w (f + g)
  hvalgrp : AddSubgroup.closure {n : ℤ | ∃ f g, f ≠ 0 ∧ g ≠ 0 ∧ w f - w g = n} = ⊤
  hwΦ : w Φ = (h : ℤ)
  hStretch : ∀ B, B ≠ 0 → inC Φ B → w B = (e : ℤ) * wPrev B
  hR0 : R 0 = 0
  hRne : ∀ f, f ≠ 0 → R f ≠ 0
  hRmul : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → R (f * g) = R f * R g
  hRadd : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → f + g ≠ 0 → w f = w g → w (f + g) = w f →
            R (f + g) = R f + R g
  hRlt : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → f + g ≠ 0 → w f < w g → R (f + g) = R f
  hRΦ : R Φ = LaurentPolynomial.T s
  hK1 : K1At w Φ (w Φ)
  hS5 : ∀ B, B ≠ 0 → inC Φ B →
          ∃ c : (↥K)ˣ,
            R B = LaurentPolynomial.C (c : ↥K) * LaurentPolynomial.T (- t * wPrev B)
  reps : List (Polynomial ℤ_[p])
  hreps : ∀ ũ ∈ reps, ũ ≠ 0 ∧ inC Φ ũ
  Tvec : List (Polynomial ℤ_[p] × ℤ)
  hTvec : Tvec.map Prod.fst = reps
  weightSet : Set ℤ
  hWS : ∀ B, B ≠ 0 → inC Φ B → wPrev B ∈ weightSet
  hS6a : ∀ ν : ℤ, ν ∈ weightSet → ∃ b : (↥K)ˣ, ∀ c : (↥K)ˣ, ((c : ↥K) : F) ∈ FQ →
           ∃ B, B ≠ 0 ∧ inC Φ B ∧ wPrev B = ν ∧
             R B = LaurentPolynomial.C ((c * b : (↥K)ˣ) : ↥K) * LaurentPolynomial.T (- t * ν)
  hS6b : ∀ (ν : ℤ) (a : (↥K)ˣ), wPrev Φ < ν →
           ∃ B, B ≠ 0 ∧ inC Φ B ∧ wPrev B = ν ∧
             R B = LaurentPolynomial.C (a : ↥K) * LaurentPolynomial.T (- t * ν)
nodes.note: The single abstract carrier every theorem in this corpus quantifies over. The realizer axiom (S6a) was restated to the coset form after its earlier untwisted transcription (base unit hard-coded to 1) was machine-refuted on the below-threshold strip (finite-field numerics, 2026-07-28).

nodes.title: The full stage-core invariant, stated at the genuine localization objects
nodes.math: The inductive invariant carried up the tower, in three layers. (i) Core laws: the parent valuation is multiplicative and ultrametric, $p$ is among the representatives, strictness ($w(f+g)=w(f)$ when $w(f)<w(g)$) and the jump law (equal weights whose sum jumps force residual cancellation $R(f)+R(g)=0$), the augmentation inequality $e\,w_{\mathrm{prev}}(\Phi)<h$, slot decomposition, and the coefficient-field laws. (ii) The T-vector product law at the actual unit (the T-vector is the stage's recorded list of (representative, integer exponent) pairs): in the two-variable Laurent model $L=K[z^{\pm1}][T^{\pm1}]$ of the graded algebra, the product of the initial-form units of the recorded representatives to their recorded exponents, times the initial form of $\Phi$ to the Bézout power $t$, equals the normalizing unit $T$ — as an identity of units. (iii) The coefficient-localization law (S4): the subring generated by initial forms of coefficients and inverses of representative units has degree-0 part exactly the constants $K$, and $z$ is exactly (scalar 1) the value of an explicit weight-0 monomial vector in the representatives and the key — the pinning $z=V^{-h}Y^{e}$.
nodes.lean:
def TvecUnitLaw (σ : Stage p F) : Prop :=
  ∃ (uY : (LTwo ↥σ.K)ˣ) (ru : Fin σ.Tvec.length → (LTwo ↥σ.K)ˣ),
    IsGrUnit σ σ.Φ uY ∧
    (∀ i, IsGrUnit σ (σ.Tvec.get i).1 (ru i)) ∧
    (∏ i, ru i ^ (σ.Tvec.get i).2) * uY ^ σ.t = locT ↥σ.K

def CoeffLocLaw (σ : Stage p F) : Prop :=
  (∀ ℓ : LaurentPolynomial ↥σ.K, LaurentPolynomial.C ℓ ∈ σ.coeffLocSR →
      ∃ d : ↥σ.K, ℓ = LaurentPolynomial.C d)
  ∧ (∀ d : ↥σ.K, LaurentPolynomial.C (LaurentPolynomial.C d) ∈ σ.coeffLocSR)
  ∧ (∃ (zv : LVec σ) (u : (LTwo ↥σ.K)ˣ),
      σ.lvecWeight zv = 0 ∧ IsLVecVal σ zv u ∧
      (u : LTwo ↥σ.K) = LaurentPolynomial.C (zvar ↥σ.K))

structure StageCoreL (σ : Stage p F) : Prop where
  core : StageCore σ
  tvec_unit : TvecUnitLaw σ
  coeff_loc : CoeffLocLaw σ
nodes.note: The invariant the base stage constructs and every transition transports (the tower induction itself lives in the HC1 corpus, which consumes this interface); the two localization laws were re-stated at the actual unit/subring objects after semantic audit round 4 found the earlier flattened forms faithless.

nodes.title: The landing cylinder with its triangular carry chain
nodes.math: Conditions on the development data $B_0,\dots,B_{N-1}$ of a polynomial along a lifted key, defining the landing locus of a stratum: there is a side-line value $m_0$ with slot $\mu$ on it ($w(B_\mu)+\mu\, e h g=m_0$), no slot below it, and every slot $j<\mu$ strictly above it (BOX/VERTEX); and the anchored minimizing-slot Laurent terms $c_j = z^{j\hat m - a}\,R(B_j)$ (where $\hat m=-thg$; zero at non-minimizing slots) reproduce a prescribed digit pattern $(C_j)$ through a triangular carry chain: $\mathrm{carry}_0=0$, $c_j+\mathrm{carry}_j = C_j + \psi\cdot\mathrm{carry}_{j+1}$ with each digit $C_j$ the canonical representative of degree $<\deg\psi$, and — the recorded terminal no-overflow clause — every carry from level $N$ on vanishes.
nodes.lean:
def IsCarryChainL {K : Type*} [Field K] (ψ : Polynomial K) (c : ℕ → LaurentPolynomial K)
    (Cdig : ℕ → Polynomial K) (carry : ℕ → LaurentPolynomial K) : Prop :=
  carry 0 = 0 ∧
  ∀ j, (Cdig j).degree < ψ.degree ∧
    c j + carry j = Polynomial.toLaurent (Cdig j) + Polynomial.toLaurent ψ * carry (j + 1)

def CarryTransportL {K : Type*} [Field K] (ψ : Polynomial K) (c : ℕ → LaurentPolynomial K)
    (Cdig : ℕ → Polynomial K) (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ carry : ℕ → LaurentPolynomial K,
    IsCarryChainL ψ c Cdig carry ∧ ∀ j, N ≤ j → carry j = 0

def LandingCylinderL (σ : Stage p F) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (μ : ℕ) (a : ℤ)
    (Cdig : ℕ → Polynomial ↥σ.K) (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ m₀ : ℤ,
    B μ ≠ 0 ∧ σ.w (B μ) + (μ : ℤ) * ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g) = m₀ ∧
    (∀ j, j < N → B j ≠ 0 → m₀ ≤ σ.w (B j) + (j : ℤ) * ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g)) ∧
    (∀ j, j < μ → B j ≠ 0 → m₀ < σ.w (B j) + (j : ℤ) * ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g)) ∧
    ∃ cL : ℕ → LaurentPolynomial ↥σ.K,
      (∀ j, j < N →
        ((B j ≠ 0 ∧ σ.w (B j) + (j : ℤ) * ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g) = m₀) →
          cL j = LaurentPolynomial.T ((j : ℤ) * (- σ.t * σ.h * g) - a) * σ.R (B j)) ∧
        (¬ (B j ≠ 0 ∧ σ.w (B j) + (j : ℤ) * ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g) = m₀) → cL j = 0)) ∧
      (∀ j, N ≤ j → cL j = 0) ∧
      CarryTransportL ψ cL Cdig N
nodes.note: The digit-cylinder shape that turns stratum membership into finitely many triangular equations; two audit-forced fixes are built in (slot terms kept as Laurent elements, terminal no-overflow recorded), while a third omission — the anchor-exactness pin — was later exposed by a countermodel family and is supplied as an explicit hypothesis in the two-sided landing theorem.

nodes.title: Every polynomial has a development along a monic key
nodes.math: Over any commutative ring $R$: for every monic $\Phi\in R[X]$ with $\deg\Phi\ge 1$ and every $f\in R[X]$ there exist coefficients $B_0,B_1,\dots$ and a length $N$ with $\deg B_j<\deg\Phi$ for all $j$, $B_j=0$ for $j\ge N$, and $f=\sum_{j<N}B_j\,\Phi^{\,j}$ — the $\Phi$-adic development.
nodes.lean:
theorem L0_FactA_exists {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (Φ : Polynomial R) (hΦ : Φ.Monic)
    (hd : 1 ≤ Φ.natDegree) (f : Polynomial R) :
    ∃ (B : ℕ → Polynomial R) (N : ℕ), IsDevelopment Φ f B N
nodes.note: The base-of-everything Fact A: stated polymorphically over any commutative ring so it descends to the reduced digit boxes mod p^N used by the counting endpoint; heavily imported by the HC1/HC2 hard-core corpora.

nodes.title: Developments along a monic key are unique
nodes.math: Over any commutative ring: two $\Phi$-adic developments of the same polynomial $f$ along the same monic key $\Phi$ agree in every slot, $B_j = B'_j$ for all $j$ (regardless of their recorded lengths).
nodes.lean: theorem L0_FactB_unique {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (Φ : Polynomial R) (hΦ : Φ.Monic) (f : Polynomial R) {B B' : ℕ → Polynomial R} {N N' : ℕ} (h : IsDevelopment Φ f B N) (h' : IsDevelopment Φ f B' N') : ∀ j, B j = B' j
nodes.note: Fact B: uniqueness is what lets digit patterns be read off canonically — the landing theorems and the pattern-recovery direction of the capstone lean on it directly.

nodes.title: The Gauss valuation is multiplicative
nodes.math: For nonzero $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}_p[X]$, the Gauss (content) valuation $v(f)=\min_i v_p(a_i)$ over the coefficients satisfies $v(fg)=v(f)+v(g)$ — Gauss's lemma in valuation form.
nodes.lean: theorem L1_gaussVal_mul {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (f g : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) : gaussVal (f * g) = gaussVal f + gaussVal g
nodes.note: The zeroth-level valuation of the tower; the base stage valuation is built from it.

nodes.title: The first-level tower valuation is multiplicative (the MacLane base case)
nodes.math: Let $\varphi\in\mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ be monic of degree $\ge 1$ and irreducible mod $p$, and let $(e,h)$ be coprime positive integers. Define $w(f)=\min_i\big(e\,v(a_i)+i\,h\big)$ over the $\varphi$-adic development $f=\sum_i a_i\varphi^i$ ($v$ the Gauss valuation). Then $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$ for nonzero $f,g$ — the first level of the tower is a genuine valuation.
nodes.lean: theorem L1_baseWeight_valuation {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (φ : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (e h : ℕ) (hmon : φ.Monic) (hd : 1 ≤ φ.natDegree) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hh : 1 ≤ h) (hcop : Nat.gcd e h = 1) (hirred : Irreducible (φ.map (PadicInt.toZMod : ℤ_[p] →+* ZMod p))) (f g : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) : baseWeight φ e h (f * g) = baseWeight φ e h f + baseWeight φ e h g
nodes.note: The base case that anchors the whole tower in a genuine valuation; it was left open (a fenced unproved goal) for one development round and was discharged 2026-07-27 by a direct MacLane-style argument (Cauchy-product development with carries), with no graded-ring machinery.

nodes.title: Slot decomposition and slot independence of the residual map
nodes.math: Given the strictness law ($w(f+g)=w(f)$ when $w(f)<w(g)$), the jump law (equal weights whose sum's weight jumps force $R(f)+R(g)=0$), and $R(-f)=-R(f)$, the stage satisfies both halves of slot decomposition: (i) within one graded piece, the residual of a development whose nonzero slots all have total weight $\gamma$ and whose sum stays at weight $\gamma$ is the sum of the slot residuals; (ii) independence: a combination $\sum_j R(B_j)\,R(\Phi)^j$ whose nonzero slots all live in one graded piece vanishes only termwise — the class of the key is transcendental over the coefficient classes, degreewise.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_slotDecomp {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (hstrict : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → σ.w f < σ.w g → σ.w (f + g) = σ.w f) (hjump : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → f + g ≠ 0 → σ.w f = σ.w g → σ.w f < σ.w (f + g) → σ.R f + σ.R g = 0) (hneg : ∀ f, σ.R (-f) = - σ.R f) : SlotDecomp σ
nodes.note: Converts the raw residual laws into the graded decomposition plus the transcendence half a semantic audit demanded — the two facts every downstream landing and transition argument transports.

nodes.title: The stride rule: residuals of coefficient-times-key-power
nodes.math: For a nonzero coefficient $B$ (i.e. $\deg B<\deg\Phi$) and any $j\ge 0$: $R(B\cdot\Phi^j)=R(B)\cdot z^{\,s j}$. Multiplying by the key strides the residual by a fixed power of $z$.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_strideRule {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (B : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hBc : inC σ.Φ B) (j : ℕ) : σ.R (B * σ.Φ ^ j) = σ.R B * LaurentPolynomial.T (σ.s * j)
nodes.note: The workhorse computation rule: it forces the distinct z-positions that make slot terms independent, and feeds the realizer and landing arguments throughout.

nodes.title: Structure of a graded piece: injective, additive, base-field-linear, with known image
nodes.math: Fix a weight $\gamma$. On the weight-$\gamma$ piece: (1) the residual map is injective up to higher weight — $R(f)=R(f')$ forces $f=f'$ or $w(f-f')>\gamma$; (2) it is additive when the sum stays at weight $\gamma$; (3) multiplication by a weight-0 coefficient lift $\hat u$ whose residual is a base-field constant $c\in F_Q$ preserves the piece and scales the residual by $c$ — an $F_Q$-linear endomorphism of the graded piece; (4)+(5) the image of the piece under $R$ is exactly the nonzero part of the additive span of the slot images.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_P6i {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (hcore : StageCore σ) (γ : ℤ) : (∀ f f', f ≠ 0 → f' ≠ 0 → σ.w f = γ → σ.w f' = γ → σ.R f = σ.R f' → f - f' = 0 ∨ γ < σ.w (f - f')) ∧ (∀ f f', f ≠ 0 → f' ≠ 0 → f + f' ≠ 0 → σ.w f = γ → σ.w f' = γ → σ.w (f + f') = γ → σ.R (f + f') = σ.R f + σ.R f') ∧ (∀ (û : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (c : ↥σ.FQ), û ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → inC σ.Φ û → σ.w û = 0 → σ.R û = LaurentPolynomial.C (Subfield.inclusion σ.hFQ_le c) * LaurentPolynomial.T (0 : ℤ) → ∀ f, f ≠ 0 → σ.w f = γ → σ.w (û * f) = γ ∧ σ.R (û * f) = LaurentPolynomial.C (Subfield.inclusion σ.hFQ_le c) * σ.R f) ∧ (∀ f, f ≠ 0 → σ.w f = γ → σ.R f ∈ AddSubgroup.closure (σ.slotImages γ)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ AddSubgroup.closure (σ.slotImages γ), x ≠ 0 → ∃ f, f ≠ 0 ∧ σ.w f = γ ∧ σ.R f = x)
nodes.note: Identifies each graded piece of the valuation completely; the scalar clause was repaired at audit round 4 (the earlier form did not conclude weight preservation, so it was not an endomorphism of the piece), and this final restatement is fully proved.

nodes.title: The attained-minimum weight law at a lifted key
nodes.math: Let $\psi$ be monic irreducible over the current residue field $K$, $\psi\ne z$, $\deg\psi=g$, and let $\hat\Phi$ be its standard lift (the displayed formula $\hat\Phi=\Phi^{eg}+\sum_k t_k\Phi^{ek}$ with prescribed realizer coefficients). Then for every nonzero $f$ and every development $f=\sum_j B_j\hat\Phi^j$: $w(f)=\min_j\big(w(B_j)+j\cdot ehg\big)$, and the minimum is attained.
nodes.lean: theorem L3_K1 {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (hg : ψ.natDegree = g) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X) (hmon : ψ.Monic) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat) : K1At σ.w Φhat ((σ.e : ℤ) * σ.h * g)
nodes.note: The central weight formula of the engine (MacLane's key lemma at the lifted key): it is what lets weights and residuals be read off development slots, and both landing directions reduce to it.

nodes.title: Weights and digits multiply through division by the lifted key
nodes.math: Same setup, with $\bar z\in F$ a root of $\psi$: for nonzero $B,B''$ in the coefficient space of the lifted key $\hat\Phi$ (degree $<eg\cdot\deg\Phi$), writing $B\cdot B''=Q\hat\Phi+R_{\mathrm{dev}}$ with $\deg R_{\mathrm{dev}}<eg\cdot\deg\Phi$: the remainder is nonzero, $w(R_{\mathrm{dev}})=w(B)+w(B'')$, and the residue digit is multiplicative, $\mathrm{dig}'_{\bar z}(R_{\mathrm{dev}})=\mathrm{dig}'_{\bar z}(B)\cdot\mathrm{dig}'_{\bar z}(B'')$.
nodes.lean: theorem L3_DIV {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (hg : ψ.natDegree = g) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat) (zbar : Fˣ) (hzbar : Polynomial.eval₂ σ.K.subtype (zbar : F) ψ = 0) (B B'' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hB'' : B'' ≠ 0) (hBd : B.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree) (hB''d : B''.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree) (Rdev Q : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hdiv : B * B'' = Q * Φhat + Rdev) (hRd : Rdev.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree) : Rdev ≠ 0 ∧ σ.w Rdev = σ.w B + σ.w B'' ∧ σ.digPrime zbar Rdev = σ.digPrime zbar B * σ.digPrime zbar B''
nodes.note: The one-step residue-field multiplication: it is how the residue field grows by the degree of psi at each tower step, feeding the transition construction in HC1.

nodes.title: The index recursion and single-orbit realizers at a tower transition
nodes.math: At a recorded transition from stage $\sigma$ to child $\sigma'$ along a lifted key of degree $eg\cdot\deg\Phi$: (1) the parent-scale weights occurring in the child coefficient space are exactly $\{\gamma+jh : \gamma$ an occurring parent weight, $0\le j<eg\}$; and (2) for each such index $(\gamma,j)$ there is one fixed base unit $d_0$ of the child residue field such that every base-field orbit scalar $c\in F_Q^\times$ is realized by an element $B$ of the child coefficient space with parent weight $\gamma+jh$, child weight $e'(\gamma+jh)$, and child residual a monomial at the forced position with digit scalar $d=c\cdot d_0$ — the realizer digits of one index sweep exactly one coset of the base-field orbit.
nodes.lean: theorem L4_TRANSviii_a {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ σ' : Stage p F) (hcore : StageCoreL σ) (g : ℕ) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hΦdeg : Φhat.natDegree = σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree) (e' h' : ℕ) (zbar : Fˣ) (htrans : TransitionCoreL σ σ' Φhat e' h' zbar) : (∀ W' : ℤ, (∃ B, B ≠ 0 ∧ inC Φhat B ∧ σ'.wPrev B = W') ↔ (∃ (γ : ℤ) (j : ℕ), (∃ C, C ≠ 0 ∧ inC σ.Φ C ∧ σ.w C = γ) ∧ j < σ.e * g ∧ W' = γ + (j : ℤ) * σ.h)) ∧ (∀ (γ : ℤ) (j : ℕ), (∃ C, C ≠ 0 ∧ inC σ.Φ C ∧ σ.w C = γ) → j < σ.e * g → ∃ d₀ : (↥σ'.K)ˣ, ∀ c : (↥σ'.K)ˣ, ((c : ↥σ'.K) : F) ∈ σ'.FQ → ∃ B, B ≠ 0 ∧ inC Φhat B ∧ σ'.wPrev B = γ + (j : ℤ) * σ.h ∧ σ'.w B = (σ'.e : ℤ) * (γ + (j : ℤ) * σ.h) ∧ ∃ d : (↥σ'.K)ˣ, σ'.R B = LaurentPolynomial.C (d : ↥σ'.K) * LaurentPolynomial.T (- σ'.t * (γ + (j : ℤ) * σ.h)) ∧ ((d : ↥σ'.K) : F) = ((c : ↥σ'.K) : F) * ((d₀ : ↥σ'.K) : F))
nodes.note: The realizer supply that lets the induction climb one level: how the coefficient-weight index set and its realizing digits recur at a transition; its conclusion was weakened from a fixed root-monomial class to the coset form (2026-07-28) after the stronger untwisted form was machine-refuted, and a companion child-stage-free variant was added to break a circularity found in the HC1 induction.

nodes.title: The two-sided landing theorem: stratum membership equals cylinder membership
nodes.math:
Let $\psi$ be monic irreducible over $K$, $\psi
e z$, of degree $g$, with standard lift $\hat\Phi$; let $f
e 0$ have $\hat\Phi$-adic development $(B_j)_{j<N}$, let $\mu<N$, and assume the anchor-exactness pin: $X
mid\sum_{j<N}C_j\psi^j$ (the prescribed digit pattern's total has nonzero constant coefficient). Then $f$ lies in the $(\mu,a,(C_j))$-stratum — meaning $z^{-a}R(f)$ is a polynomial with nonzero constant term whose $\psi$-adic development has digits $(C_j)$, vanishing below slot $\mu$ and nonzero at $\mu$ — if and only if the development data $(B_j)$ lies in the landing cylinder (the side-line BOX/VERTEX conditions plus the anchored Laurent slot terms reproducing $(C_j)$ through the terminating carry chain).
nodes.lean: theorem L5_landTwoSided {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (hcore : StageCore σ) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (hg : ψ.natDegree = g) (hgpos : 1 ≤ g) (hmon : ψ.Monic) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat) (μ : ℕ) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N : ℕ) (hμN : μ < N) (hdev : IsDevelopment Φhat f B N) (a : ℤ) (Cdig : ℕ → Polynomial ↥σ.K) (hexact : ¬ Polynomial.X ∣ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, Cdig j * ψ ^ j) : StratumData σ ψ μ a Cdig N f ↔ LandingCylinderL σ ψ g μ a Cdig B N
nodes.note: THE capstone of this corpus, proved in both directions with no sorry: it converts Newton-polygon stratum membership into digit equations on development data; the hexact hypothesis was added in a round-6 repair after a countermodel family (shifting the anchor and re-developing) showed the pin-free version false, and the audit record scopes the result to the abstract stage laws (the graded-localization provenance is certified separately in HC1).

nodes.title: Residuals are determined by slot data (transport)
nodes.math: With $\hat\Phi$ the standard lift of an irreducible $\psi\ne z$ and the attained-minimum law holding at $\hat\Phi$: if two nonzero polynomials $f,f'$ have developments along $\hat\Phi$ that agree slotwise in both residual and weight ($R(B_j)=R(B'_j)$ and $w(B_j)=w(B'_j)$ for all $j<N$), then $R(f)=R(f')$.
nodes.lean: theorem L5_landTransport {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (hcore : StageCore σ) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (hg : ψ.natDegree = g) (hgpos : 1 ≤ g) (hmon : ψ.Monic) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat) (hK1 : K1At σ.w Φhat (σ.w Φhat)) (f f' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hf' : f' ≠ 0) (B B' : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N : ℕ) (hd : IsDevelopment Φhat f B N) (hd' : IsDevelopment Φhat f' B' N) (hslotR : ∀ j, j < N → σ.R (B j) = σ.R (B' j)) (hslotw : ∀ j, j < N → σ.w (B j) = σ.w (B' j)) : σ.R f = σ.R f'
nodes.note: The determinacy fact behind measure exactness — elements with the same digit data are residually indistinguishable; this is the corrected restatement after the untied original was refuted (see the refutation-record node).

nodes.title: Transport without tying the key to the stage is false (refutation record)
nodes.math: The same transport statement quantified over an arbitrary development key $\hat\Phi$, untied to the stage (no standard-lift or attained-minimum hypothesis), is false in the intended base-stage model: with $\hat\Phi=1+X$, $f=p+X$, $f'=p^2+X$, all slot residuals and slot weights agree, yet $R(f)\ne R(f')$ — the minimal-weight block cancels residually and the residual is read off sub-leading data that slot residuals do not pin.
nodes.lean: theorem L5_landTransport {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (f f' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hf' : f' ≠ 0) (B B' : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N : ℕ) (hd : IsDevelopment Φhat f B N) (hd' : IsDevelopment Φhat f' B' N) (hslotR : ∀ j, j < N → σ.R (B j) = σ.R (B' j)) (hslotw : ∀ j, j < N → σ.w (B j) = σ.w (B' j)) : σ.R f = σ.R f'
nodes.note: A refutation record kept on disk: the fenced round-3 statement is deliberately left unproved because it is refuted — the explicit countermodel is documented in the file header (as a verified analysis in the intended model, not a compiled Lean disproof) — and the repaired restatement with the key tied to the stage is the proved transport node.

nodes.title: Machine-checked disproof: reduction of developments fails at level zero
nodes.math: It is NOT the case that for every prime $p$, monic key $\hat\Phi$, development $f=\sum_j B_j\hat\Phi^j$, and every $M\ge 0$, the coefficientwise reduction mod $p^M$ is again a development: at $M=0$ the target ring $\mathbb{Z}/p^0=\mathbb{Z}/1$ is trivial, so all mapped polynomials vanish and the degree clause $\deg B_j<\deg\hat\Phi$ fails. Compiled disproof by the witness $\hat\Phi=X$, $f=1$ over $\mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.lean:
theorem L6_moveReduceCommute_statement_false :
    ¬ (∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (Φhat f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), Φhat.Monic →
        ∀ (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N M : ℕ), IsDevelopment Φhat f B N →
        IsDevelopment (Φhat.map (PadicInt.toZModPow M)) (f.map (PadicInt.toZModPow M))
          (fun j => (B j).map (PadicInt.toZModPow M)) N)
nodes.note: A compiled refutation from development: the originally specified statement is false-as-stated and was disproved in Lean rather than silently weakened — the false version is kept on record behind a statement fence (an unproved goal), and the corrected version (next node) was proved separately.

nodes.title: Developments commute with reduction modulo prime powers
nodes.math: For every $M\ge 1$: if $f=\sum_{j<N}B_j\hat\Phi^j$ is a development along the monic key $\hat\Phi$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, then reducing every ingredient mod $p^M$ yields a development of the reduction of $f$ along the reduction of $\hat\Phi$, with the same slots and length.
nodes.lean: theorem L6_moveReduceCommute {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (Φhat f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hmon : Φhat.Monic) (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (N M : ℕ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hdev : IsDevelopment Φhat f B N) : IsDevelopment (Φhat.map (PadicInt.toZModPow M)) (f.map (PadicInt.toZModPow M)) (fun j => (B j).map (PadicInt.toZModPow M)) N
nodes.note: The bridge from p-adic development data to the finite digit boxes where counting happens; corrected form (adds M >= 1) after the machine-checked disproof of the unguarded original.

nodes.title: The stratum measure is exactly 1/p^k, independently of the reading level
nodes.math: Fix a stratum (a vertex $\mu$, anchor $a$, digit pattern $(C_j)$ with the anchor-exactness pin) and let $D$ be the degree budget. Suppose that at two levels $N$ and $M$ we are given coordinate presentations: surjective codes of polynomials of degree $<D$ onto the digit boxes $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^{DN}$ and $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^{DM}$ presenting the stratum, coordinate changes $\Theta$, and digit systems each pinning exactly $k$ coordinates whose solution sets present the landing cylinder (and reject the zero polynomial's coordinates). Then the two densities agree: $\#\{\text{stratum solutions at level }N\}/p^{DN} = \#\{\text{stratum solutions at level }M\}/p^{DM}$ — the stratum has one exact measure, $1/p^k$, at every level.

(hmon : ψ.Monic) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat) (μ : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (Cdig : ℕ → Polynomial ↥σ.K) (Nslots : ℕ) (hμN : μ < Nslots) (hexact : ¬ Polynomial.X ∣ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range Nslots, Cdig j * ψ ^ j) (D k : ℕ) (hD : D = Φhat.natDegree * Nslots) (N M : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hkN : k ≤ D * N) (hkM : k ≤ D * M) (stratN : (Fin (D * N) → ZMod p) → Prop) (stratM : (Fin (D * M) → ZMod p) → Prop) (codeN : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → (Fin (D * N) → ZMod p)) (codeM : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → (Fin (D * M) → ZMod p)) (hcodeN : ∀ x, nodes.note: The counting endpoint of the corpus: machine-checked with no axioms beyond Lean's core since a 2026-07-30 revision (approved by the project lead) made it consume the two-sided landing theorem — but conditional: the jet-coordinate presentations are hypothesized, not built, so this is the shape of the measure-exactness endpoint rather than the derived endpoint itself; the corresponding statement change still awaits an independent semantic review.

nodes.title: A stratum cut by k digit equations has exactly p^(nN-k) points
nodes.math: If the solution set of a stratum on the digit box $(\mathbb{Z}/p^N)^n$ is in bijection with $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^{nN-k}$ — the shape produced by $k$ unitriangular digit equations — then its cardinality is exactly $p^{\,nN-k}$.
nodes.lean: theorem L6_ledgerCount {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (n N k : ℕ) (stratum : (Fin n → ZMod (p ^ N)) → Prop) (e : {x // stratum x} ≃ (Fin (n * N - k) → ZMod p)) : Nat.card {x // stratum x} = p ^ (n * N - k)
nodes.note: The final arithmetic step of the story: once the landing theorems have turned a stratum into k triangular digit equations, this is why its density is a power of 1/p — the q-uniformity the whole project is about.

role: MovesC formalizes the composition-and-counting theorem (Theorem C) of the classifier analysis: it makes exact the volume bookkeeping of the Okutsu–Montes classifier's successive reads on the digit box of a monic degree-n p-adic polynomial truncated at p-adic level N. The bottom layers prove that triangular digit systems have mass p^(m−pins) (pins = the number of coordinates the system forces to a single value), that pinned-or-free status is determined by the solution set alone, and that the classifier's coordinate moves are pin-preserving bijections of the box; the middle layers prove each read cuts its state cylinder by exactly its nominal volume p^(−m*); the top layer assembles Theorem C: the classifier locus S(H,Z) satisfies #S(H,Z)·p^(Σm* + pins(Z)) = p^(nN), division-free. All 36 units (one stated Lean theorem or definition per unit) are proved — machine-checked, with no axioms beyond Lean's core — after six rounds of adversarial review that killed several vacuity loopholes (including a certified empty-stratum countermodel). The conditionality: every theorem about a real read history is stated against a hypothesized jet-presentation interface whose construction from the actual classifier — the graded-ring bridge — is the corpus's declared open boundary.
oneLiner: Each classifier read cuts exact volume; masses multiply to Theorem C

nodes.title: Loci as triangular digit systems, and their mass
nodes.math: The ambient box is $\mathbb{F}_p^{\,m}$ with $m = nN$: the first $N$ base-$p$ digits of each of the $n$ coefficients of a monic degree-$n$ polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, listed in a fixed global solving order $\prec$ (digit level ascending; within a level, top coefficient first). A locus is a triangular digit system on this box: a subset of pinned coordinates, each pinned coordinate given as a function of the strictly $\prec$-earlier coordinates. Its solution set is a cylinder, and its mass is the number of solutions among the $p^m$ box points.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
abbrev Locus (p m : ℕ) : Type := DigitSystem m (ZMod p)

noncomputable def Locus.mass {p m : ℕ} (D : Locus p m) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {x : Fin m → ZMod p // D.IsSolution x}
nodes.note: The common currency of the corpus: every counting statement is an identity between masses of loci, and "codimension" always means number of pinned coordinates (the underlying digit-system structure is inherited from the Moves corpus).

nodes.title: Address-free fresh clause: support, codimension, exact count
nodes.math: A fresh clause on the box is carried by exactly three statistics: a support $S$ (the coordinates it is allowed to read — enforced as an axiom of the structure), a codimension $a$, and the exact-count law $\#\{y \text{ supported on } S : y \text{ satisfies the clause}\}\cdot p^{a} = p^{|S|}$ — the clause cuts exactly the fraction $p^{-a}$, stated division-free. The fresh data of one classifier read is a finite list of such clauses with pairwise disjoint supports; its total codimension is $m^* = \sum a$.
nodes.lean:
structure LevelClause (p m : ℕ) where
  support : Finset (Fin m)
  codim : ℕ
  sat : (Fin m → ZMod p) → Prop
  dep : ∀ x y : Fin m → ZMod p, (∀ c ∈ support, x c = y c) → (sat x ↔ sat y)
  count : Nat.card {y : Fin m → ZMod p // sat y ∧ ∀ c ∉ support, y c = 0} * p ^ codim
    = p ^ support.card

structure FreshData (p m : ℕ) where
  clauses : List (LevelClause p m)
  disj : clauses.Pairwise (fun c₁ c₂ => Disjoint c₁.support c₂.support)

def FreshData.mstar {p m : ℕ} (fd : FreshData p m) : ℕ :=
  (fd.clauses.map LevelClause.codim).sum
nodes.note: The audit-driven "address-free" design: counting consumes only support, codimension, and the exact-count law, so no clause can smuggle in an unverified pin address — and the count law is self-policing (an unsatisfiable clause cannot even be instantiated).

nodes.title: Admissible transitions and realizable histories (the empty-stratum fence)
nodes.math: A read $\nu$ appended after the standing node $\nu_p$ is transition-admissible when three conditions hold on the recorded data alone: (NA) if the new side ends strictly left of the standing window vertex, the extended new line passes strictly below the pinned old vertex height; (HV) if the read is adjacent (its side reaches the vertex), its lead pattern digit equals the transported vertex value in the residue field; (SAE) the new side lies strictly above the old line at every span slot left of the vertex, with equality at the vertex in the adjacent case. A history is realizable when every consecutive pair of its nodes is transition-admissible. Theorem C's quantifier ranges over realizable histories only: a history failing any of the three conditions has empty stratum and is never emitted by the classifier.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
def TransitionAdmissible (νp ν : Node p F) : Prop :=
  (ν.s0 + ν.wSide < νp.μ →
    ν.line.at (νp.μ * νp.childWidth) < νp.line.at (νp.μ * νp.childWidth)) ∧
  (ν.s0 + ν.wSide = νp.μ →
    ((ν.pat (ν.wSide / ν.e) : ↥ν.σ.K) : F) = νp.vtx) ∧
  (∀ j : ℕ, ν.s0 ≤ j → j ≤ ν.s0 + ν.wSide → j < νp.μ →
    νp.line.at (j * νp.childWidth) < ν.line.at (j * νp.childWidth)) ∧
  (ν.s0 + ν.wSide = νp.μ →
    ν.line.at (νp.μ * νp.childWidth) = νp.line.at (νp.μ * νp.childWidth))

def Realizable (H : History p F) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < H.nodes.length),
    TransitionAdmissible (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)) (H.nodes[i+1]'hi)
nodes.note: An earlier two-condition version admitted a certified countermodel (the "F-EMPTY" instance — a history with nominal fresh volume $2^{-6}$ whose actual stratum census is 0 points); the strict span-entry condition (SAE) was added at audit round 4 to exclude it, and all downstream theorems now hypothesize the full class.

nodes.title: The jet-presentation interface: the declared boundary with the unbuilt graded ring
nodes.math: A jet presentation of a read history $H$ at level cutoff $N \geq 1$ bundles everything Theorem C needs, each field a provenance sentence tied to the recorded nodes: a $\prec$-sorted chart of the $nN$-digit box; coherence and realizability of $H$; state cylinders $\Sigma_i$ (with $\Sigma_0$ the full box); per-read fresh clause data; unitriangular move maps $\Theta_i$; recorded landing keys; a presentation predicate "$x$ is the frame-$i$ digit presentation of the polynomial $f$" that is literal $p$-adic digits at frame 0, total on monic degree-$n$ polynomials, intertwined by the moves, and block-local over key developments; the stratum recursion $\Sigma_{i+1} = \Theta_i^*(\Sigma_i \cap \text{stratum}_i)$ with inherited content implied on the cylinder; the exact zero-downset invariant (a coordinate is pinned iff its height is at most the cumulative floor, and interior pins are literal zeros); and the fresh-band laws forcing every clause to be either a strip (one coordinate, codimension 1, a literal zero, never at a value position) or a value clause (the complete level set of one recorded span slot, codimension = its size), with the total $m^*$ equal to the geometric band count computed from node data.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
structure JetSetup (H : History p F) (n N m : ℕ) where
  hm : m = n * N
  hN : 1 ≤ N
  coordOf : Fin m → Coord
  coordOf_sorted : ∀ j j' : Fin m, j < j' ↔ CoordPrec (coordOf j) (coordOf j')
  coordOf_lt : ∀ j : Fin m, (coordOf j).1 < N ∧ (coordOf j).2 < n
  coherent : HistoryCoherent H
  realizable : Realizable H
  root_height : ∀ (hj : 0 < H.nodes.length) (b : ℕ),
    b < (H.nodes[0]'hj).μ * (H.nodes[0]'hj).childWidth → 1 ≤ (H.nodes[0]'hj).line.at b
  Sigma : ℕ → Locus p m
  init : ∀ c : Fin m, (Sigma 0).pinned c = false
  fresh : ℕ → FreshData p m
  Theta : ℕ → ((Fin m → ZMod p) → (Fin m → ZMod p))
  Theta_uni : ∀ i : ℕ, IsUnitriangular (Theta i)
  keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]
  keys_mid : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 < H.nodes.length), keys i = (H.nodes[i+1]'hi).σ.Φ
  landing : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length), LandingKey (H.nodes[i]'hi) (keys i)
  pres : ℕ → (Fin m → ZMod p) → Polynomial ℤ_[p] → Prop
  pres_zero : ∀ (x : Fin m → ZMod p) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]),
    pres 0 x f ↔ ∀ j : Fin m, x j = baseDigit p (coordOf j).1 (f.coeff (coordOf j).2)
  pres_total : ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ H.nodes.length → ∀ f : Polynomial ℤ_[p],
    f.Monic → f.natDegree = n → ∃ x, pres i x f
  pres_theta : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length →
    ∀ (x : Fin m → ZMod p) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), pres (i+1) x f → pres i (Theta i x) f
  pres_block : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length →
    ∀ (f f' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (x x' : Fin m → ZMod p), pres (i+1) x f → pres (i+1) x' f' →
    ∀ (B B' : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (Nd Nd' : ℕ),
      IsDevelopment (keys i) f B Nd → IsDevelopment (keys i) f' B' Nd' →
      ∀ c : Fin m,
        B ((coordOf c).2 / (keys i).natDegree) = B' ((coordOf c).2 / (keys i).natDegree) →
        x c = x' c
  stratum : ℕ → (Fin m → ZMod p) → Prop
  recursion : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length → ∀ x : Fin m → ZMod p,
    (Sigma (i+1)).IsSolution x ↔ ((Sigma i).IsSolution (Theta i x) ∧ stratum i (Theta i x))
  inh_implied : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length → ∀ y : Fin m → ZMod p,
    (Sigma i).IsSolution y → (stratum i y ↔ (fresh i).sat y)
  zc : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length),
    ZCData (Sigma (i+1)) coordOf (H.htH (i+1)) (H.floorH (i+1))
      ((H.nodes[i]'hi).μ * (H.nodes[i]'hi).childWidth)
  fresh_band : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length), ∀ cl ∈ (fresh i).clauses,
    ∀ c ∈ cl.support, inFreshBand H n coordOf i (H.nodes[i]'hi) c
  fresh_cover : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length), ∀ c : Fin m,
    inFreshBand H n coordOf i (H.nodes[i]'hi) c → ∃ cl ∈ (fresh i).clauses, c ∈ cl.support
  fresh_assembled : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length), ∀ cl ∈ (fresh i).clauses,
    (∃ c : Fin m, cl.support = {c} ∧ cl.codim = 1 ∧ (∀ x, (cl.sat x ↔ x c = 0)) ∧
      ¬ IsValueCoord H coordOf i (H.nodes[i]'hi) c) ∨
    (IsValueSupport H coordOf i (H.nodes[i]'hi) cl.support ∧
      cl.codim = cl.support.card ∧
      ∃ (T : TypObject p m cl.support (Fin cl.codim → ZMod p)) (v : Fin cl.codim → ZMod p),
        ∀ x, (cl.sat x ↔ T.φ x = v))
  mstar_eq : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length),
    (fresh i).mstar = Nat.card {c : Fin m // inFreshBand H n coordOf i (H.nodes[i]'hi) c}
nodes.note: The corpus's declared trust boundary, hardened over six adversarial audit rounds (the fresh-band laws kill clause-permutation and all-singleton-zero impersonations that earlier rounds admitted); what remains open is constructing this bundle for a real classifier history — the unbuilt graded-ring bridge — plus two flagged identifications on the height function.

nodes.title: Mass of a digit system is p to the number of free coordinates
nodes.math: Let $D$ be a triangular digit system on $m$ coordinates over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $k$ pinned coordinates. Then the number of solutions of $D$ in the box $\mathbb{F}_p^m$ is exactly $p^{m-k}$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C0_digitSystemMass {m : ℕ} (D : Locus p m) : D.mass = p ^ (m - D.numPinned)
nodes.note: The base counting law: every density computation in the corpus reduces to pin bookkeeping through this identity (a specialization of the general alphabet count proved in the Moves corpus).

nodes.title: Pinned-or-free status is determined by the solution set alone
nodes.math: If two triangular digit systems $D, D'$ on the same $m$-coordinate box have identical solution sets, then every coordinate has the same pinned/free status in both. In particular the codimension (pin count) is an invariant of the cylinder, not of its presentation.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C0_pinStatus {m : ℕ} (D D' : Locus p m) (h : ∀ x, D.IsSolution x ↔ D'.IsSolution x) : ∀ j : Fin m, D.pinned j = D'.pinned j
nodes.note: Makes codimension bookkeeping well-defined coordinate by coordinate (strengthening the mass-equality version), so systems transported through moves can be compared pin by pin.

nodes.title: Unitriangular moves are bijections of the digit box
nodes.math: Call a self-map $\Theta$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^m$ unitriangular for the solving order if $(\Theta x)_i = x_i + \varphi_i(x_j : j \prec i)$ for every coordinate $i$, where each correction $\varphi_i$ reads only strictly earlier coordinates. Every unitriangular map is a bijection of the box.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C0_unitriBij {m : ℕ} {Θ : (Fin m → ZMod p) → (Fin m → ZMod p)} (h : IsUnitriangular Θ) : Function.Bijective Θ
nodes.note: The classifier's coordinate moves (its division-and-carry accounting) have exactly this shape, so they permute the box and preserve all counting; inversion proceeds coordinate by coordinate in the solving order.

nodes.title: Pulling back a system along a move preserves its pins
nodes.math: For a digit system $D$ and a unitriangular move $\Theta$, the pullback $\{x : \Theta x \text{ solves } D\}$ is again the solution set of a digit system $D'$, and $D'$ has exactly the same pinned coordinates as $D$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C0_pinTransport {m : ℕ} (D : Locus p m) {Θ : (Fin m → ZMod p) → (Fin m → ZMod p)} (h : IsUnitriangular Θ) : ∃ D' : Locus p m, (∀ x, D'.IsSolution x ↔ D.IsSolution (Θ x)) ∧ ∀ j : Fin m, D'.pinned j = D.pinned j
nodes.note: Why coordinate changes between frames never distort mass or codimension: the transported constraint system is constructed explicitly, with pins unchanged.

nodes.title: Value digits cut exactly the reciprocal of their alphabet
nodes.math: Let $S$ be a set of coordinates and $\varphi \colon \mathbb{F}_p^m \to \alpha$ an additive homomorphism onto a finite abelian group $\alpha$ that reads only the coordinates in $S$. Then all fibers are equal kernel cosets: for every value $v \in \alpha$, $\#\{y \text{ supported on } S : \varphi(y) = v\} \cdot |\alpha| = p^{|S|}$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C1_TYP_fiberCount {m : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin m)} {α : Type*} [AddCommGroup α] [Fintype α] (T : TypObject p m S α) (v : α) : Nat.card {y : Fin m → ZMod p // T.φ y = v ∧ ∀ c ∉ S, y c = 0} * Nat.card α = p ^ S.card
nodes.gate: TypObject T — hypothesizes an additive surjection reading only the level set S; machine-checked for every such T, but the instance tying it to a real fresh digit (the graded-piece map of the classifier) awaits the unbuilt graded-ring bridge.
nodes.note: The counting content of the fresh value clauses: a value digit cuts exactly the reciprocal of its alphabet — the reason level-set constraints contribute exact codimension.

nodes.title: Disjoint fresh clauses cut the box by exactly their total codimension
nodes.math: Let one read's fresh data be a finite list of clauses with pairwise disjoint supports, each cutting exactly $p^{-\mathrm{codim}}$ among its supported assignments. Then the joint cut on the whole box is exactly the product: $\#\{x \in \mathbb{F}_p^m : x \text{ satisfies every clause}\}\cdot p^{m^*} = p^m$, where $m^* = \sum \mathrm{codim}$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C1_clausesCount {m : ℕ} (fd : FreshData p m) : Nat.card {x : Fin m → ZMod p // fd.sat x} * p ^ fd.mstar = p ^ m
nodes.note: The multi-clause counting engine: disjoint supports make the conditional factors multiply exactly, division-free; consumed by the per-step conditional-exactness theorem.

nodes.title: Fresh clauses only constrain coordinates still free on the state cylinder
nodes.math: In any jet presentation of a read history, every coordinate in the support of a fresh clause of read $i$ is free (unpinned) on the state cylinder $\Sigma_i$ entering that read.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C2_freshFree {n N m : ℕ} {H : History p F} (J : JetSetup H n N m) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length) : ∀ cl ∈ (J.fresh i).clauses, ∀ c ∈ cl.support, (J.Sigma i).pinned c = false
nodes.gate: JetSetup J — the hypothesized jet presentation of the history (sorted chart, state cylinders, fresh data, unitriangular moves, presentation spine, exact-downset invariant, fresh-band laws); machine-checked for every such bundle, but constructing one for a real classifier history is the declared open boundary (the unbuilt graded-ring bridge).
nodes.note: The bridge from geometry to counting: fresh content sits strictly above the cumulative Newton floor, and the exact-downset invariant converts "above the floor" into "unpinned" — so no read double-charges a coordinate already pinned by earlier reads.

nodes.title: Along a realizable history, the newest line dominates all earlier ones on its interior
nodes.math: Let $H$ be a coherent, realizable read history. For $j \le i$ and every base index $b$ in read $i$'s factor interior ($b < \mu_i \cdot w_i$, where $w_i$ is the child block width), the earlier line lies below the current one: $\mathrm{line}_j(b) \le \mathrm{line}_i(b)$. Consequently, on each factor interior the cumulative floor of all recorded lines equals the current line.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C3_lineDom (H : History p F) (hcoh : HistoryCoherent H) (hreal : Realizable H) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length) (j : ℕ) (hij : j ≤ i) (b : ℕ) (hb : b < (H.nodes[i]'hi).μ * (H.nodes[i]'hi).childWidth) : (H.nodes[j]'(by omega)).line.at b ≤ (H.nodes[i]'hi).line.at b
nodes.note: The Newton-line domination behind the floor bookkeeping; restated at audit round 4 to hypothesize the full realizability class after the empty-stratum countermodel showed coherence alone is insufficient — the span-entry inequality is sourced from admissibility, not assumed.

nodes.title: The transported vertex value's polynomial factor is nonzero
nodes.math: Let $\psi$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree over a field $K$, and let $R$ have $\psi$-order exactly $\mu$ (that is, $\psi^{\mu} \mid R$ but $\psi^{\mu+1} \nmid R$). Then $(R/\psi^{\mu}) \bmod \psi \neq 0$.
nodes.lean: theorem C3_vtxPolyNe {K : Type*} [Field K] (ψ Ranch : Polynomial K) (μ : ℕ) (hmonic : ψ.Monic) (hdeg : 0 < ψ.natDegree) (hord : OrdPsiPoly ψ Ranch μ) : (Ranch /ₘ ψ ^ μ) %ₘ ψ ≠ 0
nodes.note: A deliberately partial result: the file explicitly does NOT claim the transported vertex value itself is nonzero — evaluating at the residue root would need the field isomorphism $K(\bar z) \cong K[z]/(\psi)$, which is outside this corpus's scope.

nodes.title: One read cuts the state cylinder by exactly its nominal volume
nodes.math: Let $\Sigma$ be a state cylinder (a digit system) and let fresh data with pairwise disjoint supports constrain only coordinates free on $\Sigma$. Then the fresh clauses cut $\Sigma$ exactly: $\#\{x : x \text{ solves } \Sigma \text{ and satisfies all clauses}\} \cdot p^{m^*} = \mathrm{mass}(\Sigma)$ — the conditional volume is exactly $p^{-m^*}$, an equality rather than a bound.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C4_conditionalMass {m : ℕ} (Sigma : Locus p m) (fd : FreshData p m) (hfree : ∀ cl ∈ fd.clauses, ∀ c ∈ cl.support, Sigma.pinned c = false) : Nat.card {x : Fin m → ZMod p // Sigma.IsSolution x ∧ fd.sat x} * p ^ fd.mstar = Sigma.mass
nodes.note: THE per-step conditional exactness of the counting argument, in fully address-free form: proved by solving the cylinder onto its free coordinates and applying the disjoint-clause product law inside them.

nodes.title: The mass recursion: each read divides the surviving mass by its fresh count
nodes.math:
In any jet presentation $J$ of a history $H$: $\mathrm{mass}(\Sigma_{i+1}) \cdot p^{m^*(
u_i)} = \mathrm{mass}(\Sigma_i)$, where $m^*(
u_i)$ is read $
u_i$'s total fresh codimension — consuming one read divides the mass by exactly $p^{m^*}$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C4_stepMass {n N m : ℕ} {H : History p F} (J : JetSetup H n N m) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length) : (J.Sigma (i+1)).mass * p ^ (J.fresh i).mstar = (J.Sigma i).mass
nodes.gate: JetSetup J — the hypothesized jet presentation of the history; machine-checked for every such bundle, but constructing one for a real classifier history is the declared open boundary (the unbuilt graded-ring bridge).
nodes.note: The recursion assembled on the interface: move bijectivity transports the count, the stratum recursion plus the inherited-content law reduce read i to its fresh clauses, and the per-step conditional exactness fires.

nodes.title: After k reads the surviving mass is the box divided by the accumulated codimension
nodes.math: In any jet presentation, after the first $k$ reads: $\mathrm{mass}(\Sigma_k) = p^{\,m - \sum_{i<k} m^*(\nu_i)}$ — the state cylinder's codimension is the running sum of the reads' fresh counts.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C5_massCodim {n N m : ℕ} {H : History p F} (J : JetSetup H n N m) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ H.nodes.length) : (J.Sigma k).mass = p ^ (m - (Finset.range k).sum (fun i => (J.fresh i).mstar))
nodes.gate: JetSetup J — the hypothesized jet presentation of the history; machine-checked for every such bundle, but constructing one for a real classifier history is the declared open boundary (the unbuilt graded-ring bridge).
nodes.note: The division-free running total behind Theorem C(b): the product of the reads' nominal volumes is realized exactly on the state cylinder.

nodes.title: An admissible terminal system cuts exactly its own volume
nodes.math: If a terminal digit system $Z$ pins only coordinates that are free on $\Sigma$, then $\#\{x : x \text{ solves both } \Sigma \text{ and } Z\}\cdot p^{\#\mathrm{pins}(Z)} = \mathrm{mass}(\Sigma)$.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
theorem C6_transportedAdmissible {m : ℕ} (Sigma Z : Locus p m) (hZ : AdmissibleZ Sigma Z) : Nat.card {x : Fin m → ZMod p // Sigma.IsSolution x ∧ Z.IsSolution x} * p ^ Z.numPinned = Sigma.mass
nodes.note: The final factor of Theorem C(b): the splitting condition imposed at the end of the history contributes exactly its own nominal volume on the final cylinder.

nodes.title: Theorem C(a): the classifier locus is the bijective transport of the final joint locus
nodes.math: Fix a jet presentation $J$ of a read history $H$ with $k$ reads and an admissible terminal system $Z$ (pinning only coordinates free on the final cylinder $\Sigma_k$). The classifier locus $S(H,Z)$ is defined with no reference to the cylinders: a frame-0 digit vector $x$ lies in $S(H,Z)$ iff it carries a chain $y_0 = x$, $y_i = \Theta_i(y_{i+1})$ through the recorded moves such that each $y_i$ satisfies read $\nu_i$'s fresh clauses and $y_k$ solves $Z$. Then (i) the composite move $\Psi_H = \Theta_0 \circ \cdots \circ \Theta_{k-1}$ is a bijection of the box; (ii) $S(H,Z)$ equals the $\Psi_H$-image of $\{x : x \text{ solves } \Sigma_k \text{ and } Z\}$; (iii) the two sets have equal cardinality.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C6_thmC_a {n N m : ℕ} {H : History p F} (J : JetSetup H n N m) (Z : Locus p m) (hZ : AdmissibleZ (J.Sigma H.nodes.length) Z) : Function.Bijective (J.Psi H.nodes.length) ∧ J.SHZ Z = (J.Psi H.nodes.length) '' {x : Fin m → ZMod p | (J.Sigma H.nodes.length).IsSolution x ∧ Z.IsSolution x} ∧ Nat.card (J.SHZ Z) = Nat.card {x : Fin m → ZMod p // (J.Sigma H.nodes.length).IsSolution x ∧ Z.IsSolution x}
nodes.gate: JetSetup J — the hypothesized jet presentation of the history; machine-checked for every such bundle, but constructing one for a real classifier history is the declared open boundary (the unbuilt graded-ring bridge). AdmissibleZ — the terminal system pins only coordinates free on the final cylinder (a genuine mathematical hypothesis of Theorem C, not a deferral).
nodes.note: Capstone (a): the audit forced the classifier locus to be defined independently (an existential chain over the recorded moves, no images, no cylinders), so the proved equality with the transported final locus is contentful rather than definitional.

nodes.title: Theorem C(b): the exact box identity — count times p to the total pins equals the whole box
nodes.math: Under the same hypotheses, $\#S(H,Z) \cdot p^{\,\sum_{i<k} m^*(\nu_i) \,+\, \#\mathrm{pins}(Z)} = p^{nN}$: one history stratum occupies exactly the fraction $p^{-\sum m^* - \#\mathrm{pins}(Z)}$ of the coefficient box, stated division-free. The exponents $m^*(\nu_i)$ are tied by the interface to each read's geometric fresh-band count computed from node data, so the formula is the intended species inventory and not a presentation artifact.
nodes.lean:
-- section variables: {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
theorem C6_thmC_b {n N m : ℕ} {H : History p F} (J : JetSetup H n N m) (Z : Locus p m) (hZ : AdmissibleZ (J.Sigma H.nodes.length) Z) : Nat.card (J.SHZ Z) * p ^ totalPins J Z = boxMass p m
nodes.gate: JetSetup J — the hypothesized jet presentation of the history; machine-checked for every such bundle, but constructing one for a real classifier history is the declared open boundary (the unbuilt graded-ring bridge). AdmissibleZ — the terminal system pins only coordinates free on the final cylinder (a genuine mathematical hypothesis of Theorem C, not a deferral).
nodes.note: Capstone (b), the exact mass formula consumed by the density pipeline: assembled purely from (a), the terminal cut, and the mass recursion; all 36 units of the corpus are proved with no axioms beyond Lean's core.

role: The solve layer of the pipeline: it converts the infinite-depth factorization recursion into finite linear algebra over the field Q(q) of rational functions in a variable q standing for the residue-field size. A transfer matrix per block size collects the one-step masses; inverting 1 - K resums all depths into a block solve, and a finite convolution over shallow shapes assembles the one fixed rational function R_sigma for each factorization type. Rigidity of rational functions - two that agree at infinitely many primes are equal - yields uniqueness of the interpolant and the checksum that all the R_sigma sum to 1. All 95 units (one stated Lean declaration per unit) are proved — machine-checked, with no axioms beyond Lean's core; the corpus imports nothing outside Mathlib, and its hypothesis structures (the measured counting ledger, the wild-pool read-off gate, the shallow-weight production law) are the explicit seam where the counting corpora (MovesT, MovesV) plug in and where the remaining conditionality lives.
oneLiner: Resums the branching recursion into one rational function per factorization type

nodes.title: Rational functions in q, with partial evaluation at a prime power
nodes.math: The symbolic carrier is the field $\mathbb{Q}(q)$ of rational functions in one variable $q$ (standing for the residue-field size). For each rational number $q_0$, the functions whose reduced denominator does not vanish at $q_0$ form a subring, and evaluation $f \mapsto f(q_0)$ is a ring homomorphism on that subring. Every passage from a symbolic identity to its value at an actual prime power goes through this partial evaluation; membership is after cancellation, so a removable singularity is harmless but a genuine pole blocks evaluation.
nodes.lean:
abbrev Qq := RatFunc ℚ

def OKat (q₀ : ℚ) : Subring Qq where
  carrier := {f : Qq | f.denom.eval q₀ ≠ 0}
  -- (zero/one/add/mul/neg closure proofs omitted)

theorem mem_OKat_iff {q₀ : ℚ} {f : Qq} : f ∈ OKat q₀ ↔ f.denom.eval q₀ ≠ 0

noncomputable def evalAt (q₀ : ℚ) : OKat q₀ →+* ℚ
nodes.note: Every 'evaluate the symbolic density at a prime' step in the project passes through this partial evaluation; a pole surviving cancellation blocks read-off — detecting exactly this is the job of the wild-pool gate.

nodes.title: The transfer table: states, verdicts, and one-step outcomes
nodes.math: A transfer table for degree $n$ packages the finite combinatorics of one step of the factorization process: for each block size $e$, a finite set of states; a finite alphabet of verdicts, structurally identified with the pairs $(e,f)$ of positive integers with $ef \le n$ (ramification index and residue degree of a finished factor), the verdict's degree being $ef$; and for each state a finite roster of outcomes, each a nonempty list of members carrying a size, a base-change factor $\delta \ge 1$, and a status that is either a verdict (finished) or a state (continuing). With $m$ the number of members and $c$ the number of continuing ones, every outcome is dispatched to exactly one route: terminal ($c=0$), column move ($c \ge 1$, $m=1$), or split ($c \ge 1$, $m \ge 2$).
nodes.lean:
structure TableShape (n : ℕ) where
  State  : ℕ → Type
  fin    : ∀ e, Fintype (State e)
  deq    : ∀ e, DecidableEq (State e)
  VType  : Type
  deqV   : DecidableEq VType
  finV   : Fintype VType
  vdeg   : VType → ℕ+
  vEquiv : VType ≃ {ef : ℕ+ × ℕ+ // ((ef.1 : ℕ) * (ef.2 : ℕ)) ≤ n}
  vdeg_spec : ∀ v, (vdeg v : ℕ) = ((vEquiv v).1.1 : ℕ) * ((vEquiv v).1.2 : ℕ)
  Out    : ∀ e, State e → Type
  finO   : ∀ e (τ : State e), Fintype (Out e τ)
  odata  : ∀ e (τ : State e), Out e τ → Outcome VType State
  Wloc   : ∀ e (τ : State e), Out e τ → ℕ
  Wstate : ∀ e, State e → ℕ
nodes.note: The shared vocabulary every theorem in the corpus is typed over; the verdict-to-(e,f) identification is what keys the densities to factorization types.

nodes.title: The transfer matrix of continuing moves
nodes.math: For each block size $e$ the transfer matrix $K_e$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q)$ is indexed by the states of block $e$: entry $(\tau,\beta)$ sums the rational one-step masses of the outcomes at $\tau$ that are column moves (a single continuing member, necessarily of size $e$) with target state $\beta$. Powers of $K_e$ generate the multi-step masses of the depth process; the hypothesis feeding the construction — every column-move member has size exactly $e$ — is itself a proved unit.
nodes.lean:
abbrev KmatHyp (T : TableShape n) (e : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (τ : T.State e) (o : T.Out e τ), routeOf (T.odata e τ o) = .kcol →
    ∀ μ ∈ (T.odata e τ o).mem, μ.size = e

noncomputable def Kmat (T : TableShape n) {M : MeasuredSide T} (RB : RatBurdens T M)
    (e : ℕ) (hK : KmatHyp T e) : Matrix (T.State e) (T.State e) Qq :=
  fun τ β => ∑ o : T.Out e τ,
    if hk : routeOf (T.odata e τ o) = .kcol then
      (if kTarget T e τ o hk (hK τ o hk) = β then RB.TG e τ o else 0)
    else 0
nodes.note: The object whose inversion performs the depth resummation; the entries' rationality is supplied by the rationality-burden interface, never assumed of the measured process directly.

nodes.title: The block solve: resumming infinite depth by one matrix inversion
nodes.math: The block solve is defined by strong recursion on the block size $e$: $\beta_e(\tau,\sigma') = \big((1-K_e)^{-1}(b_e^{\mathrm{term}} + b_e^{\mathrm{split}})\big)_\tau$, where $b^{\mathrm{term}}$ collects the terminal outcomes emitting the verdict multiset $\sigma'$, and $b^{\mathrm{split}}$ collects the split outcomes, each contributing its splitting mass $J$ times a convolution, over decompositions $\sigma' = \sum_j \sigma_j$, of the already-computed solves at the strictly smaller member sizes, with each leg's variable rescaled $q \mapsto q^{\delta}$ by its base-change factor. One matrix inversion thus resums the entire infinite-depth branching recursion of a block into a single element of $\mathbb{Q}(q)$.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def blockSolve (T : TableShape n) {M : MeasuredSide T}
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (hdc : DegCons T)
    (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e) (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK) :
    ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → T.State e → Multiset T.VType → Qq

theorem blockSolve_eq (T : TableShape n) {M : MeasuredSide T}
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (hdc : DegCons T)
    (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e) (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK)
    (e : ℕ) (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n) (τ : T.State e) (σ' : Multiset T.VType) :
    blockSolve T RB hdc hK hdet e he τ σ' =
      ((1 - Kmat T RB e (hK e he))⁻¹ *ᵥ
        (bTerm T RB e σ' +
          bSplit T RB hdc e he
            (fun e' _ τ' σ'' =>
              if he' : e' ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n then
                blockSolve T RB hdc hK hdet e' he' τ' σ''
              else 0) σ')) τ
nodes.note: The central construction of the corpus: one matrix inversion replaces an infinite recursion; the capstone corpus (MovesU) identifies its density function R with sums of exactly these solves.

nodes.title: The candidate density: one fixed rational function per factorization type
nodes.math: For a factorization type $\sigma$ (a multiset of verdicts $(e,f)$ of total degree $n$), the candidate density is the single rational function $R_\sigma(q) = \sum_{\hat S} W_{\hat S}(q) \cdot \sum_{\sigma = \sigma_0(\hat S) + \sum_i \sigma_i} \prod_i \beta_{e_i,\tau_i}(\sigma_i)(q^{\delta_i})$: a finite sum over shallow shapes $\hat S$, each weighted by its rational shallow weight and by the convolution of block solves at the shape's blocks, base-changed by the shape's $\delta$'s. This is the one fixed rational function of the uniformity theorem — derived from the transfer-matrix solve, not postulated.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def shConv (T : TableShape n) (M : MeasuredSide T)
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (hdc : DegCons T)
    (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e) (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK)
    (Ŝ : Shape T) (σ : Multiset T.VType) : Qq :=
  ∑ g : {g : Fin Ŝ.k → Multiset T.VType // σ = Ŝ.σ0 + ∑ i, g i},
    ∏ i, powSubst (Ŝ.δOf i)
      (blockSolve T RB hdc hK hdet (Ŝ.eOf i) (Ŝ.eIcc i) (Ŝ.τOf i) (g.1 i))

noncomputable def Rsh (T : TableShape n) (M : MeasuredSide T)
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (hdc : DegCons T)
    (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e) (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK)
    (F : ShapeFam T) (WshP : Shape T → PolyGeom) (σ : Multiset T.VType) : Qq :=
  ∑ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, (WshP Ŝ).val * shConv T M RB hdc hK hdet Ŝ σ
nodes.note: THE object of the uniformity theorem: the capstone theorem in MovesU pins its density function R to exactly this definition (the solve identification S.R = Rsh).

nodes.title: The escape condition on an evaluated kernel
nodes.math: A square matrix $A$ with rational entries satisfies the escape condition if all entries are nonnegative and $A^k \mathbf{1} \to 0$ as $k \to \infty$: the total mass remaining after $k$ steps of the process tends to zero, i.e. every trajectory eventually terminates. This is the per-prime analytic regularity input, playing the role of a spectral-radius-below-one bound without ever invoking spectra.
nodes.lean:
structure EscapeE0 {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : Matrix ι ι ℚ) :
    Prop where
  nonneg : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ A i j
  escape : Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (A ^ k) *ᵥ (fun _ => (1 : ℚ)))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
nodes.note: Part of the typed per-prime regularity gate: it is the hypothesis from which invertibility of the solve system is derived, and its general discharge at all pools is on the project's open mathematical surface.

nodes.title: The full inherited hypothesis ledger of the checksum
nodes.math: The complete set of conditions the checksum inherits, packaged as one structure: the nine measured counting laws of the cell/height ledger; the raw measured subtree values with their fixed-point law and height-independence; null-set exactness; the base-prime pools with escape packages at every all-active base prime and at every consumed base-change leg pool $p^{\delta}$; the wild-pool read-off gate at every consumed non-all-active pool; the set of factorization types of total degree $n$; the shallow-shape weight presentations with denominator regularity, interpolation, boundedness, and height/counting carriers; and the measured densities with their total-mass identity and the interpolation law tying $R_\sigma$'s evaluations to them. Nothing rides implicitly: everything inherited is an explicit field.
nodes.lean:
structure RS4Chain (T : TableShape n) (M : MeasuredSide T) (RB : RatBurdens T M)
    (hdc : DegCons T) (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e)
    (F : ShapeFam T) where
  L : LedgerIV T M
  B : RS1Bundle T M RB hdc hK
  hns : B.nsNull
  PrimePools : Set ℚ
  prime_sub : PrimePools ⊆ M.Pools
  prime_base : ∀ q₀, q₀ ∈ PrimePools ↔ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q₀ = (p : ℚ)
  pools_e0 : ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n), ∀ q₀ ∈ PrimePools ∩ allActivePools M,
    Nonempty (PoolHyp T M RB e (hK e he) q₀)
  legs_reg : ∀ p : ℕ, (p : ℚ) ∈ PrimePools → RegP T M RB p hK F
  legs_read : ∀ p : ℕ, (p : ℚ) ∈ PrimePools → ∀ δ ∈ consumedDeltas T F,
    ((p : ℚ) ^ (δ : ℕ)) ∉ allActivePools M → ∀ hdet : DetHyp T RB hK,
      LegAgree T M RB hdc hK hdet B.βmeas ((p : ℚ) ^ (δ : ℕ))
  Sigmas : Finset (Multiset T.VType)
  sig_exact : ∀ σ, σ ∈ Sigmas ↔ (σ.map fun v => ((T.vdeg v : ℕ))).sum = n
  WshP : Shape T → PolyGeom
  wsh_ok : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ M.Pools, (WshP Ŝ).val ∈ OKat q₀
  WshVal : Shape T → ℚ → ℝ
  wsh_interp : ∀ Ŝ (hŜ : Ŝ ∈ F.Sh), ∀ q₀ (h : q₀ ∈ M.Pools),
    ((evalAt q₀ ⟨(WshP Ŝ).val, wsh_ok Ŝ hŜ q₀ h⟩ : ℚ) : ℝ) = WshVal Ŝ q₀
  wshval_bdd : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ M.Pools, WshVal Ŝ q₀ ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1
  shDom  : Shape T → Set M.Hgt
  shEvtH : Shape T → M.Hgt → ∀ (q₀ : ℚ) (N : ℕ), Finset (M.Box q₀ N)
  visH   : Shape T → ∀ (q₀ : ℚ) (N : ℕ), Finset M.Hgt
  shEvt  : Shape T → ∀ (q₀ : ℚ) (N : ℕ), Finset (M.Box q₀ N)
  shWeightH : Shape T → M.Hgt → ℚ → ℝ
  shevt_grouping : ∀ Ŝ (q₀ : ℚ) (N : ℕ),
    shEvt Ŝ q₀ N = (visH Ŝ q₀ N).biUnion (fun h => shEvtH Ŝ h q₀ N)
  shDom_ne : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, (shDom Ŝ).Nonempty
  sh_realized : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ allActivePools M,
    ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, (shEvt Ŝ q₀ N).Nonempty
  shweight_card : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ h : M.Hgt, h ∈ shDom Ŝ → ∀ q₀ ∈ M.Pools,
    ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, shWeightH Ŝ h q₀ * (Fintype.card (M.Box q₀ N) : ℝ)
      = ((shEvtH Ŝ h q₀ N).card : ℝ)
  wshval_card : ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ M.Pools, ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀,
    WshVal Ŝ q₀ * (Fintype.card (M.Box q₀ N) : ℝ) = ((shEvt Ŝ q₀ N).card : ℝ)
  Rval : Multiset T.VType → ℚ → ℝ
  r_bdd : ∀ σ (q₀ : ℚ), q₀ ∈ M.Pools → Rval σ q₀ ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1
  decidedTotal : ℚ → ℝ
  x3_total : ∀ p ∈ PrimePools, decidedTotal p = 1
  rs1_equates : ∀ p ∈ PrimePools, (∑ σ ∈ Sigmas, Rval σ p) = decidedTotal p
  rsh_interp : ∀ σ ∈ Sigmas, ∀ p ∈ PrimePools, ∀ hdet : DetHyp T RB hK,
    ∃ hok : Rsh T M RB hdc hK hdet F WshP σ ∈ OKat p,
      ((evalAt p ⟨Rsh T M RB hdc hK hdet F WshP σ, hok⟩ : ℚ) : ℝ) = Rval σ p
nodes.note: The single structure the checksum inherits from; its field list is the exact boundary of what the counting corpora (MovesT, MovesV) must still supply at general n (instantiated in full at the n=2 gate).

nodes.title: The wild-prime read-off gate
nodes.math: The read-off gate at one pool $q_0$ (a 'pool' is one evaluation site: a prime power $q_0$ together with its measured counting data): for every block size there exists a per-pool package under which the symbolic block solve, evaluated at $q_0$ after cancellation, agrees with the solve $\big((1-A)^{-1} b\big)$ of the active subsystem against the measured exit vector, at every active state, verdict multiset, and entrance height. At a wildly ramified (non-all-active) pool this check must pass before the symbolic value may be read off; a pole surviving cancellation there is a failure of the gate. Determinants of the inactive (junk) blocks are recorded but never required nonzero.
nodes.lean:
def LegAgree (T : TableShape n) (M : MeasuredSide T) (RB : RatBurdens T M)
    (hdc : DegCons T) (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e)
    (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK)
    (βm : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → ℕ → T.State e → Multiset T.VType → ℚ → ℝ)
    (q₀ : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n), ∃ P : PoolHyp T M RB e (hK e he) q₀,
    ∀ (τA : P.Act) (σ' : Multiset T.VType) (h_ent : ℕ),
      AVAgree P (blockSolve T RB hdc hK hdet e he (↑τA) σ')
        (bhatMeas P (fun e' he' => βm e' he' h_ent) σ') τA
nodes.note: The guard at wildly ramified primes: it forbids silently reading off a symbolic value where a pole survives; vacuously discharged at the n=2 gate (every pool there is fully active), live at general n.

nodes.title: The shallow-weight production law (the named open burden)
nodes.math: The production law for the shallow weights — the checksum's one explicitly open inheritance: for every shallow shape in the family and every pool, (i) the shape's weight presentation evaluates to its weight value, and (ii) that value equals the sum of the shape's height weights over its height domain. The capstone consumes this as an explicit hypothesis and, by the repo's standing discipline, may not be recorded unconditional while the law is open.
nodes.lean:
def W17ii (T : TableShape n) (M : MeasuredSide T) (F : ShapeFam T)
    (WshP : Shape T → PolyGeom) (WshVal : Shape T → ℚ → ℝ)
    (shDom : Shape T → Set M.Hgt) (shWeightH : Shape T → M.Hgt → ℚ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ Ŝ ∈ F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ M.Pools,
    (∃ hok : (WshP Ŝ).val ∈ OKat q₀,
      ((evalAt q₀ ⟨(WshP Ŝ).val, hok⟩ : ℚ) : ℝ) = WshVal Ŝ q₀) ∧
    HasSum (fun h : shDom Ŝ => shWeightH Ŝ (↑h) q₀) (WshVal Ŝ q₀)

def RS4Chain.wsh17_pin {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T} {RB : RatBurdens T M}
    {hdc : DegCons T} {hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e} {F : ShapeFam T}
    (C : RS4Chain T M RB hdc hK F) : Prop :=
  W17ii T M F C.WshP C.WshVal C.shDom C.shWeightH
nodes.note: The named open burden inside the checksum's hypothesis surface: its general-carrier discharge is this corpus family's single fenced unproved goal (a recorded `sorry` in MovesV/V7_w17ii, clause (ii)); the n=2 device instance is fully discharged. Keeping it explicit is what licenses calling the rest of the corpus proved.

nodes.title: Rigidity: vanishing at infinitely many points forces zero
nodes.math: If $f \in \mathbb{Q}(q)$ has denominator nonvanishing on an infinite set $S \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ and $f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in S$, then $f = 0$ identically. This is the engine converting agreement at infinitely many primes into identity of rational functions — the mechanism behind one fixed rational function serving all regular primes.
nodes.lean:
theorem ratfunc_eval_infinite (f : Qq) (S : Set ℚ) (hS : S.Infinite)
    (hden : ∀ x ∈ S, f.denom.eval x ≠ 0)
    (hval : ∀ x ∈ S, RatFunc.eval (RingHom.id ℚ) x f = 0) :
    f = 0
nodes.note: The corpus-wide workhorse: uniqueness of R_sigma, the symbolic row sums, the symbolic determinant, and the checksum all reduce to this rigidity over an infinite prime locus.

nodes.title: The one-step masses sum to one, symbolically
nodes.math: For every block size $e \in [1,n]$ and state $\tau$, the route-dispatched one-step masses over all outcomes sum to $1$ identically in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$ (split outcomes contribute their splitting mass $J$, all others their terminal/column mass $TG$). Proved by evaluating at every all-active pool — where the measured row masses sum to $1$ by the counting ledger — and applying rigidity on the infinite all-active locus.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def routedMass {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T}
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (e : ℕ) (τ : T.State e) (o : T.Out e τ) : Qq :=
  if routeOf (T.odata e τ o) = .split then RB.J e τ o else RB.TG e τ o

theorem ksub {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T} (RB : RatBurdens T M)
    (L : LedgerIV T M) (hdc : DegCons T) {e : ℕ} (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n)
    (τ : T.State e) (hK : KmatHyp T e) :
    ∑ o : T.Out e τ, routedMass RB e τ o = 1
nodes.note: The conservation law (the note's K-SUB) that makes the solve a probability resummation rather than formal algebra; consumes the measured counting ledger and the rationality burdens as typed hypotheses.

nodes.title: Escape makes the linear system invertible
nodes.math: If $A$ satisfies the escape condition (nonnegative entries, $A^k\mathbf{1} \to 0$) then $\det(1-A) \neq 0$. For an empty active block the determinant is $1$ (vacuously nonsingular, matching the realized-states-only scope). Otherwise a vanishing determinant would give a nonzero fixed vector $v$ of $A$, and nonnegativity bounds $|v_i| \le (\max_j |v_j|)\,(A^k\mathbf{1})_i \to 0$, forcing $v = 0$.
nodes.lean:
theorem e0_det_ne_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {A : Matrix ι ι ℚ} (h : EscapeE0 A) : (1 - A).det ≠ 0
nodes.note: Turns the per-prime termination condition into well-posedness of the resummation's linear system at each evaluated prime.

nodes.title: The symbolic determinant never vanishes
nodes.math: Given escape packages at all all-active base-prime pools, the symbolic determinant $\det(1-K_e)$ is nonzero in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$ for every block size $e \in [1,n]$: all but finitely many base primes are all-active, so an all-active base prime exists; if the determinant vanished identically its evaluation there would vanish, contradicting escape-invertibility. This discharges — from the ledger's own fields — the determinant hypothesis every solve consumer carries.
nodes.lean:
theorem rs3_det_symbolic {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T}
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (hdc : DegCons T)
    (hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e)
    (PP : Set ℚ) (hsub : PP ⊆ M.Pools)
    (hbase : ∀ q₀, q₀ ∈ PP ↔ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q₀ = (p : ℚ))
    (hact : ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n), ∀ q₀ ∈ PP ∩ allActivePools M,
      Nonempty (PoolHyp T M RB e (hK e he) q₀)) :
    ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n), (1 - Kmat T RB e (hK e he)).det ≠ 0
nodes.note: Lifts per-prime invertibility to invertibility in Q(q): the reason the block solve is well-defined symbolically and not merely prime by prime.

nodes.title: All but finitely many primes are fully active
nodes.math: Among the base-prime pools, only finitely many fail to be all-active (i.e. have some inactive state). A state is inactive at $q_0$ exactly when some per-cell count polynomial vanishes at $q_0$; each such polynomial is nonzero, so it contributes only finitely many roots. This cofiniteness supplies the infinite identification locus on which rational-function identities are forced.
nodes.lean:
theorem allActive_cofinite_primes {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T}
    (RB : RatBurdens T M) (PP : Set ℚ) (hsub : PP ⊆ M.Pools)
    (hbase : ∀ q₀, q₀ ∈ PP ↔ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q₀ = (p : ℚ)) :
    {q₀ ∈ PP | q₀ ∉ allActivePools M}.Finite
nodes.note: Why one rational function can serve almost all primes: the finitely many exceptional (wild) primes cannot break an identity of rational functions, and at them the read-off gate takes over.

nodes.title: The rational function is unique: any interpolant equals the solve
nodes.math: On an infinite set $S$ of all-active pools, any family of rational functions that is denominator-regular on $S$ and interpolates the measured subtree values there is equal — coordinate by coordinate, at every block size, state, and verdict multiset — to the block solve: every $\beta_{e,\tau}(\sigma')$ is one fixed rational function. The identification reads the symbolic solve off against the measured values at each point of $S$ (through the read-off bundle) and then applies per-coordinate uniqueness of interpolants.
nodes.lean:
theorem rs2_unique_interp {T : TableShape n} {M : MeasuredSide T}
    {RB : RatBurdens T M} {hdc : DegCons T}
    {hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → KmatHyp T e}
    (S : Set ℚ) (hS : S ⊆ allActivePools M) (hinf : S.Infinite)
    (B : RS1Bundle T M RB hdc hK) (L : LedgerIV T M) (hdet : DetHyp T RB hK)
    (hread : ReadOffBundle S hS B hdet)
    (f : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → T.State e → Multiset T.VType → Qq)
    (hfok : ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n) (τ : T.State e)
      (σ' : Multiset T.VType) (q₀ : ℚ), q₀ ∈ S → f e he τ σ' ∈ OKat q₀)
    (hfin : ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n) (τ : T.State e)
      (σ' : Multiset T.VType) (q₀ : ℚ) (hq : q₀ ∈ S) (h_ent : ℕ),
      ((evalAt q₀ ⟨f e he τ σ', hfok e he τ σ' q₀ hq⟩ : ℚ) : ℝ)
        = B.βmeas e he h_ent τ σ' q₀) :
    ∀ e (he : e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n) (τ : T.State e) (σ' : Multiset T.VType),
      f e he τ σ' = blockSolve T RB hdc hK hdet e he τ σ'
nodes.gate: hread : ReadOffBundle S hS B hdet — the per-pool active-value agreement (read-off) burden across S, a recorded open obligation (instantiated at the n=2 gate, open at general n); L : LedgerIV T M — the nine measured counting laws (a scoped binder confirmed necessary by independent review 2026-07-30); hdet : DetHyp T RB hK — nonvanishing of every det(1-K_e), dischargeable via the symbolic-determinant theorem.
nodes.note: The uniqueness half of uniformity: whatever rational function the measured densities trace out, it can only be the block solve. The Lean proof itself is complete (no axioms beyond Lean's core); the statement is conditional on the named hypothesis surface.

nodes.title: The checksum: the candidate densities sum to one
nodes.math: $\sum_{\sigma} R_\sigma = 1$ identically in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$, summing over all factorization types of total degree $n$: the candidate densities form an exact probability distribution as rational functions, not merely at each prime. Proof: at every base-prime pool the ledger's interpolation fields evaluate the sum to the measured decided total, which is $1$; the primes are infinite; rigidity closes the identity.
nodes.gate: h17 : C.wsh17_pin — the shallow-weight production law (the source note's W17ii), OPEN: its general-carrier discharge is the single fenced unproved goal (`sorry`) in MovesV/V7_w17ii; the n=2 device instance is discharged; C : RS4Chain — the full inherited measured/rationality ledger (fully instantiated at n=2; its general-n instantiation is still owed by the counting corpora MovesT/MovesV); hdet : DetHyp T RB hK — determinant nonvanishing, derivable from the chain's own escape packages via the symbolic-determinant theorem.
nodes.note: The corpus capstone (the source note's RS.4): the resummation is exact.
