The Lean proof is complete (no axioms beyond Lean's core); by the project's standing discipline it may not be recorded unconditional while the production law is open — the conditionality is carried as the explicit typed premise h17.

nodes.title: The complete worked instance at degree two
nodes.math: A complete instantiation of the full hypothesis ledger at degree $n = 2$: pools are all prime powers, block $2$ has a unique state, the verdicts are $(1,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, the factorization types are the three degree-2 multisets, the measured row values at every pool are $q^{-3}$, $1 - q^{-1}$, $q^{-1} - q^{-3}$, and every field — the nine counting laws, escape packages, cofinite activity, interpolation, and total mass — is discharged by proof.
nodes.note: The non-vacuity certificate for the interface: every field of the ledger can be discharged simultaneously on a real model. Per the corpus scope fence this is the internal-consistency gate (schema consistency), NOT the intended general counting-model inhabitation — that duty belongs to the counting corpora (MovesT/MovesV); its shallow-weight fields are the disclosed trivial device (see the device node).

nodes.title: Degree-two solve values: explicit rational functions
nodes.math: At the degree-2 instance the block-2 solves reduce to explicit rational functions: $\beta_{\{(1,2)\}} = \dfrac{q+1}{q^2+q+1}$ and $\beta_{\{(1,1),(1,1)\}} = \dfrac{q^2}{q^2+q+1}$ — with exactly the denominator $q^2+q+1$ displayed in the source note (the symbolic determinant $\det(1-K_2) = (q^3-1)/q^3$ is a separately proved companion check).
nodes.lean:
theorem n2_solve_vals (he : 2 ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2) :
    blockSolve n2T n2RB n2hdc n2hK n2hdet 2 he n2τ {n2v12}
      = algebraMap (Polynomial ℚ) Qq (X + 1)
        / algebraMap (Polynomial ℚ) Qq (X ^ 2 + X + 1) ∧
    blockSolve n2T n2RB n2hdc n2hK n2hdet 2 he n2τ {n2v11, n2v11}
      = algebraMap (Polynomial ℚ) Qq (X ^ 2)
        / algebraMap (Polynomial ℚ) Qq (X ^ 2 + X + 1)
nodes.note: A concrete, human-checkable output of the machinery: the abstract matrix-inversion solve reduces to the exact rational functions the source note predicts, denominator and all.

nodes.title: Degree-two checksum: the two masses sum to one
nodes.math: $\beta_{\{(1,2)\}} + \beta_{\{(1,1),(1,1)\}} = 1$ in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$: the two block-2 subtree masses of the degree-2 instance sum exactly to one — the degree-2 shadow of the checksum, computed from the explicit solve values.
nodes.note: The end-to-end degree-2 check: dispatch, solve, and interpolation compose to an exact total of 1 on the worked instance.

nodes.title: Degree-two shallow weights: a declared device, not content
nodes.math: At the degree-2 gate the shallow-weight presentation of every shape is the trivial one — both count polynomials equal $1$, geometric part $1$, no $q$-power — and the weight value is identically $1$ at every pool. It witnesses that the shallow-weight schema composes; it carries no shallow-weight content.
nodes.lean:
theorem n2_wshp_device :
    (∀ Ŝ : Shape n2T, (n2Chain.WshP Ŝ).countT = 1 ∧ (n2Chain.WshP Ŝ).countS = 1 ∧
      (n2Chain.WshP Ŝ).geom = 1 ∧ (n2Chain.WshP Ŝ).qpow = 0) ∧
    (∀ Ŝ ∈ n2F.Sh, ∀ q₀ ∈ n2M.Pools, n2Chain.WshVal Ŝ q₀ = 1)
nodes.note: The file marks itself DEVICE-ONLY, and the planned general-n re-keying (owed by the counting corpora) is specified to replace exactly these fields — device content is disclosed rather than silently counted as verification of the shallow layer.

role: This corpus builds the species alphabet: the finite, prime-independent set of bookkeeping states ("species") that a single read of the canonical p-adic factorization tree retains once all digit values, heights and lifts are forgotten. It proves the alphabet finite with an explicit bound, shows the successor graph becomes a DAG once self-loops are struck (every collapsed walk has at most 6n² letters), and proves exact catalogues at degree 1 (one letter) and degree 3 (53 letters with their complete edge menus) by exhaustive kernel computation (native_decide banned). Its completeness theorems connect the alphabet to the actual tree computation through an explicitly conditional engine interface: the per-read laws are consumed as named hypotheses whose discharge belongs to the tree-computation corpus (MovesD), with a real-carrier instantiation and a non-vacuity witness at n = 2 answering a finding of an independent adversarial review.
oneLiner: The finite, prime-independent alphabet of tree-reading states, exactly enumerated

nodes.title: The species: what one tree read retains
nodes.math: A species is the bookkeeping tuple retained from one read of the canonical factorization tree: a position tag (root / post-increment / post-recentering), the current key degree $D$, pool residue degree $w$, window width $W$, stride $e$, raw left endpoint $s_0'$, normalized side length $\ell$, the census anchor $a = \lfloor s_0'/e \rfloor$, digit count $d$, the slot set $\{a, \dots, a+\ell\}$, the residual partition $\lambda = \{(g^{(i)}, \mu^{(i)})\}$ (a multiset of degree–multiplicity pairs), an optional selected pair $(g,\mu) \in \lambda$, and the two flank compositions. Heights, depths, digit values and lifts are deliberately forgotten — the datum is value-free, which is what makes the alphabet finite and independent of the prime.
nodes.lean:
structure Species where
  tag : Tag
  D : ℕ            -- current key degree
  w : ℕ            -- pool residue degree
  W : ℕ            -- window width
  e : ℕ            -- stride e = e_read
  s0 : ℕ           -- raw left endpoint s₀′
  ell : ℕ          -- normalized side length ℓ = w′/e = deg R_anch
  a : ℕ            -- CENSUS anchor ⌊s₀′/e⌋
  d : ℕ            -- digit count = #slots
  slots : Finset ℕ -- census slot set {p̂_k}
  lam : Multiset (ℕ × ℕ)   -- residual partition λ = {(g⁽ⁱ⁾, μ⁽ⁱ⁾)}
  sel : Option (ℕ × ℕ)     -- selection (g, μ) ∈ λ, or ⊥ = none
  lflank : List ℕ  -- left flank composition (composition of span s₀′)
  rflank : List ℕ  -- right flank composition (span W − s₀′ − w′)
deriving DecidableEq
nodes.note: The letter of the alphabet: every finiteness, DAG, and catalogue statement in this corpus quantifies over these tuples, and no field mentions a prime.

nodes.title: The catalogue: root letters closed under the generation rule
nodes.math: The degree-$n$ catalogue $\mathcal{S}_n^{\mathrm{raw}}$ is the least set of species containing every coherent, budget-admissible root-stage letter (root tag, $(D,w,W)=(1,1,n)$) and closed under the successor rule: $s'$ may follow $s$ when the raw stage laws hold — for the selected pair $(g,\mu)$ of $s$, $D' = e g D$, $w' = g w$, $W' = \mu$, with the new tag determined by whether $eg \ge 2$ — and $s'$ is itself coherent and budget-admissible. Coherence is the geometric bookkeeping (flank–span accounting, anchor–position, slot-set, residual-sum, and the terminal rule: no selection iff $W = 1$); budgets cap every field by $n$. No prime appears anywhere in the definition.
nodes.note: The central object of the corpus; the prime-independence of the alphabet is discharged by typing — the same catalogue serves every prime.

nodes.title: The engine interface: an abstract canonical tree with per-read laws
nodes.math: An abstract model of the canonical factorization tree of a monic degree-$n$ polynomial $f$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$: a nonempty type of branches, each carrying a catalogue-word length in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and a species datum per read, subject to the engine laws — the first read is root-admissible, consecutive reads obey the raw stage recursion, coherence and budgets hold at every read, the word closes at its first confirming $W = 1$ read, and every finitely-ended nonempty word carries some terminal verdict. Infinite branches are represented (length $\infty$, catalogued prefixwise).
nodes.lean:
structure CanTreeModel (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) where
  Branch : Type
  hTotal : Nonempty Branch
  len : Branch → ℕ∞
  hN1 : n = 1 → ∀ η, 0 < len η
  datum : Branch → ℕ → Species
  hRoot : ∀ η, 0 < len η →
    RootStage n (datum η 0) ∧ Coherent (datum η 0) ∧ Budget n (datum η 0)
  hStage : ∀ η (r : ℕ), (r + 1 : ℕ∞) < len η →
    StageLaws (datum η r) (datum η (r + 1))
  hCoh : ∀ η (r : ℕ), (r : ℕ∞) < len η →
    Coherent (datum η r) ∧ Budget n (datum η r)
  hHalt : ∀ η (r : ℕ), (r : ℕ∞) < len η → (datum η r).W = 1 →
    len η = (r + 1 : ℕ∞)
  verdict : Branch → Option Verdict
  hVerdictPin : ∀ η (m : ℕ), len η = (m : ℕ∞) → 0 < m → (verdict η).isSome
nodes.note: The conditionality of every completeness theorem lives here: each law field is an open engine obligation to be discharged by the tree-computation corpus (MovesD), and the verdict field is deliberately weak — it says only that some verdict exists, with the full halting-rule content recorded separately as the strong verdict pin.

nodes.title: Collapsing self-loop runs of a word
nodes.math: The run-collapse of a list of species keeps one letter per maximal run of equal consecutive letters, striking the depth direction of self-loops: the empty and singleton lists are fixed, and in $s :: s' :: r$ the head $s$ is dropped exactly when $s = s'$.
nodes.note: The device that turns arbitrarily deep self-looping walks into boundedly long DAG walks; all length bounds in the corpus are stated for the collapsed word.

nodes.title: The species alphabet is finite, with an explicit prime-independent bound
nodes.math: For every $n \ge 1$ the catalogue $\mathcal{S}_n^{\mathrm{raw}}$ is finite, with the explicit (deliberately crude) bound $|\mathcal{S}_n^{\mathrm{raw}}| \le (n+2)^{n^2+3n+12}$. The proof injects each coherent, admissible species into the vectors of length $n^2+3n+12$ with entries in $\{0,\dots,n+1\}$. Since no field of a species mentions a prime, the same alphabet serves every prime $p$ — $p$-independence is discharged by the type itself, not by a clause.
nodes.lean:
theorem SP_FIN (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : (SnRaw n).Finite ∧
    Nat.card (SnRaw n) ≤ (n+2)^(n^2 + 3*n + 12)
nodes.note: A cornerstone of uniformity: one fixed finite alphabet of tower behaviors covers all primes at once, so densities can be organized by finitely many species patterns.

nodes.title: The generated enumeration covers every coherent admissible species
nodes.math: There is an explicitly computed finite list of species — generated by ranging each field over its budget-forced bounds, with the anchor and slot set computed from the other fields — that contains every coherent, budget-admissible species at level $n$. This is the completeness half of the reflection layer: it reduces any 'for all species' claim to a finite kernel scan.
nodes.lean:
theorem speciesEnum_complete {n : ℕ} {s : Species} (hc : Coherent s)
    (hb : Budget n s) : s ∈ speciesEnum n
nodes.note: The kernel bridge: every exhaustively computed n = 3 and n = 1 fact routes universal quantification over species through this list (567 candidate species tuples at n = 3), with native_decide banned corpus-wide.

nodes.title: Collapsed walks in the successor graph have at most 6n² letters
nodes.math: Along any walk in the successor graph whose consecutive letters are distinct (a collapsed walk, all letters in the catalogue), a rank function — lexicographic in key degree $D$, tag, $n - W$, and non-fullness, packed as a natural number below $6n^2$ — strictly increases. Hence the menu graph with self-loops struck is a DAG, and every collapsed walk has length at most $6n^2$.
nodes.lean:
theorem SP_DAG_walk {n} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {l : List Species}
    (h : CollapsedWalk n l) : l.length ≤ 6 * n^2
nodes.note: Bounds the tower: however deep a branch recenters, it passes through at most 6n² distinct species states — the finiteness input for entrance-shape and collapsed-word counting.

nodes.title: Self-loops are exactly the post-recentering fixed windows
nodes.math: A catalogue letter $s$ has a self-loop edge (it lies in its own successor menu) if and only if $s$ is post-recentering with stride $e = 1$ and selection $(g,\mu) = (1, W)$ — the window equal to its own selection multiplicity. Any other selection strictly grows the key degree, so no other letter can repeat.
nodes.lean:
theorem selfloop_iff {n : ℕ} {s : Species} (hs : InCatalogue n s) :
    s ∈ Succ n s ↔ (s.tag = .postRec ∧ s.e = 1 ∧ s.sel = some (1, s.W))
nodes.note: Isolates the single unbounded direction of a walk — the wild recentering spin — which is exactly what the run-collapse strikes before the 6n² bound applies.

nodes.title: Every read of a canonical-tree branch lands in the catalogue
nodes.math: For every prime $p$, every monic degree-$n$ polynomial $f$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, every abstract canonical-tree model of $f$ satisfying the engine laws, every branch $\eta$, and every read $r$ before the word's end: the retained species datum of read $r$ is a member of $\mathcal{S}_n^{\mathrm{raw}}$. The proof is a closure induction: the root read enters via root-admissibility, and each successor read assembles the generation rule from the stage, coherence, and budget laws — the assembly is derived, never assumed.
nodes.lean:
theorem SP_COMP (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p])
    (hf : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n) (M : CanTreeModel n p f)
    (η : M.Branch) (r : ℕ) (hr : (r : ℕ∞) < M.len η) :
    InCatalogue n (M.datum η r)
nodes.gate: hRoot / hStage / hCoh / hHalt — the interface's per-read engine laws (root read is root-admissible; consecutive reads obey the raw stage recursion; coherence and budgets hold at every read; the word halts at its first W = 1 read), consumed as hypotheses and cited to the tree-computation corpus (MovesD), where they remain OPEN engine obligations; hVerdictPin — the weak verdict pin (every finitely-ended nonempty word carries some verdict), a deliberately weak named carrier of the halting-rule residual, unused by this proof but part of the quantified interface.
nodes.note: The connecting theorem between the tree computation and the alphabet; its Lean proof is complete, but its substance is conditional on the engine interface being instantiated by the real tree — see the instantiation and non-vacuity nodes for how far that has been discharged.

nodes.title: The membership theorem fired through the real tree carrier
nodes.math: For the actually built canonical-tree object — branches are the realized chains of the constructed tree model at a coefficient-box point, with the root's presence a proved law rather than a hypothesis — and given a species readout (the single named remaining premise supplying the per-read retained datum together with its mirrored engine laws), every read of every realized chain lands in $\mathcal{S}_n^{\mathrm{raw}}$. This answers an external review finding that the membership theorem was 'an interface closure lemma, not the note's actual-tree completeness theorem': the branch carrier is now the real one, and what remains open is exactly one named seam.
nodes.lean:
theorem SP_COMP_ofTreeModel (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p])
    (hf : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n)
    (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol) (x : Box p m) (R : SpeciesReadout T x)
    (o : Option (History p F)) (ho : T.mem o x)
    (r : ℕ) (hr : (r : ℕ∞) < R.lenOf o) :
    InCatalogue n (R.datumOf o r)
nodes.gate: SpeciesReadout T x — the one named interface premise: a per-read retained-species readout of the built canonical tree, with each engine law restated at the realized carrier; the built vocabulary cannot yet express the datum map itself (the residual partition needs the full residual factorization, and each read's window width is the parent read's μ threaded along the chain).
nodes.note: The instantiation record: everything the built tree vocabulary reaches is discharged (including nonemptiness, from a proved root law), and the residual conditionality is compressed into one named, documented premise.

nodes.title: The interface is non-vacuous: a real three-read witness at degree 2
nodes.math: There exists a canonical-tree model at $n = 2$, $p = 2$, $f = (x-1)^2$ whose single branch has catalogue-word length 3, whose first read is an actual root-stage letter, and all of whose reads land in $\mathcal{S}_2^{\mathrm{raw}}$ through the membership theorem. The three-letter word is transported from a built toy tree branch, and every interface law is discharged by computation on actual letters — no vacuous premise fires.
nodes.lean:
theorem SP_COMP_nonvacuous_at_n2 :
    ∃ (M : CanTreeModel 2 2 f₂) (η : M.Branch),
      M.len η = 3 ∧
      M.datum η 0 = wordHead ∧ RootStage 2 (M.datum η 0) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, (r : ℕ∞) < M.len η → InCatalogue 2 (M.datum η r))
nodes.note: Answers-by-exhibition an adversarial review finding that the membership theorems 'can all hold with zero reads and no engine content'; the zero-read model does still satisfy the interface — that residual weakness is documented, not hidden.

nodes.title: The strong verdict pin: the full halting-rule residual, recorded
nodes.math: The interface's weak verdict field asserts only that a finitely-ended nonempty word carries some verdict. The strong pin records what a faithful verdict model must actually supply: a halting rule $\tau$ computed from cell data alone (never from $f$) into a fixed verdict alphabet, a dictionary onto the bare labels, the exactly-one-verdict law (a word of length $r+1$ carries exactly the $\tau$-verdict of its closing read; infinite branches carry none), and a uniform detection cap (the verdict is determined by the cap-truncated word). Strong implies weak is proved, so every existing consumer stands, and a strong pin is exhibited on the degree-2 witness.
nodes.lean:
structure StrongVerdictPin {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} (M : CanTreeModel n p f) where
  tauV : Species → MovesT.Vd
  dict : MovesT.Vd → Verdict
  htau : ∀ η (r : ℕ), M.len η = ((r + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) →
    M.verdict η = some (dict (tauV (M.datum η r)))
  hinf : ∀ η, M.len η = ⊤ → M.verdict η = none
  cap : ℕ
  hcap : ∀ η η', M.len η = M.len η' →
    (∀ r : ℕ, r < cap → M.datum η r = M.datum η' r) →
    M.verdict η = M.verdict η'

theorem StrongVerdictPin.weak {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} {M : CanTreeModel n p f}
    (S : StrongVerdictPin M) :
    ∀ η (k : ℕ), M.len η = (k : ℕ∞) → 0 < k → (M.verdict η).isSome
nodes.note: The recorded residual for the halting rule: an external review found the weak field insufficient (it determines neither which verdict, nor where the rule fires, nor the detection cap), so the full-content residual is now typed and named, with the strong-implies-weak bridge proved.

nodes.title: At degree 3 the catalogue is exactly the 53 listed letters
nodes.math: A species lies in $\mathcal{S}_3^{\mathrm{raw}}$ if and only if it is one of 53 explicitly listed, pairwise-distinct letters: 21 root letters, 21 + 6 post-recentering window letters (windows 3 and 2), and 5 terminal letters ($53 = 21+21+6+1+4$, established by exhaustive kernel computation in a companion count). Forward direction: closure induction, with exhaustive kernel scans certifying that root admissibility picks out exactly the 21 root letters and that the successor step never leaves the list of 53; backward: kernel-computed reachability of each letter from a root letter.
nodes.lean: theorem SnRaw3_eq : ∀ s, InCatalogue 3 s ↔ s ∈ catalogue3
nodes.note: The exact degree-3 alphabet the density instantiation consumes — the hand catalogue from the source notes is now a machine-checked exact enumeration, proved by kernel decide (native_decide banned).

nodes.title: Exact successor menus at degree 3
nodes.math: For every letter $s$ of the 53-letter degree-3 catalogue and every species $s'$ whatsoever: $s'$ is a legal successor of $s$ if and only if $s'$ appears in $s$'s recorded menu list. The full edge table of the degree-3 successor graph is thereby determined exactly — no off-catalogue edge exists.
nodes.lean:
theorem menu3_exact_global (s : Species) (hs : s ∈ catalogue3)
    (s' : Species) : SuccStep 3 s s' ↔ s' ∈ menuMap3 s
nodes.note: Upgrades the kernel-computed 53×53 edge table to a statement about all species: the degree-3 walk combinatorics downstream can trust the menus as exhaustive.

nodes.title: Exactly two self-loops at degree 3
nodes.math: Filtering the 53-letter degree-3 catalogue for letters with a self-loop edge yields exactly two: the window-3 loop and the window-2 loop, both post-recentering — matching the general self-loop characterization (stride 1, selection equal to the window).
nodes.lean:
theorem loops3 : catalogue3.filter (fun s => succStepB 3 s s) =
    [loopQ3, loopQ23]
nodes.note: Identifies the two loop classes where a degree-3 branch can spin to arbitrary depth; everything else in the catalogued graph moves strictly forward.

nodes.title: At degree 1 the catalogue is a single letter
nodes.math: $\mathcal{S}_1^{\mathrm{raw}}$ contains exactly one species: the confirming root letter at stage $(D,w,W) = (1,1,1)$ with no selection (window 1 forces the terminal rule). Degree 1 admits no moves at all — the catalogue word is this single letter and its move word is empty.
nodes.lean: theorem SnRaw1_eq : ∀ s, InCatalogue 1 s ↔ s = confirmingRoot1
nodes.note: The degenerate base case, needed to make the degree-1 branch-word packaging exact (length-1 word, empty move word) in the interface-facing units.

nodes.title: The recorded p = 3 census thresholds for the six multi-side letters
nodes.math: A partial table assigns to each of the six designated multi-side letters of the degree-3 catalogue its censused threshold value $N^*_3$ — 7 for one letter and 6 for the other five — and is undefined off those six. The theorem certifies only that the recorded table reads back these values.
nodes.lean:
theorem nstar_values : Nstar3six msQ3R1 = some 7 ∧
    Nstar3six msQ3R2 = some 6 ∧ Nstar3six msQ3R3 = some 6 ∧
    Nstar3six msQ3R4a = some 6 ∧ Nstar3six msQ3R4b = some 6 ∧
    Nstar3six msQ3R4c = some 6
nodes.note: These values are DATA from a finite computational census at p = 3 plus a recorded prediction, deliberately kept as a table and never claimed as theorems — no realizability semantics (that actual polynomials attain them) is formalized.

nodes.title: Which letters demand larger residue fields: the exact exclusion lists
nodes.math: Filtering the 53 degree-3 letters for those whose residual partition contains at least two (respectively at least three) linear factors — which cannot all be realized by distinct nonzero roots when the residue field is too small — yields exactly the recorded 11-letter (respectively 2-letter) lists. Passing this field-size gate is necessary for a letter to be realized at a given prime, not sufficient.
nodes.lean:
theorem exclusion_lists_pinned :
    catalogue3.filter (fun s => decide (2 ≤ linCount s)) = fieldSizeExcluded2 ∧
    catalogue3.filter (fun s => decide (3 ≤ linCount s)) = fieldSizeExcluded3
nodes.note: The typed-gate story in miniature: it identifies exactly which species patterns are excluded at the smallest primes, while the docstrings state the necessary-not-sufficient caveat so the exclusion is never over-read as a realizability claim.

nodes.title: The anchored residual is shift-invariant (the link to the moves corpus)
nodes.math: If a Laurent polynomial $x$ has anchored residual $R$ at anchor $a$ — that is, $x = z^a \cdot R(z)$ with $R(0) \neq 0$, the anchoring stripping off the power of $z$ — then $z^{\sigma} x$ has the same anchored residual $R$ at anchor $a + \sigma$. Consequently the residual partition $\lambda$, the selection, and $\ell = \deg R$ never see the relabeling $p \mapsto p + \sigma$ between the census and geometric coordinate systems.
nodes.lean:
theorem hasAnchorK_T_mul {K : Type*} [Field K] (x : LaurentPolynomial K)
    (a σ : ℤ) (R : Polynomial K) (h : Moves.HasAnchorK x a R) :
    Moves.HasAnchorK (LaurentPolynomial.T σ * x) (a + σ) R
nodes.note: The corpus-link unit: it reuses the main moves corpus's anchored-residual predicate rather than duplicating it, tying the species bookkeeping (two coordinate systems, one anchor) to the carry-algebra development.

role: MovesX is the exhaustiveness ("drainage") layer of the proof, formalizing the source note's Section X-EXHAUST. Working against an audited interface that presents, for each prime p, the canonical branching tree the classifier attaches to every monic degree-n p-adic polynomial, it proves that the fraction of polynomials still undecided at inspection level N tends to zero — qualitatively (the density limit) and quantitatively, with p-uniform envelopes c3·p^(−c4·N) and c3'·p^(−c4'·√N) whose constants depend only on the degree and a fixed constant pack. Drainage then yields the per-splitting-type series identity: summing the content of the countable family of decided trees of a given type recovers exactly that type's density. Every analytic theorem is conditional on named kernel hypotheses (alignment, weight-charge, threshold/cap linearity, progress, bridge, tall-tails, and 'ns-null' — that every non-standard-track fiber has content zero), whose discharge — and the interface's concrete instance — must come from the classifier corpora.
oneLiner: Undecided polynomials drain to density zero, with explicit p-uniform envelopes

nodes.title: Nodes of the branching tower
nodes.math: A node of the residual tower for degree $n$ carries letter data $(e, \ell, h, s_0, u_0)$ with $e, h, \ell \ge 1$ and $\gcd(e,h) = 1$: $e$ the ramification jump, $h$ the slope numerator, $\ell$ the residual length, $(s_0, u_0)$ the current base point. A continuing node additionally selects a pair $(g, \mu)$ with $1 \le g$, $1 \le \mu$, $\mu g \le \ell$, and carries an increment-vs-recentering flag; coherence laws force the flag on the $\ell = 1$ rows (increment when $e \ge 2$, recentering when $e = 1$). Histories are finite lists of nodes, classified into rows: T1 ($\ell \ge 2$), T2 ($\ell = 1, e \ge 2, h \ge 2$), T3 ($\ell = 1, e \ge 2, h = 1$), T4 ($\ell = 1, e = 1$), T5 (terminal, no selection).
nodes.lean:
structure XNode (n : ℕ) where
  e : ℕ
  ell : ℕ
  h : ℕ
  s0 : ℕ
  u0 : ℕ
  sel : Option (ℕ × ℕ)
  isIncrement : Bool
  epos : 1 ≤ e
  hpos : 1 ≤ h
  ellpos : 1 ≤ ell
  hcop : Nat.Coprime e h
  selBound : ∀ g μ, sel = some (g, μ) → 1 ≤ g ∧ 1 ≤ μ ∧ μ * g ≤ ell
  t2inc : ell = 1 → 2 ≤ e → 2 ≤ h → sel.isSome → isIncrement = true
  t3inc : ell = 1 → 2 ≤ e → h = 1 → sel.isSome → isIncrement = true
  t4rec : ell = 1 → e = 1 → sel.isSome → isIncrement = false
nodes.note: The combinatorial vocabulary of the whole corpus: every depth, height, and index statement is about finite lists of these nodes.

nodes.title: The space of monic p-adic polynomials and its discriminant valuation
nodes.math: The carrier is the set of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}_p$. Its zero-discriminant locus is $\{f : \operatorname{disc} f = 0\}$, and for $f$ in the carrier $v(f) := v_p(\operatorname{disc} f) \in \mathbb{N}$ is the $p$-adic valuation of the discriminant (junk value $0$ on the zero locus, which every statement using $v$ excludes explicitly).
nodes.note: The concrete probability space of the drainage statements: all densities are contents of subsets of this box, keyed by the discriminant valuation.

nodes.title: The per-prime classifier-tree interface
nodes.math: For each prime $p$, an audited package presenting: for every polynomial $f$ in the carrier, a rooted, finitely branching tree of branches, each with a node history; a detection theory — per-branch threshold and cap such that leaf branches free of the non-standard track are detected at every level $N \ge \mathrm{thr}(b) + \mathrm{cap}(b)$; the undecided sets $U(N)$, antitone in $N$, with $f \notin U(N)$ iff its tree is finite and every leaf is detected at level $N$; a countable family of non-standard-track fibers covering all ns-leaves; and a normalized, monotone, finitely subadditive content $\mu$ on the carrier that kills countable unions of null sets, satisfies the monotone convergence $\mu(U(N)) \to \mu(\bigcap_N U(N))$, and the cylinder bound $\mu\{f : v_p(\operatorname{disc} f) \ge D \text{ or } \operatorname{disc} f = 0\} \le T(p,n,D)/p^{nD}$, where $T$ is the level-$D$ vanishing-discriminant count. Each field is one note-cited accepted or owed input.
nodes.lean:
structure XCtx (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] where
  Branch : MonicBox n p → Type
  hist : ∀ {f}, Branch f → XHistory n
  wf : ∀ {f} (b : Branch f), HistWF n (hist b)
  root : ∀ f, Branch f
  hist_root : ∀ f, hist (root f) = ([] : XHistory n)
  parent : ∀ {f}, Branch f → Option (Branch f)
  parent_hist : ∀ {f} (b b' : Branch f), parent b = some b' → ∃ ν, hist b = hist b' ++ [ν]
  parent_root : ∀ f, parent (root f) = none
  reach : ∀ {f} (b : Branch f),
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun c d => parent c = some d) b (root f)
  children : ∀ {f}, Branch f → Finset (Branch f)
  children_iff : ∀ {f} (b c : Branch f), c ∈ children b ↔ parent c = some b
  complete : ∀ {f}, Branch f → Prop
  nsTrack : XNode n → Prop
  nsDec : DecidablePred nsTrack
  capDetectable : ∀ {f}, Branch f → Prop
  capDec : ∀ f, DecidablePred (@capDetectable f)
  detCap : ∀ {f}, Branch f → ℕ
  threshold : ∀ {f}, Branch f → ℕ
  DetectedAt : ∀ {f}, Branch f → ℕ → Prop
  detectBranch :
    ∀ {f} (b : Branch f), children b = ∅ → (∀ ν ∈ hist b, ¬ nsTrack ν) →
      ∀ N, threshold b + @ite ℕ (capDetectable b) (capDec f b) (detCap b) 0 ≤ N →
        DetectedAt b N
  Undec : ℕ → Set (MonicBox n p)
  undec_spec :
    ∀ f N, f ∉ Undec N ↔
      (Finite (Branch f) ∧ ∀ b : Branch f, children b = ∅ → DetectedAt b N)
  undec_antitone : Antitone Undec
  nsIdx : Type
  nsCountable : Countable nsIdx
  nsFiber : nsIdx → Set (MonicBox n p)
  nsCover :
    ∀ f, (∃ b : Branch f, children b = ∅ ∧ ∃ ν ∈ hist b, nsTrack ν) → ∃ i, f ∈ nsFiber i
  frac : Set (MonicBox n p) → ℚ
  frac_univ : frac Set.univ = 1
  frac_nonneg : ∀ s, 0 ≤ frac s
  frac_mono : ∀ s t, s ⊆ t → frac s ≤ frac t
  frac_union_le : ∀ s t, frac (s ∪ t) ≤ frac s + frac t
  frac_iUnion_null :
    ∀ (s : ℕ → Set (MonicBox n p)), (∀ i, frac (s i) = 0) → frac (⋃ i, s i) = 0
  frac_inter_tendsto :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => frac (Undec N)) Filter.atTop (nhds (frac (⋂ N, Undec N)))
  vdisc_le_tail :
    ∀ D, frac { f | D ≤ vdisc f ∨ f ∈ discZero n p } ≤ (tailCount p n D : ℚ) / p ^ (n * D)
nodes.note: The audited consumption surface: every analytic theorem of the corpus is proved against this interface, whose real instance (the Okutsu-Montes classifier engine) is owed by the classifier corpora.

nodes.title: The all-primes family with the published index inequality
nodes.math: The corpus's single shared parameter: for every prime $p$, a classifier-tree context as above together with an index interface — an index function and a stratum-membership relation satisfying the published inequality $2\,\mathrm{ind}(f) \le v_p(\operatorname{disc} f)$ off the zero-discriminant locus — linked by the requirement that every $f$ lies in the stratum of each of its own branch histories.
nodes.lean:
structure GMNIndex (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] where
  ind : MonicBox n p → ℕ
  inStratum : MonicBox n p → XHistory n → Prop
  p2 : ∀ f, f ∉ discZero n p → 2 * ind f ≤ vdisc f

structure XFamily (n : ℕ) where
  ctx : ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], XCtx n p
  gmn : ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], GMNIndex n p
  gmnLink :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : MonicBox n p) (b : (ctx p).Branch f),
      (gmn p).inStratum f ((ctx p).hist b)
nodes.note: The index inequality 2·ind ≤ v_p(disc) is the cited Guardia–Montes–Nart (GMN) theorem of the index; the family carries the corpus's ONE inhabitation obligation, which the classifier corpora must supply — recorded as open.

nodes.title: The named kernel hypotheses everything is conditional on
nodes.math: The corpus's conditional inputs, stated once as named propositions about the shared family: alignment (the certified depth of any stratum is at most the index, off $\operatorname{disc}=0$); weight-charge (recentering and T4 step counts are at most $s(n)\, v_p(\operatorname{disc} f)$); threshold and cap linearity in the total height $\sum_r h_r$; progress (branches undetected at level $N$ are deep or tall at linear rates); tall-tails ($\mu(\text{some node of height} \ge h^*) \le C_T\, p^{-c_T h^*}$); ns-null (every non-standard-track fiber has content zero); the route disjunction combining alignment and weight-charge in two admissible ways; and the bridge, displayed here: at every level $N$ the undecided set is contained in (disc-zero) $\cup$ (ns-fibers) $\cup$ (infinite-tree locus) $\cup$ (leaf, ns-free witness branches with $N < \mathrm{thr}(b)+\mathrm{cap}(b)$), and the undecided mass carrying no such witness is zero.
nodes.lean:
def X2BridgeP (n : ℕ) (X : XFamily n) : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (N : ℕ),
    ((X.ctx p).Undec N ⊆ discZero n p ∪ (⋃ i, (X.ctx p).nsFiber i) ∪ InfTree (X.ctx p) ∪
      { f | ∃ b : (X.ctx p).Branch f,
          IsLeafB (X.ctx p) b ∧ NsFreeB (X.ctx p) b ∧
            N < (X.ctx p).threshold b + capHB (X.ctx p) b }) ∧
    (X.ctx p).frac { f | f ∈ (X.ctx p).Undec N ∧
      ¬ ∃ b : (X.ctx p).Branch f,
          IsLeafB (X.ctx p) b ∧ NsFreeB (X.ctx p) b ∧
            N < (X.ctx p).threshold b + capHB (X.ctx p) b } = 0

def X3aRouteP (n : ℕ) (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n) : Prop :=
  (X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, true⟩  ∧ WeightChargeT4P n X K) ∨
  (X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, false⟩ ∧ WeightChargeFullP n X K)
nodes.note: These named propositions (the full list: alignment, weight-charge T4/full, affine threshold, cap, progress, tall-tails, bridge, ns-null, route) are exactly the gates of every conditional theorem below; they must be discharged by the classifier corpora.

nodes.title: Decided-tree series data and the density of a splitting type
nodes.math: A per-prime series presentation: a countable family of complete realizable finite trees, each carrying a fiber (a set of polynomials) and a letter-computed splitting type, together with the true splitting type of each polynomial. Fibers are pairwise disjoint, disjoint from the never-decided set $\bigcap_N U(N)$, and cover every decided polynomial off the zero-discriminant locus. The density of a splitting type $\sigma$ is defined as the content of its true-type event: $\mathrm{density}(\sigma) := \mu\{f : \mathrm{type}(f) = \sigma\}$.
nodes.lean:
structure SeriesData (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (C : XCtx n p) where
  FinTree : Type
  treeCountable : Countable FinTree
  fiber : FinTree → Set (MonicBox n p)
  typemult : FinTree → SplitType n
  splitType : MonicBox n p → SplitType n
  fiber_disjoint : ∀ T T', T ≠ T' → Disjoint (fiber T) (fiber T')
  fiber_decided : ∀ T, Disjoint (fiber T) (⋂ N, C.Undec N)
  decided_covered : ∀ f, f ∉ (⋂ N, C.Undec N) → f ∉ discZero n p → ∃ T, f ∈ fiber T

def densityOf (S : SeriesData n p C) (σ : SplitType n) : ℚ :=
  C.frac { f | S.splitType f = σ }
nodes.note: Defines what 'the density of a splitting type' means and packages the countable decided-tree family that the series identity sums over; the concrete instance is owed to the classifier corpora.

nodes.title: The index column counts lattice points
nodes.math: For every continuing node $\nu$, the doubled table index — $\ell(eh\ell + 1 - e - h)$ on row T1, $(e-1)(h-1)$ on row T2, $0$ on the other rows — equals twice the number of lattice points $(x,y)$ with $s_0 < x \le s_0 + e\ell$, $u_0 < y \le u_0 + h\ell$, and $h(x - s_0) + e(y - u_0) \le eh\ell$ (strictly right/above the base point, on or below the Newton-polygon segment); moreover on rows T1 and T2 the doubled index is at least $1$.
nodes.lean:
theorem ind2Region {n : ℕ} (ν : XNode n) (hc : ν.continuing) :
    ind2 ν = 2 * ν.region.card ∧ ((rowOf ν = .T1 ∨ rowOf ν = .T2) → 1 ≤ ind2 ν)
nodes.note: Checks the index column of the row table against Newton-polygon lattice geometry; the 0 on rows T3/T4 records 'no positive per-side bound from the table', never 'the actual index is 0', and the T1/T2 positivity is what makes certified steps consume index in the depth bound.

nodes.title: Tower depth is linearly bounded by the discriminant valuation
nodes.math: Assume the alignment hypothesis (increments certified, recenterings not) and the full weight-charge hypothesis. If $f$ has nonzero discriminant and lies in a well-formed stratum $H$, then $2\, d_{\mathrm{total}}(H) \le (2s+1)\, v_p(\operatorname{disc} f) + 2 \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, where $d_{\mathrm{total}}(H)$ counts the continuing nodes of $H$ and $s = s(n)$ is the weight-charge constant.
nodes.lean:
theorem x1bReduction {n : ℕ} (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n)
    (AL : X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, false⟩) (WC : WeightChargeFullP n X K)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : MonicBox n p) (H : XHistory n)
    (hf : (X.gmn p).inStratum f H) (hd : f ∉ discZero n p) (W : HistWF n H) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    2 * dTotal H ≤ (2 * K.s + 1) * vdisc f + 2 * Nat.log 2 n
nodes.gate: X1aAlignP ⟨true,false⟩ — the certified depth of any stratum is at most the GMN index (T1/T2 increments certified, recenterings not); WeightChargeFullP — #T1-recenterings + #T4 steps ≤ s(n)·v_p(disc f). Both owed to the classifier corpora.
nodes.note: The engine of finiteness: certified tower depth is linear in the discriminant valuation, so trees over polynomials of bounded disc-valuation cannot be deep.

nodes.title: Undetected branches are deep or tall at rate square-root-of-N
nodes.math: Assume the affine threshold and cap hypotheses. If a fourth-piece branch $b$ (leaf-terminated or a prefix of a complete branch, and free of the non-standard track) is undetected at level $N$, i.e. $N < \mathrm{thr}(b) + \mathrm{cap}(b)$, then $N - 1 - c_{\mathrm{cap}} < (c_0 + c_{\mathrm{cap}})(d_{\mathrm{total}} + 1)^2$ or $N - 1 - c_{\mathrm{cap}} < (c_0 + c_{\mathrm{cap}})(\max_r h_r)^2$: escaping detection at level $N$ forces depth or height of order $\sqrt N$.
nodes.lean:
theorem x2hypAssembled {n : ℕ} (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n)
    (AF : X2AffP n X K) (CP : X2CapP n X K)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : MonicBox n p) (b : (X.ctx p).Branch f)
    (hb : FourthPieceB (X.ctx p) b) (N : ℕ)
    (hN : N < (X.ctx p).threshold b + capHB (X.ctx p) b) :
    (N : ℚ) - 1 - K.ccap < (K.c0 + K.ccap) * ((dTotal ((X.ctx p).hist b) : ℚ) + 1) ^ 2 ∨
    (N : ℚ) - 1 - K.ccap < (K.c0 + K.ccap) * (maxH ((X.ctx p).hist b) : ℚ) ^ 2
nodes.gate: X2AffP — the detection threshold of a fourth-piece branch is ≤ 1 + c₀·Σ h_r; X2CapP — its detection cap is ≤ c_cap·(1 + Σ h_r). Both open, to be discharged by the classifier corpora.
nodes.note: Both prices are paid in the one currency Σ h_r; this dichotomy is the driver of the square-root fallback envelope.

nodes.title: A norm-compatible splitting extension exists
nodes.math: Every nonzero polynomial $g$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ admits a field extension $L / \mathbb{Q}_p$ carrying a multiplicative absolute value that extends the $p$-adic norm and over which $g$ splits into linear factors — constructed as the splitting field of $g$ equipped with the spectral norm.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def valExtOf (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (g : Polynomial ℚ_[p]) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    ValExt p g
nodes.note: An existence witness (a definition whose fields carry the proof obligations) supplying the valued splitting extension the covering argument needs; by design it appears in no public statement and is discharged inside the tail bound's proof.

nodes.title: The discriminant event on a coefficient line is covered by n−1 small balls
nodes.math: Fix $n \ge 2$, a level $D$, and tail coefficients $a_1, \dots, a_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. There is a labeling of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by at most $n - 1$ labels such that any two constant terms $a_0, b_0$ for which $p^D$ divides $\operatorname{disc}(X^n + a_{n-1}X^{n-1} + \cdots + a_1 X + a_0)$ (resp. with $b_0$), and which receive the same label, satisfy $a_0 \equiv b_0 \pmod{p^E}$ with $E = \lceil (D - n\, v_p(n))/(n-1) \rceil$. Equivalently: on each constant-term line the level-$D$ discriminant event is covered by at most $n-1$ balls of radius $p^{-E}$, clustered near the critical points of the polynomial.
nodes.lean:
theorem ballCover (p n D : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (h2 : 2 ≤ n) (aTail : Fin (n - 1) → ℤ_[p])
    (V : ValExt p (fTail n p (by omega) aTail)) :
    ∃ idx : ℤ_[p] → Fin (n - 1), ∀ a0 b0,
      Event p n D (by omega) aTail a0 → Event p n D (by omega) aTail b0 →
      idx a0 = idx b0 → (p : ℤ_[p]) ^ (tailExp p n D).toNat ∣ (a0 - b0)
nodes.note: The geometric heart of the tail bound (the valued-extension argument is supplied by the norm-extension construction, so nothing here is owed); an earlier draft proof failed independent re-verification (a deterministic kernel timeout) and was rebuilt — the final proof uses no axioms beyond Lean's core.

nodes.title: Counting bound for high discriminant divisibility
nodes.math: Unconditionally: the number $T(p,n,D)$ of coefficient tuples in $(\mathbb{Z}/p^D)^n$ whose monic degree-$n$ polynomial has discriminant $\equiv 0 \bmod p^D$ satisfies $T(p,n,D)\, p^{E} \le (n-1)\, p^{nD}$, where $E = \lceil (D - n\, v_p(n))/(n-1) \rceil$. Equivalently, the fraction of level-$D$ coefficient boxes with $p^D \mid \operatorname{disc}$ is at most $(n-1)\, p^{-\lceil (D - n v_p(n))/(n-1) \rceil}$ — the note's display (3b).
nodes.lean:
theorem tailCountBound (p n D : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (h2 : 2 ≤ n) :
    (tailCount p n D : ℚ) * (p : ℚ) ^ (tailExp p n D) ≤
      (n - 1 : ℚ) * (p : ℚ) ^ ((n * D : ℕ) : ℤ)
nodes.note: The corpus's fully concrete analytic estimate, proved over ℤ_p with no interface hypotheses at all; through the interface's cylinder-bound field it feeds every measure statement downstream.

nodes.title: The zero-discriminant locus has density zero
nodes.math: For every degree $n \ge 2$, every prime $p$, and every context satisfying the audited interface, the set of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with discriminant exactly zero has content zero: $\mu\{f : \operatorname{disc} f = 0\} = 0$.
nodes.lean:
theorem discZeroNull (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (h2 : 2 ≤ n) (C : XCtx n p) :
    C.frac (discZero n p) = 0
nodes.note: The polynomials on which the classifier can never halt carry no density, so drainage need only be asserted off a null set; proved for every context satisfying the interface (whose concrete instance is owed), by squeezing the interface's cylinder bound against the unconditional tail count.

nodes.title: Koenig's lemma for the classifier tree
nodes.math: For any context and any polynomial $f$: if the rooted, finitely branching tree of branches of $f$ admits no infinite root-descending path (no sequence $g$ with $g_0$ the root and each $g_{k+1}$ a child of $g_k$), then $f$ has only finitely many branches — Koenig's lemma in contrapositive form, with finite branching supplied by the interface's finite child menus.
nodes.lean:
theorem koenigFinite {n p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (C : XCtx n p) (f : MonicBox n p)
    (hbranch : ¬ ∃ g : ℕ → C.Branch f,
      g 0 = C.root f ∧ ∀ k, C.parent (g (k + 1)) = some (g k)) :
    Finite (C.Branch f)
nodes.note: Pure interface combinatorics upgrading 'every branch is finite' to 'the whole tree is finite'; no kernel hypotheses consumed.

nodes.title: Off the discriminant locus, every classifier tree is finite
nodes.math: Assume the route hypothesis (alignment plus weight-charge, in either admissible combination). Then for every prime $p$ and every monic degree-$n$ polynomial $f$ with nonzero discriminant, the canonical tree of $f$ is finite: an infinite path would produce strata of unbounded certified depth, contradicting the linear bound $2\, d_{\mathrm{total}} \le (2s+1) v_p(\operatorname{disc} f) + 2\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$; Koenig's lemma then closes the tree.
nodes.lean:
theorem treeFinite {n : ℕ} (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n) (R : X3aRouteP n X K)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hn : 1 ≤ n) (f : MonicBox n p) (hd : f ∉ discZero n p) :
    Finite ((X.ctx p).Branch f)
nodes.gate: X3aRouteP — either (alignment with recenterings certified + T4-only weight-charge) or (alignment without recenterings + full weight-charge); owed to the classifier corpora.
nodes.note: The pointwise exhaustiveness statement X.3(a): off the null discriminant locus every classifier tree halts.

nodes.title: Exponential envelope for the undecided fraction
nodes.math: For each degree $n \ge 2$ and each constant pack $K$ there exist a level $N_0$ and constants $c_3, c_4 > 0$, all depending only on $(n, K)$ — in particular bound before the prime — such that for every family satisfying the nine named kernel hypotheses, every prime $p$, and every $N \ge N_0$: $\mu(U(N)) \le c_3\, p^{-c_4 N}$.
nodes.lean:
theorem envelopeExp (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (K : XConsts n) :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ c3 c4 : ℝ, 0 < c3 ∧ 0 < c4 ∧
      ∀ (X : XFamily n), X2ProgressP n X K → X2BridgeP n X → X2AffP n X K → X2CapP n X K →
        X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, false⟩ → WeightChargeFullP n X K →
        X2TailsP n X K → NsNullP n X → X3aRouteP n X K →
        ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N →
          ((X.ctx p).frac ((X.ctx p).Undec N) : ℝ) ≤ c3 * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(c4 * N))
nodes.gate: X2ProgressP — undetected fourth-piece branches are deep or tall at linear rates in N; X2BridgeP — Undec(N) splits into disc-zero / ns-fiber / infinite-tree / witness-branch pieces with the witness-free remainder of content zero; X2AffP and X2CapP — detection threshold and cap linear in Σ h_r; X1aAlignP ⟨true,false⟩ and WeightChargeFullP — depth charged against v_p(disc); X2TailsP — content of the height-≥h* event ≤ C_T·p^(−c_T·h*); NsNullP — ns fibers null; X3aRouteP — the route disjunction. All owed to the classifier corpora.
nodes.note: The strongest quantitative drainage claim, restated after its original all-N form was refuted by a compiled countermodel: the threshold N₀ and constants are now bound before the prime, giving p-uniform exponential decay only above N₀.

nodes.title: Square-root fallback envelope for the undecided fraction
nodes.math: Without the progress hypothesis: for each $n \ge 2$ and constant pack $K$ there exist $N_0$ and $c_3', c_4' > 0$ depending only on $(n, K)$ such that for every family satisfying the remaining eight kernel hypotheses, every prime $p$, and every $N \ge N_0$: $\mu(U(N)) \le c_3'\, p^{-c_4' \sqrt{N}}$ — subexponential decay, enough for the qualitative drainage but not for squeeze constants.
nodes.lean:
theorem envelopeSqrt (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (K : XConsts n) :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ c3' c4' : ℝ, 0 < c3' ∧ 0 < c4' ∧
      ∀ (X : XFamily n), X2BridgeP n X → X2AffP n X K → X2CapP n X K →
        X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, false⟩ → WeightChargeFullP n X K →
        X2TailsP n X K → NsNullP n X → X3aRouteP n X K →
        ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N →
          ((X.ctx p).frac ((X.ctx p).Undec N) : ℝ) ≤ c3' * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(c4' * Real.sqrt N))
nodes.gate: Same hypothesis list as the exponential envelope minus X2ProgressP: X2BridgeP, X2AffP, X2CapP, X1aAlignP ⟨true,false⟩, WeightChargeFullP, X2TailsP, NsNullP, X3aRouteP; the square-root dichotomy replaces the linear progress hypothesis. All open, to be discharged by the classifier corpora.
nodes.note: The fallback route that trades the hardest hypothesis (linear progress) for a weaker p^(−c√N) rate, restated after the same refutation as the exponential envelope.

nodes.title: The undecided fraction tends to zero (drainage)
nodes.math: For every degree $n \ge 2$, every family satisfying the route and ns-null hypotheses, and every prime $p$: $\mu(U(N)) \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$ — the classifier eventually decides asymptotically every monic degree-$n$ polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}_p$.
nodes.lean:
theorem x3Density {n : ℕ} (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (R : X3aRouteP n X K) (NS : NsNullP n X) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (X.ctx p).frac ((X.ctx p).Undec N)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
nodes.gate: X3aRouteP — the alignment/weight-charge route disjunction; NsNullP — every non-standard-track fiber has content zero. Both owed to the classifier corpora, as is the family's real instance.
nodes.note: THE drainage capstone (the note's X.3): the exhaustiveness leg that the project's full density theorem still needs, obtained by squeezing the never-decided set inside the null discriminant locus and the null ns-fibers.

nodes.title: The tree series computes each splitting-type density
nodes.math: Under the route and ns-null hypotheses plus type-soundness and countable fiber additivity: for each splitting type $\sigma$, the countable family $\big(\mu(\text{fiber of } T)\big)$, indexed by the decided trees $T$ whose letter-computed type is $\sigma$, sums (unconditionally, as a convergent sum) to exactly $\mathrm{density}(\sigma) = \mu\{f : \mathrm{type}(f) = \sigma\}$.
nodes.lean:
theorem x3Series {n : ℕ} (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (R : X3aRouteP n X K) (NS : NsNullP n X)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (S : SeriesData n p (X.ctx p))
    (VP : VPSoundP S) (ADD : CountableFiberAdditive S) (σ : SplitType n) :
    HasSum (fun T : { T // S.typemult T = σ } => (X.ctx p).frac (S.fiber T))
      (densityOf S σ)
nodes.gate: X3aRouteP — route disjunction; NsNullP — ns fibers null; VPSoundP — membership in a tree fiber pins the true splitting type to the letter-computed one; CountableFiberAdditive — the content is countably additive over the disjoint tree-fiber family (the Tonelli positive-term regrouping, owed); plus the series presentation itself, whose instance is owed.
nodes.note: The corpus's final output: the bridge from tree-by-tree computation to the exact density of every splitting type — what the uniformity theorem's rational function ultimately evaluates.

nodes.title: Compiled countermodel: the original all-levels envelope was false
nodes.math: The originally stated form of the exponential envelope — constants allowed to depend on the family, with the bound asserted at every level $N$ — is false: a point-mass content at $f_0 = X^2 + X$ (whose discriminant is $1$, a unit at every prime) with the root-only tree and threshold $+$ cap $= 2$ satisfies all nine kernel hypotheses, yet the undecided mass at level $N = 1$ equals $1$ for every prime, contradicting $c_3\, p^{-c_4} \to 0$ as $p \to \infty$. The file derives False from the verbatim universal closure of the old statement.
nodes.lean:
theorem envelopeExp_statement_false :
    ¬ (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (X : XFamily n) (K : XConsts n),
        X2ProgressP n X K → X2BridgeP n X → X2AffP n X K → X2CapP n X K →
        X1aAlignP n X ⟨true, false⟩ → WeightChargeFullP n X K →
        X2TailsP n X K → NsNullP n X → X3aRouteP n X K →
        ∃ c3 c4 : ℝ, 0 < c3 ∧ 0 < c4 ∧ ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (N : ℕ),
          ((X.ctx p).frac ((X.ctx p).Undec N) : ℝ) ≤ c3 * (p : ℝ) ^ (-(c4 * N)))
nodes.note: The refutation record of the corpus: this machine-checked refutation (2026-07-27) forced the restatement of both envelope theorems to bind a threshold N₀ before the prime; the square-root analogue is refuted the same way in lean/notes/XE3_REFUTATION_2026-07-27.lean, and the adjudication is recorded in the blueprint's refutation section.

role: MovesD proves the per-shape mass law: for each well-formed "shape" — the discrete skeleton of one run of the p-adic factorization classifier (per read: Newton-polygon side, factor degree, multiplicity, window position, residue-pool degree) — the number of degree-n coefficient boxes mod p^N realizing that shape obeys exact division-free counting laws, whose two constants (the class count and the digit-ledger exponent) are computed from the shape alone and are independent of the precision N beyond an explicit threshold. This is the counting engine behind uniformity: it converts each classifier outcome into a single monomial C·p^(−A′). It consumes the box-counting layer of MovesC (its Theorem C, part (b): the exact stratum-count identity) and the stage vocabulary of Moves, and exports the mass laws, the well-formedness gate, and explicitly typed interface obligations (a structural tree model, the canonical-policy specification, a threshold identification) to the tree-assembly corpus MovesT.
oneLiner: Per-shape mass law: each shape's density is C·p^(−A′), machine-checked

nodes.title: What counts as a shape: the twelve-clause well-formedness certificate
nodes.math: A shape-prefix is a finite list of reads, each retaining the discrete data of one classifier step: its species (root, increment, or recentering), the Newton-polygon side in lowest terms $(e,h)$, the chosen factor's degree $g$ and its order $\mu$ in the anchor polynomial, an anchor offset $a$, the window position $(s_0, w_{\mathrm{side}})$, the frame width $D$, an intercept datum $u^*$, the total side weight $\gamma$, the residue-pool degree $w$, and a flag marking whether the side's top slot is the box's monic lead. The certificate is the conjunction of twelve laws every genuine shape satisfies: the root occurs exactly at read 0 and its side fits the degree-$n$ box; successive windows nest ($s_0^{(r+1)} + w_{\mathrm{side}}^{(r+1)} \le \mu_r$); $g_r\mu_r \le \ell_r$ where $\ell_r = w_{\mathrm{side},r}/e_r$ is the normalized side length; $e_r \mid w_{\mathrm{side},r}$; the frame-width chain $D_0 = 1$, $D_{r+1} = e_r g_r D_r$; the monic-slot tie (the flag holds exactly at a root read whose side spans the whole box); the residue-degree chain $w_0 = 1$, $w_{r+1} = w_r g_r$; the $\gamma$-tie $\gamma_r = e_r(\mathrm{STR}_r\, u^*_r) + (s_0 + w_{\mathrm{side}})_r\, h_r$ with stretch $\mathrm{STR}_r = \prod_{m<r} e_m$; and the Bézout anchor tie $e_r a_r = s_{0,r} - t^B(e_r,h_r)\,\gamma_r$, where $t^B(e,h)$ is the unique Bézout coefficient of $(e,h)$ in $[0,e)$. A shape of degree $n$ is by definition a certified prefix.
nodes.lean:
structure ShapeWF (n : ℕ) (P : ShapePrefix) : Prop where
  species_iff : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < P.reads.length),
    (P.reads[r]'hr).species = ReadSpecies.root ↔ r = 0
  root_box : ∀ h0 : 0 < P.reads.length, (P.reads[0]'h0).s0 + (P.reads[0]'h0).wSide ≤ n
  window : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r + 1 < P.reads.length),
    (P.reads[r+1]'hr).s0 + (P.reads[r+1]'hr).wSide ≤ (P.reads[r]'(by omega)).μ
  gmu : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < P.reads.length),
    (P.reads[r]'hr).g * (P.reads[r]'hr).μ ≤ (P.reads[r]'hr).len
  edvd : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < P.reads.length), (P.reads[r]'hr).e ∣ (P.reads[r]'hr).wSide
  dchain0 : ∀ h0 : 0 < P.reads.length, (P.reads[0]'h0).Dwidth = 1
  dchain : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r + 1 < P.reads.length),
    (P.reads[r+1]'hr).Dwidth = (P.reads[r]'(by omega)).childWidthS
  monic : P.MonicTie n
  w0 : ∀ h0 : 0 < P.reads.length, (P.reads[0]'h0).w = 1
  wchain : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r + 1 < P.reads.length),
    (P.reads[r+1]'hr).w = (P.reads[r]'(by omega)).w * (P.reads[r]'(by omega)).g
  gamTie : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < P.reads.length),
    (((P.reads[r]'hr).gam : ℤ) : ℚ)
      = ((P.reads[r]'hr).e : ℚ) * ((P.strS r : ℚ) * (P.reads[r]'hr).ustar)
        + ((((P.reads[r]'hr).s0 + (P.reads[r]'hr).wSide) : ℕ) : ℚ) * ((P.reads[r]'hr).h : ℚ)
  anchorTie : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < P.reads.length),
    ((P.reads[r]'hr).e : ℤ) * (P.reads[r]'hr).a
      = ((P.reads[r]'hr).s0 : ℤ) - bezT (P.reads[r]'hr).e (P.reads[r]'hr).h * (P.reads[r]'hr).gam

abbrev Shape (n : ℕ) : Type := {P : ShapePrefix // ShapeWF n P}
nodes.note: The subtype ruling makes well-formedness a matter of type: junk encodings lie outside every quantifier's domain, so the mass laws hold unconditionally over exactly the source note's shape universe.

nodes.title: The class index: realized value-prefixes of a shape, up to canonical presentation
nodes.math: A history (a chain of concrete classifier steps) matches a shape $\hat P$ when its nodes agree with $\hat P$'s reads on every retained field. The prefix set of $\hat P$ consists of the histories that match $\hat P$, are coherent and realizable, live in the degree-$n$ box, and carry the canonical presentation (the policy's canonical lifts and the canonical residue root at every read). The $\eta$-class data of a history records, per read, the tuple of its side digits and the coefficient tuple of its chosen factor $\psi$, valued in the ambient finite field $F$; the class index is the finite image of the prefix set under this map. The class count is $C_{\hat P}(p) := \#\{\eta\text{-classes}\}$ on nonempty shapes and $:= 1$ on the empty shape, whose unique prefix is the empty chain.
nodes.note: The class count is the numerator constant of the shape's density monomial — the quantity the mass laws and the uniform bound are about; the empty-shape dispatch bakes in the note's own convention that the empty prefix set is a singleton.

nodes.title: Presentation data: one jet chart per class, plus the dictionary pin
nodes.math: The corpus's only assumed data. A presentation of a shape at level $N$ assigns to each $\eta$-class a jet chart for its chosen representative — the coordinate system in which the box-counting theorem (Theorem C(b) of the jet corpus) counts that class's locus — together with the dictionary pin: (i) every policy-free realizable prefix is Galois-conjugate to some normalized class, and (ii) Galois-related normalized classes coincide. From a presentation one defines the class fiber $S(\eta,\top) \subseteq (\mathbb{Z}/p)^m$ (the representative's classifier locus at the full box, $m = nN$ base-$p$ digits), the event $S(\hat P,\top) = \bigcup_\eta S(\eta,\top)$ (the whole box on the empty shape), and the multiplicity $\mathrm{mult}(x) = \#\{\eta : x \in S(\eta,\top)\}$ (identically $1$ on the empty shape). A threshold datum is a presentation at every level $N \ge N(\hat P)$.
nodes.lean:
structure Presented (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (n N m : ℕ) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) (P : Shape n) where
  jet : (i : PrefIdx n pol P) → JetSetup (reprOf i) n N m
  hnorm : PresentNorm n pol P

structure Threshold (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (n : ℕ) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) (P : Shape n) where
  jets : ∀ N : ℕ, P.NP pol ≤ N → Presented p F n N (n * N) pol P

def Presented.fiber (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) (i : PrefIdx n pol P) :
    Set (Box p m) := (S.jet i).SHZ (topLocus p m)

def Presented.event (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) : Set (Box p m) :=
  if (P : ShapePrefix).reads = [] then Set.univ else ⋃ i, S.fiber i

noncomputable def Presented.mult (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) (x : Box p m) : ℕ :=
  if (P : ShapePrefix).reads = [] then 1
  else Nat.card {i : PrefIdx n pol P // x ∈ S.fiber i}
nodes.note: The corpus's entire open surface is these two structure fields (the jet charts and the dictionary pin, both to be supplied by the presentation corpus HC2); everything else in MovesD is constructed or proved.

nodes.title: The ledger exponent and the level threshold
nodes.math: The ledger exponent $A(\hat P,n,N)$ counts, summed over reads, the lattice points $(\text{level},\text{position}) \in [0,N)\times[0,n)$ lying in that read's fresh band — the region of coefficient digits the classifier pins at that read, reconstructed from shape data alone (lines, staircases, cumulative floors, rim thresholds). $N_{\mathrm{shape}}$ is an a-priori shape bound on the constrained levels; $A'(\hat P,n) := A(\hat P,n,N_{\mathrm{shape}})$ is the stabilized, level-free exponent. The threshold is $N(\hat P) := 1 + (\text{largest constrained level})$ when the shape has at least one class, and $1$ otherwise — the source note's piecewise convention.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def ShapePrefix.A (P : ShapePrefix) (n N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range P.reads.length).sum (fun r =>
    ((Finset.range N ×ˢ Finset.range n).filter (fun c => P.bandS n r c)).card)

noncomputable def ShapePrefix.Nshape (P : ShapePrefix) : ℕ :=
  1 + ((List.range P.reads.length).map (fun r => ⌈(P.lineS r).intercept⌉.toNat)).foldr max 0

noncomputable def ShapePrefix.A' (P : ShapePrefix) (n : ℕ) : ℕ := P.A n (P.Nshape)

noncomputable def Shape.NP {n : ℕ} (P : Shape n) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) : ℕ :=
  if Nonempty (PrefIdx n pol P) then (P : ShapePrefix).NPband n else 1
nodes.note: A′ is the exponent of the shape's density monomial; its level-freeness (proved in the threshold unit) is what lets one formula serve every precision.

nodes.title: Capstone: the per-shape mass law at every level past the threshold
nodes.math: Fix a nonempty certified shape $\hat P$ of degree $n$ and presentation data at every level $N \ge N(\hat P)$. Then for every such $N$: $\big(\sum_{\eta} \#S(\eta,\top)\big)\, p^{A'(\hat P,n)} = C_{\hat P}(p)\, p^{nN}$ (sum law, an equality) and $\#S(\hat P,\top)\, p^{A'(\hat P,n)} \le C_{\hat P}(p)\, p^{nN}$ (event bound) — the division-free forms of $\sum_\eta \mu(S(\eta,\top)) = C_{\hat P}(p)\,p^{-A}$ and $\mu(S(\hat P,\top)) \le C_{\hat P}(p)\,p^{-A}$. Both constants are computed from the shape alone and are the same at every level: one monomial in $p$ governs the shape's mass at all sufficiently fine precisions. When the shape has no classes, both sides vanish (the source's empty clause). A companion witness theorem constructs the threshold datum from a bare existence hypothesis for presentations.
nodes.lean:
theorem D4R4_all (hne : (P : ShapePrefix).reads ≠ []) (T : Threshold p F n pol P) :

          * p ^ ((P : ShapePrefix).A' n) = P.CD pol * p ^ (n * N)) ∧
      (Nat.card ↥(T.jets N hNP).event * p ^ ((P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
          ≤ P.CD pol * p ^ (n * N))

nodes.title: The sum law: every class contributes exactly p^(nN−A′)
nodes.math: At any level $N$ where the ledger has stabilized ($A(\hat P,n,N) = A'(\hat P,n)$, automatic for $N \ge N(\hat P)$) and for any presentation: $\big(\sum_{\eta} \#S(\eta,\top)\big)\, p^{A'} = \#\{\eta\text{-classes}\}\cdot p^{nN}$. Equivalently each class fiber has exactly $p^{nN-A'}$ points: Theorem C(b) gives $\#S(\eta,\top)\cdot p^{\#\mathrm{pins}(\eta)} = p^{nN}$ per class, and the pin-count transport identifies $\#\mathrm{pins}(\eta) = A'$ for every class. No disjointness of fibers is used anywhere.
nodes.lean:
theorem D4R1_SUM (hne : (P : ShapePrefix).reads ≠ []) (N : ℕ)
    (hA : (P : ShapePrefix).A n N = (P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
    (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) :
    (∑ᶠ i : PrefIdx n pol P, Nat.card ↥(S.fiber i)) * p ^ ((P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
      = Nat.card (PrefIdx n pol P) * p ^ (n * N)
nodes.gate: S : Presented — a jet chart per class plus the dictionary pin (the HC-2 seam data); hA — ledger stabilization at level N, discharged internally by the threshold theorems whenever N ≥ N(P̂); hne — nonempty shape (the empty shape has its own separately proved law).
nodes.note: The heart of the counting: equal fibers via the jet corpus's Theorem C(b) at the full box, plus one shared shape exponent — this is where MovesC's counting engine is consumed.

nodes.title: The event bound: the union bound, division-free
nodes.math: Under the same hypotheses, the event obeys $\#S(\hat P,\top)\cdot p^{A'} \le \#\{\eta\text{-classes}\}\cdot p^{nN}$: every event point has multiplicity $\ge 1$, so $\#S(\hat P,\top) \le \sum_x \mathrm{mult}(x) = \sum_\eta \#S(\eta,\top)$ (double counting of the incidence set), and the sum law finishes.
nodes.lean:
theorem D4R1_EV (hne : (P : ShapePrefix).reads ≠ []) (N : ℕ)
    (hA : (P : ShapePrefix).A n N = (P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
    (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) :
    Nat.card ↥S.event * p ^ ((P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
      ≤ Nat.card (PrefIdx n pol P) * p ^ (n * N)
nodes.gate: Same as the sum law: S : Presented (HC-2 seam data), hA (discharged internally past the threshold), hne (nonempty shape).
nodes.note: The subadditivity half of the mass law; the incidence identity behind it provably FAILS on the empty shape (there the left side is the full box, the right side zero), so its nonemptiness hypothesis was forced by a compiled near-countermodel and is recorded as a deviation.

nodes.title: Equality criterion: exact counting iff every event point is covered once
nodes.math: Equality holds in the event bound if and only if the multiplicity is identically $1$ on the event — i.e. iff the class fibers cover each event point exactly once: $\#S(\hat P,\top)\, p^{A'} = C\, p^{nN} \iff \forall x \in S(\hat P,\top),\ \mathrm{mult}(x) = 1$. The finite-level statement is pointwise and carries no measure-zero exception.
nodes.lean:
theorem D4R1_EV_iff (hne : (P : ShapePrefix).reads ≠ []) (N : ℕ)
    (hA : (P : ShapePrefix).A n N = (P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
    (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) :
    (Nat.card ↥S.event * p ^ ((P : ShapePrefix).A' n)
        = Nat.card (PrefIdx n pol P) * p ^ (n * N))
      ↔ (∀ x ∈ S.event, S.mult x = 1)
nodes.gate: Same as the sum law: S : Presented (HC-2 seam data), hA (discharged internally past the threshold), hne (nonempty shape).

nodes.title: The encoding injection: a class is determined by its digits and ranks
nodes.math: Each $\eta$-class of a shape $\hat P$ is determined by its encoding: for each read $r$, the tuple of its $d_r$ counted side digits — which provably lie in the pool $\mathbb{A}_r = \{x \in F : x^{p^{w_r}} = x\}$ of size at most $p^{w_r}$ — together with its selection rank $s_r < \bar m_r$, the position of its chosen factor $\psi$ among the eligible degree-$g_r$ factors of the anchor polynomial in a fixed lexicographic order. The map $\mathrm{enc}: \mathrm{Pref}(\hat P) \hookrightarrow \prod_r \mathbb{A}_r^{d_r} \times \prod_r \{0,\dots,\bar m_r - 1\}$ is injective — with no side hypotheses at all. At the empty shape the target is the empty product, of cardinality $1 = C_\varnothing$.
nodes.lean:
theorem encIdx_inj :
    Function.Injective (encIdx : PrefIdx n pol P → EncTargetP p F (P : ShapePrefix))

theorem encTargetP_empty (hP : (P : ShapePrefix).reads = []) :
    Nat.card (EncTargetP p F (P : ShapePrefix)) = 1
nodes.note: The source note's L11 upgraded from claim to hypothesis-free theorem — the combinatorial core of the class-count bound, assembled from a chain of proved auxiliaries (digits lie in the pool, frame fields equal the pool, rank bounds and rank injectivity).

nodes.title: The uniform class-count bound, with a prime-free selection factor
nodes.math: For every certified shape: $C_{\hat P}(p) \le M(\hat P)\, p^{W(\hat P)}$ and $M(\hat P) \le n^{|\hat P|}$, where $W(\hat P) = \sum_r w_r d_r$ is the pool-weighted count of retained digits, $M(\hat P) = \prod_r \lfloor \ell_r/(g_r\mu_r)\rfloor$ the factor-selection bound, and $|\hat P|$ the number of reads. The second inequality is prime-free — the uniformity-in-$p$ input. Proof: the class count injects into the encoding target (the encoding injection), whose cardinality is at most $M\cdot p^W$; at the empty shape both sides are $1$.

theorem D4R2'_full (hnorm : PresentNorm n pol P) :
    P.CD pol ≤ (P : ShapePrefix).Mfac * p ^ (P : ShapePrefix).W ∧
      (P : ShapePrefix).Mfac ≤ n ^ (P : ShapePrefix).reads.length

nodes.note: The uniformity input: the numerator of every shape's density monomial is bounded by shape data with a prime-free selection factor, which is what makes the density a single rational function of q across primes.

nodes.title: One exponent per shape: pinned digits equal the shape's ledger count
nodes.math: For every presented $\eta$-class $i$ of a shape $\hat P$: the total number of digits pinned by that class's jet chart at the full box equals $A(\hat P,n,N)$, a quantity computed from the shape alone. The pin count is a priori history data; this theorem transports it read-by-read to pure shape data by matching the jet's fresh bands against the shape's reconstructed bands on the $N \times n$ coordinate grid. Consequence: all classes of one shape share one exponent — the mechanism that turns the per-class counting into an exact sum law.

nodes.note: The geometric hinge of the corpus: a long proved chain (band transport, chart counting, shape replicas of lines/staircases/floors/rims) collapses here into one identity between history data and shape data.

nodes.title: The threshold works: the ledger stabilizes from N(P̂) on

Proved outright from the definitions — every band-constrained coordinate has level below the threshold.

nodes.title: The gate is sound: realizable histories always pass the certificate
nodes.math: If a shape matches an actual classifier history field-by-field on all retained data, and the history is coherent and lives in the degree-$n$ box, then the shape satisfies all twelve certificate clauses — provided two named encoding hypotheses: (hmt0) the root read's monic flag is set iff its side spans the whole box, and (hw0) the root frame field has exactly $p$ elements. So restricting the theory to certified shapes loses none of the realizable universe, modulo those two ledgered pins.

    (hmt0 : ∀ h0 : 0 < Q.reads.length,

nodes.title: The class count is absolute: normalized classes equal Galois classes
nodes.math: Under the dictionary pin, the normalized class count equals the number of classes of the policy-free realizable prefix set modulo the Galois relation — two histories being related iff a field automorphism of $F$ carries the class data (side digits and factor coefficients, per read) of one to the other. So the formalized count is the source note's literal finite count of realized value-prefixes with conjugate presentations identified: the normalization construction neither collapses distinct classes (uniqueness half of the pin) nor misses any (totality half).

nodes.title: The canonical-policy pin: what the one lift rule must satisfy
nodes.math: The counting theorems quantify over any blind, deterministic lift policy; which policy is the note's canonical one is pinned by this typed interface. A pin for a policy consists of a predicate ('$t$ is the canonical offset lift realizer at node $\nu$' — whose exact formula is deferred to the carry-algebra corpus) together with five laws: totality at every recentering node; realizers are nonzero; a realizer's monomial support lies in a single arithmetic progression of stride $e$ and length $g$, anchored in the forced Bézout congruence class $j_0 \equiv t^B(e,h)\,\gamma \pmod e$ (with $t^B(e,h)$ the unique Bézout coefficient of $(e,h)$ in $[0,e)$, as in the shape certificate); uniqueness (exactly one realizer per node); and the digit-value law — at a recentering the realizer lies in the frame's coefficient space, carries the key weight, and its top graded residual equals the recorded center. Together these force every pinned policy's recentering lift to be a genuine, nonzero center realizer.
nodes.lean:
structure OffsetPPin {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (pol : CanonPolicy p F) where
  Realizes : Node p F → Polynomial ℤ_[p] → Prop
  total : ∀ ν : Node p F, ν.species = ReadSpecies.recentering → Realizes ν (pol.liftOf ν)
  realizes_ne_zero : ∀ (ν : Node p F) (t : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), Realizes ν t → t ≠ 0
  support_forced : ∀ (ν : Node p F) (t : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), Realizes ν t →
    ∃ j₀ : ℕ, (j₀ : ℤ) % (ν.e : ℤ) = (bezT ν.e ν.h * ν.gam) % (ν.e : ℤ) ∧
      ∀ j ∈ t.support, ∃ k : ℕ, k < ν.g ∧ j = j₀ + k * ν.e
  realizes_unique : ∀ (ν : Node p F) (t t' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]),
    Realizes ν t → Realizes ν t' → t = t'
  digits_prescribed : ∀ (ν : Node p F) (t : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), Realizes ν t →
    ν.species = ReadSpecies.recentering →
    inC ν.σ.Φ t ∧ ν.σ.w t = ν.σ.w ν.σ.Φ ∧
      ν.σ.R t = LaurentPolynomial.C ν.center * LaurentPolynomial.T 0
nodes.note: Interface typing: it specifies the note's one lift rule to the maximal extent expressible in exported vocabulary; the residual slot-selection law (WHICH weight-and-residual-equal realizer) is a NAMED open boundary to be discharged by the carry-algebra corpus HC1 — until then, a non-canonical but compatible realizer could also satisfy the specification, and the file says so.

nodes.title: Kernel refutations for the policy specification: degenerate and wrong-valued policies are excluded
nodes.math: Three compiled refutations guard the policy pin against degenerate instantiations found during adversarial review: (1) no pin's realizer predicate can be the bare nonzero predicate — the uniqueness law would force $1 = X$ in $\mathbb{Z}_p[X]$; (2) a policy whose lift at even one recentering node has the wrong top residual value (not the recorded center) admits no pin at all — the pin type is empty; (3) likewise for a lift with the wrong weight. Wrong-valued policies are thus excluded by type, not by prose.
nodes.lean:
theorem OffsetPPin.not_realizes_bare_ne_zero {pol : CanonPolicy p F}
    (pin : OffsetPPin pol) (ν : Node p F) :
    pin.Realizes ν ≠ fun t : Polynomial ℤ_[p] => t ≠ 0

theorem OffsetPPin.no_pin_of_wrong_value {pol : CanonPolicy p F} (ν : Node p F)
    (hν : ν.species = ReadSpecies.recentering)
    (hwrong : ν.σ.R (pol.liftOf ν)
      ≠ LaurentPolynomial.C ν.center * LaurentPolynomial.T 0) :
    IsEmpty (OffsetPPin pol)

theorem OffsetPPin.no_pin_of_wrong_weight {pol : CanonPolicy p F} (ν : Node p F)
    (hν : ν.species = ReadSpecies.recentering)
    (hwrong : ν.σ.w (pol.liftOf ν) ≠ ν.σ.w ν.σ.Φ) :
    IsEmpty (OffsetPPin pol)
nodes.note: The compiled refutations that killed two reviewer-found bypasses of the policy specification (a bare-nonzero instantiation and a singleton-realizer instantiation with wrong digit values) — each round of adversarial review left a compiled refutation behind.
