nodes.title: The tree interface, structural half only: a declared boundary
nodes.math: A structural model of the canonical tree $T_{\mathrm{can}}(f)$ attached to each coefficient box $f$: a membership relation between (possibly empty) history chains and boxes such that the empty chain is a member for every box (the root's presence is a law), membership of an extended chain factors through a child relation, and members are coherent, realizable, and canonically presented. Alongside it, two properties are declared but neither used nor proved in this corpus: the cylinder law — the class fiber $S(\eta,\top)$ equals $\{f : \eta \in T_{\mathrm{can}}(f)\}$ — and representative independence — any two histories in the same class present the same fiber under any jet charts. The tree's semantic layer (eligibility of children, verdicts) is deliberately absent.
nodes.lean:
structure TreeModel (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (n N m : ℕ) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) where
  mem : Option (History p F) → Box p m → Prop
  child : Option (History p F) → Node p F → Box p m → Prop
  root_mem : ∀ x : Box p m, mem none x
  mem_single : ∀ (ν : Node p F)
      (h1 : ([ν] : List (Node p F)) ≠ [] ∧
        ∀ (j : ℕ) (hj : j < ([ν] : List (Node p F)).length),
          ((([ν] : List (Node p F))[j]'hj).species = ReadSpecies.root ↔ j = 0))
      (x : Box p m),
    mem (some ⟨[ν], h1.1, h1.2⟩) x ↔ child none ν x
  mem_snoc : ∀ (H : History p F) (ν : Node p F) (hν : ν.species ≠ ReadSpecies.root)
      (x : Box p m),
    mem (some (H.snoc ν hν)) x ↔ (mem (some H) x ∧ child (some H) ν x)
  mem_realizable : ∀ (H : History p F) (x : Box p m), mem (some H) x →
    HistoryCoherent H ∧ Realizable H ∧ pol.IsCanonPres H

def D4R_CYL {n N m : ℕ} {pol : CanonPolicy p F} {P : Shape n}
    (S : Presented p F n N m pol P) (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : PrefIdx n pol P) (x : Box p m), x ∈ S.fiber i ↔ T.mem (some (reprOf i)) x

def ClassFiberWelldef (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (n N m : ℕ) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) (P : Shape n) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H H' : History p F), H ∈ PrefSet n pol P → H' ∈ PrefSet n pol P →
    etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H = etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H' →
    ∀ (J : JetSetup H n N m) (J' : JetSetup H' n N m),
      J.SHZ (topLocus p m) = J'.SHZ (topLocus p m)
nodes.note: The declared interface to the tree-assembly corpus (MovesT): only the structural counting half of the tree interface exists here — the stated cylinder and well-definedness properties are consumed by NOTHING in this corpus, the semantic child layer and the verdict structure are not declared at all, and the file says so explicitly rather than smuggling them in.

role: MovesT is the branch-to-tree assembly layer: it defines the finite canonical verdict tree that records, branch by branch, how a p-adic polynomial's factorization is discovered, and proves — unconditionally — that every "decided" polynomial grows exactly one such tree. The pricing of trees is conditional: the set of polynomials growing a given tree has mass an explicit power of p, computed by charging each site of the tree exactly once (root split, unbranched segments, multi-branch splits) — but the root-split clause carries one fenced unproved goal (to be discharged by the HC2 corpus) and the per-site laws are consumed as an assumed ledger; a dictionary theorem then converts these per-tree masses back into the per-class masses the density tables use, under further named class-system hypotheses. The whole layer is exported as one named package of propositions that the density-assembly interface consumes, carrying both what is proved and what is open. Refutation records are kept public: a compiled countermodel showing the sibling-independence counting law is genuinely extra content, and two toy-model obligations recorded as false at their fixed toy tables (discharging them requires re-adjudicating the tables).
oneLiner: Each decided polynomial grows one canonical tree; tree fibers get exact masses

nodes.title: The finite verdict tree
nodes.math: A verdict tree is a finite set of nonempty branch histories (chains of factorization-discovery reads), closed under nonempty prefixes, together with: a multiset of root verdicts recording the unramified (Hensel) part, each of type $\{(e,f)\}=\{(1,g)\}$ (unramified of residue degree $g$); a verdict attached to exactly the maximal chains (the leaves); and a marking of some leaves as non-split ("ns") leaves. It is the finite combinatorial record of how one $p$-adic polynomial's factorization is discovered branch by branch.
nodes.lean:
structure VTree (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] where
  chains : Set (History p F)
  hfin : chains.Finite
  hne_nodes : ∀ H ∈ chains, H.nodes ≠ []
  hclosed : ∀ H ∈ chains, ∀ H' : History p F,
    H'.IsPrefixOf H → H'.nodes ≠ [] → H' ∈ chains
  henV : Multiset Vd
  hhen : ∀ v ∈ henV, ∃ g : ℕ, 1 ≤ g ∧ v.1 = {(1, g)}
  leafV : History p F → Option Vd
  hleaf : ∀ H, (leafV H).isSome ↔ (H ∈ chains ∧ IsMaximalIn chains H)
  nsLeaf : History p F → Prop
  hns_leaf : ∀ H, nsLeaf H → H ∈ chains ∧ IsMaximalIn chains H
nodes.note: The summation object of the whole corpus: densities are assembled tree by tree, so every counting theorem below quantifies over these.

nodes.title: The fiber of a tree: which polynomials grow it
nodes.math: Fix a counting model $T$, a chart $\chi$ embedding the $n$ coefficients into the $m$-coordinate digit box, and a digit vector $x$. The tree $\mathrm{Tr}$ "fibers" $x$ when six clauses hold: (i) the chains of $\mathrm{Tr}$ are exactly the nonempty branch histories realized at $x$, pruned at the first halt; (ii) each leaf carries the correct verdict — its branch halted with an irreducible factor, or it is a marked non-split halt; (iii) the root payload equals the unramified part read from $x$; (iv) no non-leaf has halted; (v) the degrees $e\cdot f$ carried by all verdicts sum to $n$; (vi) the root branches correspond exactly to the repeated irreducible factors of the mod-$p$ reduction of $x$, with matching degrees. "$x$ is decided" means some verdict tree fibers $x$; the fiber $\{x : \mathrm{Tr}\text{ fibers }x\}$ is the set whose mass all the pricing theorems compute.
nodes.lean:
def VTree.fiberAt (Tr : VTree p F) (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (x : Box p m) : Prop :=
  (∀ H : History p F, H ∈ Tr.chains ↔ (H.nodes ≠ [] ∧ PrunedMem T H x)) ∧
  (∀ H ∈ Tr.chains, IsMaximalIn Tr.chains H →
    ((IrrHalts H ∧ ¬ Tr.nsLeaf H ∧ Tr.leafV H = some (irrVerdictOf H)) ∨
     (NsHalts T (some H) x ∧ ¬ IrrHalts H ∧ Tr.nsLeaf H ∧
       Tr.leafV H = some (nsVerdictOf H)))) ∧
  Tr.henV = henPayload χ x ∧
  (∀ H ∈ Tr.chains, ¬ IsMaximalIn Tr.chains H →
    ¬ IrrHalts H ∧ ¬ NsHalts T (some H) x) ∧
  ((Tr.typemult.map fun ef => ef.1 * ef.2).sum = n) ∧
  (Tr.heads.val.map Tr.trackDeg
    = ((UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizedFactors (redPoly χ x)).toFinset.filter
        (fun ψ => 2 ≤ Multiset.count ψ
          (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizedFactors (redPoly χ x)))).val.map
        (fun ψ => Multiset.count ψ
          (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizedFactors (redPoly χ x))
            * ψ.natDegree))

def Decided (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol) (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (x : Box p m) : Prop :=
  ∃ Tr : VTree p F, Tr.fiberAt T χ x
nodes.note: The graph-equality form of "the canonical tree of x is Tr"; its six clauses are what the uniqueness and mass theorems dissect.

nodes.title: Every decided polynomial has exactly one canonical tree
nodes.math: If $x$ is decided — some finite verdict tree fibers it — then there is a tree $\mathrm{Tr}$ fibering $x$, unique up to extensional equality (same chains, same root payload, same leaf verdicts and non-split marks). "The canonical tree of $x$" is therefore a well-defined map on the decided set, obtained with no choice principle beyond the deciding witness and no counting hypotheses at all.
nodes.lean:
theorem oneF (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol) (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (x : Box p m)
    (hx : Decided T χ x) :
    ∃ Tr : VTree p F, Tr.fiberAt T χ x ∧
      ∀ Tr' : VTree p F, Tr'.fiberAt T χ x → VTree.ext Tr Tr'
nodes.note: The ONE-F capstone: it makes the tree-indexed sums well-posed and is consumed by the class-tree partition and the dictionary sum.

nodes.title: Distinct trees have disjoint fibers
nodes.math: If two verdict trees both fiber the same digit vector $x$, they agree extensionally: equal chain sets, equal root payloads, and equal leaf verdicts and non-split marks on every chain. Consequently the fibers of extensionally distinct trees are disjoint — the tree fibers partition the decided set.
nodes.lean:
theorem tree_fiber_disjoint (Tr Tr' : VTree p F) (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (x : Box p m)
    (h : Tr.fiberAt T χ x) (h' : Tr'.fiberAt T χ x) :
    Tr.chains = Tr'.chains ∧ Tr.henV = Tr'.henV ∧
    ∀ H ∈ Tr.chains, Tr.leafV H = Tr'.leafV H ∧ (Tr.nsLeaf H ↔ Tr'.nsLeaf H)
nodes.note: The unconditional partition kernel: uniqueness is read off the fiber clauses alone, which is what makes the one-tree theorem choice-free.

nodes.title: The one-site mass step: passing a site costs an exact power of p
nodes.math: Let $H$ be a chain of the tree with ledgered site data (entrance event, state event, fresh coordinates, site exponent $e_H$). For every event $E$ that is a spectator of the site's fresh coordinates (membership in $E$ does not depend on them): $\#(\text{state}\cap E)\cdot p^{e_H} = \#(\text{entrance}\cap E)$. Passing a single tree site multiplies the conditional mass by exactly $p^{-e_H}$, uniformly in the spectator conditioning — the uniformity in $E$ is what lets the tree recursion condition on everything decided elsewhere in the tree.
nodes.lean:
theorem fiber_seg_step (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (CA : CellData p F n N m pol T) (Tr : VTree p F) (χ : Fin n → Fin m)
    (L : SiteLedger Tr T CA χ) (H : History p F) (hH : H ∈ Tr.chains)
    (E : Set (Box p m)) (hspec : SpectatorFor (L.freshCoords H) E) :
    Nat.card ↥(stateEvent T (some H) ∩ E) * p ^ L.siteExp H
      = Nat.card ↥(entEvent T χ (L.parentSt H) ∩ E)
nodes.note: The per-site kernel of the whole assembly, proved from a new spectator-relativized counting law; the site ledger it consumes bundles per-site laws asserted as data (their discharge belongs to the classifier corpora), so applying it requires such a ledger to be built.

nodes.title: The open multi-branch pricing law already follows from the ledger's assumed faces
nodes.math: At a multi-branch site, any site ledger discharging the presented faces (the exact per-site cell tie, freshness, spectator, and side-exponent laws) already satisfies the multi-branch pricing law at that site: $\#(\text{site cell event})\cdot p^{\sum_j e_j} = \#(\text{entrance event})$ over the per-side exponents $e_j$. So the pricing hypothesis that the tree-mass theorems carry explicitly is not an assumption beyond the ledger — its content sits inside the (still open) discharge of the ledger's own faces.
nodes.lean:
theorem presents_imply_jcMultiAt (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (CA : CellData p F n N m pol T) (Tr : VTree p F) (χ : Fin n → Fin m)
    (L : SiteLedger Tr T CA χ) (H : History p F) (hH : H ∈ Tr.chains)
    (h2 : 2 ≤ L.sides H) :
    JCmultiAt T CA χ (L.parentSt H) H.lastNode (L.splitAt H hH h2)
nodes.note: Added after an adversarial review found the tree-mass theorem advertised a pricing hypothesis its proof did not consume; the proofs were rewired to consume it and this lemma documents exactly where its strength actually lives.

nodes.title: The root clause: the tree fiber splits along root branches
nodes.math: Suppose the tree $\mathrm{Tr}$ is realizable and its fiber lies in the root cell $R_g=\{x:\bar f_x = g\}$ (digit vectors whose mod-$p$ reduction is $g$), with the chains of $\mathrm{Tr}$ split into $t$ root tracks (one per repeated factor of $g$). Then $\#\{x:\mathrm{Tr}\text{ fibers }x\}\cdot(\#R_g)^t\cdot p^n = p^m\cdot\prod_{i=1}^{t}\#(R_g\cap E_i)$, where $E_i$ is the event that track $i$'s subtree is realized as specified: conditionally on the root cell, the $t$ track events are independent and the fiber's mass is the product of the per-track masses.
nodes.lean:
theorem fiber_root_split (Tr : VTree p F) (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (trackOf : Node p F → Polynomial (ZMod p))
    (CA : CellAssign p F n N m pol T χ trackOf)
    (hχ : Function.Injective χ) (hrc : RootCellsOf T CA.toCellData χ)
    (hred : RedCellPartition T CA.toCellData χ trackOf)
    (hsib : SibCount T CA.toCellData χ) (hreal : Realizes T χ Tr)
    (g : Fin n → ZMod p) (htracks : RootSplitData Tr g)
    (hcr : ∀ i, ChildRoot none (htracks.headOf i))
    (hfib : ∀ x, Tr.fiberAt T χ x → x ∈ rootCell χ g) :
    Nat.card ↥{x | Tr.fiberAt T χ x}
        * (Nat.card ↥(rootCell χ g)) ^ htracks.t * p ^ n
      = p ^ m * ∏ i : Fin htracks.t,
          Nat.card ↥(rootCell χ g ∩ trackEvent Tr T htracks i (hcr i))

-- the single fenced admission inside the proof (the corpus's one assembly sorry):
have hD4R0K :
    (∀ y ∈ rootCell χ g, ∀ ν ν' : Node p F, T.child none ν y →
        T.child none ν' y → trackOf ν = trackOf ν' → ν = ν') ∧
    (∀ y ∈ rootCell χ g, ∀ ν : Node p F, T.child none ν y →
        2 ≤ Multiset.count (trackOf ν)
          (UniqueFactorizationMonoid.normalizedFactors (redPoly χ y))) := by
  sorry

nodes.note: Everything except the single fenced hD4R0K clause is machine-checked (roster completeness is a proved consequence of (U)+(R)); the sorry site records the exact countermodel shape it fences and a fence-rule check that no in-corpus witness can refute or discharge it — this is the one admission all downstream mass capstones inherit.

nodes.title: TREE-EXP: the tree fiber's mass is an exact power of p, charged site by site
nodes.math: $\#\{x:\mathrm{Tr}\text{ fibers }x\}\cdot p^{\,n+\sum_H e_H} = p^m$: the number of digit vectors growing the tree $\mathrm{Tr}$, times $p$ raised to ($n$ plus the sum of the ledger exponents $e_H$ over all sites of the tree), equals the full box $p^m$. Equivalently the tree fiber has mass exactly $p^{-(n+\sum_H e_H)}$, every site charged exactly once, the root included — the law making each factorization type's mass an explicit power of $p$ read off its tree.
nodes.lean:
theorem treeExp (Tr : VTree p F) (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (trackOf : Node p F → Polynomial (ZMod p))
    (CA : CellAssign p F n N m pol T χ trackOf)
    (hχ : Function.Injective χ) (hrc : RootCellsOf T CA.toCellData χ)
    (hred : RedCellPartition T CA.toCellData χ trackOf)
    (hsib : SibCount T CA.toCellData χ) (hreal : Realizes T χ Tr)
    (L : SiteLedger Tr T CA.toCellData χ)
    (sc : TreeScaffold Tr T CA.toCellData χ L trackOf)
    (hjcm : ∀ H (hH : H ∈ multiSites Tr T CA.toCellData χ L) (h2 : 2 ≤ L.sides H),
      JCmultiAt T CA.toCellData χ (L.parentSt H) H.lastNode (L.splitAt H hH.1 h2))
    (hsibT : ∀ H (hH : H ∈ Tr.chains),
      2 ≤ (CA.toCellData.branchSetOf (L.cellAt H)).card →
      SibCountAt T CA.toCellData χ (L.parentSt H) H.lastNode (L.cellAt H)
        (sc.splitFrame H hH).S)
    (hdet : ∀ H ∈ Tr.chains, ¬ Tr.nsLeaf H) :
    Nat.card ↥{x | Tr.fiberAt T χ x}
        * p ^ (n + ∑ H ∈ Tr.hfin.toFinset, L.siteExp H)
      = p ^ m

nodes.title: TREE-N: the mass identity at the standard working level
nodes.math: At the standard working level $m = nN$: $\#\{x:\mathrm{Tr}\text{ fibers }x\}\cdot p^{A(\mathrm{Tr})} = p^{nN}$, where $A(\mathrm{Tr}) = n + \sum_H e_H$ is the tree's total ledger exponent. The density of the tree's factorization type at level $N$ is thus $p^{-A(\mathrm{Tr})}$; as proved the identity is threshold-free (an unused threshold premise was deleted at review).

theorem treeN (Tr : VTree p F) (T : TreeModel p F n N (n * N) pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin (n * N)) (trackOf : Node p F → Polynomial (ZMod p))
    (CA : CellAssign p F n N (n * N) pol T χ trackOf)
    (hχ : Function.Injective χ) (hrc : RootCellsOf T CA.toCellData χ)
    (hred : RedCellPartition T CA.toCellData χ trackOf)
    (hreal : Realizes T χ Tr)
    (hdet : ∀ H ∈ Tr.chains, ¬ Tr.nsLeaf H)
    (hsib : SibCount T CA.toCellData χ)
    (L : SiteLedger Tr T CA.toCellData χ)
    (sc : TreeScaffold Tr T CA.toCellData χ L trackOf)
    (hjcm : ∀ H (hH : H ∈ multiSites Tr T CA.toCellData χ L) (h2 : 2 ≤ L.sides H),
      JCmultiAt T CA.toCellData χ (L.parentSt H) H.lastNode (L.splitAt H hH.1 h2))
    (hsibT : ∀ H (hH : H ∈ Tr.chains),

nodes.title: The dictionary sum: class masses equal chain-count weighted tree masses
nodes.math: On the decided set, for a fixed branch shape $\hat P$: $\sum_{\eta}\#\{x \in \text{fiber}(\eta) : \eta\text{ pre-halts},\ x\text{ decided}\} \;=\; \sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}} c_{\hat P}(T)\,\#\{x : T\text{ fibers }x\}$, where $\eta$ ranges over the enumerated branch classes of shape $\hat P$, $\mathcal{T}$ is a finite menu of trees partitioning the decided set, and $c_{\hat P}(T)$ counts the chains of $T$ of shape $\hat P$. This dictionary converts the per-class masses of the density tables into per-tree masses.
nodes.lean:
theorem preHalt_dict_sum {P : Shape n} (S : Presented p F n N m pol P)
    (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol) (χ : Fin n → Fin m)
    (hcyl : D4R_CYL S T) (hwd : ClassFiberWelldef p F n N m pol P)
    (heta : EtaLoc T P) (hib : InBoxOfMem T n)
    (hph : PreHaltClassData (P := P) pol)
    (𝒯 : Finset (VTree p F))
    (hsep : ∀ Tr ∈ 𝒯, ∀ H H', H ∈ VTree.chains Tr → H' ∈ VTree.chains Tr →
      H ∈ PrefSet n pol P → H' ∈ PrefSet n pol P →
      (∃ i : PrefIdx n pol P, SameClass i H ∧ SameClass i H') → H = H')
    (hpart : PartitionsDecided 𝒯 T χ) :
    ∑ᶠ i : PrefIdx n pol P,
        Nat.card ↥{x | x ∈ S.fiber i ∧ PreHalt (reprOf i) ∧ Decided T χ x}
      = ∑ Tr ∈ 𝒯, Tr.chainCount n P * Nat.card ↥{x | Tr.fiberAt T χ x}

nodes.title: Pruned membership equals pre-halting for realized branches
nodes.math: For a nonempty branch history $H$ realized at $x$: $H$ survives pruning at $x$ if and only if no proper nonempty prefix of $H$ has halted. The chains of the canonical tree are therefore exactly the realized histories all of whose ancestors are still running — pruning is a purely combinatorial condition on the history.

nodes.title: Every decided polynomial's tree is realized by a class-labelled tree

  rel2_c : Prop
  rel2_d : Prop
  rel2_e : Prop

def rs1GivenOfMovesT (T : TreeModel p F n N m pol)
    (χ : Fin n → Fin m) (trackOf : Node p F → Polynomial (ZMod p))
    (CA : CellAssign p F n N m pol T χ trackOf)
    {N₀ : ℕ} (Tat : ∀ N', N₀ ≤ N' → TreeModel p F n N' (n * N') pol)
    (χat : ∀ N', Fin n → Fin (n * N'))
    (CAat : ∀ N' h,
      CellAssign p F n N' (n * N') pol (Tat N' h) (χat N') trackOf)
    (rel2_a rel2_b rel2_c rel2_d rel2_e : Prop) : RS1GivenPackage :=
  { tree_exp_fin := TreeExpFin T χ trackOf CA,
    tree_exp_ns := TreeExpNs (n := n) pol,
    tree_n := TreeNStmt (n := n) pol ∧ TreeNStableStmt (n := n) pol,
    one_f := OneFStmt T χ,
    sib := SibCount T CA.toCellData χ,
    tb_cap := TBCapPinned (n := n) pol m ∧ NsAmendedPair (n := n) pol,
    vp := VPPinned pol Tat χat trackOf CAat,
    pci := PCI T CA.toCellData χ,
    rel2_a := rel2_a, rel2_b := rel2_b, rel2_c := rel2_c,
    rel2_d := rel2_d, rel2_e := rel2_e }

def RS1GivenHolds (Pi' : RS1GivenPackage) : Prop :=
  Pi'.tree_exp_fin ∧ Pi'.tree_exp_ns ∧ Pi'.tree_n ∧ Pi'.one_f ∧ Pi'.sib ∧
  Pi'.tb_cap ∧ Pi'.vp ∧ Pi'.pci ∧
  Pi'.rel2_a ∧ Pi'.rel2_b ∧ Pi'.rel2_c ∧ Pi'.rel2_d ∧ Pi'.rel2_e
nodes.note: The single interface node other corpora import; a repeat review finding forced the tree-count leg to carry the open stability closure alongside the proved mass identity so the advertised package matches exactly what is and is not proved.

role: MovesV formalizes the value-table layer of the proof: it builds the measured transition system whose states are the classifier's branch cells (skeleton × digit cell) and attaches to every move the fixed symbolic value tables. Its capstone proves the twenty-clause measured-transition-system theorem (called CTS-M) FROM a substantial ledger of named hypotheses — table data, burden laws, three total-mass legs, and several open rows — concluding that at every admissible prime power the realized masses of the factorization process agree with evaluations of fixed rational tables: cell masses at an active state sum to exactly 1, entrance masses are geometric-series rationals, realized chain counts equal path-product polynomials, and the composition laws hold. All analytic content rides on a typed summability package supplied as hypotheses, and the height-domain factorization kernel of clause (v) (called HMC) is stated but never proved — every consumer takes it as an explicit antecedent. The corpus also keeps its refutation record in compiled form: three machine-checked countermodels that refuted the originally drafted species-word, height-writing, and template-totality statements (each replaced by a scoped-true repair), plus four named open duties fenced as the only remaining unproved goals.
oneLiner: The measured transition system: value tables, masses, theorem CTS-M

nodes.title: The measured transition-system theorem: all twenty clauses, given the hypothesis ledger
nodes.math: Fix a degree $n$ and a ledger $L$ packaging the transition system: the symbolic table family, the step system, its measured realization at prime-power evaluation points $q_0$ (the 'pool points'), the marked-event carriers, the analytic summability package, and the named burden laws (the polynomial value law, mark-fiber and domain ties, realization completeness, entrance count and uniformity). Assume the three total-mass legs (countable additivity, no mass at infinite height, fixed-height exactness), that every continuing marked cell carries mark weight $\geq 1$, the order-0 perimeter certificates on entrance domains, the composite product law, cross-level entrance-mass stability, and the solve sentence. Then all twenty ledgered clauses of Theorem CTS-M hold, among them: the state partition at each $q_0$ is finite with unique cell indices; every table value is the $q_0$-evaluation of a fixed polynomial, and the realized linked count $T_\gamma(x,h)$ equals the path-product polynomial on domain heights; no mass enters states inactive at $q_0$; entrance masses aggregate exactly and each is a rational geometric series in $q_0$; the cell masses at any active state sum to exactly $1$ (PART-1) and marked $+$ terminal $= 1 +$ surplus (PART-2; the surplus is the overcount $\sum(\text{mark weight}-1)\times\text{cell mass}$ from cells carrying more than one eligible mark); row values are independent of the history; events of distinct marks are disjoint; and the composition laws COMP-h/COMP-$\Sigma$/COMP-AGG hold, the latter two conditionally on the open factorization kernel.
nodes.lean:
theorem ctsM {n : ℕ} (L : CtsmLedger n)
    (hb : P1CtblAdd L.V L.X.w) (hc : P1NullRem L.V L.X.w)
    (hd : P1FixedHeightExact L.V L.X.w)
    (hmark : ∀ (τ : L.S.Cell) (c : DCellAll L.V τ),
      c.isLeft → 1 ≤ markWeight L.V c)
    (hdom : EntDomOrder0 L.V)
    (hcomp : CompProduct L.cc L.X.w)
    (hstab : IotaLvlStable L.cc)
    (hsolve : SolveCond_Stmt L) :
    CtsmConclusions L
nodes.gate: hb/hc/hd (the three PART-1 legs: countable additivity of cell masses, null remainder at infinite height, fixed-height exactness); hmark (every continuing digit cell has mark weight ≥ 1, the mark weight being the number of eligible marks the cell carries — refutable without it, an all-zero-multiplicity model breaks PART-2); hdom (every entrance-domain point carries an order-0 perimeter certificate — the scoping predicate defined in its own node below); hcomp (the composite marked-event value factorizes — a named open row, deferred future work); hstab (entrance mass is stable across levels — a named open row, deferred future work); hsolve (the solve sentence: determinant hypothesis + Neumann convergence, given escape/agreement/kernel/count premises); plus the ledger's own burden fields (value law VAL(a), mark-fiber tie, domain tie, realization completeness, entrance count/uniformity, stage laws)
nodes.note: The corpus capstone: machine-checked as an implication (no axioms beyond Lean's core, no unproved goals in its own proof), with its conditionality fully displayed as the hypothesis ledger — three of the hypotheses (composite product, level stability, solve sentence) are named open rows, and the height-domain factorization kernel (HMC) is never proved anywhere, riding only as an antecedent inside individual clauses.

nodes.title: The hypothesis ledger: all data and burdens of the measured theorem in one record
nodes.math: The single record over which Theorem CTS-M quantifies: the symbolic table family, the step system, its measured realization, the marked-event carrier, the analytic summability package (weights, uniformity, listed semilinear domains, geometric-series laws), polynomial cell packs, the composite-value carrier and refined cells, and the named burden hypotheses — the domain tie, the mark-fiber tie, realization completeness (the marking map onto chains is surjective), the supply pack, the polynomial value law, entrance count, entrance uniformity, affine entrance exponents — together with the seam-side data consumed from the solver corpus (table shape, measured side, rational burdens, kernel hypotheses, species stage data, stage laws).
nodes.lean:
structure CtsmLedger (n : ℕ) where
  C : CtsFamily n
  S : StepSys n
  V : CtsMeasured n C S
  TE : TmplEvents n S
  X : XHD n S TE V
  cp : CellPolyPack n C S V
  cc : CompCarrier V TE
  J : JCells n C S V
  hTie : MDomTie V TE X.d
  hMark : MarkFiberTie TE
  hRC : RealizationComplete TE
  pack : C15Pack n S
  hVA : ValA n C S V
  hEC : EntCount V
  hEU : EntU V
  hAff : AffEnt n
  T : MovesS.TableShape n
  M : MovesS.MeasuredSide T
  RB : MovesS.RatBurdens T M
  hK : ∀ e, e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n → MovesS.KmatHyp T e
  scs : MovesS.SCSData T
  stage_laws : StageLawBurden n T scs
nodes.note: The interface other corpora instantiate: proving the measured theorem for a concrete classifier engine amounts to building one such ledger, and its typed fields are exactly the conditionality inventory of the capstone.

nodes.title: The open kernel: height-domain membership factorizes along composite templates
nodes.math: The height-domain membership factorization: for every one-step move $m$ followed by a template $\gamma$, a concatenated height point $(h_1, h_2)$ lies in the listed semilinear domain of the composite template if and only if $h_1$ lies in the domain of the single step and $h_2$ in the domain of $\gamma$. This is clause (v) of Theorem CTS-M — stated, numerically probed, and never proved in this corpus; a machine-checked toy shows it can genuinely fail, so every consumer (the composition clauses and the solve sentence) takes it as an explicit antecedent.
nodes.lean:
def HMC {n : ℕ} {S : StepSys n} (TE : TmplEvents n S) (D : XHDd n S TE) : Prop :=
  ∀ {α β} (m : S.Move α β) (γ : Template n S β) (h₁ : Hpt (S.dim m))
    (h₂ : Hpt γ.D),
    (D.dom (.cons m γ)).Mem (Hpt.append h₁ h₂) ↔
      (D.dom (.last m)).Mem h₁ ∧ (D.dom γ).Mem h₂
nodes.note: The hinge of clauses (v)/(vi): no unit proves it and none assumes it silently — a compiled census toy elsewhere in this corpus exhibits a system where it is false, so it can only ever ride as a hypothesis.

nodes.title: Entrance shapes: a height-retaining prefix plus selection data
nodes.math: An entrance shape $\varepsilon = (\hat P, (g_{\mathrm{sel}}, \mu_{\mathrm{sel}}), \sigma_{\mathrm{sel}})$: a nonempty shallow shape-prefix $\hat P$ that retains its per-read height data, whose last read carries the selected pair $(g, \mu)$ subject to the eligibility budget, together with a branch-selection record listing, for each branching read of $\hat P$, which item of its finite menu was chosen. Entrance masses and entrance counts (clause (iii) of the measured theorem) are refined by these shapes; their heights are ranged through finitely many height-forgetting templates and an instantiation bijection.
nodes.lean:
structure EntShapeV (n : ℕ) where
  Phat   : MovesD.Shape n
  hne    : (Phat : MovesD.ShapePrefix).reads ≠ []
  gsel   : ℕ
  musel  : ℕ
  hsel_g : 1 ≤ gsel
  hsel_μ : 1 ≤ musel
  hentry : ∀ R, (Phat : MovesD.ShapePrefix).reads.getLast? = some R →
    R.g = gsel ∧ R.μ = musel
  helig  : ∀ R, (Phat : MovesD.ShapePrefix).reads.getLast? = some R →
    EligPair R gsel musel
  selRec : List ℕ
  hlen   : selRec.length =
    ((Phat : MovesD.ShapePrefix).reads.filter
      (fun R => decide (IsBranchSlot R))).length
  hmenu  : ∀ i (hi : i < selRec.length),
    selRec.get ⟨i, hi⟩ < branchMenuCard n Phat i
nodes.note: The central new object of the note this corpus formalizes: entrances into a block are post-split objects, so at a branching each sibling carries its own shape and its own mark — the granularity every entrance-mass statement is keyed to.

nodes.title: The order-0 perimeter certificate for entrance-height points
nodes.math: The order-0 perimeter at one slot point: the entrance template's word is a single non-self-loop letter $s$, and every retained slot pair $(h, c)$ is anchor-admissible — $h \geq 1$, $\gcd(e_s, h) = 1$, and the Bezout anchor congruence $e_s \mid s_0 - \mathrm{bez}(e_s, h)\cdot \gamma$ holds. This is exactly the stratum on which the height-writing map is proved total; the unscoped totality is refuted by a compiled countermodel, so every downstream consumer threads this certificate as a hypothesis.
nodes.note: Born of a soundness emergency: an earlier sorried unscoped totality shim contradicted the compiled countermodel (the environment briefly derived False), so it was deleted and replaced by this named scoping predicate — analogous to the order-0 decided stratum to which the project's main capstone is scoped.

nodes.title: Sums over semilinear height sets split exactly into their disjoint linear components
nodes.math: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}^D$ be a semilinear set presented as a listed disjoint union of linear components (explicit bases and periods), let $f \geq 0$, and suppose $f$ sums to $v_j$ over the $j$-th component. Then $f$ sums over all of $S$ to $\sum_j v_j$ — exactly, with no overlap terms, because disjointness of the components is part of the presentation type.
nodes.lean:
theorem semilin_sum_exact {D : ℕ} (S : SemilinPart D) (f : Hpt D → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ h, 0 ≤ f h) (v : Fin S.comps.length → ℝ)
    (hv : ∀ j, HasSum (fun h : {h // (S.comps.get j).Mem h} => f h.1) (v j)) :
    HasSum (fun h : {h // S.Mem h} => f h.1) (∑ j, v j)
nodes.note: The summation kernel of the corpus: every aggregate identity (entrance aggregation, total mass one, the composition aggregate) reduces its geometric-series bookkeeping to this exact component-splitting lemma.

nodes.title: Total mass one: the cell masses at any active state sum to exactly 1
nodes.math: PART-1 of the measured theorem: at any pool point $q_0$ and any state active at $q_0$, for every admissible history, the fixed-height cell masses — summed over the full countable partition of all digit cells of the state and all height points of every dimension — form a convergent sum with value exactly $1$. Never a finite-pool identity: the proof squeezes the countable-additivity upper bound against the null-remainder lower bound.
nodes.lean:
theorem part1 {n : ℕ} {C : CtsFamily n} {S : StepSys n}
    {V : CtsMeasured n C S} (X : XHDw n S)
    (hb : P1CtblAdd V X) (hc : P1NullRem V X) (hd : P1FixedHeightExact V X)
    {τ : S.Cell} {q₀ : ℚ} (x : S.Hist q₀ τ) (hzc : S.zc x)
    (hq : q₀ ∈ V.Pools) (hact : V.activeState q₀ τ) :
    HasSum (fun ch : Σ c : DCellAll V τ, Σ D : ℕ, Hpt D =>
      μcellH V X x ch.1 ch.2) 1
nodes.gate: P1CtblAdd (the countable-partition sum exists and is at most 1), P1NullRem (no mass escapes to infinite height), P1FixedHeightExact (below-height blocks plus the height strip sum to exactly 1 at every truncation)
nodes.note: Proved (no axioms beyond Lean's core) from the three typed legs; the exactness equality in the third leg had been dropped in an early draft and was restored after a machine-checked countermodel (the identically-zero mass) refuted the weakened form.

nodes.title: The realized chain count equals a fixed polynomial evaluated at the prime power
nodes.math: VAL(b), the chain-count identification: for a template $\gamma$, any admissible history $x$ at a pool point $q_0$, and any height $h$ in the listed process-side domain, the realized linked count $T_\gamma(x, h)$ — the census of marked boxes at the defining level — equals the path-product polynomial of $\gamma$ evaluated at $q_0$. Proved given the polynomial value law VAL(a), the uniformity face, the domain tie, and realization completeness (every chain is realized by a mark: the marking map is surjective).
nodes.lean:
theorem val_b {n} {C : CtsFamily n} {S : StepSys n} {V : CtsMeasured n C S}
    {TE : TmplEvents n S} {D : XHDd n S TE}
    (hVA : ValA n C S V) (U : XHDu n S) (hTie : MDomTie V TE D)
    (hRC : RealizationComplete TE)
    {α} (γ : Template n S α) {q₀} (x : S.Hist q₀ α) (hzc : S.zc x)
    (hq : q₀ ∈ V.Pools) (h : Hpt γ.D) (hmem : (D.dom γ).Mem h) :
    (Tgam TE γ x h : ℚ) = (pathProdPoly V γ).eval q₀
nodes.gate: hVA (VAL(a): tables and cell sizes are polynomial), U (the same-pool uniformity face), hTie (the measured/process domain tie), hRC (realization completeness: the marking map onto chains is surjective — a compiled toy shows a positive table count with zero realized marks is otherwise consistent, so this premise has real content)
nodes.note: Re-keyed at review from the internal table-side count to the note's realized linked count: the exported clause of the capstone now goes through this theorem via the ledger's realization-completeness field.

nodes.title: Composition aggregate: total composite mass = entrance mass times step product
nodes.math: COMP-AGG: for a landing state $\beta_0$ and any template $\gamma$, at a pool point $q_0$, the aggregate of the composite marked-event masses over all entrance templates into $\beta_0$ and all components of their semilinear height domains equals (the total entrance mass into $\beta_0$) $\times$ (the stepwise product value of $\gamma$). Aggregation runs through the exact semilinear component sums, fiber constancy of the entrance data, and the law that non-landing templates carry zero entrance mass at every level.
nodes.lean:
theorem comp_agg {n : ℕ} {C : CtsFamily n} {S : StepSys n}
    {V : CtsMeasured n C S} {TE : TmplEvents n S} {D : XHDd n S TE}
    (cc : CompCarrier V TE) (X : XHDw n S)
    (Xs : XHDs n S X D) (XsEnt : XHDsEnt n S V)
    (hdom : EntDomOrder0 V) (hEU : EntU V)
    (β₀ : S.Cell) {α} (γ : Template n S α) {q₀ : ℚ} (hq : q₀ ∈ V.Pools) :
    aggMass cc Xs hdom β₀ γ q₀
      = iotaValV V XsEnt β₀ q₀ * stepProdVal V Xs γ q₀
nodes.gate: cc (the composite carrier's measure-definition laws, including the adjudicated lands law: non-landing templates carry zero entrance mass), Xs/XsEnt (the geometric-series summability faces), hdom (order-0 perimeter certificates on the entrance domain), hEU (entrance uniformity)
nodes.note: Proved with no axioms beyond Lean's core after the adjudicated lands law closed a genuine leakage (the drafted statement let non-landing templates contribute) and after the soundness repair re-keyed its height-writing dependence onto the order-0 perimeter.

nodes.title: The cubic root-pattern census over every finite field: five exact polynomial counts
nodes.math: For every finite field $F$ with $|F| = q$, the monic cubics $x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c$ over $F$, classified by root profile (number of distinct roots in $F$, maximal multiplicity), are counted by five fixed polynomials in $q$: three distinct roots, $\tfrac{1}{6}q(q-1)(q-2)$; exactly one simple root (irreducible quadratic cofactor), $\tfrac{1}{2}q^2(q-1)$; no roots (irreducible cubic), $\tfrac{1}{3}(q^3 - q)$; a double plus a simple root, $q(q-1)$; a triple root, $q$. These five classes are exhaustive and sum to $q^3$.
nodes.lean:
theorem rootTable_census_complete (F : Type*) [Field F] [Fintype F]
    [DecidableEq F] (q : ℚ) (hq : (Fintype.card F : ℚ) = q) :
    (classCount F (3, 1) : ℚ) = TH3.eval q ∧
    (classCount F (1, 1) : ℚ) = TH12.eval q ∧
    (classCount F (0, 0) : ℚ) = TH3c.eval q ∧
    (classCount F (2, 2) : ℚ) = T21.eval q ∧
    (classCount F (1, 3) : ℚ) = T3.eval q
nodes.note: The concrete degree-3 gate census behind the value tables, proved for every finite field (strictly stronger than the nine prime-power spot values checked by kernel computation); one conjunct's keying was repaired after a machine-checked refutation of the drafted version (the count at profile (2,2) over the 3-element field is 6, not 9).

nodes.title: The compiled table instance handed to the solver corpus, tied to the transition-system data
nodes.math: Given the table family of the transition system (and finiteness of the skeleton catalogue at degree $n$), there exists a table-shape instance — the interface object the solver corpus consumes — whose absorbing-label type, per-block state carriers (which carry the transition system's cell indices), outcome menus, degree bounds, and outcome member rosters are all tied to the transition-system data by an explicit pin bundle of equivalences and transported equalities, and all of whose outcome rosters are nonempty.
nodes.lean:
theorem tableShape_inst {n : ℕ} (C : CtsFamily n)
    (hfin : Finite (Skeleton n)) :
    ∃ T : MovesS.TableShape n,
      TablePins C T ∧
      ∀ e (τ : T.State e) (o : T.Out e τ), (T.odata e τ o).mem ≠ []
nodes.note: The seam to the solver corpus, strengthened at the final review round after it caught stubbed degree bounds and a state carrier missing the cell index; the finite-skeleton hypothesis is discharged outright at the build target n = 3.

nodes.title: Every coherent well-formed shape prefix is realized by a species word (order-0 scope)
nodes.math: On the scoped stratum, the letter alphabet realizes the read grammar: every well-formed shape prefix $P$ (a sequence of reads carrying degrees, heights, and window data) with $n \geq 2$, all continued reads of width $\geq 2$, and satisfying the cross-read species-coherence law — read $r{+}1$ is increment-species exactly when read $r$'s selected move is proper, $2 \leq e_r g_r$ — admits a fitting species word: a word of catalogue letters, one per read, each realizing its read's data, chained by the stage-successor relation. The proof is an explicit letter-by-letter construction.
nodes.lean:
theorem spWord_exists (n : ℕ) (P : MovesD.ShapePrefix)
    (hWF : MovesD.ShapeWF n P) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hcont : ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r + 1 < P.reads.length),
      2 ≤ (P.reads[r]'(Nat.lt_of_succ_lt hr)).μ)
    (hspec : SpeciesCoherent P) :
    ∃ ws, SpWordFits n P ws
nodes.gate: hn + hcont (the width-≥-2 continuation scope: the catalogue's terminal rule forbids selections at window 1), hspec (the cross-read species-coherence law, which the well-formedness predicate does not carry)
nodes.note: The scoped-true survivor of two rounds of compiled refutation: both extra hypotheses are exactly the laws whose absence the two countermodels exploit, and discharging species coherence from the classifier engine's output laws is a named open item of the next work phase.

nodes.title: Height-writing is total on the order-0, anchor-admissible stratum
nodes.math: The height-writing map — which reconstructs a concrete entrance shape from a height-forgetting entrance template and a numeric slot point — succeeds (returns a value) whenever the template's word is a single non-self-loop letter $s$ and every slot pair $(h, c)$ is anchor-admissible: $h \geq 1$, $\gcd(e_s, h) = 1$, and the Bezout anchor congruence $e_s \mid s_0 - \mathrm{bez}(e_s, h)\cdot\gamma$. The reconstruction exhibits an explicit fitting read with exact-division anchor, a well-formedness certificate, and the entrance ties.
nodes.lean:
theorem writeHeights_total {n : ℕ} (εT : EntTemplate n) (h : Hpt εT.entDim)
    (s : MovesSp.Species) (hword : εT.word = [s])
    (hsl : SelfLoopLetter n s = false)
    (hadm : ∀ pr ∈ εT.pairSlots h, AnchorAdmissible s pr) :
    (writeHeights? εT h).isSome
nodes.gate: hword + hsl (the order-0/self-loop-free stratum: the template word is one non-self-loop letter), hadm (anchor admissibility of every slot point — the semilinear conditions the entrance domain is required to own)
nodes.note: The proved half of the delete-and-scope repair: unrestricted totality is refuted by a compiled countermodel, so this scoped theorem, packaged as the order-0 perimeter certificate (the anchor-admissibility predicate defined above), is what every consumer up to the capstone actually threads.

nodes.title: Countermodel: unrestricted species-word existence is false
nodes.math: It is not true that every well-formed shape prefix admits a fitting species word. Compiled witness at $n = 3$: the two-read prefix [root read with $(e, g, \mu) = (1, 1, 1)$; recentering read inside its width-1 window] is machine-checked well-formed, yet the stage laws force the second letter's window to $1$, where the catalogue's terminal rule forbids the selection that the fit clauses demand — so no fitting word exists.
nodes.lean:
theorem spWord_exists_false :
    ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (P : MovesD.ShapePrefix), MovesD.ShapeWF n P →
        ∃ ws, SpWordFits n P ws
nodes.note: The first of the refutation records for the species-word family: it forced the width scoping of the existence theorem, and a second compiled witness (in the round-2 countermodel file) shows even the width-scoped form fails without the species-coherence law.

nodes.title: Countermodel: unrestricted height-writing totality is false
nodes.math: The height-writing map is not total: at the one-letter root template, the all-zero slot point already fails, because every read carries height $\geq 1$ by type; and the countermodel's record notes that positivity alone cannot repair it — a Bezout anchor congruence is needed at every letter with $e \geq 2$, so totality can only hold on a restricted semilinear domain (which became the order-0 perimeter).
nodes.lean: theorem writeHeights_total_false : ¬ (writeHeights? T0 h0).isSome
nodes.note: The countermodel that triggered the corpus's one soundness emergency: an unproved unscoped totality shim coexisted with this compiled negation (so the environment briefly derived False) and was deleted, with every consumer re-keyed onto the order-0 perimeter certificate — all now proved with no axioms beyond Lean's core.

nodes.title: Countermodel: not every entrance shape has a template
nodes.math: The sentence "every entrance shape yields a height-forgetting template" is false: the entrance shape built over the two-read witness prefix admits no fitting species word, so its species word is the junk empty word and the template extraction returns nothing. The scoped-true replacement holds under a named word-level scoping predicate (the species word must be a genuine fitting word).
nodes.lean:
theorem template_total_false :
    ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ) (ε : EntShapeV n), (ε.template?).isSome
nodes.note: Per the final review verdict the countermodel was compiled first and the drafted totality claim then deleted-and-scoped — the template-bearing consumers now demand that word-level scoping certificate instead of a totality that is simply false.

nodes.title: The shallow height-sum face of the per-shape interface: the one fenced open clause
nodes.math: For a full chain instance of the solver interface (MovesS), two clauses are asserted per shape: (i) the shallow-shape presentation evaluates to the shallow-shape value (this half holds by the chain's own fields), and (ii) the shallow-shape value is the height sum, over the shallow domain, of the shallow height weights — a convergent-sum identity over the per-shape layer. Clause (ii) is the corpus's one deliberately fenced open obligation (a recorded `sorry`).
nodes.note: Clause (i) is proved and clause (ii) is the one fenced unproved goal, counted as zero proved content while it stands; the fence record discloses that no compiled countermodel exists (the in-corpus witness satisfies it) but that an infinite-domain chain might break summability, so a domain-census guard adjudication is queued before any proof attempt.

nodes.title: Open duty: a table-and-measure witness, tied to the real data, for the solver's ledger interface
nodes.math: There exist a table shape $T$ and a measured side $M$ such that: $T$ is tied to the transition-system family by the table-side pin bundle (label/state/outcome equivalences, real degree bounds, roster ties); $M$'s box cardinalities agree with the transition system's at every pool point (guarded on nonemptiness); and the solver corpus's ledger-IV interface is inhabited over $(T, M)$. Stated under the full hypothesis set the eventual witness will consume (the analytic package, polynomial packs, the value law, the factorization kernel, the three total-mass legs, entrance count and uniformity).
nodes.lean:
theorem ledgerIV_inst {n : ℕ} {C : CtsFamily n} {S : StepSys n}
    (V : CtsMeasured n C S) {TE : TmplEvents n S}
    (X : XHD n S TE V) (cp : CellPolyPack n C S V) (hVA : ValA n C S V)
    (hHMC : HMC TE X.d)
    (hb : P1CtblAdd V X.w) (hc : P1NullRem V X.w)
    (hd : P1FixedHeightExact V X.w)
    (hEC : EntCount V) (hEU : EntU V) :
    ∃ (T : MovesS.TableShape n) (M : MovesS.MeasuredSide T),
      TablePins C T ∧
      (∀ q₀ ∈ V.Pools, ∀ N : ℕ, Nonempty (V.Box q₀ N) →
        Fintype.card (M.Box q₀ N) = @Fintype.card _ (V.finB q₀ N)) ∧
      Nonempty (MovesS.LedgerIV T M)
nodes.note: A named open instantiation duty with an exact disclosed inventory of ties (what the tie bundle equates and what it deliberately does not): the existential form replaced an earlier vacuous escape clause, is the strongest sound statement (the universal form is provably false for adversarial measured sides), and the eventual witness is the compiled table instance plus a measured-side map of roughly 30 structure fields — a witness satisfying only the ties would not discharge the duty.

nodes.title: Open duty: a tied witness carrying the rational-burden polynomial data
nodes.math: There exist a table shape $T$ and a measured side $M$, tied to the transition-system data by the same pin bundle and guarded box-cardinality tie as the ledger duty, over which the solver corpus's rational-burden interface (the per-outcome count and geometric-series polynomial packs) is inhabited. The intended witness draws its polynomial data from the cell-size/count wiring and the per-entrance rational packs.
nodes.lean:
theorem ratBurdens_exists {n : ℕ} {C : CtsFamily n} {S : StepSys n}
    (V : CtsMeasured n C S) {TE : TmplEvents n S}
    (X : XHD n S TE V) (cp : CellPolyPack n C S V) (hVA : ValA n C S V)
    (hTie : MDomTie V TE X.d) (J : JCells n C S V) (hEU : EntU V)
    (hEC : EntCount V) (hA : AffEnt n) :
    ∃ (T : MovesS.TableShape n) (M : MovesS.MeasuredSide T),
      TablePins C T ∧
      (∀ q₀ ∈ V.Pools, ∀ N : ℕ, Nonempty (V.Box q₀ N) →
        Fintype.card (M.Box q₀ N) = @Fintype.card _ (V.finB q₀ N)) ∧
      Nonempty (MovesS.RatBurdens T M)
nodes.note: One of the four fenced unproved goals: same existential shape and disclosed tie inventory as the ledger duty; the accompanying roster-nonemptiness step is proved on file, and the recorded instantiation attempt names exactly which polynomial wiring the eventual witness must supply.

nodes.title: Open duty: a tied table carrying the species stage-field data
nodes.math: For the transition-system family (with finite skeleton catalogue) there exists a table shape, tied to it by the pin bundle, over which the solver corpus's species-stage data interface is inhabited — the stage fields (window, degree, budget, selection, cluster laws) wired from the species catalogue through the outcome rosters.
nodes.lean:
theorem scs_data_supply {n : ℕ} (C : CtsFamily n)
    (hfin : Finite (Skeleton n)) :
    ∃ T : MovesS.TableShape n,
      TablePins C T ∧
      Nonempty (MovesS.SCSData T)
nodes.note: The last of the four fenced unproved goals: the file records that a trivial stage supply passes the algebraic laws but fails the selected-member laws against the real rosters — disclosing that the duty needs the true species stage-field wiring, not a degenerate witness.

role: This corpus states and proves the project's capstone, Theorem U: for each splitting type σ of degree n there is one fixed rational function R_σ(q), with Σ_σ R_σ = 1 identically, such that at every prime p passing a typed regularity gate — wildly ramified primes included — the density of monic degree-n p-adic polynomials of factorization type σ exists and equals the literal value R_σ(p). The proof is a squeeze: an exact partition of the level-N coefficient box, a two-sided bracket whose upper leg comes from a positive tree-fiber series and whose lower leg comes from the checksum, and a vanishing undecided envelope. The theorem is machine-checked (no axioms beyond Lean's core, no unproved goals in its own proof) but conditional: its hypothesis surface is a fully typed ledger of named premises tied to the other corpora's real objects (the tree-count and solve interfaces, identifications of the abstract data with the real block system and the real tree corpus, a p-adic reading bridge), plus 13 explicitly untyped bare assumptions recorded as awaiting their carriers — and no per-prime instantiation bundle is constructed anywhere in the repository. MovesU consumes every other corpus and is imported by none — it is the top of the pipeline.
oneLiner: Assembles Theorem U: one rational function per splitting type, every prime

nodes.title: Theorem U: one rational function computes every p-adic splitting density (conditional capstone)
nodes.math: Fix $n \ge 2$. Assume the full typed hypothesis ledger: the carrier pack of the built resolvent-solve corpus, the upstream kernel carriers with their typed rows, the prime-uniform finiteness kernel, thirteen named auxiliary assumptions, and — for every prime $p$ — a per-prime instantiation bundle. Then there exists one family of rational functions $R_\sigma \in \mathbb{Q}(q)$, indexed by the splitting types $\sigma$ of degree $n$ and identified with the solver's own output family, with $\sum_\sigma R_\sigma = 1$ identically in $q$, such that at every prime $p$ passing the regularity gate (REG-$p$): (U-n) for all $\sigma$ and all levels $N$, $(R_\sigma(p) - \mathrm{env}(N))\,p^{nN} \le \#\{\text{level-}N\text{ classes decided }\sigma\} \le R_\sigma(p)\,p^{nN}$, where $\mathrm{env}(N)$ is the undecided fraction; (i) the decided density $\#\{\text{decided }\sigma\}/p^{nN}$ converges to $R_\sigma(p)$; (ii) the true-factorization-type density converges to the same limit; (ii-$\mathbb{Z}_p$) the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-read density — the fraction of level-$N$ classes all of whose monic degree-$n$ lifts to $\mathbb{Z}_p$ factor over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ with shape $\sigma$, each pair read as (ramification index, residue degree) of the factor — converges to the same limit; and (iii) $\mathrm{env}(N) \to 0$. At a prime failing the gate, nothing is asserted.
nodes.lean:
theorem theoremU (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (C : UCarriers n) (KC : KernelCarriers n C)
    (K7 : Cl7Kernel n KC) (S : SolveData n)
    (KT : UpstreamTyped n KC)
    (rel1 rel2a rel2b rel2d rel2e rel3 : Prop)
    (rs0Lump trackRule dnLattice : Prop)
    (m1m5Echo x1aDict m4bConst jcInvHist : Prop)
    (hrel1 : rel1) (hrel2a : rel2a) (hrel2b : rel2b) (hrel2d : rel2d)
    (hrel2e : rel2e) (hrel3 : rel3)
    (hrs0 : rs0Lump) (htrk : trackRule) (hdn : dnLattice)
    (hm15 : m1m5Echo) (hx1a : x1aDict) (hm4b : m4bConst) (hjc : jcInvHist)
    (inst : ∀ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), UInstance n C KC K7 S p hp) :
    ∃ R : SplittingType n → RatFunc ℚ,
      R = S.R ∧
      (∑ σ, R σ = 1) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), RegP (inst p hp).D →
        (∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ),
          (evalℝ ⟨R⟩ σ p - (inst p hp).X.env N) * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N)
              ≤ ((inst p hp).X.decided σ N : ℝ) ∧
            ((inst p hp).X.decided σ N : ℝ)
              ≤ evalℝ ⟨R⟩ σ p * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N))
        ∧ (∀ σ : SplittingType n,
          Tendsto ((inst p hp).X.dmass σ) atTop (𝓝 (evalℝ ⟨R⟩ σ p)))
        ∧ (∀ σ : SplittingType n,
          Tendsto ((inst p hp).X.trueDmass σ) atTop (𝓝 (evalℝ ⟨R⟩ σ p)))
        ∧ (∀ σ : SplittingType n,
          Tendsto (@ZpBridge.zpDmass n p ⟨hp⟩ _ (inst p hp).bridge σ) atTop
            (𝓝 (evalℝ ⟨R⟩ σ p)))
        ∧ Tendsto (inst p hp).X.env atTop (𝓝 0)
nodes.gate: C (the built resolvent-solve corpus's carrier pack: table, measured side, rational burdens, degree conservation, K-matrix hypotheses, shape family, measured chain); KC (the built MovesX/MovesV/MovesRBase carrier corpora); KT (five numbered upstream counting laws of the source note — its rows CL-2/CL-3/CL-8/CL-13/CL-15 — stated at those carriers); K7 (the prime-uniform finiteness kernel with its counting laws); rel1, rel2a, rel2b, rel2d, rel2e, rel3, rs0Lump, trackRule, dnLattice, m1m5Echo, x1aDict, m4bConst, jcInvHist (13 named bare assumptions — untyped and trivially instantiable per the adjudicated audit record: the vocabulary needed to type them is not yet built, so they impose no mathematical obligation yet); inst (for EVERY prime, a per-prime bundle: the ledger with its tree and solve seams, roster pin, tree pin plus sibling/junction counting rows, p-adic bridge with stated residue, and slice bound — constructed nowhere in the repository); per-prime RegP (the (REG-p) regularity gate, gating each prime's conclusion).
nodes.note: The capstone of the whole project — machine-checked with no unproved goals and no axioms beyond Lean's core (verified in the corpus record) — but conditional: no instance of the per-prime bundle exists in the repository, and its own docstring records that the 13 bare parameters await their carriers; the named premises ARE the measured distance to an unconditional theorem.

nodes.title: Splitting types of degree n
nodes.math: A splitting type of degree $n$ is a multiset of pairs $(e_i, f_i)$ with $e_i, f_i \ge 1$ and $\sum_i e_i f_i = n$ — the shape of a factorization of a degree-$n$ polynomial into irreducible factors with ramification indices $e_i$ and residue degrees $f_i$. A companion unit proves there are finitely many splitting types for each $n$.
nodes.note: The index of the entire theorem: densities, rational functions, and classifier verdicts are all keyed by these; finiteness (proved in U0b) is what makes the checksum sum well-defined.

nodes.title: The classifier interface: verdicts on coefficient boxes
nodes.math: The classifier at a prime $p$: for each level $N$, a verdict map assigning to every class of the level-$N$ box (the $n$ free coefficients of a monic degree-$n$ polynomial mod $p^N$, giving $p^{nN}$ classes) either a splitting type or 'undecided'; a true-type field on the same classes; a stability law — a verdict made at level $N$ persists at every higher level; and a declared digit-section convention. From the verdict map the corpus defines $\mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N)$, $\mathrm{undec}(N)$, the envelope $\mathrm{env}(N) = \mathrm{undec}(N)/p^{nN}$, and the decided and true-type densities.
nodes.lean:
structure ClassifierSpec (n p : ℕ) where
  canonical : ∀ N : ℕ, Box p n N → Option (SplittingType n)
  trueType : ∀ N : ℕ, Box p n N → Option (SplittingType n)
  canonical_stable : ∀ {N N'} (h : N ≤ N') (f : Box p n N') (σ : SplittingType n),
    canonical N (boxProj p n h f) = some σ → canonical N' f = some σ
  baseSection : BaseSection
nodes.note: The vocabulary every density statement is typed in; soundness of verdicts is deliberately NOT an interface axiom but a separately carried hypothesis (an audit-driven design choice), and the interface is later identified with the built tree corpus by the tree pin.

nodes.title: The regularity gate (REG-p)
nodes.math: (REG-$p$): for every value $q_0$ in the pool $Q(p) = \{p^\delta : \delta \in \text{depth set}\}$ and every block $e$ of the block system: (r1) the determinant $\det(I - K_e)$ is defined and nonzero at $q_0$; and (r2) every member of the displayed entry list $E(e)$ — the entries of $K_e$, the terminal and split vectors, the per-cell branching entries, the injection entries, the shallow-shape weights, and the $\beta$-legs at every depth — is defined at $q_0$ and its literal value equals the prescribed active value. This is exactly the note's (r1) ∧ (r2) schema; definedness and agreement of $R_\sigma$ itself are derived consequences, not extra conjuncts.
nodes.lean:
def RegP {p : ℕ} (D : RegData p) : Prop :=
  ∀ q₀ ∈ D.Pool, ∀ e : D.Block,
    (letI := D.instBi e; letI := D.instBd e;
     DefinedAt (Matrix.det (1 - D.K e)) (q₀ : ℚ) ∧
     (Matrix.det (1 - D.K e)).eval (RingHom.id ℚ) (q₀ : ℚ) ≠ 0) ∧
    ∀ g ∈ D.entryList e,
      DefinedAt g (q₀ : ℚ) ∧ g.eval (RingHom.id ℚ) (q₀ : ℚ) = D.act g q₀
nodes.note: The typed per-prime gate in the theorem's quantifier: the conclusion is asserted exactly at primes passing it and nothing is claimed otherwise — this is how one fixed rational function can cover wild primes without overclaiming.

nodes.title: The canonical-tree fiber series
nodes.math: For each splitting type $\sigma$: an index family of canonical trees, each carrying a mass $\mu(\mathrm{fiber}\,T) \in [0,\infty]$ and a decision threshold, together with the finite threshold-$\le N$ slices (characterized, not chosen). The full series $\sum_T \mu(\mathrm{fiber}\,T)$ exists unconditionally as an extended real; every partial sum over a slice is dominated by it (the Tonelli unit).
nodes.lean:
structure FiberSeries (n p : ℕ) (X : ClassifierSpec n p) where
  Tree : SplittingType n → Type
  instTreeDeq : ∀ σ, DecidableEq (Tree σ)
  mass : ∀ σ, Tree σ → ℝ≥0∞
  thr : ∀ σ, Tree σ → ℕ
  thrSlice : ∀ σ : SplittingType n, ℕ → Finset (Tree σ)
  mem_slice_iff : ∀ σ N (T : Tree σ), T ∈ thrSlice σ N ↔ thr σ T ≤ N
  slice_exhausts : ∀ σ (T : Tree σ), T ∈ thrSlice σ (thr σ T)
nodes.note: The positive series whose threshold-N partial sums ARE the decided counts — the route to the upper bracket leg; its sum is later tied to the measured solver value by the solve seam.

nodes.title: The tree-count seam: exact fiber counts per canonical tree (named open premise)
nodes.math: The named open TREE-N premises: (a) every level-$N$ class decided as $\sigma$ is assigned a canonical tree of type $\sigma$; (b) the assigned tree has decision threshold $\le N$; and (c) the exact count tie — for each tree $T$ of threshold $\le N$, $\mu(\mathrm{fiber}\,T)\cdot p^{nN}$ equals the exact number of decided-$\sigma$ classes assigned $T$.
nodes.lean:
structure TreeSeam (n p : ℕ) (X : ClassifierSpec n p) (F : FiberSeries n p X) where
  treeOf : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ)
    (f : {f : Box p n N // X.canonical N f = some σ}), F.Tree σ
  thr_le : ∀ σ N f, F.thr σ (treeOf σ N f) ≤ N
  count_tie : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ) (T : F.Tree σ), F.thr σ T ≤ N →
    F.mass σ T * (p : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (n * N)
      = (Nat.card {f : {f : Box p n N // X.canonical N f = some σ} //
          treeOf σ N f = T} : ℝ≥0∞)
nodes.note: The distance to unconditionality on the tree side: the count tie is the open premise, with the built tree-expansion theorem of the MovesT corpus recorded as its named discharge candidate through the tree pin.

nodes.title: Decided counts are partial sums of the tree-fiber series
nodes.math: Given the tree seam: $\mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) = p^{nN} \sum_{T:\ \mathrm{thr}(T) \le N} \mu(\mathrm{fiber}\,T)$ — partition the decided-$\sigma$ classes by their assigned canonical tree and sum the exact per-tree count tie over the threshold-$\le N$ slice.
nodes.lean:
theorem TreeSeam.finiteness_stack {n p : ℕ} [NeZero p] {X : ClassifierSpec n p}
    {F : FiberSeries n p X} (seam : TreeSeam n p X F)
    (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ) :
    (X.decided σ N : ℝ≥0∞)
      = (p : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (n * N) * ∑ T ∈ F.thrSlice σ N, F.mass σ T
nodes.gate: seam — the tree seam: the canonical-tree assignment, its threshold bound, and the exact per-tree count tie (the open TREE-N premise, supplied per prime by the instantiation bundle).
nodes.note: Formerly an assumed ledger field; an independent review demanded it be derived from the seam's named premises — an audit-driven de-vacuification that shrank the trusted surface.

nodes.title: The exact box partition: decided plus undecided fills the box
nodes.math: For every level $N$: $\sum_\sigma \mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) + \mathrm{undec}(N) = p^{nN}$ — the level-$N$ box of monic coefficient classes partitions exactly into the decided-$\sigma$ classes and the undecided complement. Tag-free: a pure counting identity for any classifier.
nodes.lean:
theorem boxN {n p : ℕ} (X : ClassifierSpec n p) [NeZero p] (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ σ : SplittingType n, X.decided σ N) + X.undec N = p ^ (n * N)
nodes.note: The exact identity that lets the checksum convert per-type upper bounds at all types except σ into the lower bracket leg at σ.

nodes.title: The two-sided density bracket (U-n)
nodes.math: Given the tree seam, the solve seam, the roster pin, the checksum $\sum_\sigma R_\sigma = 1$ in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$, and the gate (REG-$p$) at a prime $p$: for every splitting type $\sigma$ and level $N$, $(R_\sigma(p) - \mathrm{env}(N))\, p^{nN} \le \mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) \le R_\sigma(p)\, p^{nN}$. Upper leg: the decided count is a partial sum of the positive tree series whose full sum is identified with $R_\sigma(p)$. Lower leg: the box partition plus the evaluated checksum turn the upper bounds at all $\tau \ne \sigma$ into the lower bound at $\sigma$.
nodes.lean:
variable {n p : ℕ} {C : UCarriers n} {X : ClassifierSpec n p} {F : FiberSeries n p X}
  {S : SolveData n} {D : RegData p}

theorem un_bracket (seam : TreeSeam n p X F) (ss : SolveSeam n p C F S)
    (P : RegPin C D) (hchk : ∑ σ, S.R σ = 1) (hreg : RegP D) (hp : p.Prime)
    (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ) :
    (evalℝ S σ p - X.env N) * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N) ≤ (X.decided σ N : ℝ) ∧
    (X.decided σ N : ℝ) ≤ evalℝ S σ p * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N)
nodes.gate: seam (tree seam: the exact per-tree fiber count tie — open premise); ss (solve seam: the rational family is the real solver output and the series sums to the measured value — open premise); P (roster pin identifying the regularity data with the real block system); hchk (the ℚ(q) checksum Σ_σ R_σ = 1); hreg (the (REG-p) gate); hp (p prime).
nodes.note: Assembles the upper-bound leg (SQ.2, via the fiber series) and the lower-bound arithmetic (SQ.3, via the box partition and checksum) into the exported bracket the capstone feeds to the squeeze.

nodes.title: The squeeze: a vanishing envelope forces the density limit
nodes.math: If $(r - \mathrm{env}(N))\,p^{nN} \le \mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) \le r\,p^{nN}$ for every level $N$, and $\mathrm{env}(N) \to 0$, then the density $\mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N)/p^{nN}$ converges and its limit is $r$.
nodes.lean:
theorem squeeze_limit {n p : ℕ} (X : ClassifierSpec n p) (hp : 1 < p) (r : ℝ)
    (σ : SplittingType n)
    (hbr : ∀ N, (r - X.env N) * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N) ≤ (X.decided σ N : ℝ) ∧
      (X.decided σ N : ℝ) ≤ r * (p : ℝ) ^ (n * N))
    (henv : Tendsto X.env atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    Tendsto (X.dmass σ) atTop (𝓝 r)
nodes.note: The analytic engine of clause (i): existence of the splitting density and its exact value both fall out of the bracket plus the vanishing undecided envelope — an unconditional real-analysis lemma.

nodes.title: Identification: decided density equals the true-type density
nodes.math: Suppose the classifier is verdict-sound: every class it decides as $\sigma$ truly has factorization type $\sigma$. If the decided density tends to $r$ and the undecided fraction tends to $0$, then the TRUE-type density also tends to $r$ — via the exact sandwich $\mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) \le \mathrm{true}_\sigma(N) \le \mathrm{decided}_\sigma(N) + \mathrm{undec}(N)$ (a true-$\sigma$ class is either decided $\sigma$ or undecided).
nodes.lean:
theorem identification {n p : ℕ} (X : ClassifierSpec n p) [NeZero p] (hp : 1 < p)
    (r : ℝ) (σ : SplittingType n) (hvs : VPSound X)
    (hd : Tendsto (X.dmass σ) atTop (𝓝 r))
    (henv : Tendsto X.env atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    Tendsto (X.trueDmass σ) atTop (𝓝 r)
nodes.gate: hvs — verdict soundness: every class decided σ truly has type σ (an open kernel with a citation duty, carried as a per-prime ledger row, never proved here); hd, henv — the decided-density limit and vanishing envelope (supplied by the squeeze and the ledger).
nodes.note: Upgrades the classifier-keyed limit to the true-factorization-type density — the step that makes Theorem U about actual splitting behavior rather than about one algorithm's labels.

nodes.title: The solve seam: the rational family is the solver's output (named open premise)
nodes.math: Two named open premises tying the abstract data to the built solver corpus: (a) for each $\sigma$, the tree-fiber series sums exactly to the measured chain value at $q = p$; and (b) under the determinant hypothesis, $R_\sigma$ IS the shallow resolvent solve — the fixed rational function output by the Cramer/adjugate route of the block system.
nodes.lean:
structure SolveSeam (n p : ℕ) (C : UCarriers n) {X : ClassifierSpec n p}
    (F : FiberSeries n p X) (S : SolveData n) : Prop where
  series_tie : ∀ σ : SplittingType n,
    F.seriesSum σ = ENNReal.ofReal (C.chain.Rval (vmap C.T σ) (p : ℚ))
  r_is_solve : ∀ (hdet : MovesS.DetHyp C.T C.RB C.hK) (σ : SplittingType n),
    S.R σ = MovesS.Rsh C.T C.MS C.RB C.hdc C.hK hdet C.Fam C.chain.WshP (vmap C.T σ)
nodes.note: Ties the existential witness of the capstone to the real solver output — killing the 'any rational function would do' bypass; the series tie is the named open premise matching Haar mass of canonical fibers to the measured chain.

nodes.title: The evaluated checksum: the densities sum to one at each regular prime
nodes.math: From the identity $\sum_\sigma R_\sigma = 1$ in $\mathbb{Q}(q)$, at any prime $p$ passing (REG-$p$): each $R_\sigma$ is defined at $q = p$ (definedness is itself derived through the pins), and the literal evaluations satisfy $\sum_\sigma R_\sigma(p) = 1$ in $\mathbb{R}$ — evaluation is a ring homomorphism on the subring of rational functions regular at $p$.
nodes.gate: ss (solve seam — open premise); P (roster pin); hreg (the (REG-p) gate); hchk (the ℚ(q) checksum Σ_σ R_σ = 1, a ledger row).
nodes.note: An audit-gap repair: the evaluated checksum used to be an assumed ledger field; it is now derived from the symbolic checksum plus derived definedness, shrinking the assumption surface.

nodes.title: The roster pin: abstract regularity data equals the real block system
nodes.math: Every piece of the abstract regularity data is equated to the real built block system: blocks biject with the working degrees $e \in [1,n]$ and per-block indices with the real table states; depth set, matrix entries $K_e$, injections $\iota_e$, per-cell branching entries $J$, and shape weights $W$ equal the real tables'; the active-value operation is the real post-cancellation evaluation semantics on its defined locus; the terminal and split vectors are the designated assembled solver entries (no instance-chosen type); and the $\beta$-leg labels BIJECT onto the real consumed roster — one label per continuing member of each split outcome of each state — each reading its true target (degree, state). As a corollary the gate's (r1) forces the real symbolic determinant hypothesis.
nodes.lean:
structure RegPin {n : ℕ} (C : UCarriers n) {p : ℕ} (D : RegData p) where
  blk : D.Block ≃ {e : ℕ // e ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n}
  st : ∀ b : D.Block, D.bidx b ≃ C.T.State (blk b).1
  depth_pin : D.depthSet
    = (MovesS.consumedDeltas C.T C.Fam).image (fun d : ℕ+ => (d : ℕ))
  K_pin : ∀ (b : D.Block) (i j : D.bidx b),
    D.K b i j
      = MovesS.Kmat C.T C.RB (blk b).1 (C.hK (blk b).1 (blk b).2) (st b i) (st b j)
  iota_pin : ∀ (b : D.Block) (i : D.bidx b),
    D.iota b i = C.RB.ι (blk b).1 (st b i)
  act_pin : ∀ (g : RatFunc ℚ) (q₀ : ℕ) (hok : g ∈ MovesS.OKat (q₀ : ℚ)),
    D.act g q₀ = MovesS.evalAt (q₀ : ℚ) ⟨g, hok⟩
  bterm_pin : ∀ (b : D.Block) (i : D.bidx b),
    D.bterm b i
      = ∑ σ' ∈ MovesS.verdictImage C.T (blk b).1 (st b i),
          MovesS.bTerm C.T C.RB (blk b).1 σ' (st b i)
  bsplit_pin : ∀ (hdet : MovesS.DetHyp C.T C.RB C.hK) (b : D.Block) (i : D.bidx b),
    D.bsplit b i
      = ∑ σ' ∈ C.chain.Sigmas,
          MovesS.bSplit C.T C.RB C.hdc (blk b).1 (blk b).2
            (MovesS.blockSolveLt C.RB C.hdc C.hK hdet (blk b).1) σ' (st b i)
  legSt : ∀ b : D.Block,
    D.legIdx b → (e' : {e' : ℕ // e' ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n}) × C.T.State e'.1
  legEquiv : ∀ b : D.Block, D.legIdx b ≃ LegRoster C.T (blk b).1
  legSt_pin : ∀ (b : D.Block) (l : D.legIdx b),
    legSt b l = legTarget C (blk b).1 (blk b).2 (legEquiv b l)
  betaLeg_pin : ∀ (hdet : MovesS.DetHyp C.T C.RB C.hK) (b : D.Block)
    (l : D.legIdx b) (δ : ℕ) (hδ : 0 < δ), δ ∈ D.depthSet →
    D.betaLeg b l δ
      = MovesS.powSubst ⟨δ, hδ⟩
          (∑ σ' ∈ C.chain.Sigmas,
            MovesS.blockSolve C.T C.RB C.hdc C.hK hdet
              (legSt b l).1.1 (legSt b l).1.2 (legSt b l).2 σ')
  blockDim_pin : ∀ b, D.blockDim b = Fintype.card (C.T.State (blk b).1)
  cell_pin : ∀ b, D.cellCount b
    = ∑ τ : C.T.State (blk b).1, ∑ o ∈ MovesS.splitOuts C.T (blk b).1 τ,
        (C.MS.cells (blk b).1 τ o).card
  Jcell_pin : ∀ b,
    (letI := D.instJ b; letI := Classical.decEq (RatFunc ℚ)

nodes.title: The tree pin: abstract trees are the built canonical-tree corpus
nodes.math: Identifies the abstract canonical trees with the built verified-tree corpus: an injective map sending each abstract $\sigma$-tree to a complete finite canonical tree with the same verdict type and the same threshold, realizable at every positive level at or above its threshold; conversely (completeness) every such realizable tree of type $\sigma$ and threshold $\le N$ is hit. The level-$N$ coefficient box is identified with the digit box via the base-$p$ digit expansion (no free relabeling), and the classifier verdict is pinned: 'decided $\sigma$ at level $N$' holds iff the class fibers at a carried $\sigma$-tree within threshold, and the seam's assigned tree is exactly that fibering tree. The coefficient chart is restricted to positive levels $N > 0$; the pin is silent at $N = 0$ (a single-class box).
nodes.lean:
structure TreePin (X : ClassifierSpec n p) (F : FiberSeries n p X)
    (seam : TreeSeam n p X F) where
  pol : MovesD.CanonPolicy p (ZMod p)
  Tm : ∀ N : ℕ, MovesD.TreeModel p (ZMod p) n N (n * N) pol
  chart : ∀ N : ℕ, 0 < N → Fin n → Fin (n * N)
  chart_inj : ∀ (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N), Function.Injective (chart N hN)
  boxeq : ∀ N : ℕ, Box p n N ≃ MovesD.Box p (n * N)
  boxeq_digits : ∀ (N : ℕ) (f : Box p n N) (i : Fin n),
    f i = ∑ k : Fin N,
      ((boxeq N f (digitIdx n N i k)).val : ZMod (p ^ N))
        * (p : ZMod (p ^ N)) ^ (k : ℕ)
  vt : ∀ σ : SplittingType n, F.Tree σ → MovesT.VTree p (ZMod p)
  vt_inj : ∀ σ, Function.Injective (vt σ)
  vt_typemult : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (T : F.Tree σ), (vt σ T).typemult = σ.1
  vt_thr : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (T : F.Tree σ), F.thr σ T = (vt σ T).thr n
  vt_real : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (T : F.Tree σ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N),
    F.thr σ T ≤ N → MovesT.Realizes (Tm N) (chart N hN) (vt σ T)
  vt_surj : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (V : MovesT.VTree p (ZMod p)) (N : ℕ)
    (hN : 0 < N), V.typemult = σ.1 → V.thr n ≤ N →
    MovesT.Realizes (Tm N) (chart N hN) V →
    ∃ T : F.Tree σ, vt σ T = V
  canonical_pin : ∀ (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (f : Box p n N) (σ : SplittingType n),
    X.canonical N f = some σ ↔
      ∃ T : F.Tree σ, F.thr σ T ≤ N ∧
        (vt σ T).fiberAt (Tm N) (chart N hN) (boxeq N f)
  treeOf_pin : ∀ (σ : SplittingType n) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (f : {f : Box p n N // X.canonical N f = some σ}),
    (vt σ (seam.treeOf σ N f)).fiberAt (Tm N) (chart N hN) (boxeq N f.1)

  fun i => digitIdx n N i ⟨0, hN⟩

nodes.title: The p-adic reading bridge: verdicts as true ramification and residue data (named open premise)
nodes.math: The named bridge from classifier verdicts to genuine $p$-adic factorizations: a reading assigning to each monic degree-$n$ polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ a multiset of pairs $(e,f)$, subject to: all entries have $e, f \ge 1$; the polynomial factors over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ into monic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-coefficient irreducible factors whose (ramification index, residue degree) pairs — the true valuation-theoretic invariants, read through the local ring obtained by adjoining a root — form exactly that multiset, with $e\cdot f$ equal to each factor's degree; every level-$N$ class has a monic lift; and the classifier's true type is $\sigma$ exactly when EVERY monic lift reads $\sigma$. Consequently the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-read density equals the true-type density.
nodes.lean:
variable (n p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]

structure ZpBridge (X : ClassifierSpec n p) where
  zfType : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → Multiset (ℕ × ℕ)
  zf_pos : ∀ g : Polynomial ℤ_[p], g.Monic → g.natDegree = n →
    ∀ ef ∈ zfType g, 1 ≤ ef.1 ∧ 1 ≤ ef.2
  zf_factor : ∀ g : Polynomial ℤ_[p], g.Monic → g.natDegree = n →
    ∃ factors : Multiset (Polynomial ℤ_[p]),
      g.map (PadicInt.Coe.ringHom)
          = (factors.map (Polynomial.map PadicInt.Coe.ringHom)).prod ∧
      (∀ h ∈ factors, h.Monic ∧ Irreducible (h.map PadicInt.Coe.ringHom)) ∧
      zfType g = factors.map (fun h => (MovesT.ramIdx h, MovesT.resDeg h)) ∧
      (zfType g).map (fun ef => ef.1 * ef.2) = factors.map Polynomial.natDegree
  lift_exists : ∀ (N : ℕ) (f : Box p n N), ∃ g : Polynomial ℤ_[p],
    g.Monic ∧ g.natDegree = n ∧ g.map (PadicInt.toZModPow N) = f.toPoly
  lift_true : ∀ (N : ℕ) (f : Box p n N) (σ : SplittingType n),
    X.trueType N f = some σ ↔ ZpReads n p zfType N f σ
nodes.note: Makes clause (ii-Z_p) about genuine ramification/residue invariants rather than bare (e,f) labels (an audit showed the earlier version could not distinguish (1,6) from (2,3)); its instantiation at the real classifier, plus the local-ring plumbing and two local-field laws, is the exactly stated open residue.
