role: The graded-ring bridge. The tower formalization (the Moves corpus) works with a formal interface for each stage of the Okutsu-Montes tower in which the graded residual is defined backwards from the stage's residual map; an adversarial audit objected that this makes the residual layer a 'definitional facade'. This corpus constructs the genuine objects — the associated graded ring of a stage's own valuation, its homogeneous localization, the degree-1 normalizing unit and the structure isomorphism — and proves the formal residual laws (multiplicativity, rank-1 normalization, and the facade identity itself) as theorems of that genuine structure. Where the planned statements turned out vacuous or unprovable as stated, it ships compiled refutation certificates instead of proofs, and one interface repair (the componentwise-addition field) was forced by a verifier countermodel and adopted, with the project lead's approval, before the domain criterion could be proved.
oneLiner: The genuine graded ring behind stage residuals; the facade identity proved conditionally

nodes.title: Side valuations and the associated graded ring of the p-adic polynomial ring
nodes.math: A *side valuation* on $A=\mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ is a map $w\colon A\to\mathbb{Z}\cup\{\infty\}$ with $w(0)=\infty$ and $w(f)<\infty$ for $f\neq 0$, $w(-f)=w(f)$, the ultrametric law $\min(w(f),w(g))\le w(f+g)$, submultiplicativity $w(f)+w(g)\le w(fg)$, $w(cf)\ge w(f)$ for scalars $c\in\mathbb{Z}_p$, and $w(1)=0$. From it the file builds the filtration $A_{\ge\gamma}=\{f: w(f)\ge\gamma\}\supseteq A_{>\gamma}$, the graded pieces $\mathrm{gr}_\gamma=A_{\ge\gamma}/A_{>\gamma}$, the associated graded group $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)=\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\mathbb{Z}}\mathrm{gr}_\gamma$, the piece products $\mathrm{gr}_\gamma\times\mathrm{gr}_\delta\to\mathrm{gr}_{\gamma+\delta}$ induced from multiplication in $A$ (well-defined by submultiplicativity), and the initial-form map $f\mapsto[f]\in\mathrm{gr}_{w(f)}$. The valuation of any stage of the Okutsu-Montes tower is such a bundle (a stage's $w$ in fact satisfies the product law with equality, $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$; the bundle demands only the inequality).
nodes.lean:
structure SideVal (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] where
  w : Polynomial ℤ_[p] → WithTop ℤ
  w_zero : w 0 = ⊤
  w_ne_top : ∀ f, f ≠ 0 → w f ≠ ⊤
  w_neg : ∀ f, w (-f) = w f
  w_add : ∀ f g, min (w f) (w g) ≤ w (f + g)
  w_smul : ∀ (c : ℤ_[p]) f, w f ≤ w (Polynomial.C c * f)
  w_mul : ∀ f g, w f + w g ≤ w (f * g)
  w_one : w 1 = 0
nodes.note: The ground object of the whole bridge: the graded ring is built from the stage's own valuation, not from its residual map — the exact point of the facade audit.

nodes.title: What it means to put the genuine graded ring structure on the associated graded
nodes.math: A graded ring structure on $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ is a commutative ring structure whose addition is the componentwise direct-sum addition, whose product restricts on homogeneous elements to the piece product induced from $A$, whose unit is the initial form $[1]$, for which the initial form is multiplicative — $[fg]=[f]\,[g]$ for $f,g\neq 0$ (equivalently: the submultiplicative inequality holds with equality, i.e. $w$ is a genuine valuation, as every stage valuation is) — and which obeys the tie law: if $w(f)<w(g)$ then $[f+g]=[f]$ — the summand of strictly lower weight determines the initial form of the sum (here the graded "degree" of a class is its weight $w$, not the polynomial degree).
nodes.lean:
structure GradedRingStr {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (S : SideVal p) where
  ring : CommRing S.Gr
  add_def : ∀ (x y : S.Gr) (γ : ℤ), (letI := ring; x + y) γ = x γ + y γ
  mul_of : letI := ring; ∀ (γ δ : ℤ) (x : S.grPiece γ) (y : S.grPiece δ),
      DirectSum.of _ γ x * DirectSum.of _ δ y = DirectSum.of _ (γ + δ) (S.pmul γ δ x y)
  one_def : letI := ring; (1 : S.Gr) = S.initialForm 1
  if_mul : letI := ring; ∀ f g : Polynomial ℤ_[p], f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 →
      S.initialForm (f * g) = S.initialForm f * S.initialForm g
  if_add_lt : ∀ f g : Polynomial ℤ_[p], f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → f + g ≠ 0 →
      S.deg f < S.deg g → S.initialForm (f + g) = S.initialForm f
nodes.note: The componentwise-addition field was added (adopted 2026-07-28 with the project lead's approval) only after a verifier countermodel showed the original four-field version admitted pathological models — see the domain-criterion refutation record below.

nodes.title: The genuine graded model of a tower stage
nodes.math: For a stage $\sigma$ of the Okutsu-Montes tower (with valuation $w_\sigma$, key polynomial $\Phi$, residue field $K$, and residual map $R$ into Laurent polynomials over $K$), a genuine model consists of: a side valuation agreeing with $w_\sigma$ on nonzero polynomials; a genuine graded ring structure on $\mathrm{gr}_{w_\sigma}(A)$; the localization $L$ of the graded ring at the multiplicative set generated by the initial forms of $\sigma$'s representatives and its key; a distinguished unit $T\in L^\times$; a ring isomorphism $\Theta\colon L\cong L_0[T^{\pm1}]$ with $L_0=K[z^{\pm1}]$ sending $T$ to the outer Laurent variable; and the discharge identity $\Theta(\iota[f]) = C(R(f))\cdot T^{\,w_\sigma(f)}$ for all $f\neq 0$ — the stage's residual data is computed by the genuine initial form, never read backwards.
nodes.lean:
structure GenuineStageModel (σ : Stage p F) where
  S : SideVal p
  hSw : ∀ f, f ≠ 0 → S.w f = (σ.w f : WithTop ℤ)
  Rg : GradedRingStr S
  homMon : letI := Rg.ring; Submonoid S.Gr
  homMon_gen : letI := Rg.ring;
      homMon = Submonoid.closure
        ((fun ũ => S.initialForm ũ) '' {ũ | ũ ∈ σ.reps} ∪ {S.initialForm σ.Φ})
  Lo : Type
  Loring : CommRing Lo
  alg : letI := Rg.ring; Algebra S.Gr Lo
  isLoc : letI := Rg.ring; letI := alg; IsLocalization homMon Lo
  Tunit : letI := Loring; Loˣ
  Θ : letI := Loring; Lo ≃+* LExt ↥σ.K
  hT : letI := Loring; Θ (Tunit : Lo) = (LeanUrat.Moves.locT ↥σ.K : LeanUrat.Moves.LTwo ↥σ.K)
  discharge : letI := Rg.ring; letI := alg; ∀ f : Polynomial ℤ_[p], f ≠ 0 →
      Θ (algebraMap S.Gr Lo (S.initialForm f)) = σ.grRes f
nodes.note: Conditionality: the identification $L_0\cong K[z^{\pm1}]$ — the last standing fiat — is not even a dischargeable hypothesis: it is hard-coded into the codomain type of the isomorphism $\Theta$ (a silent codomain choice, per the corpus's own audit record), and NO inhabitant of this bundle is constructed in the corpus — the planned base-stage inhabitation was refuted as stated (see the vacuity certificates).

nodes.title: The graded product of classes is the class of the product
nodes.math: For $a\in A_{\ge\gamma}$ and $b\in A_{\ge\delta}$: $[a]\cdot[b]=[ab]$ in $\mathrm{gr}_{\gamma+\delta}$ — the piece multiplication is literally the one induced from multiplication in $A$ through the two quotients (it holds by definitional unfolding).
nodes.lean: theorem L0_pmul_mk (S : SideVal p) (γ δ : ℤ) (a : S.ge γ) (b : S.ge δ) : S.pmul γ δ (Submodule.Quotient.mk a) (Submodule.Quotient.mk b) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (S.mulToGe γ δ a b)
nodes.note: Machine-checked certificate that the graded product is induced from the ambient ring, not read off the residual map — the exact point the facade audit demanded.

nodes.title: The initial form of a nonzero polynomial is nonzero
nodes.math: If $f\neq 0$ then $[f]\in\mathrm{gr}_{w(f)}$ is nonzero: the class of $f$ in its own degree cannot vanish, since $w(f)$ equals that degree exactly rather than exceeding it.
nodes.lean: theorem L0_initialForm_ne_zero (S : SideVal p) {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} (hf : f ≠ 0) : S.initialForm f ≠ 0
nodes.note: Non-vacuity of the graded pieces; makes the domain criterion and everything downstream non-trivial.

nodes.title: The genuine graded ring exists whenever the weight is a valuation
nodes.math: If $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$ for all nonzero $f,g$ (i.e. $w$ is a genuine valuation, not merely submultiplicative), then $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ carries a graded commutative ring structure in the above sense: the proof assembles the graded monoid on the direct sum from the piece products and derives associativity, commutativity, the unit law, multiplicativity of the initial form, and the tie law from the corresponding facts in $A$.
nodes.lean: theorem L1_gradedRingStr_exists (S : SideVal p) (hval : ∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → S.w (f * g) = S.w f + S.w g) : Nonempty (GradedRingStr S)
nodes.note: The construction capstone: inhabits the graded-ring bundle non-vacuously (componentwise addition holds definitionally for the direct-sum ring), discharging the facade objection at its root; stage valuations satisfy the hypothesis by their exact product law $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$. Supersedes an earlier draft file of the same name (which retains one unproved goal).

nodes.title: The associated graded is a domain exactly when the weight is a valuation
nodes.math: For any graded ring structure on $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$: $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ is an integral domain $\iff$ $w(fg)=w(f)+w(g)$ for all nonzero $f,g$. Forward: multiplicativity of the initial form plus injectivity of degree placement force additivity of $w$ — in fact without the domain hypothesis. Backward: the graded leading-term argument — the top-degree component of a product of nonzero elements is the piece product of their top classes, nonzero when $w$ is additive.
nodes.lean: theorem L1_gr_domain_iff_val (S : SideVal p) (Rg : GradedRingStr S) : (letI := Rg.ring; IsDomain S.Gr) ↔ (∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → S.w (f * g) = S.w f + S.w g)
nodes.note: The domain/valuation equivalence of the design (D.1(c)); its backward direction became provable only after the adopted componentwise-addition repair — see the refutation record.

nodes.title: Refutation record: the domain criterion was false against the original interface
nodes.math: Against the original four-field interface (which never tied the ring's addition to the direct-sum addition), the backward direction 'if $w$ is a valuation then $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ is a domain' is FALSE: transporting the product ring $R_0\times R_0$ (which has zero divisors, $(1,0)\cdot(0,1)=0$) along a bijection fixing all homogeneous elements yields a ring structure satisfying every interface field. The file proves the forward direction and nontriviality, and records the impossible leg as a single fenced unproved goal carrying this diagnosis.
nodes.lean: theorem L1_gr_domain_iff_val (S : SideVal p) (Rg : GradedRingStr S) : (letI := Rg.ring; IsDomain S.Gr) ↔ (∀ f g, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → S.w (f * g) = S.w f + S.w g)
nodes.note: The refutation record that drove the interface repair: the counterexample is a documented scheme (not compiled), the unproved leg is fenced (open), and the repaired statement is fully proved in a later revision — kept as the record of why the componentwise-addition field exists.

nodes.title: The degree-zero part of the associated graded is a subring
nodes.math: Under any graded ring structure on $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$, the elements supported purely in degree $0$ form a subring: closed under product (degree $0+0=0$ via the piece product), containing the unit ($[1]$ has degree $0$ since $w(1)=0$), and closed under addition, zero, and negation via the componentwise-addition law.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_degZero_subring (S : SideVal p) (Rg : GradedRingStr S) : letI := Rg.ring; ∃ (R0 : Subring S.Gr), ∀ x : S.Gr, x ∈ R0 ↔ (∀ γ ≠ (0:ℤ), (x γ : S.grPiece γ) = 0)
nodes.note: The degree-0 ring $L_0$ that the localization layer lives over; also a cautionary record — first recorded as proved while the file actually failed to compile (a build-tool discrepancy hid an instance diamond), caught by the axiom census and repaired 2026-07-29.

nodes.title: Localizations of the graded ring exist
nodes.math: For every multiplicative subset $M$ of $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ there exist a commutative ring $L$, an algebra structure over $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$, and a proof that $L$ is the localization of $\mathrm{gr}_w(A)$ at $M$ (the standard construction from the mathematical library).
nodes.lean: theorem L2_loc_exists (S : SideVal p) (Rg : GradedRingStr S) (M : letI := Rg.ring; Submonoid S.Gr) : letI := Rg.ring; ∃ (L : Type) (_ : CommRing L) (_ : Algebra S.Gr L), IsLocalization M L
nodes.note: Deliberately scope-fenced in its own docstring: generic existence only, and it must NOT be cited as the full homogeneous-localization theorem of the design — those are the separate degree-0, homogeneity, and isomorphism units.

nodes.title: The localizing multiplicative set is homogeneous
nodes.math: In a genuine model of a stage $\sigma$, every element of the multiplicative set generated by the initial forms of $\sigma$'s representatives and its key polynomial is homogeneous: it equals a single class in a single degree. Generators are single-degree by construction, and products stay single-degree by the piece-product law.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_homMon_homogeneous (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) : letI := M.Rg.ring; ∀ x ∈ M.homMon, ∃ (γ : ℤ) (c : M.S.grPiece γ), x = DirectSum.of _ γ c
nodes.gate: GenuineStageModel σ — the bundled genuine graded model of the stage (including the $L_0\cong K[z^{\pm1}]$ fiat); no inhabitant is constructed anywhere in this corpus.
nodes.note: Certifies that the localization is genuinely the homogeneous one — inverting only single-degree elements.

nodes.title: The coefficient localization has residue-field constants in degree zero (one of three clauses proved)
nodes.math: The coefficient-localization law for a stage $\sigma$: (i) every degree-$0$ element of the subring of $L_0[T^{\pm1}]$ generated by the initial forms of the nonzero coefficients together with the inverses of the representative units is a constant from the residue field $K$; (ii) conversely every $K$-constant lies in that subring; (iii) the inner variable $z$ is exactly the value of an explicit weight-$0$ monomial in the representative and key units. Clause (i) is fully proved via a weight-detecting evaluation ($z\mapsto z^{e}$, $T\mapsto z^{t}$) under which every generator becomes an inner constant; clauses (ii) and (iii) are open.
nodes.lean: theorem L2_coeffLoc (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) : CoeffLocLaw σ
nodes.note: The two open clauses carry a documented obstruction: they need construction data (that representative weights generate the parent value group) which neither the stage interface nor the model bundle supplies — an interface gap recorded rather than papered over.

nodes.title: The residual map is the initial form normalized by the degree-one unit
nodes.math: In a genuine model of $\sigma$: for every $f\neq 0$, $\Theta(\iota[f])\cdot T^{-w_\sigma(f)} = C(R(f))$ in $L_0[T^{\pm1}]$ — the stage residual $R(f)$ is exactly the genuine initial form of $f$, transported by the structure isomorphism and normalized by the degree-1 unit $T$.
nodes.lean: theorem L3_rank1_residual (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) : letI := M.Rg.ring; letI := M.Loring; letI := M.alg; M.Θ (algebraMap M.S.Gr M.Lo (M.S.initialForm f)) * LaurentPolynomial.T (- σ.w f) = LaurentPolynomial.C (σ.R f)
nodes.gate: GenuineStageModel σ — the bundled genuine graded model of the stage (including the $L_0\cong K[z^{\pm1}]$ fiat); no inhabitant is constructed anywhere in this corpus.
nodes.note: The rank-1 normalization equation of the design; its content flows from the model's bundled discharge identity plus a definitional computation.

nodes.title: Residual multiplicativity becomes a theorem of the genuine structure
nodes.math: In a genuine model of $\sigma$: $R(fg)=R(f)\,R(g)$ for all nonzero $f,g$ — derived by transporting multiplicativity of the genuine initial form along the localization map and $\Theta$, then cancelling the unit $T^{\,w(f)+w(g)}$ and using injectivity of the constant embedding. The residual multiplicativity axiom of the formal layer is thus a consequence, not a postulate.
nodes.lean: theorem L3_residual_mul (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) (f g : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) : σ.R (f * g) = σ.R f * σ.R g
nodes.gate: GenuineStageModel σ — the bundled genuine graded model of the stage (including the $L_0\cong K[z^{\pm1}]$ fiat); no inhabitant is constructed anywhere in this corpus.
nodes.note: Shows a formal-layer residual law is recovered from the genuine graded structure without citing the stage's own multiplicativity axiom for R.

nodes.title: The formally defined graded residual equals the genuine initial form
nodes.math: For every genuine model of $\sigma$ and every $f\neq 0$: the graded residual $C(R(f))\cdot T^{\,w_\sigma(f)}$ — which the earlier development DEFINED backwards from the residual map $R$ — equals $\Theta$ applied to the image of the genuine initial form $[f]$ in the localization. This is the identity the audit said the theorem signatures lacked.
nodes.lean: theorem L4_grRes_eq_genuine (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f ≠ 0) : letI := M.Rg.ring; letI := M.Loring; letI := M.alg; σ.grRes f = M.Θ (algebraMap M.S.Gr M.Lo (M.S.initialForm f))
nodes.gate: GenuineStageModel σ — the bundled genuine graded model of the stage (including the $L_0\cong K[z^{\pm1}]$ fiat); no inhabitant is constructed anywhere in this corpus.
nodes.note: The fiat-discharge identity itself; a one-line read-off of the model's discharge field, so its entire force is the (still open) inhabitation of the model bundle — that gap is what the vacuity certificates map out.

nodes.title: Bridge: a genuine model implies the stage certificate (partial, with recorded gaps)
nodes.math: Claim: any stage carrying a genuine graded model satisfies the full round-5 certificate package (eleven core stage laws, the T-vector unit product law, and the coefficient-localization law). Machine-checked part: the strict additive tie, the valuation-jump law, negation-invariance of the residual, the additive half of the slot decomposition, and the coefficient-supply clause. Fenced open: the parent-valuation laws, the representative-list laws, the T-vector laws, and the remaining localization clauses.
nodes.lean: theorem L4_genuine_imp_stageCoreL (σ : Stage p F) (M : GenuineStageModel σ) : StageCoreL σ
nodes.note: The open obligations carry a machine-audited classification: most are provably UNDERIVABLE from the interface (the model is blind to the stage's parent valuation, T-vector exponents, and representative list — each can be perturbed preserving every hypothesis), so the unit is held for a faithful restatement rather than forced through as stated.

nodes.title: Compiled certificate: the planned base-stage hypothesis is unsatisfiable
nodes.math: No stage satisfies the planned base-stage hypothesis 'the parent valuation is identically $0$': every stage's coefficient-supply law produces a coefficient of parent weight $w_{\mathrm{prev}}(\Phi)+1$, contradicting constancy at $0$. Hence the planned base-existence unit is provable only vacuously as stated, and proving it would certify nothing.
nodes.lean: theorem baseStage_hbase_empty (σ : Stage p F) (hbase : σ.wPrev = fun _ => (0 : ℤ)) : False
nodes.note: The refutation record for a held unit: the base-stage inhabitation of the genuine model — the tower's non-vacuity anchor — remains open pending a faithful base-data restatement.

nodes.title: Compiled certificate: the planned transition unit can only hold vacuously
nodes.math: The stage-transition record at child ramification index $e'=0$ is self-contradictory (it forces the child stage's ramification index to be $0$ against that stage's own positivity law $e\ge 1$). Since the planned transition-existence unit quantifies over arbitrary $e'$ with no positivity hypothesis, it could be proved only if no stage had a genuine model at all.
nodes.lean: theorem transitionCoreL_e0_false (σ σ' : Stage p F) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (h' : ℕ) (zbar : Fˣ) (ht : TransitionCoreL σ σ' Φhat 0 h' zbar) : False

nodes.math: If the planned statement — 'a recentering of a stage with a genuine model again has a genuine model and satisfies the certificate' — were provable as stated, then no recentering parent would have a genuine model at all: the recentering relation cannot see the child's representative list, so applying the statement to the clone with the representatives stripped (which recenters identically) contradicts the certificate's non-empty-representatives law.

nodes.title: The derivable fragment of the T-vector unit law
nodes.math: From the stage laws alone: the initial form of the key polynomial and the initial form of every T-vector entry are genuinely units of the concrete localization $L_0[T^{\pm1}]$. The remaining product law $\prod_i u_i^{a_i}\cdot Y^{t} = T$ is NOT derivable from the current interface — the integer exponents of the T-vector are left free by the stage's laws.
nodes.lean: theorem tvec_units_fragment (σ : Stage p F) : ∃ (uY : (LTwo ↥σ.K)ˣ) (ru : Fin σ.Tvec.length → (LTwo ↥σ.K)ˣ), IsGrUnit σ σ.Φ uY ∧ ∀ i, IsGrUnit σ (σ.Tvec.get i).1 (ru i)
nodes.note: Draws the exact boundary of what the interface supports for the held T-vector unit: unit-ness of every factor proved, the product law recorded as needing data absent from the stage.

role: MovesRBase is the Witt-vector base layer for the tower's coefficient rings. It fixes one ambient ring W(F̄_p) — the p-typical Witt vectors over a fixed algebraic closure of F_p — and realizes every unramified coefficient ring literally inside it: F_m is THE subfield of F̄_p with p^m elements (the fixed field of the m-th Frobenius iterate, with the cardinality proved, not assumed) and O_m := W(F_m) is an actual subring of W(F̄_p), so towers of base rings nest as genuine set inclusions with no per-pair embedding choices. Unramified base change is then index arithmetic by convention — the degree-δ′ extension of O_m IS O_{mδ′}, so composing base changes is literally multiplying indices — and the corpus proves the nesting, composition, chain, and residue-size laws (q_{mδ′} = q_m^{δ′}) that the tower recursion's bookkeeping rides on, all machine-checked with no axioms beyond Lean's core. Two statement-layer carriers (species letters, alphabet data) are transcribed for typing only, and the one substantive law about them — the re-basing law EQ-2 — is stated as an explicitly open hypothesis, with its lone consequence proved conditionally from it.
oneLiner: Unramified Witt coefficient rings as literal subrings; composition is index arithmetic

nodes.title: The ambient ring: Witt vectors over a fixed algebraic closure
nodes.math: Fix once and for all an algebraic closure $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of the field with $p$ elements, and form the ring of $p$-typical Witt vectors $W(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ (the completed ring of integers of the maximal unramified extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$). Every coefficient ring in this corpus is a literal subring of this one ambient ring.
nodes.lean:
variable (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime]

abbrev Kbar := AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p)

abbrev Wbar := WittVector p (Kbar p)
nodes.note: The design decision the whole corpus rests on: one ambient ring, so nested base changes compose as actual subrings rather than up to isomorphism; every declaration below is parameterized by an arbitrary prime p via this variable line.

nodes.title: The finite subfield of each order, fixed once
nodes.math: For each $m \ge 1$, $F_m$ is the subfield of $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$ fixed by the $m$-th iterate of the Frobenius $x \mapsto x^p$; equivalently $F_m = \{x \in \bar{\mathbb{F}}_p : x^{p^m} = x\}$. It is the unique subfield with $p^m$ elements — the cardinality is a separate theorem of this corpus, not part of the definition.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def Fsub (m : ℕ+) : Subfield (Kbar p) :=
  RingHom.eqLocusField (iterateFrobenius (Kbar p) p (m : ℕ)) (RingHom.id _)
nodes.note: The residue fields of all unramified extensions, realized as concrete subfields of one closure so their lattice is literal set inclusion.

nodes.title: Unramified coefficient rings as literal subrings
nodes.math: $\mathcal{O}_m := W(F_m)$, realized inside $W(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ as the image of the Witt-vector functor applied to the inclusion $F_m \hookrightarrow \bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$. Mathematically this is the ring of integers of the degree-$m$ unramified extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, but realized as an actual subring, so towers of base rings nest literally.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def O (m : ℕ+) : Subring (Wbar p) :=
  (WittVector.map (Subfield.subtype (Fsub p m))).range
nodes.note: The central object: the base rings over which the tower induction's polynomials live, with no per-pair embedding choices anywhere in the corpus.

nodes.title: Unramified base change by absolute index
nodes.math: The degree-$\delta'$ unramified base change of $\mathcal{O}_m$ is defined to be $\mathcal{O}_{m\delta'}$. Indices are absolute, so the composition rule $(\mathcal{O}_\delta)_{\delta'} = \mathcal{O}_{\delta\delta'}$ holds by definition — 'never an identification up to isomorphism'.
nodes.lean: noncomputable def relExt (m δ' : ℕ+) : Subring (Wbar p) := O p (m * δ')
nodes.note: The convention that turns the recursion's base-change bookkeeping into arithmetic of indices; its composition laws are the one-line theorems below.

nodes.title: Digit cylinders: congruence classes mod p^N
nodes.math: For a tuple $g = (g_1, \ldots, g_n)$ of elements of $\mathcal{O}_m$ (the coefficients of a monic degree-$n$ polynomial), the level-$N$ cylinder at $g$ is the set of tuples agreeing with $g$ in their first $N$ Witt coordinates. Since $F_m$ is perfect this is exactly the congruence class of $g$ modulo $p^N$ — the basic event whose normalized count the splitting-density computations measure.
nodes.lean:
def cyl (m : ℕ+) {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (g : Fin n → ↥(O p m)) : Set (Fin n → ↥(O p m)) :=
  {h | ∀ (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ), i < N → ((h j : Wbar p)).coeff i = ((g j : Wbar p)).coeff i}
nodes.note: Defines the counting object (the level-N box) that the density and volume layers of the parked parent corpus are built over.

nodes.title: Functoriality of the Witt-vector construction
nodes.math: Applying the Witt-vector functor to ring homomorphisms $f: R \to S$ and $g: S \to T$ in succession is the same as applying it once to $g \circ f$: $W(g)(W(f)(x)) = W(g \circ f)(x)$ coordinatewise.
nodes.lean:
theorem map_comp {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    (g : S →+* T) (f : R →+* S) (x : WittVector p R) :
    WittVector.map g (WittVector.map f x) = WittVector.map (g.comp f) x
nodes.note: A three-line fact absent from Mathlib at formalization time; the subring-nesting theorem consumes it to rewrite inclusions through the Witt functor.

nodes.title: Subfields nest along divisibility
nodes.math: If $d \mid m$ then $F_d \subseteq F_m$ inside $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p$: any $x$ with $x^{p^d} = x$ also satisfies $x^{p^m} = x$ (iterate the relation $m/d$ times).
nodes.lean: theorem Fsub_le {d m : ℕ+} (h : d ∣ m) : Fsub p d ≤ Fsub p m
nodes.note: The residue-field half of 'nested base changes compose literally as subrings'; feeds directly into the ring-level nesting theorem.

nodes.title: Unramified rings nest along divisibility
nodes.math: If $d \mid m$ then $W(F_d) \subseteq W(F_m)$ inside $W(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$. This is the substantive content behind the composition convention: once the subfields nest, the Witt rings nest as actual subrings.
nodes.lean: theorem O_le {d m : ℕ+} (h : d ∣ m) : O p d ≤ O p m
nodes.note: The workhorse inclusion every base-change step of the tower recursion rides on; proved via subfield nesting plus Witt functoriality.

nodes.title: Base changes compose by multiplying degrees
nodes.math: A degree-$\delta''$ base change applied to the degree-$\delta'$ base change of $\mathcal{O}_m$ equals the degree-$\delta'\delta''$ base change of $\mathcal{O}_m$: under the absolute-index convention, composition of unramified base changes is literally associativity of index multiplication.
nodes.lean:
theorem relExt_relExt (m δ' δ'' : ℕ+) :
    relExt p (m * δ') δ'' = relExt p m (δ' * δ'')
nodes.note: Together with the companion facts in the same file (the base-change convention is a definitional equality, and each ring sits inside its own base change), this makes '(O_δ)_δ′ = O_δδ′' pure bookkeeping.

nodes.title: Residue-field size under base change
nodes.math: With $q_m := p^m$ (the size of the residue field $F_m$), one has $q_{m\delta'} = q_m^{\delta'}$ — the identity governing how the density formulas' variable $q$ transforms when the base ring is extended.
nodes.lean: theorem qq_mul (m δ' : ℕ+) : qq p (m * δ') = qq p m ^ (δ' : ℕ)
nodes.note: The uniformity theorem substitutes q = p^δ into one fixed rational function; this is the bookkeeping for how that argument changes along the tower. The unit's second half (the same identity read through the tower's parameter bundle) stays with the parked parent corpus, per the recorded deviation.

nodes.title: The fixed field has exactly p^m elements
nodes.math: $|F_m| = p^m$: the fixed field of the $m$-th Frobenius iterate is the finite field with exactly $p^m$ elements. Proof: $F_m$ is the root set of $X^{p^m} - X$, a separable polynomial that splits with $p^m$ distinct roots in the algebraically closed field.
nodes.lean: theorem Fsub_card (m : ℕ+) : Nat.card ↥(Fsub p m) = p ^ (m : ℕ)
nodes.note: The corpus's hardest unit, and the one that makes F_m 'THE subfield of order p^m' rather than merely 'a fixed field' — added after an audit found the cardinality claim was part of the display, not a free convention.

nodes.title: The subring chain a tower branch descends
nodes.math: For any $m, \delta, \delta''$, the literal subring chain $W(F_m) \subseteq W(F_{m\delta}) \subseteq W(F_{m\delta\delta''})$ holds inside $W(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_p)$: a branch of relative degree $\delta''$ created at accumulated level $m\delta$ lands in exactly the ring the recursion says it should.
nodes.lean:
theorem O_chain (m δrel δ'' : ℕ+) :
    O p m ≤ O p (m * δrel) ∧ O p (m * δrel) ≤ O p (m * δrel * δ'')
nodes.note: The ring-theoretic witness for the recursion clause of the tower induction; restated here with explicit indices in place of the parked corpus's parameter bundle (a definitional translation recorded in the MANIFEST — ring content unchanged).

nodes.title: Species letters as finite syntax
nodes.math: A 'species letter' — the label classifying local behavior at a tower position — is purely syntactic data: a stage tuple $(e, h, g, \mu)$ of numerical invariants together with side/lattice and polygon-convention data, with the requirement that a letter is determined by these data (defined by syntax, never by the residue field's size). Each level $\delta$ carries a finite menu of realized letters.
nodes.lean:
structure SpeciesSyntax where
  Letter : Type
  shape : Letter → ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ
  SideData : Type
  side : Letter → SideData
  PolyConv : Type
  poly : Letter → PolyConv
  letter_det : Function.Injective (fun l => (shape l, side l, poly l))
  menu : ℕ+ → Finset Letter
nodes.note: Statement-layer carrier only — transcribed so the re-basing law below can be typed; it is never constructed in this corpus (instantiation belongs to the tower-induction hard core).

nodes.title: Alphabet carriers with their cardinality law
nodes.math: The data of an 'alphabet' at each shape-position class $x$ and each level $\delta$: an $F_{p^\delta}$-module carrier, a family of slot maps into it, the alphabet $\mathbb{A}_\delta(x)$ defined as the additive span of the slot maps' ranges, a dimension $a_\delta(x)$ with $|\mathbb{A}_\delta(x)| = p^{a_\delta(x)}$, and the realized species letter at each level. The cardinality identity is a field of the structure — part of what it means to be alphabet data, not a theorem proved here.
nodes.lean:
structure AlphabetData (Sp : SpeciesSyntax) where
  Pos : Type
  posNe : Nonempty Pos
  Carrier : ℕ+ → Pos → Type
  [carrierGrp : ∀ δ x, AddCommGroup (Carrier δ x)]
  [carrierMod : ∀ δ x, Module ↥(Fsub p δ) (Carrier δ x)]
  SlotDom : ℕ+ → Pos → Type
  [slotDomGrp : ∀ δ x, AddCommGroup (SlotDom δ x)]
  [slotDomMod : ∀ δ x, Module ↥(Fsub p δ) (SlotDom δ x)]
  slotMap : ∀ δ x, SlotDom δ x → Carrier δ x
  alpha : ∀ δ x, Set (Carrier δ x)
  alpha_attain : ∀ δ x,
    alpha δ x = ↑(AddSubgroup.closure (Set.range (slotMap δ x)))
  aDim : ℕ+ → Pos → ℕ
  card_eq : ∀ δ x, Nat.card (alpha δ x) = p ^ aDim δ x
  posLetter : ℕ+ → Pos → Sp.Letter
nodes.note: The interface packaging the note's alphabet objects together with their laws, per the recorded design lesson that a faithful obligation statement must be false for instances the source would reject; not constructed in this corpus.

nodes.title: Stable positions: the letter survives re-basing
nodes.math: A position class $x$ is $\delta$-stable when its realized species letter at level $\delta$ equals its letter at level $1$ — the classifying label persists under re-basing. Positions that split under base change fail this and are excluded from the comparison domain of the re-basing law.
nodes.lean:
def AlphabetData.Stable {Sp} (AD : AlphabetData p Sp) (δ : ℕ+) (x : AD.Pos) : Prop :=
  AD.posLetter δ x = AD.posLetter 1 x
nodes.note: The domain restriction that keeps the re-basing law faithful: it is asserted only where comparison across levels is meaningful.

nodes.title: The open re-basing law for alphabets
nodes.math: The hypothesized law (EQ-2): at every $\delta$-stable position, the re-based slot maps are $F_{p^\delta}$-linear and the alphabet dimension scales linearly, $a_\delta = \delta \cdot a_1$. Stated as a named proposition only — this is an open conjecture of the parked parent corpus, conditional on its ambient re-basing theory, and is proved nowhere in the repository; consumers must take it as an explicit hypothesis.
nodes.lean:
def EQ2law {Sp} (AD : AlphabetData p Sp) : Prop :=
  ∀ (δ : ℕ+) (x : AD.Pos), AlphabetData.Stable p AD δ x →
    IsLinearMap ↥(Fsub p δ) (AD.slotMap δ x) ∧
    AD.aDim δ x = (δ : ℕ) * AD.aDim 1 x
nodes.note: The source file itself marks this law OPEN (conditional on its ambient re-basing theory). Naming the open law as an explicit proposition, rather than assuming it silently, is the project's standing discipline for unproved steps.

nodes.title: Alphabet size under re-basing, assuming the open law
nodes.math: Assuming the open law (EQ-2), at every $\delta$-stable position the alphabet's size obeys the displayed consequence $|\mathbb{A}_\delta| = q_\delta^{\,a} = |\mathbb{A}_1|^{\delta}$, where $q_\delta = p^\delta$ and $a = a_1(x)$ is the level-one dimension — the cardinality identity the density bookkeeping uses.
nodes.lean:
theorem EQ2law_card {Sp} (AD : AlphabetData p Sp) (h : EQ2law p AD) :
    ∀ (δ : ℕ+) (x : AD.Pos), AlphabetData.Stable p AD δ x →
      Nat.card (AD.alpha δ x) = qq p δ ^ AD.aDim 1 x ∧
      Nat.card (AD.alpha δ x) = Nat.card (AD.alpha 1 x) ^ (δ : ℕ)
nodes.gate: h : EQ2law — the open (EQ-2) re-basing law (linearity of the re-based slot maps plus linear dimension scaling), hypothesized and discharged nowhere in the repository; additionally the carrier structure's own cardinality field (|𝔸_δ| = p^{a_δ}) enters as data of the structure, not as a proved fact.
nodes.note: The implication itself is machine-checked with no axioms beyond Lean's core; what remains open is its antecedent, which is exactly the parked parent corpus's central unproved law.

role: This corpus is the kernel of the tower induction behind the wildly ramified case of the uniformity theorem. It builds, in Lean, the Montes-style tower of valuation stages obtained by successive Newton-polygon reads of a p-adic polynomial — base stage, increment step (with a machine-checked refutation showing the step's growth guard is necessary), and recentering step — together with the carry algebra F[u]/(u^e − z̄) that makes higher-digit residue arithmetic exact: multiplying digits produces explicit carries. On top of the tower it proves the height/slot-minimum/staircase combinatorics and the exact measure count of a landing stratum — each level fixes exactly the predicted number of base-p digits — both conditional on the tower's recorded Newton-polygon side data (an interface hypothesis never discharged inside this corpus) and, for the measure count, on supplied coding inputs; this is the mechanism that makes densities at wild primes computable. Its exports are the abstract carrier contract consumed by the density-assembly corpora — whose concrete instantiation is still open, blocked by two machine-certified statement-transcription bugs in the abstract statement shapes — and the vertex-pin kernel consumed by the run-level classifier side, substantive only on its recentering-shaped legs (the steep legs are vacuous under the current recording interface, as disclosed on the card).
oneLiner: Tower-of-stages and carry-arithmetic kernel for wild-prime digit counting

nodes.title: The carry algebra: digit arithmetic with explicit carries
nodes.math: For a finite field $F$, an integer $e \ge 1$ and a unit $\bar z \in F^\times$, the carry algebra is the space of functions $\mathcal{D} = \{x : \mathbb{Z}/e \to F\}$ with pointwise addition and the twisted convolution $(x \star y)(\tau) = \sum_{\rho} x(\rho)\, y(\tau-\rho)\, \bar z^{\,c(\rho,\tau-\rho)}$, where the carry cocycle $c(\rho,\sigma)$ is $1$ exactly when the canonical representatives overflow ($\rho + \sigma \ge e$). The homogeneous generators $u_\rho c$ (the function supported at $\rho$ with value $c$) multiply by $u_\rho c \cdot u_\sigma c' = u_{\rho+\sigma}(c\,c'\,\bar z^{\,c(\rho,\sigma)})$: multiplying digits produces an explicit carry weighted by $\bar z$. A carry-ring pack is a commutative ring structure on $\mathcal{D}$ whose product is exactly this convolution and whose unit is $u_0 1$ — a concrete model of $F[u]/(u^e - \bar z)$.
nodes.lean:
def CarryAlg (F : Type u) (e : ℕ) : Type u := ZMod e → F

def carryExp (ρ σ : ZMod e) : ℕ := if e ≤ ρ.val + σ.val then 1 else 0

noncomputable def cmul [NeZero e] (zbar : Fˣ) (x y : CarryAlg F e) : CarryAlg F e :=
  fun τ => ∑ ρ : ZMod e, x ρ * y (τ - ρ) * (zbar : F) ^ carryExp ρ (τ - ρ)

noncomputable def dOf (ρ : ZMod e) (c : F) : CarryAlg F e := Pi.single ρ c

structure CarryRingPack (F : Type u) [Field F] (e : ℕ) [NeZero e] (zbar : Fˣ) where
  ring : CommRing (CarryAlg F e)
  mul_def : ∀ x y : CarryAlg F e, (letI := ring; x * y) = cmul zbar x y
  add_def : ∀ (x y : CarryAlg F e) (τ : ZMod e), (letI := ring; x + y) τ = x τ + y τ
  one_def : (letI := ring; (1 : CarryAlg F e)) = dOf 0 1
nodes.note: The portable digit-arithmetic object of the whole corpus: every deep-level residue computation is bookkept in this twisted group algebra, with the wild carry phenomenon isolated into one 2-cocycle.

nodes.title: Reading a residual into the carry algebra
nodes.math: Each valuation stage $\sigma$ carries a residual map $R$ sending a nonzero $p$-adic polynomial $B$ in general position to a Laurent monomial $c\,z^{k}$ over the stage's residue field. The digit map reads this into the carry algebra born at index $e_b$: if $R(B) = c\,z^k$ is a monomial unit, $\mathrm{dig}(B)$ is the homogeneous element of grade $k \bmod e_b$ with the aligned scalar $c \cdot \bar z^{(k - (k \bmod e_b))/e_b}$; otherwise $0$. It converts valuation-theoretic residues into positional digits subject to carries.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def _root_.LeanUrat.Moves.Stage.digD {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Finite F] (σ : Stage p F) (zbar : Fˣ) (e_b : ℕ) [NeZero e_b]
    (B : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) : CarryAlg F e_b :=
  open scoped Classical in
  if h : IsMonomialUnit (σ.R B) then
    dOf ((h.choose_spec.choose : ℤ) : ZMod e_b)
      (((h.choose : ↥σ.K) : F) *
        ((zbar ^ ((h.choose_spec.choose -
            (((h.choose_spec.choose : ℤ) : ZMod e_b)).val) / (e_b : ℤ)) : Fˣ) : F))
  else 0
nodes.note: The bridge between the valuation tower and the carry algebra; the multiplicativity theorem below is stated about exactly this map.

nodes.title: A tower of valuation stages with witnessed moves
nodes.math: A tower is a finite chain of valuation stages $\sigma_0, \dots, \sigma_K$ on $\mathbb{Z}_p[x]$: the base stage carries the Gauss valuation with uniformizer $p$ and residue field fixed to the base field, and each step is a witnessed move — either an increment (a legal Newton-polygon read: a monic irreducible descend polynomial $\psi \ne X$ of degree $g$ with root $\bar z$, a standard lift $\hat\Phi$, coprime new invariants $e', h'$ with the steepness condition $h' > e' \cdot w(\hat\Phi)$, plus the recorded transition core and the child's stage laws) or a recentering (change of center at the same level); the ambient residue field has characteristic $p$. From the move data one defines per-level slopes $\kappa_k = h_k/(e_0 \cdots e_k)$, coordinates $c = (l, \text{slots})$ addressing basis monomials $m_c = p^{l} \prod_r \Phi_r^{s_r}$, and the absolute height $\mathrm{ht}(c) = l + \sum_r s_r \kappa_r$.
nodes.lean:
inductive MoveWitness (σ σ' : Stage p F) : Type u
  | inc (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (e' h' : ℕ) (zbar : Fˣ)
      (hyp : TransHyp σ ψ g Φhat e' h' zbar)
      (core : TransitionCoreL σ σ' Φhat e' h' zbar)
      (core' : StageCoreL σ') : MoveWitness σ σ'
  | recenter (cc : ↥σ.K) (tt : Polynomial ℤ_[p])
      (core : IsRecenteringCore σ σ' cc tt)
      (core' : StageCoreL σ') : MoveWitness σ σ'

structure Tower (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] where
  K : ℕ
  stg : Fin (K + 1) → Stage p F
  base : IsBaseStage (stg 0) ∧ StageCoreL (stg 0)
  move : ∀ k : Fin K, MoveWitness (stg k.castSucc) (stg k.succ)
  hcharF : CharP F p
nodes.note: The central inductive object: the formal counterpart of an Okutsu–Montes chain of augmented valuations, with every step carrying its own machine-checked witness data (each move records the child's stage laws; the existence theorems below show such enriched witnesses exist for every legal read).

nodes.title: Recorded Newton-polygon side data of a tower (open interface)
nodes.math: The realizability data of a tower: for each read $k$, a side line, a window (left slot $s_0$ and width), a descend order $\mu$, a recorded vertex height $u^*$, and per-read factor-interior ends, subject to: the slope law (line $k$ descends at $\kappa_k$ per fine slot), the vertex-height tie (the line passes through the window's right endpoint at height $u^*$), the strictly-steeper chain, vertex-entry domination at each interior end, and window nesting (each read's window sits inside the previous read's rim).
nodes.lean:
structure TowerRealizable (T : Tower p F) where
  line : ℕ → MovesC.Line
  s0 : ℕ → ℕ
  wSide : ℕ → ℕ
  mu : ℕ → ℕ
  ustar : ℕ → ℚ
  interiorEnd : ℕ → ℕ
  slope_law : ∀ k : Fin (T.K + 1), (line k.val).slope * (T.frameWidth k.val : ℚ) = T.kappa k
  vertex_tie : ∀ k : Fin (T.K + 1),
    (line k.val).at ((s0 k.val + wSide k.val) * T.frameWidth k.val) = ustar k.val
  steeper : ∀ k : Fin (T.K + 1), ∀ m, m < k.val → (line m).slope < (line k.val).slope
  vertex_entry : ∀ k : Fin (T.K + 1), ∀ m, m ≤ k.val →
    (line m).at (interiorEnd k.val) ≤ (line k.val).at (interiorEnd k.val)
  window : ∀ k : ℕ, k < T.K → s0 (k + 1) + wSide (k + 1) ≤ mu k
nodes.note: The corpus's named open kernel: theorems consume it as an explicit hypothesis and it is never discharged inside this corpus — its per-instance discharge is classifier-side work, so every result gated on it is conditional.

nodes.title: The abstract carrier contract exported to the density pipeline
nodes.math: An abstract package of a graded carrier (the graded object of a valuation) together with abstract histories, coordinates and digits, plus height, block, level-set, slot-coefficient, alphabet-dimension, line, block-edge, interior-end, window, monomial and floor data. Over this pack four statement shapes — the height/slot-minimum/level-locality/staircase package, the typicality (additivity + alphabet-count) package, the line-domination package, and the graded additivity law — form the typed contract that downstream density corpora hypothesize rather than assert; a distinguished implication shape says a consequence follows once every pack satisfies the contract.
nodes.lean:
structure CarrierPackR (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] where
  G : GradedCarrierR p
  Hist : Type
  Coord : Type
  Digit : Type
  [digitAdd : AddCommGroup Digit]
  kIdx : Hist → ℕ
  ht : Hist → Coord → ℚ
  blk : Hist → Coord → ℕ
  lvl : Hist → ℕ → ℚ → Set Coord
  slotCoeff : Hist → ℕ → (Coord → Digit) → G.Coeff
  aDim : Hist → ℕ → ℚ → ℕ
  lines : Hist → ℕ → MovesC.Line
  blockEdge : Hist → ℕ → ℕ
  interiorEnd : Hist → ℕ → ℕ
  window : Hist → ℕ → Prop
  mono : Hist → Coord → G.Coeff
  floorB : Hist → ℕ → ℚ

def REL1Pack (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : CarrierPackR p) : Prop :=
  LSTStmt' p K ∧ TYPStmt' p K ∧ DOMStmt' p K ∧ SecB1Stmt' p K

def EQ2lawIfREL1' (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (EQ2law : Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ K : CarrierPackR p, REL1Pack p K) → EQ2law
nodes.note: The seam other corpora consume: they hypothesize this contract, and the (still open) instance node below is the obligation to realize it with a genuine tower.

nodes.title: The carry algebra is the ring F[u]/(u^e − z̄)
nodes.math: For any carry-ring pack on the carry algebra there is a ring isomorphism $\Theta : \mathcal{D} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} F[u]/(u^e - \bar z)$ sending the homogeneous generator $u_\rho c$ to $c \cdot u^{\rho}$ (with $u$ the class of $X$ in the quotient by $X^e - \bar z$). The concrete function-space model with twisted convolution really is this quotient ring.
nodes.lean:
theorem D4_carryAdjoinRoot {F : Type*} [Field F] {e : ℕ} [NeZero e] {zbar : Fˣ}
    (P : CarryRingPack F e zbar) :
    ∃ Θ : (letI := P.ring;
        CarryAlg F e ≃+* AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ e - Polynomial.C ((zbar : F)))),
      ∀ (ρ : ZMod e) (c : F),
        Θ (dOf ρ c) = algebraMap F _ c *
          AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ e - Polynomial.C ((zbar : F))) ^ ρ.val
nodes.note: Certifies that the hand-rolled carry-cocycle object is faithfully the intended algebra, so all digit computations downstream are computations in F[u]/(u^e − z̄).

nodes.title: Digit reading is multiplicative up to carries
nodes.math: Let $\sigma$ be a stage satisfying the core laws, $\psi$ an irreducible descend polynomial of degree $g$ with root $\bar z$, and $\hat\Phi$ a standard lift of the key. Suppose $B, B''$ are nonzero polynomials of degree below the key block, division gives $B \cdot B'' = Q\,\hat\Phi + R_{\mathrm{dev}}$ with small remainder, and the three residuals are monomial units $R(B) = c_B z^{k_B}$, $R(B'') = c_{B''} z^{k_{B''}}$, $R(R_{\mathrm{dev}}) = c_R z^{k_B + k_{B''}}$ (the anchor positions add — the exact-remainder bookkeeping). Then $\mathrm{dig}(R_{\mathrm{dev}}) = \mathrm{dig}(B) \star \mathrm{dig}(B'')$ in the carry algebra: multiplying residual digits and reducing modulo the key is exactly carry-algebra multiplication.
nodes.lean:
theorem D7_digD_mul {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (σ : Stage p F) (hσ : StageCoreL σ) (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ)
    (hg : ψ.natDegree = g) (hψ : Irreducible ψ) (hψz : ψ ≠ Polynomial.X)
    (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hlift : IsStandardLift σ ψ g Φhat)
    (zbar : Fˣ) (hzbar : Polynomial.eval₂ σ.K.subtype ((zbar : Fˣ) : F) ψ = 0)
    (e_b : ℕ) [NeZero e_b]
    (B B'' Rdev Q : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hB'' : B'' ≠ 0)
    (hBd : B.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree)
    (hB''d : B''.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree)
    (hdiv : B * B'' = Q * Φhat + Rdev)
    (hRd : Rdev.natDegree < σ.e * g * σ.Φ.natDegree)
    (cB cB'' cR : (↥σ.K)ˣ) (kB kB'' : ℤ)
    (h5B : σ.R B = LaurentPolynomial.C (cB : ↥σ.K) * LaurentPolynomial.T kB)
    (h5B'' : σ.R B'' = LaurentPolynomial.C (cB'' : ↥σ.K) * LaurentPolynomial.T kB'')
    (h5R : σ.R Rdev = LaurentPolynomial.C (cR : ↥σ.K) * LaurentPolynomial.T (kB + kB'')) :
    σ.digD zbar e_b Rdev = cmul zbar (σ.digD zbar e_b B) (σ.digD zbar e_b B'')
nodes.note: The heart of the carry calculus: an earlier untwisted form of this law was refuted by a compiled counterexample condition, forcing the twisted restatement — with the anchor position made explicit — before the proof went through.

nodes.title: The tower induction starts: base stages exist
nodes.math: Given base read data at invariants $(e,h)$ — a monic polynomial $\varphi$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ whose reduction mod $p$ is irreducible with a root $z_0$ in the ambient finite field, and coprime $e, h \ge 1$ — there exists a base stage: parent valuation the Gauss valuation, uniformizer representative $p$, residue field fixed to the base field, satisfying all core stage laws, with invariants exactly $(e,h)$.
nodes.lean:
theorem T1_baseStage {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (e h : ℕ) (bdata : BaseReadData p F e h) :
    ∃ σ : Stage p F, IsBaseStage σ ∧ StageCoreL σ ∧ σ.e = e ∧ σ.h = h
nodes.note: The base case of the tower induction, with a genuinely faithful base pin (Gauss valuation, not a vacuous clone) — the non-vacuity the earlier corpus certified was missing from a degenerate variant.

nodes.title: The induction step: every legal read produces a child stage
nodes.math: If $\sigma$ is a stage satisfying the core laws, $(\psi, g, \hat\Phi, e', h', \bar z)$ is a legal increment read (the full hypothesis interface: $\psi$ monic irreducible of degree $g$ with $\psi \ne X$ and root $\bar z$, $\hat\Phi$ a standard lift, $e', h' \ge 1$ coprime, and the steepness $h' > e' \cdot w(\hat\Phi)$), and the growth guard $e \cdot g > 1$ holds, then there exists a child stage $\sigma'$ realizing the recorded transition core, satisfying the core laws, whose residue field is the extension of $\sigma$'s generated by $\bar z$, with new invariants $(e', h')$.
nodes.note: The hardest constructive theorem of the corpus (the full child-stage construction: child valuation, residual laws, digit frame, all stage axioms), assembled from a six-unit decomposition; the growth guard it carries was forced by the compiled countermodel in the next node.

nodes.title: Countermodel: the induction step is false without the growth guard
nodes.math: Under the same legal-read hypotheses but with $e \cdot g = 1$, NO child stage realizing the recorded transition core exists: the record's representative and degree clauses collide, forcing $\deg \Phi < \deg \hat\Phi = e\,g \cdot \deg \Phi$, impossible at $e g = 1$. The $e g = 1$ boundary is a different species of move — recentering — handled by its own theorem.
nodes.note: A machine-checked refutation of the unguarded induction step: it caught a real specification error during development, forced the e·g > 1 guard onto the whole S9 family, and documents why recentering is a separate species.

nodes.title: Recentering produces a stage (the boundary species)
nodes.math: If $\sigma$ has $e = 1$ and $c \ne 0$ is a recentering constant in its residue field realized by some polynomial $t$ (nonzero, in the key's coefficient class, of weight $w(\Phi)$, with residual exactly the constant $c$), then there exist a recentered stage $\sigma'$ and such a $t$ with the recorded recentering core, and $\sigma'$ satisfies the core stage laws.
nodes.lean:
theorem S10_recStage {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (σ : Stage p F) (hσ : StageCoreL σ) (he1 : σ.e = 1)
    (cc : ↥σ.K) (hcc : cc ≠ 0)
    (hlift : ∃ tt : Polynomial ℤ_[p], tt ≠ 0 ∧ inC σ.Φ tt ∧ σ.w tt = σ.w σ.Φ ∧
      σ.R tt = LaurentPolynomial.C cc * LaurentPolynomial.T 0) :
    ∃ (σ' : Stage p F) (tt : Polynomial ℤ_[p]),
      IsRecenteringCore σ σ' cc tt ∧ StageCoreL σ'
nodes.note: Covers exactly the e·g = 1 corner that the increment step provably cannot: together with the base and increment theorems it makes every tower move inhabitable.

nodes.title: Every stage of every tower obeys the stage laws
nodes.math: In any tower, every stage satisfies the core laws; and each move's bookkeeping holds as recorded — an increment step sets the residue field to the extension generated by the read's root $\bar z$ and the invariants to $(e', h')$, while a recentering step keeps the residue field and sets $e = 1$.
nodes.lean:
theorem S11_towerSpine {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (T : Tower p F) :
    (∀ k : Fin (T.K + 1), StageCoreL (T.stg k)) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin T.K,
      match T.move k with
      | .inc _ _ _ e' h' zbar _ _ _ =>
          (T.stg k.succ).K = (T.stg k.castSucc).nextField zbar ∧
          (T.stg k.succ).e = e' ∧ (T.stg k.succ).h = h'
      | .recenter _ _ _ _ =>
          (T.stg k.succ).e = 1 ∧ (T.stg k.succ).K = (T.stg k.castSucc).K)
nodes.note: The assembled spine every downstream tower theorem stands on; after the move-witness enrichment its first part is by projection — the real content lives in the existence theorems (base, increment, recentering) plus a separate minimality certificate showing the enrichment added only the independently-certified twist-class laws.

nodes.title: Heights, slot minima, and the staircase floor of a tower
nodes.math: Given realizability data for the tower: (i-a) the top-stage weight of a coordinate's basis monomial equals the total stretch times its height, $w_{\mathrm{top}}(m_c) = \mathrm{STR} \cdot \mathrm{ht}(c)$, the stretch $\mathrm{STR}$ being the product of the ramification indices along the tower; (i-b) a nonzero block-supported digit vector's slot coefficient has valuation exactly the minimum height over its support, attained at a minimizing coordinate; (i-c) the graded class of a slot coefficient at level $\gamma'$ depends only on the digits on the $\gamma'$-level set (digits strictly below vanishing); (ii) on factor-interior blocks the history step-floor is constant across the block, equal to the block floor; (iii) any level set strictly above the block floor avoids the floor set.
nodes.lean:
theorem C1_LST {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (T : Tower p F) (rl : TowerRealizable T) :
    (∀ c : T.Coord, c.MonoNZ →
      (((T.stg (Fin.last T.K)).w (T.mono c) : ℤ) : ℚ) = (T.strTop : ℚ) * T.ht c) ∧
    (∀ (b : ℕ) (y : T.Coord → ↥(T.stg 0).FQ), (Function.support y).Finite →
      (∀ c, y c ≠ 0 → T.blk c = b) → T.slotCoeff b y ≠ 0 →
      ∃ c₀, y c₀ ≠ 0 ∧ T.wQ (T.slotCoeff b y) = (T.ht c₀ : WithTop ℚ) ∧
        ∀ c, y c ≠ 0 → T.ht c₀ ≤ T.ht c) ∧
    (∀ (b : ℕ) (γ' : ℚ) (x y : T.Coord → ↥(T.stg 0).FQ),
      (Function.support x).Finite → (Function.support y).Finite →
      (∀ c ∈ T.levelSet b γ', x c = y c) →
      (∀ c, T.blk c = b → T.ht c < γ' → x c = 0) →
      (∀ c, T.blk c = b → T.ht c < γ' → y c = 0) →
      T.inGr γ' (T.slotCoeff b x) = T.inGr γ' (T.slotCoeff b y)) ∧
    (∀ b, rl.interiorB b → ∀ c : T.Coord, T.blk c = b → rl.floorS c = rl.floorB b) ∧
    (∀ (b : ℕ) (γ' : ℚ), rl.interiorB b → rl.floorB b < γ' →
      T.levelSet b γ' ∩ {c | T.blk c = b ∧ T.ht c ≤ rl.floorB b} = ∅)

nodes.note: The combinatorial dictionary between tower coordinates and valuations that the counting arguments run on; its staircase leg (ii) was restated onto the step-floor after the raw-line form was machine-refuted (the refutation is kept on file in a scratch module).

nodes.title: A landing stratum has exactly the predicted measure
nodes.math: Exact stratum counting at a tower level. Fix a level move (descend polynomial $\psi$, order $\mu$, anchor, transported digit pattern, cutoff $N$) whose pattern is anchor-exact, and code polynomials of degree $< D$ by $D \cdot N$ base-$p$ digits. Suppose a unitriangular coordinate change $\Theta$ and a digit system $E$ with exactly $k$ pinned rows are such that solutions of $E$ (after $\Theta$) cut out exactly the landing cylinder of the stratum, and $0$ is not a solution. Then the stratum has exact normalized density $p^{-k}$ in digit space: $\#\{\text{stratum codes}\} \cdot p^{k} = p^{D N}$.

nodes.note: The measure-theoretic payoff of the tower: each level pins exactly the predicted number of base-p digits, which is what makes wild-prime densities exact powers of p; its original fenced form was certified unprovable, and the exact two missing hypotheses were identified by a compiled certificate before the restatement.

nodes.title: How many digit values a level can realize (open, statement mistyped)
nodes.math: As currently fenced: on a nonempty level set, (1) the alphabet — the group of graded classes reachable by level-set digit vectors — has cardinality $p^{\dim}$; (2) it is full (equal in size to the top residue field) if and only if every level-set coordinate contributes a nonzero class; (3) if some coordinate is degenerate, the dimension drops strictly. Conjunct (1) is separately proved; conjuncts (2)–(3) are mistyped (see the certificate node), so the fenced statement is not provable as written.
nodes.lean:
theorem C6_alphabetCard {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (T : Tower p F) (b : ℕ) (γ : ℚ) (hne : (T.levelSet b γ).Nonempty) :
    Nat.card ↥(T.alphabet b γ) = p ^ T.aDim b γ ∧
    (Nat.card ↥(T.alphabet b γ) = Nat.card ↥(T.stg (Fin.last T.K)).K ↔
      ∀ c : ↥(T.levelSet b γ), ∃ y : ↥(T.stg 0).FQ,
        T.typComposite b γ (Pi.single c y) ≠ 0) ∧
    ((∃ c : ↥(T.levelSet b γ), ∀ y : ↥(T.stg 0).FQ,
        T.typComposite b γ (Pi.single c y) = 0) →
      T.aDim b γ < Nat.log p (Nat.card ↥(T.stg (Fin.last T.K)).K))

nodes.title: Certificate: the alphabet-count statement collapses to a refuted claim
nodes.math: A compiled certificate that the alphabet-count statement is mistyped: for every tower, every level-set coordinate automatically realizes a nonzero class (level-set membership forces attainability by weight detection), so the right-hand side of conjunct (2) is a theorem and the hypothesis of conjunct (3) is refutable outright. Consequently the fenced statement, if it held, would force unconditional fullness $\#\mathbb{A}(b,\gamma) = \#F_{K+1}$ on every nonempty level set — precisely the uniform display already refuted at shallow heights (concrete towers exist where the alphabet is strictly smaller). The correct statement must quantify over the alignment class of heights, not over level-set coordinates.

      (Nat.card ↥(T.alphabet b γ) = Nat.card ↥(T.stg (Fin.last T.K)).K ↔
