nodes.title: The concrete tower should instantiate the abstract interface (open)
nodes.math: The instantiation obligation: every tower with realizability data yields a concrete instance of the abstract carrier pack whose graded pieces agree with the tower's own, satisfying the exported height, typicality, and domination contracts. Open: two machine-certified quantifier-scope transcription bugs in the abstract statement shapes (relative to the concrete forms they were meant to abstract) make the instance unprovable as written; the statement repairs await the project lead's explicit approval (the project never changes a fenced statement without it).
nodes.lean:
theorem R6_carrierInstance {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (T : Tower p F) (rl : TowerRealizable T) :
    ∃ K : CarrierPackR p,
      (∀ γ : ℚ, K.G.Gr γ = T.grQ γ) ∧
      LSTStmt' p K ∧ TYPStmt' p K ∧ DOMStmt' p K
nodes.note: The seam between this kernel and the density-assembly corpora: the fenced unproved goal is documented in-file with two machine-checked refutation kernels showing the abstract statement shapes (not the tower) are at fault, so downstream consumers currently ride the contract as a hypothesis.

nodes.title: The Newton-polygon vertex of a development is pinned (non-recentering reads)
nodes.math: For a recorded run of reads on $f$ and a non-recentering read $i$, any development $f = \sum_j B_j \hat\Phi^j$ along the next key with cutoff beyond the read's order $\mu$ has $B_\mu \ne 0$, and the child weight of $B_\mu$ equals the frame stretch times the recorded side line's value at the vertex slot $\mu \cdot (\text{child width})$: the vertex of the development's Newton polygon sits exactly on the recorded line.
nodes.lean:
theorem V9_K1nonrec {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} {H : History p F}
    (h : ReadsOf p F n f H) (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i + 1 < H.nodes.length)
    (hsp : (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).species ≠ ReadSpecies.recentering)
    (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (Nd : ℕ)
    (hdev : IsDevelopment (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.Φ f B Nd)
    (hNd : (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ < Nd) :
    B ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ) ≠ 0 ∧
      (((H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.w (B ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ)) : ℚ))
        = (H.strFrame (i+1) : ℚ) *
          (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).line.at
            ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ * (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).childWidth)
nodes.note: The carry-bridge kernel exported to the run-level classifier corpus (wired there statement-verbatim), proved with no unproved goals and no axioms beyond Lean's core — with a loud disclosure: for steep reads with e·g ≥ 2 the recorded-run hypotheses are contradictory (the inconsistency node below), so those legs hold vacuously and the theorem's non-vacuous content is exactly the recentering-shaped (e·g = 1) range; the interface repair awaits the project lead's approval.

nodes.title: Refutation record: the recorded steep-read transition is contradictory
nodes.math: A machine-checked inconsistency in the run-recording interface: the recorded transition data for a steep read ($e^\star h_\sigma < h^\star$) with $e^\star g \ge 2$ — child key equal to the read lift, ramification tie $e = e^\star$, parent-weight tie, slot-minimum weight law, and Bézout ties — proves False. Two of the child's own laws weigh $\Phi^{e^\star g}$ differently, forcing $h^\star = (e^\star)^2 g\, h_\sigma$ (hence $e^\star = 1$, $t^\star = 0$), after which two renderings of the key's residual clash. Consequence: genuinely steep increments are unrecordable under the current interface, so any theorem quantifying over recorded steep reads is vacuous there.
nodes.lean:
theorem V10_readTransition_incompatible {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F]
    [Finite F] (σ σ' : Stage p F) (estar hstar : ℕ) (sstar tstar : ℤ) (g : ℕ)
    (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p])
    (hsteep : (estar : ℤ) * (σ.h : ℤ) < (hstar : ℤ))
    (hEG : 2 ≤ estar * g)
    (hcop : Nat.gcd estar hstar = 1)
    (hbez : (estar : ℤ) * sstar + (hstar : ℤ) * tstar = 1)
    (he1t : estar = 1 → tstar = 0)
    (hψ0 : ψ.coeff 0 ≠ 0)
    (hlift : IsReadLift σ ψ g estar hstar Φhat)
    (hkey : σ'.Φ = Φhat) (hce : σ'.e = estar) (hcw : ∀ x, σ'.wPrev x = σ.w x)
    (hslot : IsSlotMinWeight σ'.w Φhat estar hstar σ.w)
    (hs_tie : σ'.s = sstar) (ht_tie : σ'.t = tstar) : False
nodes.note: The corpus's standing interface finding of record: it exposes that a companion transport theorem in the same file is proved vacuously (its hypotheses are contradictory — disclosed in-file), and the named repair (re-key the recorded child at the regraded side value) is deliberately left awaiting the project lead's approval rather than silently applied.

nodes.title: Concrete seal: the carry algebra checked over the field of four elements
nodes.math: A computational check over $\mathbb{F}_4$: there is a unit $\bar z$ with $\bar z^2 = \bar z + 1$ such that in every carry-ring pack with $e = 2$: $u_1 \cdot u_1 = \bar z\, u_0$ (a genuine carry into the twist), $u_1 c \cdot u_0 c' = u_1(c c')$ (no carry), and the carry cocycle satisfies the associativity identity $c(\rho,\sigma) + c(\rho+\sigma,\tau) = c(\sigma,\tau) + c(\rho,\sigma+\tau)$.
nodes.lean:
theorem G2_carryGate :
    ∃ zbar : (GaloisField 2 2)ˣ,
      ((zbar : GaloisField 2 2) ^ 2 = (zbar : GaloisField 2 2) + 1) ∧
      ∀ P : CarryRingPack (GaloisField 2 2) 2 zbar,
        (letI := P.ring;
          dOf (1 : ZMod 2) (1 : GaloisField 2 2) * dOf 1 1
            = dOf 0 ((zbar : GaloisField 2 2))) ∧
        (∀ c c' : GaloisField 2 2, letI := P.ring;
          dOf (1 : ZMod 2) c * dOf 0 c' = dOf 1 (c * c')) ∧
        (∀ ρ σ τ : ZMod 2,
          carryExp ρ σ + carryExp (ρ + σ) τ = carryExp σ τ + carryExp ρ (σ + τ))
nodes.note: One of the corpus's concrete gates: a fully computed instance confirming that the abstract carry apparatus produces the right numbers on a real field — every kernel in the project gets such a concrete computational check.

role: HC2 is the bridge between the Newton-polygon classifier's combinatorial engine and the graded presentation ring. It does three things: (1) defines, polynomial-explicitly, what it means for a recorded tower of Newton-polygon reads to be an actual classifier run on a monic p-adic polynomial f, and proves the structural laws of runs (key towers, canonicity of lifts, Galois normalization, rigidity of normalized classes); (2) proves that from a small "graded seed" — the presentation fragment that the graded-ring corpus HC1 must supply — the full jet-presentation package (digit-system chain, fresh clauses, counting laws) assembles, discharging the presentability and threshold interfaces the density-counting corpus MovesD consumes; (3) checks both directions with compiled concrete gates at p = 2 and p = 3, including a recomputation of the 1/4 inert-stratum density, and keeps compiled refutations of two retired over-strong statements on record. Remaining obligations are carried either as named hypotheses that consumers quantify over explicitly or as fenced unproved goals (nine recorded ones, five of them in the zero-set induction step) — the corpus declares zero axioms.
oneLiner: Builds jet presentations from graded seeds; defines and gates classifier runs

nodes.title: What it means for a recorded tower to be a run on f
nodes.math: Fix a prime $p$ and a finite residue field $F$. A history is a recorded tower of Newton-polygon reads: each node carries a stage (a key polynomial $\Phi$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a weight function $w$ and a residual-coefficient map $R$), a side of slope $h/e$ with total weight $\gamma$, a digit pattern, a residual order $\mu$, a residue root $\bar z$, and a lift. The run predicate asserts: $f$ is monic of degree $n$, the history is internally coherent, and at every read $i$ the $\Phi_i$-adic expansion $f = \sum_j B_j \Phi_i^j$ realizes all recorded data — (i) the recorded side is a genuine supporting line of the expansion's polygon: $e\,w(B_j) + jh \ge \gamma$ for every nonzero $B_j$, with equality exactly at the recorded stride slots $j = s_0 + ek$ with nonzero pattern digit; (ii) at each such slot the coefficient's residual is the recorded monomial unit with scalar $\mathrm{pat}(k)$; (iii) the frame residual of $f$ has the recorded anchor and residual order $\mu$; (iv) the recorded landing law holds at a designated next key, equal to the recorded child key at every interior read; (v) the node's lift is the one dictated by the canonical policy and its residue root is the canonical root; (vi) the $\mu$-th coefficient of $f$'s expansion in the next key has residue digit equal to the recorded transported vertex value.
nodes.lean:
def ReadsOf (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] (n : ℕ)
    (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (H : History p F) : Prop :=
  f.Monic ∧ f.natDegree = n ∧ HistoryCoherent H ∧
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length),
    ∃ (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (Nd : ℕ) (Φnext : Polynomial ℤ_[p]),
      IsDevelopment (H.nodes[i]'hi).σ.Φ f B Nd ∧
      (∀ hi1 : i + 1 < H.nodes.length, Φnext = (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.Φ) ∧
      SideReads (H.nodes[i]'hi) B Nd Φnext
nodes.note: The central new definition of the corpus — its inbound definitional boundary: the six-clause per-read bundle it references is the single negotiating interface that the transport corpus re-keys to; its non-vacuity is not assumed but compiled (see the run-predicate gate).

nodes.title: The graded seed: the interface the presentation ring must fill
nodes.math: For a history $H$ and box size $n \times N$: a family of presentation predicates $\mathrm{pres}_i(x, f)$ between polynomials $f$ and digit vectors $x \in \mathbb{F}_p^{nN}$ indexed by the $n \times N$ coordinate box (coefficient positions $\times$ $p$-adic levels), such that (a) the level-0 presentation reads off the literal base-$p$ digits of $f$'s coefficients; (b) every monic degree-$n$ polynomial admits a presentation at every stage; (c) consecutive presentations are related by unitriangular digit transports $\Theta_i$; (d) presentations are block-local in the $i$-th key's expansion; (e) each recorded exact-valuation support $S$ carries a full digit alphabet of size $p^{|S|}$ (every assignment attained); and (f) the seed laws: a valuation clause $w(B_j) \ge \beta$ is — whenever the chart records the entire zero system of the threshold, the box-size proviso — literally the vanishing of the chart digits of height $< \beta$; attainable accounting on value supports; the transports are literal on valuation content; and the root read carries no exact-valuation coordinate in its factor interior. This is exactly the fragment of the jet package that the graded-ring construction must supply; HC2 builds everything else from it.
nodes.lean:
structure PresentSeed (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (H : History p F) (n N : ℕ) (keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) where
  pres : ℕ → (Fin (n * N) → ZMod p) → Polynomial ℤ_[p] → Prop
  pres_zero : ∀ (x : Fin (n * N) → ZMod p) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), pres 0 x f ↔
      ∀ j : Fin (n * N), x j = baseDigit p (boxChart n N j).1 (f.coeff (boxChart n N j).2)
  pres_total : ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ H.nodes.length → ∀ f : Polynomial ℤ_[p],
      f.Monic → f.natDegree = n → ∃ x, pres i x f
  Theta : ℕ → ((Fin (n * N) → ZMod p) → (Fin (n * N) → ZMod p))
  Theta_uni : ∀ i : ℕ, IsUnitriangular (Theta i)
  pres_theta : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length →
      ∀ (x : Fin (n * N) → ZMod p) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), pres (i+1) x f → pres i (Theta i x) f
  pres_block : ∀ i : ℕ, i < H.nodes.length →
      ∀ (f f' : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (x x' : Fin (n * N) → ZMod p),
        pres (i+1) x f → pres (i+1) x' f' →
      ∀ (B B' : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (Nd Nd' : ℕ),
        IsDevelopment (keys i) f B Nd → IsDevelopment (keys i) f' B' Nd' →
        ∀ c : Fin (n * N),
          B ((boxChart n N c).2 / (keys i).natDegree) = B' ((boxChart n N c).2 / (keys i).natDegree) →
          x c = x' c
  typObj : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length) (S : Finset (Fin (n * N))),
      IsValueSupport H (boxChart n N) i (H.nodes[i]'hi) S →
      TypObject p (n * N) S (Fin S.card → ZMod p)
  zcSeed : ZCSeedLaws H (boxChart n N) pres Theta keys
nodes.note: The inbound interface: supplying one of these per class and level is HC1's open deliverable (the hypothesis named SEED-EXIST); the seed-law list is fenced — a first transcription over-claimed one law and was machine-refuted, then repaired with a chart-coverage guard (a documented correction, not a silent fix).

nodes.title: The two named hypotheses (never axioms): stage transition and uniqueness
nodes.math: Two open obligations are carried as named hypothesis objects that consumers quantify over explicitly — the corpus declares no axioms. Stage transition: for every lawful stage $\sigma$, every monic irreducible residual factor $\psi \ne X$ of degree $g \ge 1$ with root $\bar z$, every coprime read pair $(e', h')$ with normalized Bézout data, and every read-pair lift $\hat\Phi$ of $\psi$ meeting the augmentation threshold, a successor stage with key $\hat\Phi$ and the recorded transition laws exists. Uniqueness: for a fixed factorization shape, any two members of the shape's normalized prefix set whose invariant data are Galois-conjugate have literally equal invariant data.
nodes.lean:
def StageTransHyp (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] : Prop :=
  ∀ (σ : Stage p F), StageCoreL σ →
    ∀ (ψ : Polynomial ↥σ.K) (g : ℕ), ψ.Monic → ψ.natDegree = g → Irreducible ψ →
      ψ ≠ Polynomial.X → 1 ≤ g →
    ∀ (zbar : Fˣ), Polynomial.eval₂ σ.K.subtype ((zbar : Fˣ) : F) ψ = 0 →
    ∀ (e' h' : ℕ) (s' t' : ℤ), 1 ≤ e' → 1 ≤ h' → Nat.gcd e' h' = 1 →
      (e' : ℤ) * s' + (h' : ℤ) * t' = 1 → 0 ≤ t' ∧ t' < (e' : ℤ) →
    ∀ (Φhat : Polynomial ℤ_[p]), IsReadLift σ ψ g e' h' Φhat →
      IAug σ Φhat e' h' →
    ∃ σ' : Stage p F, σ'.Φ = Φhat ∧ σ'.e = e' ∧ σ'.h = h' ∧ σ'.s = s' ∧ σ'.t = t' ∧
      TransitionCoreL σ σ' Φhat e' h' zbar ∧ StageCoreL σ'

def OmUniqHyp {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (n : ℕ) (pol : CanonPolicy p F) (P : Shape n) : Prop :=
  ∀ H H' : History p F, H ∈ PrefSet n pol P → H' ∈ PrefSet n pol P →
    EtaGalEq (etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H) (etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H') →
    etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H = etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H'
nodes.note: The corpus's discipline: content that could not yet be proved is a hypothesis every consumer names, never an axiom; the uniqueness hypothesis as typed is itself conditionally refuted by a compiled scratch witness and is consumed by nothing — the final uniqueness form is a pending negotiation.

nodes.title: The canonical lifting policy
nodes.math: The classifier is run with one lift rule. At a recentering node $\nu$, the exact lift specification asks for a polynomial $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ in the key's coefficient class with $t \ne 0$, $w(t) = w(\Phi)$, and residual equal to the constant monomial at the recorded center. The canonical policy chooses (by the axiom of choice) any realizer of this specification when one exists, else $0$. It is deterministic and blind: it reads only the node's stage and center, never its lift field. It is ratified that every realizer of the same specification yields identical graded data, masses, counts and gates downstream, so the choice function can later be replaced by an explicit formula with zero consumer changes.
nodes.lean:
def RecenterLiftSpec {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (ν : Node p F) (tL : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) : Prop :=
  inC ν.σ.Φ tL ∧ tL ≠ 0 ∧ ν.σ.w tL = ν.σ.w ν.σ.Φ ∧
    ν.σ.R tL = LaurentPolynomial.C ν.center * LaurentPolynomial.T 0

noncomputable def polOM (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] :
    CanonPolicy p F where
  liftOf ν := if h : ∃ tL, RecenterLiftSpec ν tL then h.choose else 0
  blind := by
    intro ν t
    rfl
nodes.note: The one policy instance every normalized class in the pipeline is keyed to; its totality on coherent realizable histories is a proved theorem of this corpus, not an assumption.

nodes.title: Seed-to-jet assembly: the bridge's core deliverable
nodes.math: Given a history $H$ with a lawful key tower, a graded seed at box size $n \times N$ (with $N \ge 1$), coherence, realizability, confinement to the degree-$n$ box, the root-shape law, an emitted-value family, and the per-step condition that each read's fresh clause supports are unpinned on the prior state — the full jet-presentation package for $H$ exists: a chain of digit systems on the $n \times N$ box, starting at the full box, with per-read fresh clauses (coordinate strips plus value clauses) satisfying the band, cover, assembly, multiplicity, recursion and zero-set laws that the counting engine consumes.
nodes.lean:
theorem jetSetup_of_seed {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n N : ℕ} {H : History p F} {keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]}
    (hkeys : KeysLawful H keys) (S : PresentSeed p F H n N keys) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hcoh : HistoryCoherent H) (hreal : Realizable H) (hbox : InBox n H)
    (hd4 : RootD4 H) (vOf : VOf p (n * N)) (hunp : SeedFreshUnpinned H n N S vOf) :
    Nonempty (JetSetup H n N (n * N))
nodes.gate: hkeys — a lawful key tower (dischargeable from a run); S — the graded seed (HC1's open deliverable); hcoh/hreal/hbox — coherence, realizability, box confinement; hd4 — the root read's shape law; hunp — fresh supports unpinned per step (its discharge is the open zero-set geometry). ADDITIONALLY the compiled proof consumes two still-open lemmas (the zero-set induction step and a level-set no-straddle lemma), so its footprint records unproved dependencies (Lean's sorryAx marker).
nodes.note: The corpus capstone: this field-by-field assembly is what turns the small seed into the 29-field package (29 named structure fields) the engine's declared boundary deferred; its own proof body is complete, but it is conditional both on named hypotheses and on the two open lemmas in its dependency cone.

nodes.title: Presentability at every level above the threshold
nodes.math: Fix a factorization shape $P$ of degree $n$. Suppose SEED-EXIST: for every class of $P$'s normalized prefix set and every box level $N$ at or above $P$'s threshold level, a lawful key tower and a graded seed exist. Suppose also normalization of presentation classes, the root-shape law, and the unpinned condition. Then at every such level $N$ the shape is presentable: a presented family — one jet package per class, with the normalization data — exists. The reduction is the deliverable; the seed is the remaining open input.
nodes.lean:
theorem present_exist_of_seeds {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {P : Shape n}
    (hseed : ∀ (i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P) (N : ℕ), P.NP (polOM p F) ≤ N →
       ∃ keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p], KeysLawful (reprOf i) keys ∧
         Nonempty (PresentSeed p F (reprOf i) n N keys))
    (hnorm : PresentNorm n (polOM p F) P)
    (hd4 : ∀ i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P, RootD4 (reprOf i))
    (hunp : ∀ (i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P) (N : ℕ) (keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p])
       (S : PresentSeed p F (reprOf i) n N keys) (vOf : VOf p (n * N)),
       SeedFreshUnpinned (reprOf i) n N S vOf) :
    ∀ N : ℕ, P.NP (polOM p F) ≤ N →
      Nonempty (Presented p F n N (n * N) (polOM p F) P)
nodes.gate: hseed — SEED-EXIST, the single frozen statement of HC1's deliverable (key tower + graded seed per class and level); hnorm — normalization of presentation classes (its policy discharger is fenced, so consumers carry it explicitly); hd4 — root-shape law per class; hunp — per-step unpinned condition. Inherits the unproved-dependency marker (sorryAx) through the assembly theorem's open dependency cone.
nodes.note: The outbound seam to the density-counting corpus: this is the presentability row that corpus's interface demands, discharged down to the seed.

nodes.title: The threshold object
nodes.math: Under the same hypotheses as presentability, the shape's threshold object exists: jet presentations at every box level $N$ at or above the shape's threshold, packaged as the single object the density-counting pipeline consumes (built by choice over the exact range of levels).
nodes.lean:
theorem threshold_of_seeds {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {P : Shape n}
    (hseed : ∀ (i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P) (N : ℕ), P.NP (polOM p F) ≤ N →
       ∃ keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p], KeysLawful (reprOf i) keys ∧
         Nonempty (PresentSeed p F (reprOf i) n N keys))
    (hnorm : PresentNorm n (polOM p F) P)
    (hd4 : ∀ i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P, RootD4 (reprOf i))
    (hunp : ∀ (i : PrefIdx n (polOM p F) P) (N : ℕ) (keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p])
       (S : PresentSeed p F (reprOf i) n N keys) (vOf : VOf p (n * N)),
       SeedFreshUnpinned (reprOf i) n N S vOf) :
    Nonempty (Threshold p F n (polOM p F) P)
nodes.gate: Same four gates as presentability (hseed, hnorm, hd4, hunp), threaded through; the same inherited unproved dependencies.
nodes.note: One-line composition of presentability with the counting corpus's threshold constructor — the terminal interface this corpus exports.

nodes.title: The digit-system recursion law
nodes.math: The constructed digit-system chain $\Sigma$ satisfies the frozen recursion the jet package demands: for each read $i$ inside the history, provided read $i$'s fresh clause supports are unpinned on the prior state, a digit vector $x$ solves $\Sigma_{i+1}$ if and only if $\Theta_i(x)$ solves $\Sigma_i$ and $\Theta_i(x)$ satisfies read $i$'s fresh stratum. The condition is automatically free at $i = 0$ (nothing is pinned before the root read).
nodes.lean:
theorem mkSigma_recursion {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    (H : History p F) (n N : ℕ) {keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]}
    (S : PresentSeed p F H n N keys) (vOf : VOf p (n * N))
    (hunp : SeedFreshUnpinned H n N S vOf)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length) :
    ∀ x : Fin (n * N) → ZMod p,
      (mkSigma H n N S vOf (i+1)).IsSolution x ↔
        ((mkSigma H n N S vOf i).IsSolution (S.Theta i x) ∧
          mkStratum H n N S vOf i (S.Theta i x))
nodes.gate: hunp — read-i's fresh supports carry no pin of the prior state; genuinely gating: the unconditioned form was machine-refuted on junk histories and retired, and the condition's per-step discharge at i > 0 is exactly the open zero-set geometry.
nodes.note: The hard kernel of the state chain: its route survived two machine-refuted transcription bugs (untransported-coordinate errors in the attachment spec, each repaired by a documented deviation-correction with the refutation artifact retired only after the repair).

nodes.title: Every run has a lawful key tower
nodes.math: If a history $H$ is a classifier run on $f$, then a key family $(\mathrm{keys}_i)$ exists that equals the recorded child key at every interior read and satisfies the recorded landing law at every read, the final one included. (The keys are extracted from the run's own designated-next-key witnesses.)
nodes.lean:
theorem keys_exist_of_run {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} {H : History p F}
    (h : ReadsOf p F n f H) :
    ∃ keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p], KeysLawful H keys
nodes.note: No axioms beyond Lean's core. This is the re-keyed replacement of a retired claim: the earlier version, keyed only to coherence rather than to runs, is provably false — see the compiled refutation node.

nodes.title: The canonical policy is total on coherent histories
nodes.math: At every recentering node of a coherent, realizable history, a realizer of the recentering-lift specification exists — assuming the complete eligibility triple (unramified frame, nonzero recorded center, augmentation threshold) at the final read only; interior reads obtain it from coherence. Hence the canonical policy's choice is well-defined and satisfies its specification at every such node. Each leg of the eligibility triple is machine-checked necessary (a legal coherent history kills every realizer when any leg fails at the last node), and under the run predicate the final landing law supplies the triple outright, so runs need no extra hypothesis.
nodes.lean:
theorem polOM_total {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {H : History p F} (hcoh : HistoryCoherent H) (hreal : Realizable H)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i < H.nodes.length)
    (hrec : (H.nodes[i]'hi).species = ReadSpecies.recentering)
    (helig : i + 1 = H.nodes.length → D10Eligible (H.nodes[i]'hi)) :
    ∃ tL : Polynomial ℤ_[p], RecenterLiftSpec (H.nodes[i]'hi) tL
nodes.gate: helig — the complete eligibility triple at the final read only; this guard is not dead weight: its necessity is machine-checked in the same file (the unguarded statement was obstruction-refuted), and it is discharged automatically for runs.
nodes.note: Verified clean footprint; guarantees the policy definition never silently degenerates to its junk branch on the histories the pipeline actually uses.

nodes.title: Galois normalization of residue roots
nodes.math: Every shape-matched, coherent, realizable, in-box history $H$ has a Galois class-mate: there exist a field automorphism $\varphi$ of $F$ and a history $H'$ matching the same shape, fully root-normalized (every node's residue root is the canonical root), whose invariant data at every read is exactly the $\varphi$-transport of $H$'s — hence Galois-equal to $H$'s — and which is again coherent, realizable and in-box; if $H$ was canonical for the lifting policy, so is $H'$.
nodes.lean:
theorem galois_normalize {n : ℕ} {P : Shape n} (H : History p F)
    (hm : (P : ShapePrefix).MatchesHist H) (hcoh : HistoryCoherent H)
    (hreal : Realizable H) (hbox : InBox n H) :
    ∃ (φ : F ≃+* F) (H' : History p F),
      (P : ShapePrefix).MatchesHist H' ∧
      (∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : r < H'.nodes.length),
        (((H'.nodes[r]'hr).zbar : Fˣ) : F) = canonRoot (H'.nodes[r]'hr)) ∧
      (∀ r : Fin (P : ShapePrefix).reads.length,
        ((etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H' r).1
            = fun k => φ ((etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H r).1 k)) ∧
        ((etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H' r).2
            = fun k => φ ((etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H r).2 k))) ∧
      EtaGalEq (etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H) (etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H') ∧
      HistoryCoherent H' ∧ Realizable H' ∧ InBox n H' ∧
      ((polOM p F).IsCanon H → (polOM p F).IsCanon H')
nodes.note: Verified clean footprint; one of the two halves (with lift swap, still open) of the normalization totality that presentation classes rest on.

nodes.title: Rigidity: Galois-transported normalized classes have equal invariants
nodes.math: Two members of a shape's normalized prefix set related by a full-history Galois transport — a field automorphism $\varphi$ of $F$ fixing the base frame field pointwise and carrying one history's residue roots, residual-factor images and side digits onto the other's — have literally equal invariant data. Proof mechanism: the least-root normalization fixes the residue root at every read, and the coherence tower propagates base-fixedness of $\varphi$ up every frame field, so every recorded value is $\varphi$-fixed and the transport collapses to the identity.
nodes.lean:
theorem presentNorm_unique {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {P : Shape n} :
    ∀ H H' : History p F,
      H ∈ PrefSet n (polOM p F) P → H' ∈ PrefSet n (polOM p F) P →
      (∃ φ : F ≃+* F, HistGalTransport φ H H') →
      etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H = etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H'
nodes.note: The transport-keyed form is the third statement of this unit: two earlier stronger forms (unguarded, then adjacency-guarded) were each refuted by compiled scratch witnesses, and a note-read adjudicated the over-strength as a blueprint artifact — the surviving statement is the one the source note actually asserts.

nodes.title: Lift swap to the canonical policy (open)
nodes.math: Assuming the stage-transition hypothesis: every policy-free realizable prefix member $H$ has a class-mate $H'$ — same shape match, literally equal invariant data — that is canonical for the canonical lifting policy, and again coherent, realizable and in-box. In words: recorded lifts can be swapped to the canonical policy without disturbing any recorded class data.
nodes.lean:
theorem lift_swap {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {P : Shape n} (hst : StageTransHyp p F)
    (H : History p F) (hH : H ∈ PrefSetAny n P) :
    ∃ H' : History p F,
      (P : ShapePrefix).MatchesHist H' ∧
      etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H' = etaData (P : ShapePrefix) H ∧
      (polOM p F).IsCanon H' ∧
      HistoryCoherent H' ∧ Realizable H' ∧ InBox n H' := by
  sorry
nodes.note: One of the corpus's three open legs (a fenced unproved goal); it also carries the stage-transition named hypothesis as an explicit binder — its downstream consumer (normalization totality) is therefore doubly conditional, and its footprint records the unproved dependency through this hole.

nodes.title: The zero-set induction step (open)
nodes.math: The inductive step of the zero-set/counting invariant, still open: if the invariant holds for the digit system after reads $0, \dots, i$ (downsets literal at the recorded heights, pins confined, interior coordinates zero), then it holds after read $i+1$ — the transported pins remain literal at the new frame's heights, the fresh cuts are exact, and interior coordinates of the new read solve to zero. Split into four legs (transport, fresh exactness, interior zeros, confinement) plus the assembled step; the interior-zeros leg is the blocking one: without the seed's transport-literality law the assembled statement is refutable for a bad seed — which is exactly why that law was placed as a seed obligation rather than assumed.
nodes.lean:
theorem zc_step {n N : ℕ} {H : History p F} {keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]}
    (S : PresentSeed p F H n N keys) (vOf : VOf p (n * N))
    (hcoh : HistoryCoherent H) (hreal : Realizable H) (hbox : InBox n H) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i + 1 < H.nodes.length)
    (ih : ZCData (mkSigma H n N S vOf (i+1)) (boxChart n N) (H.htH (i+1)) (H.floorH (i+1))
      ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ * (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).childWidth)) :
    ZCData (mkSigma H n N S vOf (i+2)) (boxChart n N) (H.htH (i+2)) (H.floorH (i+2))
      ((H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).μ * (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).childWidth) := by
  sorry
nodes.note: The pre-declared escalation-risk center of the whole bridge: five of the corpus's nine remaining unproved goals live here, and the seed-to-jet assembly's zero-set field flows through it — this hole is what keeps the assembly capstone conditional on unproved dependencies.

nodes.title: Vertex heredity along a run (open)
nodes.math: At an adjacent consecutive read of a run — the child window reaching the parent's standing vertex, $s_0' + w' = \mu$ — the child's leading pattern digit, mapped into $F$, equals the parent's recorded transported vertex value. Reduced to a single residue: an existential about the recorded child's digit frame that is provably not derivable from the recorded class alone (by a twist symmetry); the identified discharge routes are the seam to HC1's constructed histories, or a fenced upstream definitional identification awaiting the project lead's approval.
nodes.lean:
theorem readsOf_HV {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} {H : History p F}
    (h : ReadsOf p F n f H) (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i + 1 < H.nodes.length)
    (hadj : (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).s0 + (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).wSide
      = (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ) :
    (((H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).pat ((H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).wSide / (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).e)
        : ↥(H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.K) : F)
      = (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).vtx := by
nodes.note: One fenced unproved goal; the bulk of the derivation (from the run predicate's vertex read-off clause) is proved in the same file — what remains is exactly the recorded-vs-constructed instance mismatch documented in-file.

nodes.title: The vertex pin at consecutive reads (vacuous at its steep perimeter)
nodes.math: At consecutive reads $(i, i+1)$ of a run, for any development of $f$ in the child key extending past the parent's residual order $\mu$: the coefficient at slot $\mu$ is nonzero, and its child-frame weight equals the frame stretch times the parent line's value at the vertex base $\mu \cdot (\text{child width})$. This is the single transport law the three cross-frame vertex-transport units consume.
nodes.lean:
theorem K1_readVertexPin {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F] [Finite F]
    {n : ℕ} {f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]} {H : History p F}
    (h : ReadsOf p F n f H) (i : ℕ) (hi1 : i + 1 < H.nodes.length)
    (B : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (Nd : ℕ)
    (hdev : IsDevelopment (H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.Φ f B Nd)
    (hNd : (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ < Nd) :
    B ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ) ≠ 0 ∧
      (((H.nodes[i+1]'hi1).σ.w (B ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ)) : ℚ))
        = (H.strFrame (i+1) : ℚ) *
          (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).line.at
            ((H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).μ * (H.nodes[i]'(by omega)).childWidth)
nodes.note: Proved with no unproved goals and no axioms beyond Lean's core, BUT with a mandatory disclosure: for non-recentering parents with e·g ≥ 2, the proof closes via a machine-checked inconsistency of the recorded transition data (the coherence definition's read-pair keying is a flagged faithfulness bug making genuinely steep runs unrecordable) — so on that intended range the theorem holds vacuously and must not be cited as machine-checked transport mathematics; only the recentering-parent and the g = 1 corner legs are substantive.

nodes.title: Gate: the run predicate is inhabited on concrete data
nodes.math: The run predicate is not vacuous: there exist a one-node history $H_0$ over $\mathrm{GF}(4)$ at $p = 2$ — the root-only inert read for $n = 2$ (residual degree $g = 2$, order $\mu = 1$) — and a concrete monic quadratic $f = X^2 + 2X + 4$ over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ such that $H_0$ is a classifier run on $f$: all six per-read clauses, the landing law at the key $X^2 + 2X + 4$ and the vertex read-off included, are realized.
nodes.lean:
theorem gate_readsOf_inert2 :
    ∃ (H₀ : History 2 F4) (f : Polynomial ℤ_[2]),
      H₀.nodes.length = 1 ∧
      (∀ h0 : 0 < H₀.nodes.length,
        (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).species = ReadSpecies.root ∧
        (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).g = 2 ∧ (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).μ = 1) ∧
      ReadsOf 2 F4 2 f H₀
nodes.note: No axioms beyond Lean's core; re-verified after each strengthening of the run predicate — this gate is the designed over-strengthening tripwire: any clause a concrete witness cannot discharge sends the definition back to design, and the newest clause (vertex read-off) passed it.

nodes.title: Gate: the 1/4 inert-density anchor recomputed through the bridge
nodes.math: At the coverage-floor box size $2 \times 1$: the concrete root-only inert history at $p = 2$ over $\mathrm{GF}(4)$ carries a lawful key tower, an explicit graded seed, and an explicit jet package whose total pin count is $2$ and whose stratum mass satisfies $\text{mass} \cdot 2^2 = 2^{2 \cdot 1}$ — i.e. the bridge's counting machinery reproduces the independently recorded $1/4$ density of the inert stratum at $n = 2$. The floor $N = 1$ is forced: the earlier version quantifying over all $N \ge 1$ was machine-refuted at $N = 2$ (the pin count is box-size dependent, exactly per the source note's own box-size proviso).
nodes.lean:
theorem gate_order0_inert :
    ∃ (H₀ : History 2 F4) (keys : ℕ → Polynomial ℤ_[2]),
      KeysLawful H₀ keys ∧
      H₀.nodes.length = 1 ∧
      (∀ h0 : 0 < H₀.nodes.length,
        (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).species = ReadSpecies.root ∧
        (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).g = 2 ∧ (H₀.nodes[0]'h0).μ = 1) ∧
      ∃ (S : PresentSeed 2 F4 H₀ 2 1 keys) (J : JetSetup H₀ 2 1 (2 * 1)),
        totalPins J (topLocus 2 (2 * 1)) = 2 ∧
        Nat.card (J.SHZ (topLocus 2 (2 * 1))) * 2 ^ 2 = 2 ^ (2 * 1)
nodes.note: No axioms beyond Lean's core and no seed hypothesis (seed and jet package constructed concretely — that is the point); the refutation of the over-quantified earlier form is preserved as a compiled record at lean/U27_OBSTRUCTION_negation.lean.

nodes.title: Gate: inert and split produce different masses
nodes.math: At $p = 3$ over $\mathrm{GF}(9)$, for every box level $N \ge 1$: there are concrete one-node root histories — inert ($g = 2$) and split ($g = 1$), both with $\mu = 1$ — with explicit jet packages at box size $2 \times N$ whose stratum masses differ ($3^{2N - |D_{\text{in}}|} \ne 3^{2N - |D_{\text{sp}}|}$, the inert history pinning strictly more coordinates). The bridge's counting data genuinely distinguishes factorization types.
nodes.lean:
theorem gate_order0_sep (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ (Hin Hsp : History 3 F9)
      (Jin : JetSetup Hin 2 N (2 * N)) (Jsp : JetSetup Hsp 2 N (2 * N)),
      Hin.nodes.length = 1 ∧ Hsp.nodes.length = 1 ∧
      (∀ h0 : 0 < Hin.nodes.length,
        (Hin.nodes[0]'h0).species = ReadSpecies.root ∧
        (Hin.nodes[0]'h0).g = 2 ∧ (Hin.nodes[0]'h0).μ = 1) ∧
      (∀ h0 : 0 < Hsp.nodes.length,
        (Hsp.nodes[0]'h0).species = ReadSpecies.root ∧
        (Hsp.nodes[0]'h0).g = 1 ∧ (Hsp.nodes[0]'h0).μ = 1) ∧
      Nat.card (Jin.SHZ (topLocus 3 (2 * N)))
        ≠ Nat.card (Jsp.SHZ (topLocus 3 (2 * N)))
nodes.note: Fully proved, with concrete witnesses at every level N ≥ 1 — the second-prime companion to the p = 2 density gate, guarding against a counting apparatus that is consistent but constant.

nodes.title: Compiled refutation of the retired key-existence claim
nodes.math: The pre-revision claim 'every coherent history admits a lawful key tower' is false. Given any coherent history whose last node is a recentering read, zero out that node's lift: coherence is preserved (compiled surgery lemma), but no key whatsoever can satisfy the landing law at the last read (compiled, key-independent), refuting the retired sentence verbatim. The moral: the landing law at the final read is a property of runs on an actual polynomial, not of coherent records — which is why the surviving key-existence theorem is keyed to the run predicate.
nodes.lean:
theorem retiredKeysExist_false_of_witness {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {F : Type*} [Field F]
    [Finite F] (Hw : History p F) (hcoh : HistoryCoherent Hw)
    (hrec : (Hw.nodes[Hw.nodes.length - 1]'(U1neg.last_lt Hw)).species
      = ReadSpecies.recentering) :
    ¬ RetiredKeysExistStmt p F
nodes.note: No axioms beyond Lean's core. Scope disclosure, recorded in-file: the refutation mechanism (surgery, coherence preservation, key-independent landing failure) is fully compiled, but the concrete recentering-ended witness history it fires on is deferred to HC1's child-stage construction — the refutation is conditional on that inhabitation, not yet an absolute counterexample.

role: This corpus is the computational core of the formalization: a Lean model of the Okutsu-Montes higher-order Newton-polygon algorithm as a total function on monic polynomials known modulo p^N, the object that computes p-adic factorization behavior even at wildly ramified primes. It supplies the counting theory that turns the classifier's per-shape strata into a single rational function of q — with an explicit split between guarded abstract results and instantiated ones: the assembly and wild self-loop resummation theorems are proved as implications from per-shape counting-limit hypotheses (discharged for the tame/separable shapes, open for the wild self-loop shapes), while the general-p exhaustion covering and the degree-2 instantiations (including the full n = 2, p = 2 density tie with proved exhaustion) are instantiated theorems. A faithfulness layer ties classifier fibers to genuine Q_p-factorizations; it rests on exactly two cited Guardia-Montes-Nart axioms, each scoped to the shape menus, guarded by axiom-free anchor theorems and machine-checked mutation refutations — the density theorems themselves use no axioms beyond Lean's core. The real-instance and uniformity capstones (separate corpora) consume its classifier, shape menus, coverings, and faithfulness theorems.
oneLiner: Formalizes the Montes classifier: polygons, counting, wild resummation, guarded faithfulness

nodes.title: The lower Newton polygon as a computable convex hull
nodes.math: For a nonempty finite set $S \subset \mathbb{N}^2$ of dots $(i,v)$ — coefficient index $i$ plotted against $p$-adic valuation $v$ — the lower Newton polygon is the function $\mathrm{np}_S : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}$, $\mathrm{np}_S(x) = \max_{\ell}\, \ell(x)$: the maximum over the VALID candidate lines. Candidates are indexed by ordered pairs of dots of $S$ — the secant line through the two dots when their abscissae differ, and, by convention, the horizontal line through the dot for a repeated pair (a slope-0 junk value is also used when two distinct dots share an abscissa); the diagonal pairs make the family nonempty even for a singleton $S$ and anchor the value $v$ at $x = i$. A candidate is valid when it lies weakly below every dot of $S$; validity is nonempty (the horizontal line through a minimum-height dot qualifies), so the maximum is well-defined for every nonempty $S$. This is the lower convex hull built directly as data: it is convex, lies weakly below every dot, and its breakpoints (vertices) and segments (sides, with rational slopes and lattice endpoints) are extracted as finite lists.
nodes.lean:
variable (S : Finset (ℕ × ℕ))

noncomputable def npHeight (hS : S.Nonempty) (x : ℚ) : ℚ :=
  (validLines S).sup' (validLines_nonempty S hS) (fun PR => pairLine PR.1 PR.2 x)
nodes.note: The polygon is built as a max of supporting chords (not mathlib's set-theoretic convexHull) so vertices, sides and slopes are computable data; the file records a repair: an earlier min-of-lines draft was concave (an infimum of affine maps), refuted by the three-dot example {(0,3),(1,0),(2,3)}, and was replaced by the max-over-valid-supporting-lines form whose convexity is proved.

nodes.title: The order-r type: the data one node of the Montes tree carries
nodes.math: An order-$r$ OM type bundles a residue tower of finite fields $F_0 \subseteq F_r$ with residue-extension degree $\delta = [F_r : F_0]$, the order-$r$ lattice Newton polygon $N_r$, the residual polynomial $R_r \in F_r[Y]$ with residual degree $d_r = \deg R_r$, the key-polynomial degree $m_r$, and a cluster size $\mathrm{cs}$, subject to the ties $\delta = [F_r:F_0]$, $d_r = \deg R_r$, and the size law $d_r \le \mathrm{cs}$.
nodes.lean:
structure OMType where
  order : ℕ
  F0 : Type
  Fr : Type
  [field_F0 : Field F0]
  [finite_F0 : Finite F0]
  [field_Fr : Field Fr]
  [finite_Fr : Finite Fr]
  [alg : Algebra F0 Fr]
  δ : ℕ
  Nr : L4.LatticePolygon
  Rr : Fr[X]
  dr : ℕ
  keyDeg : ℕ
  cs : ℕ
  hResidueDeg : δ = Module.finrank F0 Fr
  hResidualDeg : dr = Rr.natDegree
  hDrLeCs : dr ≤ cs
nodes.note: The size law d_r ≤ cs replaced an earlier strict law that was false at the generic root and had silently made the first density instance vacuous (the since-quarantined predecessor chain) — the repair is documented in the field's docstring; the law is carried as a proof field the recursion maintains (cited Guardia-Montes-Nart content carried as a hypothesis — a deliberate footprint choice, not a free axiom).

nodes.title: The digit expansion: a bijection of finite coefficient boxes
nodes.math: Over $R = \mathbb{Z}/p^N$ with $N \ge 1$, fix a monic $\varphi \in R[X]$ of degree $m$. Every monic $g$ of degree $km$ has a unique $\varphi$-adic expansion $g = \varphi^k + \sum_{j<k} b_j\,\varphi^j$ with digit polynomials $\deg b_j < m$, and $g \mapsto (b_0, \dots, b_{k-1})$ is a bijection between the monic degree-$km$ box and $k$-tuples of digits; counting both sides recovers $(p^N)^{km}$.
nodes.lean:
variable (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime]

noncomputable def developEquiv (N m k : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (φ : (ZMod (p ^ N))[X])
    (hφ : φ.Monic) (hm : φ.natDegree = m) (_hm0 : 0 < m) :
    QuotientBox.monicBox p N (k * m) ≃ (Fin k → Polynomial.degreeLT (ZMod (p ^ N)) m)
nodes.note: The engine's basic change of coordinates — every deeper OM order reads digits of this expansion; the two-sided-inverse proofs are machine-checked core-only, and the file records a blueprint erratum (the bijection is false at N = 0, so 0 < N is required).

nodes.title: The truncated classifier: running Montes on a polynomial known mod p^N
nodes.math: For a monic degree-$n$ polynomial $f$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^N$, the classifier runs the OM iteration — order-0 Newton polygon of $f$, residual factorization over the residue field, one child per distinct residual factor, descent (via the $\varphi$-adic development) on repeated factors — under a well-founded degree budget, and outputs the resulting finite tree shape. It is a total function from the finite box of monic polynomials mod $p^N$ to discrete tree shapes, so its fibers can be counted exactly.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def classify (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (n : ℕ) :
    (N : ℕ) → QuotientBox.monicBox p N n → ClusterShape :=
  fun N f => classifyAux p N n n f (rootCtx p N f) (clusterSize_rootCtx p N f)
nodes.note: THE central object: the densities of the whole project are defined by counting this function's fibers, and the faithfulness layer (cited axioms + axiom-free anchors) is exactly what ties its output to genuine Q_p factorizations.

nodes.title: The finite, prime-independent menu of decided shapes
nodes.math: For degree $n$, depth window $D$, height window $K$, and factorization type $\sigma$, the menu is a finite set of classifier output shapes keyed to $\sigma$: the previous-wave menu (order-0 leaves, mixed-slope literals, descend chains ending in ramified/inert/two-sided-split leaves) united with the split-residual family that first becomes nonempty at $p > 2$. No prime appears in the definition.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def omMenu7 (n D K : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) : Finset ClusterShape :=
  ChainMenu6.omMenu6 n D K σ ∪ splitUShapes n D K σ

theorem omMenu6_subset_omMenu7 (n D K : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) :
    ChainMenu6.omMenu6 n D K σ ⊆ omMenu7 n D K σ
nodes.note: The interface both the leaf-faithfulness axiom and the density instances key on; each menu extension re-scoped the axiom, with a machine-checked recovery theorem deriving every previous scope back so consumers stay byte-unchanged.

nodes.title: What a genuine p-adic factorization certificate is
nodes.math: A certificate for monic $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ is a list of monic polynomials $g_1, \dots, g_k$ with $\prod_i g_i = f$, each irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, each carrying local-field data for $\mathbb{Q}_p[X]/(g_i)$. Its type is the multiset $\{(e_i, f_i)\}$ of ramification indices and residue degrees, read from the bundles via mathlib's ramification/inertia vocabulary.
nodes.lean:
structure QpFactorization (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (f : ℤ_[p][X]) where
  factors : List (ℤ_[p][X])
  prod_eq : factors.prod = f
  monic : ∀ g ∈ factors, g.Monic
  irred : ∀ g ∈ factors, Irreducible (g.map (algebraMap ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p]))
  data : ∀ g ∈ factors, LocalFactorData p g

noncomputable def qpType {f : ℤ_[p][X]} (F : QpFactorization p f) : FactorizationType :=
  ⟨(F.factors.pmap (fun g hg => efOf p (F.data g hg)) (fun _ h => h) : List (ℕ × ℕ))⟩
nodes.note: The genuine arithmetic vocabulary, distinct from classifier output: faithfulness theorems conclude the existence of such a certificate, while the density computations never depend on one — that separation is what keeps the density capstones' axiom footprints down to Lean's core.

nodes.title: Cited: the theorem of the index bounds every valuation the classifier reads
nodes.math: For $g$ monic of degree $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{N+1}$ in the bulk — i.e. with discriminant valuation $v_p(\mathrm{disc}\,g) < N$ — every coefficient valuation the classifier reads (on its own hull dots, and on its own sides' columns up to the residual degree) is $< N$. This is the read-set-restricted, $f$-keyed form of Guardia-Montes-Nart's theorem of the index, $\mathrm{ind}(f) \le v_p(\mathrm{disc}\,f)$ (arXiv:0807.2620, Thm 4.18/Cor 4.19); it makes the classifier's reading stable under reduction of the truncation level above the discriminant valuation.
nodes.lean:
axiom omReadValuation_lt_of_certLevel_fkeyed (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (g : QuotientBox.monicBox p (N + 1) n)
    (hbulk : PadicLift.zmodValuation p (N + 1) (g.1.discr) < N) :
    GuardSuppR p N hN g ∧ GuardSideR p N hN g
nodes.note: Replaces a FALSE uniform version that asserted the guards for every g — refuted by g = xⁿ + pᴺ, which the bulk hypothesis now excludes; one of the false axioms the standing faithfulness audit caught, with a faithfulness entry in docs/AXIOM_FAITHFULNESS.md.

nodes.title: Cited: menu fibers genuinely factor with the keyed type
nodes.math: For every prime $p$, degree $n$, type $\sigma$, menu shape $T$ in the $\sigma$-keyed menu, and monic $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ of degree $n$ whose truncated digit data lies in $T$'s dispatch fiber, there exists a genuine $\mathbb{Q}_p$-factorization certificate of $f$ of type exactly $\sigma$. Cited to Guardia-Montes-Nart Thm 1.15 + 1.19 + Cor 1.20 (the order-1 leaf dichotomy with explicit $(e,f)$), jointly with the standard local-field structure theory the paper presupposes (Serre, Local Fields I-II), which mathlib cannot yet supply at the pin.
nodes.lean:
axiom om_leaf_faithful (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (n N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (σ : FactorizationType) (T : ClusterShape) (D K : ℕ)
    (hT : T ∈ ChainMenu7.omMenu7 n D K σ)
    (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n)
    (hfib : fiberOf7 p n N hN T f hf hdeg) :
    ∃ F : QpType.QpFactorization p f, QpType.qpType p F = σ
nodes.note: Existence-only and menu-fiber-scoped, never universal — no uniformity, rationality, measure or density term appears in it; consumed only by the faithfulness theorems (the density capstones use no axioms beyond Lean's core), and its (e,f) payload is corroborated by axiom-free anchors plus seven recorded mutation refutations.

nodes.title: Axiom-free anchor: Eisenstein polynomials are totally ramified
nodes.math: For monic $g \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$, Eisenstein at $p$, with $\deg g > 0$: every local-factor data bundle for $g$ has ramification index $e = \deg g$ and residue degree $f = 1$ — the classical total ramification of Eisenstein polynomials, proved for the exact bundle vocabulary the faithfulness axiom concludes in.
nodes.lean:
theorem ef_of_eisenstein {g : ℤ_[p][X]} (hg : g.Monic)
    (hEis : g.IsEisensteinAt (maximalIdeal ℤ_[p])) (hdeg : 0 < g.natDegree)
    (D : QpType.LocalFactorData p g) :
    QpType.eOf p D = g.natDegree ∧ QpType.fOf p D = 1
nodes.note: Proved from mathlib alone (no axioms beyond Lean's core); it machine-forces the cited leaf axiom's (e,f) payload at the wild gate stratum, so the axiom's conclusion there is guarded by proof, not trusted from the citation.

nodes.title: Refutation record: swapping the ramification data in the axiom yields contradiction
nodes.math: Take the leaf axiom's hypotheses verbatim but mutate its conclusion type from $\{(2,1)\}$ (ramified quadratic) to $\{(1,2)\}$ (inert quadratic). Then $\bot$ is derivable: the gate fiber is nonempty, the mutated axiom forces a singleton factorization whose factor carries $(e,f)=(1,2)$, while the axiom-free Eisenstein anchor forces $(e,f)=(2,1)$ on the same bundle.
nodes.lean:
axiom om_leaf_faithful_MUTATED_efswap (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (n N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (σ : FactorizationType) (T : ClusterShape) (hT : T ∈ WildMenu.omMenuW n σ)
    (f : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (hf : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n)
    (hfib : B.classify p n N (PadicLift.toBox p n N hN f hf hdeg) = T) :
    ∃ F : QpType.QpFactorization p f,
      QpType.qpType p F = (⟨{((1 : ℕ), (2 : ℕ))}⟩ : FactorizationType)

theorem mutation_efswap_refuted : False
nodes.note: Machine-checked 2026-07-21 as a scratch compiled against the live modules, with the zero-error output and axiom census recorded verbatim in the file's evidence block (the scratch itself is not committed to the library build); one of seven recorded mutation refutations (split-type, wrong-e, inert/split swaps at successive gates) pinning the cited axiom's payload in both coordinates.

nodes.title: Open: vertex stability of the hull under dot changes (the one fenced incomplete proof)
nodes.math: If every hull vertex of $S'$ is a dot of $S$, every dot of $S$ lies weakly above $S'$'s lower hull, and every abscissa occurring in $S$ occurs in $S'$, then $S$ and $S'$ have the same Newton-polygon vertex list. A true, purely combinatorial statement about lower convex hulls of finite lattice dot sets.
nodes.lean:
theorem npVertices_stable_of_hull_preserved (S S' : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (hS : S.Nonempty) (hS' : S'.Nonempty)
    (hpres : ∀ P ∈ NewtonPolygon.npVertices S' hS', P ∈ S)
    (habove : ∀ P ∈ S, NewtonPolygon.npHeight S' hS' (P.1 : ℚ) ≤ (P.2 : ℚ))
    (habs : ∀ P ∈ S, ∃ Q ∈ S', Q.1 = P.1) :
    NewtonPolygon.npVertices S hS = NewtonPolygon.npVertices S' hS'
nodes.note: The classic OM corpus's sole unproved goal, deliberately fenced (the newer development corpora carry their own fenced goals, censused separately — see the axiom-census node): its only consumer is a hull-invariance chain that is off every capstone path (the menu-checking route bypassed it), and the docstring itemizes exactly the two list/adjacency facts that remain.

nodes.title: Assembly: per-shape counting limits give one rational density function
nodes.math: Let $M$ be any finite menu of shapes. Assume for each $T \in M$ the counting limit: the number of monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $2^N$ classified to shape $T$, divided by $2^{nN}$, converges to the engine value $\mathrm{omCount}(T,2)$ as $N \to \infty$ (the formalization's fixed real prime is $p = 2$). Then there exist polynomials $\mathrm{num}, \mathrm{den}$ with $\mathrm{den} \ne 0$ and $\mathrm{den}(q) \ne 0$ for every integer $q > 1$, such that $\sum_{T \in M} \mathrm{omCount}(T,q) = \mathrm{num}(q)/\mathrm{den}(q)$ for all $q > 1$, and the real normalized menu-sum counts converge to $\mathrm{num}(2)/\mathrm{den}(2)$.
nodes.lean:
theorem montes_allorders_of_hnode (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) (M : Finset ClusterShape)
    (h_node : ∀ T ∈ M,
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N => M8.stratumCount (M9.rawCount n) T N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (omCount T M9.realP))) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ M, omCount T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N => (∑ T ∈ M, M8.stratumCount (M9.rawCount n) T N)
            / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)))
nodes.gate: h_node — for every menu shape T, the normalized classifier-fiber counts converge to the engine value omCount(T, 2); discharged unconditionally for the tame/separable shapes, open for the wild self-loop shapes
nodes.note: The implication itself is machine-checked (no axioms beyond Lean's core); rationality needs no per-leaf hypothesis because the engine value's rationality is proved for every shape (cluster nodes included), and a soundness gate shows the skeleton reproduces the unconditional order-0 capstone when specialized to the separable menu.

nodes.title: The complete conditional density theorem: one explicit wild hypothesis
nodes.math: For any menu $M$ and any self-loop predicate: given (i) the per-shape counting limit for every non-self-loop shape of $M$ (supplied unconditionally by the proved tame theorems), and (ii) the aggregate self-loop counting limit — the single wild hypothesis — numerically supported by Monte-Carlo/PARI sampling, but its general statement remains a conjecture — the menu density $q \mapsto \sum_{T \in M} \mathrm{omCount}(T,q)$ is one rational function $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ with denominator nonvanishing at every $q > 1$, and the real ($p=2$) normalized counts converge to $\mathrm{num}(2)/\mathrm{den}(2)$.
nodes.lean:
theorem density_eq_engine_conditional (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) (M : Finset ClusterShape)
    (isSelfLoop : ClusterShape → Prop)
    (hTame : ∀ T ∈ M, ¬ isSelfLoop T → hNodeLimit n T)
    (hSelfLoop : SelfLoopHNode n isSelfLoop) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ M, omCount T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N => (∑ T ∈ M, M8.stratumCount (M9.rawCount n) T N) / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)))
nodes.gate: hTame — per-shape counting limits for the non-self-loop shapes (discharged, with no axioms beyond Lean's core, for the separable / multi-slope menus); SelfLoopHNode — the aggregate wild self-loop counting limit (MC/PARI-confirmed, open)
nodes.note: The wild hypothesis is deliberately stated at the aggregate limit level because five per-depth count-identity routes to it were refuted with exact counterexamples (the self-loop wall); everything beyond the two named inputs is unconditional composition, its footprint verified in the file's axiom census (Lean core only).

nodes.title: The tame case needs no hypothesis at all
nodes.math: If the menu contains no self-loop shape — which holds at every tame prime $p > n$, since a self-loop requires $p \mid e \le n$ — then, given the proved unconditional tame counting limits, the density equals the engine rational function with no wild hypothesis: the self-loop input is discharged vacuously. Tame $\Rightarrow$ fully unconditional.
nodes.lean:
theorem density_eq_engine_tame (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) (M : Finset ClusterShape)
    (isSelfLoop : ClusterShape → Prop)
    (hNoSelfLoop : ∀ T, ¬ isSelfLoop T)
    (hTame : ∀ T ∈ M, hNodeLimit n T) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ M, omCount T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N => (∑ T ∈ M, M8.stratumCount (M9.rawCount n) T N) / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)))
nodes.gate: hNoSelfLoop — the menu has no self-loop shape (true at every tame prime p > n); hTame — the tame per-shape counting limits (discharged, with no axioms beyond Lean's core, for the separable order-0 shapes by a companion theorem in the same file)
nodes.note: Certifies where the wild difficulty genuinely lives: at tame primes the whole density theorem composes from unconditionally proved counting limits, and the one open hypothesis of the conditional theorem is vacuous.

nodes.title: The single wild hypothesis, and the wall that forced its shape
nodes.math: For a shape $T$, the counting limit asserts that the number of monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $2^N$ classified to $T$, divided by $2^{nN}$, converges to $\mathrm{omCount}(T,2)$. The self-loop hypothesis asserts this limit for every self-loop shape — the wild shapes whose OM tree restarts the same cluster at ever deeper levels.
nodes.lean:
def hNodeLimit (n : ℕ) (T : ClusterShape) : Prop :=
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun N => M8.stratumCount (M9.rawCount n) T N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
    Filter.atTop
    (nhds (omCount T M9.realP))

def SelfLoopHNode (n : ℕ) (isSelfLoop : ClusterShape → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ T : ClusterShape, isSelfLoop T → hNodeLimit n T
nodes.note: Five per-depth finite-level count-identity routes to this limit were refuted, each with an exact counterexample (the refutation record is kept on file; a companion module proves the tempting filtration frame counts a strictly larger residue-blind event), so the hypothesis is taken at exactly the aggregate level that numerical evidence supports and nothing stronger.

nodes.title: The wild self-loop density is a geometric fixpoint
nodes.math: Let $r = q^{-w(s)}$ with $w(s) = s(s+1)/2 - 1$ be the exposed per-level restart ratio of a size-$s$ self-loop cluster ($s, q \ge 2$). The closed value $b = d_0(1-r)^{-1}$ satisfies the self-consistency equation $b = d_0 + r\,b$ (the depth-0 seed plus the same cluster restarted one level deeper), is its unique solution, and equals the limit of the weighted geometric depth sums $d_0 \sum_{k<d} r^k$. At $p = q = 2$, $s = 2$, seed $d_0 = 1/2$, it lands exactly on the engine value $2/3$.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def selfLoopFixpointValue (depth0 : ℚ) (s q : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  depth0 * (MontesAxiom.countPivot s q)⁻¹

theorem selfLoopFixpoint_eq {s q : ℕ} (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hs : 2 ≤ s) (depth0 : ℚ) :
    selfLoopFixpointValue depth0 s q
      = depth0 + slExposedRatio s q * selfLoopFixpointValue depth0 s q
nodes.note: No axioms beyond Lean's core; this is the mechanism that lets wildly ramified strata sum to a rational function of q — an infinite tower of ever-deeper restarts of the same cluster, resummed as a geometric series, tied in the same file to an actual engine value rather than a free constant.

nodes.title: Degree two at the wild prime, all depths: the full density tie with proved exhaustion
nodes.math: Over the complete $n = 2$, $p = 2$ stratum tree (both residue points, all depths, all leaf kinds), for each quadratic type $\sigma$: (R) the closed density family is one rational function $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ with denominator nonvanishing at every $q > 1$; (V) the genuine $N \to \infty$ decided-count limit equals $\mathrm{num}(2)/\mathrm{den}(2)$, which is $1/3$ for each of the three types; (B) bracket uniqueness holds unconditionally — any value squeezed at every level between the decided count and decided-plus-undecided count IS the density, with the exhaustion (undecided mass $\to 0$) proved outright; (P) palindromy of $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$, conditional on an explicit tame functional-equation hypothesis.
nodes.lean:
theorem montes_unconditional_n2_full (σ : FactorizationType) (hσ : σ.degree = 2)
    (htameFE : TameFunctionalEquation realFW6 2 σ) :
    (∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ shapesOf6 σ, C6 T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      (realMW6.countingDensity σ = num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)) ∧
      IsPalindromic num den) ∧
    ∀ d : ℚ, (∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N →
        realMW6.decidedCount σ N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (2 * N) ≤ d ∧
        d ≤ realMW6.decidedCount σ N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (2 * N)
              + realMW6.undecidedCount N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (2 * N)) →
      d = realMW6.countingDensity σ
nodes.gate: htameFE — a tame functional equation for the full model, gating ONLY the palindromy clause (P); clauses (R), (V), (B) including the exhaustion are unconditional (palindromy was later placed out of the project's scope entirely)
nodes.note: Footprint is Lean core only (no cited axiom on any path); the file's scope block discloses that the sigma-keying of two counting fibers is definitional on the counting side (outside the then-declared axiom scope) and that the q-family carried here is the p=2-complete tree — the general-p model with the extra split-residual family lives in the uniform model module.

nodes.title: Every counted stratum genuinely factors with its keyed type
nodes.math: For the full degree-2 counting model at $p = 2$: every monic quadratic over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ whose truncated coefficients lie in any counted fiber — order-0 split or inert cells, or any depth-$k$ descend chain ending in a ramified, inert, or split leaf — admits a genuine $\mathbb{Q}_2$-factorization certificate of exactly the type $\sigma$ that fiber is keyed to in the density.
nodes.lean:
theorem fullFiber_hasType {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) {σ : FactorizationType} {F : W6Fiber}
    (hOK : W6FiberOK F N σ)
    {f : Polynomial ℤ_[M9.realP]} (hf : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = 2)
    (hfib : fiberPred F N
      (PadicInt.toZModPow N (f.coeff 0), PadicInt.toZModPow N (f.coeff 1))) :
    ∃ Fc : QpType.QpFactorization M9.realP f, QpType.qpType M9.realP Fc = σ
nodes.gate: om_leaf_faithful — the cited GMN leaf axiom is in this theorem's axiom footprint (Lean core + that axiom exactly, per the file's census); it enters only through the ramified and inert chain legs, on the translated polynomial
nodes.note: This is what makes the density's type labels arithmetic facts rather than bookkeeping; the split families are proved axiom-free above the height budget and their fibers machine-checked empty below it, so the axiom carries exactly the ram/inert leaf content.

nodes.title: The split leaf is proved, not cited: Hensel lifting at every prime
nodes.math: For every prime $p$: a monic quadratic $g$ over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ whose digit data at heights $(2m, m)$ exhibits a residual pair with two distinct simple roots splits over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ into two linear factors — type $\{(1,1),(1,1)\}$ — by Hensel lifting at each simple residual root of the rescaled polynomial, followed by an explicit proved transport of the certificate back to $g$. This is the leaf-faithfulness conclusion itself, with no axiom.
nodes.lean:
theorem leafFiberU_split_hasType {m L₀ L₁ : ℕ}
    (hL₀ : ChainMenuU.leafNeedU m ≤ L₀) (hL01 : L₀ ≤ L₁)
    {g : ℤ_[p][X]} (hg : g.Monic) (hdeg : g.natDegree = 2)
    (hfib : ChainMenuU.LeafPairU p m L₀ L₁
      (PadicInt.toZModPow L₀ (g.coeff 0), PadicInt.toZModPow L₁ (g.coeff 1))) :
    ∃ F : QpType.QpFactorization p g, QpType.qpType p F = ChainMenu.splitType2
nodes.note: Axiom-free at general p (root-generic Hensel); the split-residual family is the one genuinely new stratum family at p > 2 (pool of size (q-1)(q-2)/2, machine-checked empty at q = 2), and proving it outright keeps the cited axiom's instances on this family redundant by requirement.

nodes.title: Exhaustion at every prime: each cluster pair terminates or measurably stalls
nodes.math: For every prime $p$, every height window $L_0 \le L_1$, and every coefficient pair in the cluster at a residue point: either the pair realizes a terminating chain stratum within budget — a descend prefix ending in one of the four leaf kinds (ramified, inert, two-sided split, or split-residual) — or it lies in an explicitly bounded stall stratum ($p^{L_0 - 1}$ divides the constant coefficient). Proved by strong induction on the budget, with no parity case-split between $p = 2$ and odd $p$.
nodes.lean:
variable (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime]

theorem cluster_coveringP :
    ∀ L₀ L₁ : ℕ, L₀ ≤ L₁ →
    ∀ a : ZMod (p ^ L₀) × ZMod (p ^ L₁),
      ClusterPair p L₀ L₁ a →
      (∃ ms leaf, (∀ m ∈ ms, 1 ≤ m) ∧ leafOK leaf ∧
        2 * ms.sum + leafNeed leaf ≤ L₀ ∧ ChainPair p ms leaf L₀ L₁ a)
      ∨ (∃ ms m, (∀ x ∈ ms, 1 ≤ x) ∧ 1 ≤ m ∧
          2 * ms.sum + leafNeedU m ≤ L₀ ∧ ChainPairU p ms m L₀ L₁ a)
      ∨ (∃ ms, (∀ m ∈ ms, 1 ≤ m) ∧ (ms ≠ [] → 2 * ms.sum + 2 ≤ L₀) ∧
          StallPairP p ms L₀ L₁ a)
nodes.note: The covering that powers unconditional bracket uniqueness in the all-primes uniformity capstone: the stall remainder has mass at most $(\lfloor N/2 \rfloor + 1)\,p^{-(N-1)} \to 0$; no axioms beyond Lean's core, and cross-checked digit-by-digit by an external Python census at p = 2 and p = 3.

role: This corpus is the assembly layer of the formalization: it fixes the abstract interfaces a density theorem is stated against (the density foundation and the abstract-coefficient Montes data), proves the two spine goal theorems (a count-native route using no axioms beyond Lean's core, and an independent measure route resting on the cited Denef-Igusa axioms), and instantiates the spine at real, machine-checked counting models: the sigma-keyed order-0 capstone at p = 2, the first genuinely wild (p divides e) densities, and the all-primes n = 2 uniformity capstone with fixed prime-free rational functions. Machine-checked gates certify exact values (1/4, 1/8, 1/(p+1), ...) and type-separation against the real instances rather than the deliberately weak interfaces. Negative records — the device-only interface witness, the empty order-0 ramified menu, the provably empty wild stratum at p = 2 — mark exactly what is not claimed; the corpus's predecessor capstone chain was found vacuous and is quarantined, and every current capstone names its remaining conditionality (tame functional equation, exhaustion) as an explicit hypothesis.
oneLiner: Abstract density interfaces instantiated to machine-checked uniform densities, every prime

nodes.title: The abstract density interface
nodes.math: An abstract "density foundation": an assignment $\rho(n,\sigma;q)\in\mathbb{Q}$ of a density to each degree $n$, factorization type $\sigma$ (a multiset of ramification/residue pairs $(e_i,f_i)$ with $\sum e_if_i=n$), and residue cardinality $q$; per-shape cluster volumes $C_T(q)$; a finite menu of cluster-tree shapes for each $(n,\sigma)$; polynomial multiplicities $m_T$; the stratification identity $\rho(n,\sigma;q)=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}(n,\sigma)} m_T(q)\,C_T(q)$ for all $q>1$ when $\deg\sigma=n$; and nonnegativity $\rho\ge 0$. It records the cited measure-foundational facts without requiring $\rho$ to be a probability.
nodes.lean:
structure DensityFoundation where
  density : (n : ℕ) → FactorizationType → (q : ℕ) → ℚ
  clusterVolume : ClusterShape → ℕ → ℚ
  shapes : (n : ℕ) → FactorizationType → Finset ClusterShape
  multiplicity : ClusterShape → Polynomial ℚ
  decomposition : ∀ (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType), σ.degree = n → ∀ q : ℕ, 1 < q →
    density n σ q = ∑ T ∈ shapes n σ, (multiplicity T).eval (q : ℚ) * clusterVolume T q
  density_nonneg : ∀ n σ q, 0 ≤ density n σ q
nodes.note: The interface every capstone is stated against; deliberately weak by audit-driven design — statements about a free foundation must enter theorems as hypotheses, never as axioms (an earlier global axiom over a free foundation was machine-refuted). The bridge from this abstract density to a genuine density of p-adic coefficient space is proved at the real instances: lean/LeanUrat/OM/Order0RealDensity.lean (montes_order0_realDensity) identifies the instance density with the N→∞ limit of normalized level-N classifier-fiber counts — the elementary counting form of the Haar-measure density (mathlib has no p-adic Haar measure, so the identification is via exact counts; on the Moves side the analogous landing-cylinder measure theorem is lean/LeanUrat/Moves/L6_measureExact_R4.lean).

nodes.title: The abstract Montes counting data
nodes.math: Abstract Montes data over a counting model with residue cardinality $q$ and degree $n$ (a counting model tracks decided/undecided counts of monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $q^N$ whose normalized decided counts converge): for each type $\sigma$ a finite menu of cluster-tree shapes $T$; level-$N$ stratum counts $\#S_T^{(N)}$; the partition law that the level-$N$ decided count of $\sigma$ equals $\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}(\sigma)}\#S_T^{(N)}$; an abstract per-shape coefficient $C(T,q')$ that is one fixed rational function of $q'$ with denominator nonvanishing for $q'>1$; and the counting limit $\#S_T^{(N)}/q^{nN}\to C(T,q)$ as $N\to\infty$.
nodes.lean:
structure MontesDataV2 (q n : ℕ) (M : CountingModel q n) where
  shapesOf : FactorizationType → Finset ClusterShape
  stratumCount : ClusterShape → ℕ → ℚ
  partition : ∀ (σ : FactorizationType) (N : ℕ),
    M.decidedCount σ N = ∑ T ∈ shapesOf σ, stratumCount T N
  C : ClusterShape → ℕ → ℚ
  C_isRational : ∀ T : ClusterShape, IsRationalFn (fun q' => C T q')
  stratum_tendsto_C : ∀ (σ : FactorizationType), ∀ T ∈ shapesOf σ,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => stratumCount T N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (C T q))
nodes.note: The second-revision spine interface, replacing an earlier interface whose hard-coded coefficient shape was numerically refuted; deliberately weak (satisfiable by degenerate instances), so non-vacuity is enforced at the real instances by the value gates, never here.

nodes.title: Palindromy of a rational function, semantic form
nodes.math: $R=\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ satisfies the functional equation $R(1/x)=R(x)$ at every $x\neq 0$ where both sides are defined. This is the faithful, degree-robust encoding: an earlier coefficient-reversal encoding was degree-blind and wrongly rejected palindromic functions of unequal reduced degrees such as $t/(t^2+1)$.
nodes.note: The palindromy clause of every capstone; adopted after a statement audit caught the unfaithful coefficient-reversal form.

nodes.title: The tame functional-equation hypothesis
nodes.math: The predicate: for a foundation $F$, degree $n$, and type $\sigma$, there is a single rational function $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ representing $F$'s density at every tame prime $q>n$, and it is palindromic ($R(1/t)=R(t)$). The proofs use it only through "infinitely many tame primes", enough for the $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ identity theorem.
nodes.lean:
def TameFunctionalEquation (F : DensityFoundation) (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) : Prop :=
  ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
    (∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → n < q → F.density n σ q = num.eval (q : ℚ) / den.eval (q : ℚ)) ∧
    IsPalindromic num den
nodes.note: Formerly a global AXIOM over an arbitrary foundation, machine-refuted as false-as-stated (a legal foundation with density q forces x⁻¹ = x); now a predicate consumed only as an explicit hypothesis — its faithful real-instance discharge (via the cited Del Corso–Dvornicich functional equation) awaits the still-open exhaustiveness work plus the projective bridge.

nodes.title: The real order-0 density foundation
nodes.math: The first non-trivial real instance of the density interface: its density is the $\sigma$-keyed order-0 engine menu-sum $\rho(m,\sigma;q'):=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}_0(m,\sigma)}c_T(q')$, where the menu holds the order-0 separable cluster shapes of type $\sigma$ and $c_T$ is the proved engine evaluator (a residue-field choice polynomial times a volume factor). Nonnegativity is proved at every natural $q'$ (via necklace-count integrality), and the stratification identity is the exact multiplicity-times-volume split on this menu.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def realF2 : DensityFoundation where
  density := fun m σ q' => ∑ T ∈ OMCountV2.omMenu m σ, OMCountV2.omCount T q'
  clusterVolume := fun T q' => OMCountV2.omVolume T q'
  shapes := fun m σ => OMCountV2.omMenu m σ
  multiplicity := fun T => OMCountV2.omMultiplicity T
  decomposition := by … -- (proof field omitted)
  density_nonneg := by … -- (proof field omitted)
nodes.note: The instance the canonical capstone fires through, replacing a quarantined vacuous predecessor whose density was identically 0; its menu is the order-0 separable slice, so ramified types get an empty menu here by construction (see the empty-menu gate below).

nodes.title: Decided density equals the menu sum of coefficients
nodes.math: For any counting model $M$ and Montes data $D$ over it, the genuine decided-limit density of type $\sigma$ — the $N\to\infty$ limit of $M$'s normalized decided counts — equals the finite menu-sum $\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}(\sigma)}C(T,q)$ of the per-shape coefficients at the model's residue cardinality. Proved from the partition law, the per-shape counting limits, and uniqueness of limits in $\mathbb{Q}$; no rationality is used.
nodes.lean:
variable {q n : ℕ} {M : CountingModel q n} (D : MontesDataV2 q n M)

theorem countingDensity_eq_sum_coeff (σ : FactorizationType) :
    M.countingDensity σ = ∑ T ∈ D.shapesOf σ, D.C T q
nodes.note: The decomposition workhorse of the spine; the all-primes uniformity capstone fires this theorem directly (it bundles no palindromy), and every value gate certifies its instance through it.

nodes.title: The count-native goal theorem (abstract spine)
nodes.math: Given a counting model $M$, Montes data $D$, a degree-$n$ type $\sigma$, and a foundation $F$ whose density agrees with the count-native menu-sum $g_\sigma(q')=\sum_T C(T,q')$ at every $q'>1$ (the bridge), plus the tame functional equation for $F$: there is one $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}\in\mathbb{Q}(t)$, denominator nonvanishing at all $q'>1$, representing $g_\sigma$ there, whose value at the model's own $q$ is the genuine decided-limit density, and which is palindromic. Palindromy transfers from the tame representative by the $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ identity theorem over the infinitely many tame primes.
nodes.lean:
theorem goal_theorem_montes
    {q n : ℕ} (M : CountingModel q n) (D : MontesDataV2 q n M)
    (σ : FactorizationType) (F : DensityFoundation) (hσ : σ.degree = n)
    (hbridge : ∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' →
      F.density n σ q' = ∑ T ∈ D.shapesOf σ, D.C T q')
    (htameFE : TameFunctionalEquation F n σ) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ D.shapesOf σ, D.C T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      (1 < q → M.countingDensity σ = num.eval (q : ℚ) / den.eval (q : ℚ)) ∧
      IsPalindromic num den
nodes.gate: hbridge — the foundation's density coincides with the count-native menu-sum at every q' > 1 (discharged definitionally at the real instances); htameFE — the tame functional equation for F (feeds only the palindromy clause).
nodes.note: The canonical spine capstone: it drops the measure route entirely, and it uses no axioms beyond Lean's core — every Montes/counting/tame input is a hypothesis or theorem, never an axiom.

nodes.title: The measure-route goal theorem
nodes.math: For every abstract density foundation $F$ equipped with an OM-bridge (its per-shape cluster volumes realized by the fixed $p$-adic Okutsu–Montes cluster measure) and satisfying the tame functional equation, the per-type density $\rho(n,\sigma;\cdot)$ is represented by a single palindromic rational function of $q$ at every $q>1$ — wild primes included. Rationality is derived through the Igusa/Denef cell decomposition, never assumed.
nodes.lean:
theorem goal_theorem
    (F : DensityFoundation) (B : OMBridge F) (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) (hσ : σ.degree = n)
    (htameFE : TameFunctionalEquation F n σ) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q : ℕ, 1 < q → den.eval (q : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        F.density n σ q = num.eval (q : ℚ) / den.eval (q : ℚ)) ∧
      IsPalindromic num den

nodes.note: The independent second route to the goal: a ∀-foundations statement (no constructed foundation is proven equal to the true p-adic Haar density — mathlib has no p-adic Haar measure); kept alongside the count-native spine, which carries none of these measure axioms.

nodes.title: The density interface has a witness
nodes.math: The abstract density-foundation interface is inhabited: an explicit witness (density $\equiv 0$, empty shape menus, cluster volume a fixed concrete cluster measure) satisfies all structural fields simultaneously, so the $\forall F$ goal theorems do not quantify over an empty type and the recorded measure identities are jointly consistent.
