nodes.title: The order-0 capstone at the real prime
nodes.math: For every $n>0$ and every type $\sigma$ of degree $n$, assuming the tame functional equation for the real order-0 foundation, there is one $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}\in\mathbb{Q}(t)$ such that: (R) the $\sigma$-keyed order-0 engine density $g_\sigma(q')=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}_0(n,\sigma)}c_T(q')$ equals $\mathrm{num}(q')/\mathrm{den}(q')$ at every $q'>1$; (V) the genuine decided-limit density of the real counting model at $p=2$ — the $N\to\infty$ limit of normalized classifier-fiber counts of monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $2^N$ — equals $\mathrm{num}(2)/\mathrm{den}(2)$; (P) $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ is palindromic.
nodes.lean:
theorem montes_unconditional (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (σ : FactorizationType) (hσ : σ.degree = n)
    (htameFE : TameFunctionalEquation realF2 n σ) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ OMCountV2.omMenu n σ, OMCountV2.omCount T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      ((realM2 n hn).countingDensity σ = num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)) ∧
      IsPalindromic num den
nodes.gate: htameFE — the tame functional equation for the real order-0 foundation (certified a non-trivial constraint by a gate, but not yet discharged; it feeds only the palindromy clause (P) — clauses (R) and (V) are independently provable without it).
nodes.note: THE canonical capstone since the 2026-07-21 rebase (its vacuous predecessor is quarantined); it uses no axioms beyond Lean's core, and the certified value is the order-0 DECIDED-stratum density — the tie to the full type density sits behind the exhaustive companion's open hypothesis.

nodes.title: The order-0 capstone with the explicit full-density bracket
nodes.math: On top of the base capstone's clauses, assume additionally that the normalized undecided mass drains: $\mathrm{undecided}_N/2^{nN}\to 0$. Then bracket uniqueness holds: any $d\in\mathbb{Q}$ lying in every normalized level-$N$ bracket $[\mathrm{decided}_N,\ \mathrm{decided}_N+\mathrm{undecided}_N]$ ($N\ge1$) equals the decided-limit density. This is the only definable full-density tie short of formalizing "the true factorization type over $\mathbb{Q}_p$".
nodes.lean:
theorem montes_unconditional_exhaustive (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (σ : FactorizationType)
    (hσ : σ.degree = n) (htameFE : TameFunctionalEquation realF2 n σ)
    (hExhaust : Filter.Tendsto
      (fun N => (realM2 n hn).undecidedCount N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    (∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ OMCountV2.omMenu n σ, OMCountV2.omCount T q') = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      ((realM2 n hn).countingDensity σ = num.eval (M9.realP : ℚ) / den.eval (M9.realP : ℚ)) ∧
      IsPalindromic num den) ∧
    ∀ d : ℚ, (∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N →
        (realM2 n hn).decidedCount σ N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N) ≤ d ∧
        d ≤ (realM2 n hn).decidedCount σ N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N)
              + (realM2 n hn).undecidedCount N / (M9.realP : ℚ) ^ (n * N)) →
      d = (realM2 n hn).countingDensity σ

nodes.note: The guarded form of the full-density claim: it makes the decided-vs-full gap an explicit named hypothesis instead of papering over it.

nodes.title: Gate: the inert quadratic density is exactly 1/4

nodes.math: $3$ is prime and tame for $n=2$, and the real foundation's density at the inert quadratic type at $q=3$ is $1/3>0$. nodes.title: The order-0 density theorem at every prime
nodes.math: For each prime $p$, degree $n>0$, and type $\sigma$: one $p$-INDEPENDENT rational function represents the order-0 separable density family $q'\mapsto\sum_{T\in\mathrm{menu}_0(n,\sigma)}c_T(q')$ at all $q'>1$, and the normalized counts of monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $p^N$ whose classifier lands on a menu shape (a genuine finite fiber count) converge, as $N\to\infty$, to that function's value at $p$.
nodes.lean:
theorem montes_order0_density_general_prime (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (σ : FactorizationType) :
    ∃ (num den : Polynomial ℚ), den ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → den.eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ sepShapesOf n σ,
            rootCount M7.cellsOfShapeWF M6.treeSize M7.cellsOfShapeWF_descend T q')
          = num.eval (q' : ℚ) / den.eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun N =>
          (∑ T ∈ sepShapesOf n σ,
            (Nat.card {f : QuotientBox.monicBox p N n // B.classify p n N f = T} : ℚ))
            / (p : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (num.eval (p : ℚ) / den.eval (p : ℚ)))
nodes.note: The uniformity content at order 0, all degrees and all primes: the SAME rational function works at every prime — the general-prime, sigma-keyed strengthening of the p = 2 instance, with a companion positivity gate at every prime.

nodes.title: The all-primes uniformity capstone for quadratics
nodes.math: FIXED polynomials with no prime appearing in them — $\mathrm{num}_{\mathrm{ram}}=1$, $\mathrm{den}_{\mathrm{ram}}=X+1$; $\mathrm{num}=X$, $\mathrm{den}=2X+2$ for both inert and split — such that for EVERY prime $p$ (the wild $p=2$ included) and every degree-2 type $\sigma$: (R) the model's density family equals $\mathrm{num}_\sigma(q')/\mathrm{den}_\sigma(q')$ at every $q'>1$; (V) the genuine decided-limit density of the COMPLETE $n=2$ stratum tree at $p$ is $\mathrm{num}_\sigma(p)/\mathrm{den}_\sigma(p)$ — that is, $1/(p+1)$ ramified and $p/(2(p+1))$ inert/split; (B) bracket uniqueness holds OUTRIGHT, the exhaustion (normalized undecided mass $\to0$) being PROVED at every $p$ by a pure counting envelope $\le(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1)\,p^{-(N-1)}$. The three densities sum to $1$ at every prime.
nodes.lean:
variable (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime]

theorem montes_uniform_n2 (σ : FactorizationType) (hσ : σ.degree = 2) :
    (uniformDen σ ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ q' : ℕ, 1 < q' → (uniformDen σ).eval (q' : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧
        (∑ T ∈ shapesOfU σ, CU T q')
          = (uniformNum σ).eval (q' : ℚ) / (uniformDen σ).eval (q' : ℚ)) ∧
      ((M7 p).countingDensity σ
          = (uniformNum σ).eval ((p : ℕ) : ℚ) / (uniformDen σ).eval ((p : ℕ) : ℚ)
        ∧ (uniformDen σ).eval ((p : ℕ) : ℚ) ≠ 0)) ∧
    ∀ d : ℚ, (∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N →
        (M7 p).decidedCount σ N / (p : ℚ) ^ (2 * N) ≤ d ∧

role: This corpus is the engine room shared by both proof routes. It defines what "one fixed rational function of q" means, proves the abstract well-founded induction that turns any Okutsu-Montes-style tree recursion with rational coefficients into a single uniform rational function, and supplies the finite-field counting lemmas (squarefree count, Gauss necklace count), the Newton-polygon cell volume, and the palindromy-by-interpolation lemmas that the capstones consume. It also fixes the semantics of "density" (the limit of level-N decided counts, never the trivial box count) and the corrected nested self-loop recursion. Finally, it holds the measure route's declared analytic boundary — the cited Denef-Igusa cell-recursion axiom and the Guardia-Montes-Nart structural axioms, together with an explicit consistency model — and the axiom-census file that machine-prints every capstone theorem's trust footprint.
oneLiner: Shared rationality engine, counting lemmas, density semantics, cited-axiom boundary

nodes.title: What it means to be one fixed rational function of q
nodes.math: A function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Q}$ is a *uniform rational function of $q$* if there is a single pair of polynomials $\mathrm{num}, \mathrm{den} \in \mathbb{Q}[t]$, with $\mathrm{den}$ nonvanishing at every integer $q > 1$, such that $f(q) = \mathrm{num}(q)/\mathrm{den}(q)$ for all $q > 1$. One fraction serves every prime power simultaneously — this is the precise form of the theorem's "independent of the prime" clause.
nodes.note: The target predicate of the entire program — every density capstone concludes that some counting limit satisfies it; the file also proves closure under sums, products, finite list sums/products, and division by pole-free denominators, all with no axioms beyond Lean's core.

nodes.title: The rationality engine: well-founded tree recursions have rational solutions
nodes.math: Suppose each "shape" $T$ carries a finite list of contributions — a coefficient function of $q$ paired with a list of child shapes of strictly smaller size — and a function $\mathrm{vol}$ satisfies, for all $q > 1$, $\mathrm{vol}(T,q) = \big(\sum_{\text{cells}} \mathrm{coeff}(q) \prod_{\text{children}} \mathrm{vol}(\text{child},q)\big) / \mathrm{pivot}(T,q)$. If every coefficient is a uniform rational function of $q$ and the pivot is rational and nonzero for $q > 1$, then $\mathrm{vol}(T,\cdot)$ is itself a uniform rational function of $q$ for every shape $T$. Proof: strong induction on size, closing each step with the rational-function closure lemmas. No prime $p$ appears anywhere in the argument.
nodes.lean:
theorem clusterVol_isRational
    {Shape : Type*} (size : Shape → ℕ)
    (clusterVol : Shape → ℕ → ℚ)
    (contribs : Shape → List ((ℕ → ℚ) × List Shape))
    (pivot : Shape → (ℕ → ℚ))
    (hrec : ∀ (T : Shape) (q : ℕ), 1 < q →
        clusterVol T q
          = ((contribs T).map
                (fun c => c.1 q * (c.2.map (fun ch => clusterVol ch q)).prod)).sum / pivot T q)
    (hdescend : ∀ (T : Shape), ∀ c ∈ contribs T, ∀ ch ∈ c.2, size ch < size T)
    (hcoeff : ∀ (T : Shape), ∀ c ∈ contribs T, IsRationalFn c.1)
    (hpivot_rat : ∀ (T : Shape), IsRationalFn (pivot T))
    (hpivot_ne : ∀ (T : Shape) (q : ℕ), 1 < q → pivot T q ≠ 0) :
    ∀ T : Shape, IsRationalFn (clusterVol T)
nodes.note: The central new inductive step of the paper: both the measure route and the count-native route are instantiations of this one abstract engine.

nodes.title: Newton-polygon cell volume is a characteristic-independent power of q
nodes.math: For a lattice Newton polygon $\Pi$ of width $e$, with integer ceiling heights $\lceil h_i \rceil$ over each column and vertex count $V(\Pi)$: if the Haar volume of the cell $\{g : \mathrm{NP}(g) = \Pi\}$ factors as the product over columns of the one-variable box/shell measures ($\mu\{v(c_i) = h_i\} = (1-Q^{-1})Q^{-h_i}$ at vertex columns, $\mu\{v(c_i) \ge \lceil h_i \rceil\} = Q^{-\lceil h_i \rceil}$ elsewhere), then it equals $(1-Q^{-1})^{V(\Pi)}\, Q^{-A(\Pi)}$ with $A(\Pi) = \sum_i \lceil h_i \rceil$. Both $V$ and $A$ are pure lattice data: a wildly ramified slope $a/b$ with $p \mid b$ gives the same $(V, A)$ as a tame slope of the same reduced fraction, so the cell volume cannot see $p$.
nodes.lean:
theorem cellVolume_eq
    (cellVol : LatticePolygon → ℕ → ℚ) (pg : LatticePolygon) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q)
    (hfactor : cellVol pg Q = ∏ i : Fin pg.width, columnMeasure pg Q i) :
    cellVol pg Q = bb1Value pg Q
nodes.note: The hypothesis records the cited Igusa box/shell Haar facts (absent from mathlib at the pin) in the project's recorded-via-hypothesis convention, so the closed form is derived (no axioms beyond Lean's core), never assumed — this is section 5 (BB1) of the human proof.

nodes.title: Squarefree monic polynomials over a finite field number exactly Q^m − Q^(m−1)
nodes.math: Over a finite field $F$ with $Q = |F|$ elements, for every $m \ge 2$ the number of squarefree monic polynomials of degree $m$ is $Q^m - Q^{m-1}$. Proved from scratch via the unique decomposition $R = A \cdot B^2$ ($A$ squarefree monic, $B$ monic) and a strong-induction solve of the resulting convolution identity $Q^n = \sum_{2j \le n} S(n-2j)\, Q^j$.
nodes.lean:
theorem card_squarefreeMonicDegree (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    Nat.card (squarefreeMonicDegree F m) = Nat.card F ^ m - Nat.card F ^ (m - 1)
nodes.note: The complement count $Q^{m-1}$ of non-squarefree polynomials is the "needs refinement" residual count that becomes the genuinely q-varying factor of every wild cell coefficient — mathlib had no squarefree-polynomial count, so this is a from-scratch development.

nodes.title: The Gauss necklace count of irreducible polynomials
nodes.math: Over $\mathbb{F}_Q$, for $d \ge 1$, the number $N_d$ of monic irreducible polynomials of degree $d$ satisfies $d \cdot N_d = \sum_{e \mid d} \mu(e)\, Q^{d/e}$. Proved via the identity $\sum_{e \mid d} e \cdot N_e = Q^d$ (counting the elements of $\mathbb{F}_{Q^d}$ by their minimal polynomials) followed by Möbius inversion.
nodes.lean:
theorem gauss_necklace_count
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [Finite F] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    (d : ℚ) * (Nat.card (L3.monicIrreducibleDegree F d) : ℚ)
      = ∑ e ∈ d.divisors,
          ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius e : ℤ) : ℚ) * (Nat.card F : ℚ) ^ (d / e)
nodes.note: The base of the residue-field combinatorics: it makes the tame shape counts universal polynomials in $Q$ (section 4 of the human proof) and feeds the order-0 counting instances in the OM corpus.

nodes.title: Interpolation from tame primes: one representative rules all primes
nodes.math: Suppose $S = \mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ represents the density $\rho(n,\sigma;q)$ at every $q > 1$ (denominator pole-free there), and $R = \mathrm{tnum}/\mathrm{tden}$ represents the same density at all tame primes $q = p > n$. Then $\mathrm{num} \cdot \mathrm{tden} = \mathrm{tnum} \cdot \mathrm{den}$, i.e. $S = R$ in $\mathbb{Q}(t)$: the tame primes are infinite (Euclid), so the identity theorem for polynomials — a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots — forces the two rational functions to coincide.
nodes.lean:
theorem tame_to_all_primes
    (F : DensityFoundation) (n : ℕ) (σ : FactorizationType) (hσ : σ.degree = n)
    (num den tnum tden : Polynomial ℚ)
    (hden0 : den ≠ 0) (htden0 : tden ≠ 0)
    (hL6 : ∀ q : ℕ, 1 < q → den.eval (q : ℚ) ≠ 0 ∧ F.density n σ q = num.eval (q : ℚ) / den.eval (q : ℚ))
    (htame : ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → n < q →
      F.density n σ q = tnum.eval (q : ℚ) / tden.eval (q : ℚ)) :
    num * tden = tnum * den
nodes.note: Section 12 (L7) of the human proof: whatever holds of the density's representative at the infinitely many easy (tame) primes is forced upon its behavior at the hard (wild) primes as well.

nodes.title: Palindromy transfers along agreement of rational functions
nodes.math: If $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ and $\mathrm{tnum}/\mathrm{tden}$ agree in $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ (cross-multiplied form) and $\mathrm{tnum}/\mathrm{tden}$ is palindromic — satisfying $R(1/x) = R(x)$ — then $\mathrm{num}/\mathrm{den}$ is palindromic. The pointwise transfer fails at poles of $\mathrm{tden}$, so the proof establishes the *polynomial* identity $\widetilde{\mathrm{num}} \cdot \mathrm{den} = \mathrm{num} \cdot \widetilde{\mathrm{den}}$ (tildes = coefficient reversal) on a cofinite set and invokes the identity theorem, making it valid everywhere.
nodes.lean:
theorem isPalindromic_of_agree
    (num den tnum tden : Polynomial ℚ)
    (hden : den ≠ 0) (htden : tden ≠ 0)
    (hagree : num * tden = tnum * den)
    (htpalin : IsPalindromic tnum tden) :
    IsPalindromic num den
nodes.note: This lemma is fully proved, but its tame palindromy input is exactly the capstone hypothesis that remains undischarged on the real instance — so in the current chain the functional-equation clause is conditional even though this transfer step is not.

nodes.title: The order-r Okutsu-Montes shape datum, with anti-caricature ties
nodes.math: A shape records the data of one node of the Montes tree at order $r$: a finite residue field $F_r$ with a genuine algebra structure over the base residue field — so the residue degree is the true extension degree $[F_r : \mathbb{F}]$, not a free integer — the actual order-$r$ residual polynomial over $F_r$ with its degree field tied to the polynomial's real degree, the order-$r$ lattice Newton polygon, and the cluster size that serves as the well-founded descent measure.
nodes.lean:
structure OMShape where
  size : ℕ
  order : ℕ
  Fr : Type
  [instField : Field Fr]
  [instFinite : Finite Fr]
  baseField : Type
  [instBaseField : Field baseField]
  [instBaseFinite : Finite baseField]
  [instAlg : Algebra baseField Fr]
  residueDeg : ℕ
  hResidueDeg : residueDeg = Module.finrank baseField Fr
  polygon : L4.LatticePolygon
  residual : Polynomial Fr
  residualDeg : ℕ
  hResidualDeg : residualDeg = residual.natDegree
nodes.note: The proof-carrying fields exist to block caricature instantiations flagged in an independent audit: with them, |F_r| = q^{residueDeg} is a proved lemma rather than an assumption, and every downstream count is computed from a genuine polynomial over a genuine field extension.

nodes.title: The Guardia-Montes-Nart structural interface (cited axioms)
nodes.math: Three structural facts about the Okutsu-Montes tree, cited from Guardia-Montes-Nart (Trans. AMS 364 (2012)), are declared as axioms: every shape has a finite list of order-$r$ cells (one per Newton-polygon face × residual stratum — the GMN cell partition); a descent operation producing child shapes; and the strict descent law that every descent child of every cell has strictly smaller cluster size (the well-foundedness input). None asserts any volume, rationality, uniformity, or $p$-independence — those are always derived.
nodes.lean:
axiom omCells : (T : OMShape) → List (OMCell T)

axiom descend : OMShape → List OMShape

axiom descend_size_lt :
    ∀ (T : OMShape), ∀ c ∈ omCells T, ∀ ch ∈ c.children, ch.node.size < T.size
nodes.note: Used by the measure route only (the count-native capstones avoid them); the once-axiomatic child-factor tie was demoted to a proved projection lemma by encoding its witnesses in the cell data, and the remaining open gap — that the cell strata reconstruct the full residual — is documented in-file.

nodes.title: The Denef-Igusa cell recursion for the p-adic cluster measure (cited axiom)
nodes.math: An opaque fixed symbol denotes THE conditional $p$-adic Haar cluster measure of each shape (mathlib has no $p$-adic Haar measure, so the object itself is an interface axiom), and the load-bearing analytic axiom asserts the Igusa/Denef cell-decomposition identity for it: for $q > 1$ the cluster measure equals $\big(\sum_{\text{cells}} (\text{residual point count}) \times (\text{Newton-box volume}) \times \prod_{\text{children}} (\text{child cluster measure})\big)$ divided by the geometric self-loop pivot $1 - q^{-w}$. This is a structural measure factorization, never a rationality claim. Citations: Igusa, Local Zeta Functions §7.4; Denef, Invent. Math. 77 (1984).
nodes.lean:
axiom clusterMeasure : OMShape → ℕ → ℚ

axiom AX_cellRecursion (T : OMShape) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q) :
    clusterMeasure T q
      = ((omCells T).map (fun c =>
            residualCountFn T c.residualDeg q
            * L4.bb1Value c.polygon q
            * (c.children.map (fun ch => clusterMeasure ch.node q)).prod)).sum
        / omPivot T q
nodes.note: The history matters: an earlier free-binder form of this axiom was proven logically inconsistent, and a companion axiom was found false-as-stated and deleted (2026-07-02) — which is why the surviving axiom is stated about one fixed object and shipped with a satisfiability model.

nodes.title: The cell-recursion axiom is satisfiable: an explicit model
nodes.math: An explicitly constructed function — defined by well-founded recursion on cluster size, descending through the strict-descent axiom — satisfies exactly the identity that the cell-recursion axiom asserts. Exhibiting this model shows the axiom is satisfiable, hence relatively consistent: the fixed-object formulation cannot derive a contradiction the way its predecessor (with a freely quantified pivot, which forced $1 = 1/2$) provably could.
nodes.lean:
theorem clusterMeasureModel_rec (T : OMShape) (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q) :
    clusterMeasureModel T q
      = ((omCells T).map (fun c =>
            residualCountFn T c.residualDeg q
            * L4.bb1Value c.polygon q
            * (c.children.map (fun ch => clusterMeasureModel ch.node q)).prod)).sum
        / omPivot T q
nodes.note: An artifact of the 2026-06-19 independent verification: it certifies that the current axiom form was adopted precisely because the old one was machine-shown inconsistent — the project's own record of catching a false axiom.

nodes.title: Measure route: every cluster volume is one rational function of q
nodes.math: The fixed conditional $p$-adic cluster measure of every Okutsu-Montes shape is a uniform rational function of $q$. Proof: the cited cell recursion discharges the recursion hypothesis of the abstract rationality engine, whose other inputs are all proved — strict descent from the GMN axiom, coefficient rationality from the finite-field residual count times the Newton-box volume, and pole-freeness of the self-loop pivot. Rationality is never assumed in any axiom; it emerges only through the induction.
nodes.lean:
theorem clusterMeasure_isRational_of_AX :
    ∀ T : OMShape, IsRationalFn (clusterMeasure T)
nodes.gate: clusterMeasure — the opaque cited p-adic Haar cluster-measure interface object; AX_cellRecursion — the Denef-Igusa cell-decomposition identity for it (cited); omCells / descend_size_lt — the GMN finite cell partition and strict size descent (cited)
nodes.note: The complete but axiom-resting second route to rationality: it is independent of the canonical count-native chain, whose capstones deliberately avoid every axiom named in this gate.

nodes.title: The count-native cluster recursion (no measure axioms anywhere)
nodes.math: A cluster-count function defined by well-founded recursion on tree size: $\mathrm{count}(T, q) = \big(\sum_{\text{cells } c} (q^{\delta})^{d_S - 1} \cdot \mathrm{box}(c, q) \cdot \prod_{\text{children}} \mathrm{count}(\cdot, q)\big) / \big(1 - q^{-w(s)}\big)$, where $(q^\delta)^{d_S-1}$ is the proved non-squarefree residual count over $\mathbb{F}_{q^\delta}$, $\mathrm{box}$ is the proved Newton-box value, and $w(s) = s(s{+}1)/2 - 1$ is the self-loop exponent. Built entirely from proved counting blocks — no opaque Haar object appears.
nodes.lean:
noncomputable def clusterCount
    (cells : ClusterShape → List CountCell) (treeSize : ClusterShape → ℕ)
    (hdesc : ∀ (T : ClusterShape), ∀ c ∈ cells T, ∀ ch ∈ c.children, treeSize ch < treeSize T)
    (T : ClusterShape) (q : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ((cells T).attach.map (fun c =>
      countCellCoeff c.1 q
        * (c.1.children.attach.map (fun ch => clusterCount cells treeSize hdesc ch.1 q)).prod)).sum
    / countPivot (treeSize T) q
nodes.note: The shared engine primitive of the count-native route: because it is built only from proved blocks, the density capstones that use it keep an axiom footprint of Lean's core only — the whole point of the 2026-06-20 re-architecture away from the missing p-adic measure foundation.

nodes.title: The refinement-triggering configurations number exactly Q^(d−1)
nodes.math: Over any finite field $F$, the number of non-squarefree (i.e. refinement-triggering) monic polynomials of degree $d_S \ge 2$ is $|F|^{d_S - 1}$ — the difference between the monic count $Q^{d_S}$ and the squarefree count $Q^{d_S} - Q^{d_S - 1}$.
nodes.note: This genuine finite-field count is the q-varying wild-mechanism factor inside every cell coefficient — an earlier audit found the wild count frozen to a constant (so the wild mechanism was never exercised), and this theorem is the repair that makes it a real count rather than a free monomial.

nodes.title: What "the density" means: the decided-count model
nodes.math: A counting model at residue size $q$ and degree $n$ carries, for each factorization type $\sigma$ and precision $N$: the number of coefficient boxes mod $p^N$ whose type is already *certified* by their digits (decided), and the number still undecided; subject to the constraints that decided plus undecided partition the full box $q^{nN}$, the normalized decided counts are monotone in $N$ and converge to a rational value, and mass newly certified after level $N$ is drawn from the level-$N$ undecided pool. The density of type $\sigma$ is *defined* as that decided limit — never the trivial box count, which is identically $1$.
nodes.lean:
structure CountingModel (q n : ℕ) where
  hq : 2 ≤ q
  decidedCount : FactorizationType → ℕ → ℚ
  undecidedCount : ℕ → ℚ
  decidedCount_nonneg : ∀ σ N, 0 ≤ decidedCount σ N
  undecidedCount_nonneg : ∀ N, 0 ≤ undecidedCount N
  typeMenu : Finset FactorizationType
  typeMenu_degree : ∀ σ ∈ typeMenu, σ.degree = n
  decidedCount_off_menu : ∀ σ N, σ ∉ typeMenu → decidedCount σ N = 0
  box_partition : ∀ N, (∑ σ ∈ typeMenu, decidedCount σ N) + undecidedCount N = (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N)
  decided_mono : ∀ σ, Monotone (fun N => decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
  densityVal : FactorizationType → ℚ
  decided_tendsto : ∀ σ, Filter.Tendsto (fun N => decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N))
    Filter.atTop (nhds (densityVal σ))
  upper_tail : ∀ (σ : FactorizationType) (N K : ℕ), N ≤ K →
    decidedCount σ K / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * K)
      ≤ decidedCount σ N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N) + undecidedCount N / (q : ℚ) ^ (n * N)
nodes.note: The semantic heart of the counting route: it fixes the key point that a density is the limit of certified counts, and realizing this structure with genuine p-adic digit counts is exactly what the real instances in the OM corpus do.

nodes.title: The bracket squeeze: vanishing undecided mass determines the density
nodes.math: In any counting model, both brackets are proved: $\mathrm{decided}(\sigma, N) \le \rho(\sigma) \le \mathrm{decided}(\sigma, N) + \mathrm{undecided}(N)$ for every level $N$. If additionally the undecided mass tends to $0$, then the upper bracket also converges to $\rho(\sigma)$, so the density is the unique value squeezed between brackets of vanishing width.
nodes.lean:
theorem countingDensity_is_squeezed_limit {q n : ℕ} (M : CountingModel q n)
    (hU : UndecidedVanishes M) (σ : FactorizationType) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => M.decidedMeasure σ N + M.undecided N) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (M.countingDensity σ))
nodes.note: The vanishing-undecided hypothesis is the imported termination content (the classifier must eventually decide almost all polynomials): it was discharged unconditionally for the full degree-2 model in 2026-07-22, and its general discharge is the open exhaustion question of the later development work.

nodes.title: Guard: the box count is the total, never a density
nodes.math: At every precision $N$, the full box measure (identically $1$) equals the sum over all types of the decided measures plus the undecided remainder. The trivial count of all monic degree-$n$ polynomials mod $p^N$ is therefore the partition total across every type — categorically not the density of any single type $\sigma$.
nodes.lean:
theorem box_is_total_not_density (N : ℕ) :
    M.boxMeasure N = (∑ σ ∈ M.typeMenu, M.decidedMeasure σ N) + M.undecided N
nodes.note: An anti-vacuity record demanded by the project lead: it formally blocks the classic failure mode of "proving" a density theorem that secretly computes the trivial box count 1.

nodes.title: The corrected self-loop collapse: a nested multi-block recursion
nodes.math: The size-$s$ completely-split cluster volume $I_s$ is NOT a single geometric series for $s \ge 3$ (the original blueprint's crux was wrong — the fix is on record). The corrected equation: $I_s \cdot (1 - q^{-w(s)}) = \sum_{P} q^{\underline{r}} \prod_{B \in P} q^{-(|B| + \binom{|B|}{2})} I_{|B|}$, summing over set partitions $P$ of $\{1,\dots,s\}$ into $r \ge 2$ blocks, with $q^{\underline{r}}$ the falling factorial (distinct residue assignments), $w(s) = s(s{+}1)/2 - 1$, and base cases $I_0 = I_1 = 1$. Every block is strictly smaller than $s$ (proved), so the recursion is well-founded.
nodes.lean:
def SatisfiesNested (I : ℕ → ℕ → ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∀ q, I 0 q = 1) ∧ (∀ q, I 1 q = 1) ∧
    ∀ (s q : ℕ), 2 ≤ s → 2 ≤ q →
      I s q * (1 - ((q : ℚ) ^ L5fix.selfLoopExponent s)⁻¹) = nestedRHS I s q
nodes.note: Deliberately a predicate that a constructed solution must satisfy, not an axiom asserting a conclusion — the module records the corrected crux after the naive single-geometric-series collapse was found false for s ≥ 3.

nodes.title: The nested recursion reproduces the known closed forms
nodes.math: Any $I$ satisfying the nested recursion has $I_2 = q/(q+1)$ and $I_3 = q^3(q^2 - q + 1) / \big((q+1)(q^4+q^3+q^2+q+1)\big)$ for all $q \ge 2$: the set partitions of $2$ and $3$ elements into $\ge 2$ blocks are enumerated explicitly (one and four of them), the weights computed, and the pole-free self-loop pivot inverted.
nodes.lean:
theorem nested_reproduces_I3 (I : ℕ → ℕ → ℚ) (hI : SatisfiesNested I) (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    I 3 q = closedI3 q
nodes.note: A machine-checked unit test of the corrected crux against independently derived closed forms (the companion theorem handles $I_2$); the module also upgrades the algebraic pivot identity to the genuine counting limit of finite geometric sums.

nodes.title: The axiom census: machine-printed trust footprints for every capstone
nodes.math: A compile-time audit file containing 739 axiom-printing directives (one #print axioms line per audited declaration): for each capstone and gate theorem of the project it makes Lean's kernel print the exact set of axioms the proof term uses. This is the ground truth for every footprint claim in the documentation — the mechanism by which "this theorem rests only on Lean's core axioms" or "exactly on this one cited axiom" is machine-verified rather than asserted.
nodes.lean:
#print axioms LeanUrat.Goal.goal_theorem
#print axioms LeanUrat.PadicMeasure.clusterMeasure_isRational_of_AX
#print axioms LeanUrat.OM.RealInstanceV2.montes_unconditional
#print axioms LeanUrat.OM.SeriesAssembly.montes_unconditional_n2_full
